description: National baseline for passenger cars. MUTCD signs, signals, pavement markings, and driving practices that are the same in every state. State speed limits, BAC numbers, point systems, and fines are not in this file.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Come to a complete stop
Slow down and proceed with caution
No entry for vehicles
Yield the right-of-way
questions.explanation: An octagonal red sign is STOP (MUTCD R1-1). Stop fully, then yield to pedestrians and cross traffic.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Merge ahead
Yield
Stop ahead
No passing zone
questions.explanation: A downward triangle with a red border is YIELD (MUTCD R1-2). Slow and give the right-of-way.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A roundabout
A road closed ahead
A railroad crossing
A restricted zone
questions.explanation: The round yellow sign with a black X and RR is the railroad advance warning (MUTCD W10-1). A railroad crossing ahead.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: What does a yellow diamond sign tell you?
options: Tourist services
A construction-only rule
A law you must obey
A warning of a condition ahead
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond signs are warning signs. The curve warning shown is MUTCD W1-2.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The maximum legal speed
A minimum speed only
A truck speed only
A suggested speed in good weather
questions.explanation: A white regulatory speed limit sign (MUTCD R2-1) is the maximum legal speed for that stretch.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: One-way street
Do not enter
Stop, then proceed
No parking
questions.explanation: A red circle with a white horizontal bar is Do Not Enter (MUTCD R5-1).

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: What does this pennant-shaped sign mean?
options: Merge from the right
Yield to oncoming traffic
No passing zone
School crossing
questions.explanation: The yellow pennant (MUTCD W14-3) marks the start of a no-passing zone.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Red on a traffic sign usually means
options: Guidance toward a destination
A work-zone detour only
A warning to slow for a curve
Stop, yield, or a prohibition
questions.explanation: MUTCD uses red for stop, yield, and prohibition (do not enter, wrong way).

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An orange sign with black lettering means
options: A temporary work zone
A hospital route
A school zone at all hours
A permanent speed limit
questions.explanation: Orange is reserved for temporary traffic control, including construction and maintenance.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A brown sign is used for
options: Regulatory speed limits
Recreation and culture
Stop and yield
Railroad warnings
questions.explanation: Brown is the MUTCD color for recreation and cultural-interest guidance.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A pentagon-shaped sign means
options: County route
No passing
School
Hospital
questions.explanation: The fluorescent yellow-green or yellow pentagon is the school sign (MUTCD S1-1).

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A round yellow sign with a black X and two Rs warns of
options: A roundabout
A reversible lane
A crossroad
A railroad crossing
questions.explanation: W10-1 is placed in advance of a highway-rail grade crossing. A railroad crossing ahead.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A steady red light means
options: Stop and stay stopped until it changes
Slow and proceed
Yield only to pedestrians
Stop, then go if the way is clear
questions.explanation: A steady circular red means stop. A turn on red is allowed only where state law and the signal permit it.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A flashing red light means
options: The signal is broken
Treat it like a stop sign
Speed up to clear the intersection
Pedestrians only
questions.explanation: Flashing red has the same meaning as a stop sign.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A flashing yellow light means
options: Wrong way
Stop completely every time
Proceed with caution
The road is closed
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow warns you to slow and proceed only when the way is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A steady yellow light means
options: Turn only
Pedestrians may enter against traffic
Speed up
The green is ending
questions.explanation: Steady yellow is the clearance interval. Do not enter if you can stop safely.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A green light means
options: Go when clear, yielding to anyone already there
You must turn
Stop first
You have the automatic right-of-way over everyone
questions.explanation: Green permits movement. It does not cancel your duty to yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A red arrow means
options: Turn after yielding
Do not make that turn
The turn is protected
Flashing mode
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow prohibits the turn or movement it points to.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A solid yellow line on your side of the center of the road means
options: Parking is allowed
You may pass if the next lane is empty
You may not pass
The lane is an HOV lane
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is not allowed from your direction.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A broken yellow center line means
options: A bike lane
A stop line
No passing ever
Passing is allowed
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates opposing traffic and allows passing when it is safe. Passing is allowed when the way ahead is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: White lines separate
options: Traffic moving in the same direction
Only bike lanes
Only shoulders
Traffic moving in opposite directions
questions.explanation: White lane lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow separates opposing directions.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A solid white line on your left means
options: A railroad
You should not change lanes
You must change lanes
Opposing traffic is on your left
questions.explanation: A solid white line on your side discourages or prohibits a lane change. Stay in the lane unless you must cross it to avoid a hazard.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A stop line is
options: A row of raised blue markers
A yellow diagonal stripe
A solid white line across lanes
A broken white line
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line when one is marked. If there is none, stop before the crosswalk. A solid white line across the lane where you must stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: At an all-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time
options: Both go together
The larger vehicle goes first
The driver on the left goes first
The driver on the right goes first
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Entering a roundabout, you must
options: Yield to traffic already circulating
Use the left lane only
Sound the horn
Stop in the circle until waved on
questions.explanation: Yield signs at roundabout entries require you to give way to vehicles already in the circle.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pedestrian in a marked crosswalk
options: Must yield to every car
Has the right-of-way
May cross only on green arrows
Must wave to drivers
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians lawfully in a crosswalk. Has the right-of-way over turning and approaching vehicles.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When red lights are flashing at a railroad crossing you must
options: Honk and proceed
Speed up if no train is visible
Stop and wait until it is clear
Stop only if the gate is fully down
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights at a grade crossing mean stop. Do not go around a lowered gate. Stop and wait until the lights stop and the way is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A crossbuck at a railroad crossing means
options: The road is closed
A bus stop
A truck route
Yield to trains
questions.explanation: The crossbuck (R15-1) marks the crossing and requires yielding to trains.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Yellow flashing lights on a school bus mean
options: The bus is preparing to stop
You may pass at any speed
The bus is out of service
The bus is stopped and you must already be stopped
questions.explanation: Amber or yellow warning lights come on before the red stop lights. Slow down.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When a school bus shows flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you generally must
options: Pass slowly on the left
Stop until the arm is withdrawn
Stop only if you are behind the bus
Honk so children wait
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights and the stop arm require traffic to stop. A few states allow traffic on the far side of a divided highway to proceed; follow your state handbook. Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop and the arm is withdrawn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You should not pass another vehicle
options: In daylight
On a multi-lane highway when the lane is clear
On a hill or curve where you cannot see far enough ahead
When the vehicle ahead signals a right turn and you have a clear left lane
questions.explanation: Do not pass where sight distance is too short, including hills and curves, or where signs or pavement markings forbid it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The no-passing pennant is placed
options: Only in work zones
Overhead at every intersection
On the right shoulder at the end of the zone
On the left side at the start of the zone
questions.explanation: W14-3 is a left-side pennant at the start of a no-passing zone.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: If traffic signals are dark at an intersection, you should
options: Use only the horn
Drive through without slowing
Treat the intersection as if you have a green light
Treat it as an all-way stop
questions.explanation: A dark signal is treated as a stop. Proceed only when it is your turn and the way is clear. Treat it as an all-way stop unless a police officer directs otherwise.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Hydroplaning is most likely when
options: Tires ride on a film of water
You drive in a high gear only
The road is grooved
The pavement is dry
questions.explanation: Standing water can lift the tires off the pavement. Slow down in heavy rain. Tires ride up on a film of water and lose contact with the road.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A shared center two-way left-turn lane is marked with
options: Solid white lines
Yellow two-way arrows
Only blue markers
A red edge line
questions.explanation: The center two-way left-turn lane uses yellow markings and two-direction arrows. Use it only to turn left. Yellow lines and arrows pointing both ways.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An edge line on the right side of the road is usually
options: Blue
Yellow
White
Red
questions.explanation: The right edge line is white. A yellow edge line is used on the left edge of divided highways and one-way roads.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Wrong-way signs are
options: Blue services signs
Orange detour signs
Yellow diamonds
Red and white signs
questions.explanation: WRONG WAY (R5-1a) is a red-and-white regulatory sign used with Do Not Enter at exit ramps.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A green sign is used for
options: Direction and destination guidance
A temporary work zone
A school crossing
A stop or yield requirement
questions.explanation: Green is the MUTCD color for direction, destination, and distance guidance.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A blue sign is used for
options: A railroad crossing
Motorist services
A regulatory speed limit
A curve warning
questions.explanation: Blue is reserved for motorist services and evacuation guidance. Motorist services such as food, fuel, or a hospital.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An octagon is used only for
options: School
Yield
Stop
No passing
questions.explanation: The octagon shape is reserved for the STOP sign so drivers recognize it even if the legend is hidden.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A downward-pointing triangle is used only for
options: No passing zone
Railroad crossing
Do not enter
Yield
questions.explanation: The inverted triangle is reserved for YIELD.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A pennant-shaped sign means
options: No passing
Added lane
Hospital
School zone
questions.explanation: The pennant is the no-passing-zone warning, posted on the left at the start of the zone.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A round yellow sign with a black X and RR means
options: A crossroad
A rail crossing
A roundabout
A weigh station
questions.explanation: W10-1 is the advance warning for a highway-rail grade crossing. A railroad crossing ahead.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A fluorescent yellow-green pentagon means
options: A truck route
A county route
A school
A hospital
questions.explanation: The pentagon is the school sign. Fluorescent yellow-green is used for school and pedestrian warnings.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Orange signs and cones mean
options: A recreation area
A minimum speed
A permanent regulation
A temporary work zone
questions.explanation: Orange is the color for temporary traffic control. Obey the devices and any flagger.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A flagger's instructions in a work zone
options: Control traffic and must be obeyed
Apply only to trucks
Replace the need to watch workers
Are suggestions you may ignore if traffic is light
questions.explanation: A flagger is a temporary traffic-control device. Follow the direction you are given.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A white rectangular sign with black or red legend is generally
options: A warning
A regulation
A guide sign
A service sign
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually white with black or red legend. They state a legal requirement.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A yellow diamond sign means
options: A service
A law that is optional
A hazard warning
A destination
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped yellow signs warn of curves, intersections, merges, and other conditions. A warning of a condition ahead.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A slow-moving-vehicle emblem is
options: A blue square
A white rectangle
A red octagon
An orange triangle
questions.explanation: The orange triangle identifies a vehicle that usually travels under 25 mph. Be ready to slow down.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means
options: You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
The turn is forbidden
The signal is out
The turn is protected and oncoming traffic is stopped
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow is a permissive turn. Yield to traffic and people who conflict with the turn.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A steady green arrow means
options: Yield, then turn
A protected turn
Stop, then turn
The lane is ending
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow is a protected movement for the direction of the arrow. You may make the movement shown, and conflicting traffic is stopped.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A steady yellow arrow means
options: Pedestrians must run
Speed up to make the turn
The protected movement is ending
The turn is now forbidden forever
questions.explanation: A yellow arrow is the clearance interval for that movement. Do not enter if you can stop safely.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A red X over a lane means
options: The lane is for passing only
The lane is a shoulder you may use
The lane is open for travel
You must not drive in that lane
questions.explanation: A lane-control signal with a red X means the lane is closed to you.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A green arrow over a lane means
options: You may drive in that lane
Stop in that lane
The lane is reversible and closed
The lane is closed
questions.explanation: A downward or lane-use green arrow means the lane is open for travel.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A pedestrian signal showing a flashing upraised hand means
options: Start crossing if you have not left the curb
Do not start crossing
Cars must turn into the crosswalk
The signal is broken
questions.explanation: A flashing DON'T WALK or upraised hand means do not begin to cross. People already crossing should finish.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A walking-person symbol means
options: Only bicycles may cross
Drivers may turn through the crosswalk without looking
Pedestrians may start crossing in the direction of the indication
The crosswalk is closed
questions.explanation: The walking-person indication means a pedestrian may start to cross.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: If a traffic officer directs you through a red light, you should
options: Sound the horn and stay stopped
Treat the red light as more important than the officer
Wait for the green anyway
Obey the officer
questions.explanation: Directions from a traffic officer override the signal and the signs.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A two-way left-turn lane is for
options: Left turns both ways
Parking
Bicycles only
Passing slower traffic
questions.explanation: The shared center lane has yellow lines and two-way arrows. Enter it only to turn left. For through travel or passing. Left turns from either direction.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A solid white line between lanes means you
options: May pass on the right at any time
Should stay in your lane
Must change lanes immediately
Are facing oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: A solid white line discourages a lane change. A broken white line separates lanes where changing is allowed when safe. Should stay in your lane and not change across it unless necessary.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Yellow pavement markings separate
options: Only stop lines
Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction
Traffic moving in opposite directions
Only bike lanes
questions.explanation: Yellow separates opposing traffic. White separates same-direction lanes and marks the right edge. Traffic moving in opposite directions, or mark the left edge of a divided road.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A stop line tells you to
options: Change lanes
Speed up
Stop on top of the crosswalk
Stop before the line
questions.explanation: The wide white line across the lane is the stop line. Stop behind it so you do not sit in the crosswalk.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A painted crosswalk means
options: Drivers must yield to people crossing
Parking is allowed in the stripes
The area is a loading zone
Pedestrians must yield to every vehicle
questions.explanation: Do not stop in a crosswalk. Yield to pedestrians who are in it or about to enter it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Raised pavement markers that are yellow are used to
options: Show a hospital
Replace a stop sign
Mark the right edge only
Back up yellow center lines
questions.explanation: Yellow markers follow the yellow-line system. White markers supplement white lane lines.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: At an uncontrolled intersection, you should
options: Slow, look both ways, and be ready to yield
Honk and maintain speed
Stop only if a sign is posted a block away
Assume you have the right-of-way
questions.explanation: If no sign or signal assigns the right-of-way, approach slowly and yield to traffic that has already entered, and to the driver on your right if you arrive together.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When you turn left at a green light with no green arrow, you must
options: Turn immediately; oncoming traffic must wait
Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
Stop and wait for a red light
Use the right lane
questions.explanation: A circular green allows the turn but does not protect it. Oncoming traffic and people in the crosswalk go first. Yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians in your path.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A driver entering a road from a driveway or alley must
options: Use the left lane immediately
Force a gap
Yield to people and traffic
Honk and proceed
questions.explanation: Traffic leaving a driveway, alley, or parking space yields to the road and to people on the sidewalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and a siren, you should
options: Stop in the intersection
Follow it closely
Speed up so you are not in the way
Pull right and stop
questions.explanation: Move right and stop. Do not block an intersection. Do not follow closer than the law allows. Pull to the right edge and stop until it has passed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You must not enter an intersection when
options: You would be stuck blocking it
You can clear it on green
A pedestrian has finished crossing
The light is green and the far side is clear
questions.explanation: Do not enter unless you can get all the way through. Blocking the box traps cross traffic. Traffic ahead is backed up so you would be stuck blocking the intersection.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At a T-intersection, the driver on the road that ends must
options: Go first if they honk
Yield to traffic on the through road
Turn left only
Ignore vehicles from the left
questions.explanation: The driver who is facing the end of the road yields to traffic on the crossing road.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Before you move into a roundabout you must
options: Change lanes after you enter
Stop inside the circle
Yield to circulating traffic
Use the left lane for every exit
questions.explanation: Enter only into a gap. Once inside, do not stop except to avoid a crash. Signal your exit as you leave. Yield to traffic already circulating and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: On a freeway entrance ramp you should
options: Enter at 15 mph and force a gap
Back down the ramp if you miss the gap
Stop at the end of the ramp every time
Match traffic speed, then merge
questions.explanation: The ramp is for matching speed. Yield to freeway traffic. Never back up on a freeway or ramp. Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, then merge into a gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If you miss your freeway exit you should
options: Continue to the next exit
Make a U-turn through the median
Stop and back up
Cross the gore and turn around
questions.explanation: Do not stop, back, or cross the gore. Take the next exit and return.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The left lane of a multi-lane highway is for
options: Parking
Passing traffic
Entering from a ramp
Bicycles only
questions.explanation: Move out of the left lane after you pass. Do not linger beside another vehicle. Passing or faster through traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When you change lanes you should
options: Turn the wheel without signaling if you are in a hurry
Rely on mirrors only
Signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder for the blind spot
Brake hard in the lane first
questions.explanation: Mirrors do not show the blind spot beside your rear quarter. A shoulder check covers it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A large truck's blind spots, the No-Zones, are
options: Only on the right of a motorcycle
Only above the trailer
Only directly in front of a car
Beside, behind, and in front
questions.explanation: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you. Do not linger there. Along both sides, directly behind, and immediately in front of the truck.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A truck making a right turn often needs to
options: Swing wide to clear the corner
Turn from the left lane without space
Back up in the intersection
Stay tight against the curb the whole way
questions.explanation: Do not move into the space on the truck's right during a right turn. The trailer will track into that space. Swing left or wide first so the trailer can clear the corner.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You should never
options: Stop behind the stop line at a crossing
Enter tracks you cannot fully clear
Look both ways at a crossing
Turn off the radio to listen for a train
questions.explanation: A train overhangs the rails and cannot stop quickly. Do not stop on the tracks or shift gears while crossing. Drive onto the tracks unless you can clear them completely.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If the gate is down or the red lights are flashing at a crossing, you must
options: Honk and proceed
Drive around the gate if you do not see a train
Stop until the gate rises and lights stop
Follow the car ahead across
questions.explanation: Going around a lowered gate is illegal and deadly. Wait until the warning ends and you can see that another train is not coming. Stop and wait until the gate is up, the lights have stopped, and the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A crossbuck at a crossing means
options: A bus stop
A truck escape ramp
The road is closed
Yield to trains
questions.explanation: The crossbuck marks the crossing. If there is no signal, you still must yield to any train.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Yellow or amber lights flashing on a school bus mean
options: The bus is about to stop
The bus is out of service
Only the car behind the bus must stop
You may pass at the speed limit
questions.explanation: Amber warning lights come on before the red lights and the stop arm. Do not rush past. Slow and prepare to stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: In a school zone you should
options: Pass a stopped school bus on the left
Slow to the posted school speed and watch for children
Use the horn so children stay back
Ignore a crossing guard if the light is green
questions.explanation: The posted school speed and the crossing guard control the zone. Children are unpredictable.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You may pass on the left when
options: You are approaching a hill crest
There is a solid yellow line on your side
It is legal and you can safely return in time
You are in a no-passing zone but the car ahead is slow
questions.explanation: Pass only where sight distance, signs, and pavement markings allow it, and only when you can finish the pass safely. The way ahead is clear, passing is allowed, and you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You should not pass
options: A vehicle that has signaled and moved right to let you by
In daylight on a straight road with a broken yellow line
On a multi-lane road when the left lane is clear
Within an intersection, on a hill, or on a curve with limited sight
questions.explanation: Limited sight distance and intersections are classic no-passing locations even before a sign is posted.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When another driver starts to pass you, you should
options: Hold speed or ease off
Move left to block them
Brake hard
Speed up
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate while being passed. Help the other driver get back to the lane. Hold your speed or ease off so the pass can finish.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You should not park
options: At the curb where parking is allowed
In a crosswalk, in front of a driveway, or on a bridge
Parallel to the curb, headed with traffic
Where a sign permits timed parking and you are within the time
questions.explanation: Never block a crosswalk, driveway, intersection, fire hydrant, or sidewalk. The exact distances are set by state law, so follow the posted sign and your state handbook.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When you park on a hill with a curb, you should
options: Rely only on the parking brake
Leave the wheels straight and the car in neutral
Turn the wheels so it rolls into the curb
Face oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: Set the parking brake. Turn the front wheels toward the curb when facing downhill, and away from the curb when facing uphill, so the curb stops a roll.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A disabled-parking space marked with the access symbol
options: Is a loading zone for trucks
Is a motorcycle-only stall
May be used by anyone for a few minutes
Requires a displayed disability permit
questions.explanation: Those spaces, and the striped access aisle next to them, are reserved. Do not park or stop there without the credential. May be used only by a vehicle that displays the required credential.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: In rain, fog, or when the road is slick you should
options: Keep the same dry-road gap
Increase following distance and slow down
Use cruise control so the speed stays high
Ride the bumper of the car ahead
questions.explanation: Tires need more distance to stop on a wet or icy surface. A longer gap is the margin.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If you start to hydroplane you should
options: Set the parking brake
Brake hard and turn sharply
Ease off the gas and hold the wheel straight
Speed up so the tires cut through the water
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning means the tires are riding on water. A sudden brake or steer can start a skid. Ease off the accelerator, hold the wheel straight, and do not brake hard until the tires grip again.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: In fog you should use
options: Only parking lights
Hazard lights while you keep highway speed
High beams, because they reach farther
Low beams and a slower speed
questions.explanation: High beams reflect off the fog and reduce what you can see. Low beams and a slower speed match your sight distance.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, you should
options: Look toward the right edge of your lane and slow down
Turn your high beams on and leave them on
Close your eyes briefly
Look straight at the headlights
questions.explanation: Watch the right edge line so you are not blinded. Do not retaliate with your own high beams.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A tire blowout calls for
options: A hard brake and a quick lane change
A firm grip and easing off the gas
The parking brake immediately
Accelerating to keep the car stable
questions.explanation: Sudden braking or steering can make you lose the car. Slow gradually, then pull off when you have control. A firm grip, easing off the gas, and steering straight until the car slows.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If the rear of the car starts to skid, you should
options: Accelerate
Brake hard and steer the opposite way from the skid
Ease off the gas and steer where you want to go
Shift to neutral and close your eyes
questions.explanation: Look and steer where you want to go. Slamming the brake during a skid usually makes it worse. Ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: With anti-lock brakes in a hard stop you should
options: Use only the parking brake
Turn the engine off
Pump the pedal
Press firmly and hold
questions.explanation: ABS pumps the brakes for you. Pedal pulse is normal. Keep steering. Press the pedal firmly and hold it, steering where you need to go.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If your brakes fail you should
options: Pump, downshift, and ease on the parking brake
Turn the key off while moving at speed
Drive to a shop without slowing
Shift to neutral and jump out
questions.explanation: Pumping can build pressure. Downshift and a gradual parking-brake application can slow the car. Do not shut the engine off if that locks the steering. Pump the pedal, downshift, use the parking brake gradually, and look for an escape path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Before you drive away from the curb you should
options: Pull out and then signal
Signal, check, and yield
Honk and enter
Assume the bike lane is empty
questions.explanation: The shoulder check catches the cyclist or car in your blind spot. Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, and yield to traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child is safest
options: Sharing a seat belt with an adult
In the front seat in front of an airbag
In the back, in a fitting restraint
Standing between the front seats
questions.explanation: The back seat is the safest place for a child. Use the car seat or booster the instructions and your state law require. Never put a rear-facing seat in front of an active airbag.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A seat belt should be worn
options: Under the arm if it rubs the neck
Only when a police car is nearby
Only on highways
By everyone, snug across the hips
questions.explanation: The lap belt sits on the hips, not the stomach. The shoulder belt crosses the chest, not the neck. By the driver and every passenger, snug across the hips and shoulder.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A motorcycle is entitled to
options: A full lane
The shoulder only
The space between lanes
Half of a lane beside a car
questions.explanation: Do not share a lane side by side with a motorcycle. Lane splitting, where it exists, is a state rule, not a national one. A full lane, the same as any other vehicle.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When you pass a bicyclist you should
options: Honk and pass within a foot
Leave a wide gap or change lanes
Pass on the right
Force the rider onto the sidewalk
questions.explanation: Riders are easily blown off line by wind from a car. Pass only when you can do it with room, then return. Exact passing distances are set by state law. Move into the next lane when you can, or leave a wide gap, and do not turn across the rider.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A blind pedestrian with a white cane or a guide dog
options: Is required to stay on the sidewalk
Must yield to you if you honk
Has the right-of-way
Should be waved through only if the light is green
questions.explanation: Stop and yield. Do not honk. Do not tell the person to go unless they ask.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At a crosswalk, whether it is marked or not, you should
options: Pass a car that has stopped for a pedestrian
Wave children across against the signal
Stop in the crosswalk if the light is red
Yield to a pedestrian crossing or about to
questions.explanation: Intersections have crosswalks even when they are not painted. Never pass a vehicle that is stopped for a person on foot. Yield to a pedestrian who is crossing or about to cross at an intersection.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Driving while drowsy is dangerous because
options: Coffee removes all impairment
It slows reactions much like alcohol
It only matters after midnight
Opening a window makes it safe to continue
questions.explanation: If you cannot remember the last few miles, or you drift, stop and sleep. A window or the radio is not a cure. Microsleeps and slow reactions are similar to alcohol impairment.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Scan the road
options: Well ahead, plus mirrors and sides
Only when you hear a horn
Only in the city
Only at the car directly ahead
questions.explanation: Looking about 12 to 15 seconds ahead gives you time to change speed or lanes instead of slamming the brakes. You see hazards early.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If you drift off the right edge of the pavement you should
options: Jerk the wheel back immediately
Slow down, then ease back on
Brake hard and turn left
Accelerate
questions.explanation: A sudden return can throw the car across the lane into oncoming traffic. Ease off the gas, straighten, slow down, then steer gently back onto the pavement.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Bridges and overpasses in cold weather
options: Can be ignored if the air is above freezing
Stay warmer than the road
Freeze before the rest of the pavement
Are always salted
questions.explanation: Bridge decks lose heat from both sides. Expect ice there first.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When the sun is low and glare hides the road, you should
options: Stare at the sun so your eyes adjust
Drive on the shoulder
Speed up to get through it
Slow down and use the visor
questions.explanation: Glare hides vehicles and pedestrians. Reduce speed to your sight distance. Slow down, use the sun visor, and increase your following gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are rolling toward an eight-sided red sign at a quiet rural junction and no other traffic is visible. What must you still do?
options: Stop only after you have already entered the crossroad
Come to a full stop, then go only when the intersection is clear
Slow slightly and continue
Treat the octagon as a yield and roll through if nothing is close
questions.explanation: The octagon is reserved for stop and no other message. An empty-looking road does not erase the duty to stop fully before you decide the gap is safe.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The cross street looks open as you near an inverted triangular sign facing your lane. How should you use that shape?
options: Take the junction first
Ignore the sign unless a pedestrian is standing on the corner
Slow and give the right-of-way, stopping only if a stop is needed to yield
Make a counted full stop on every approach, the same as an octagon
questions.explanation: An inverted triangle means yield and nothing else. You must give way, but you do not have to stop when the way is clearly open. It never assigns you the right-of-way.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A pennant-shaped yellow sign faces you from the left shoulder just as the passing area ends. What is starting?
options: A school-speed zone you may enter at highway pace
Permission to pull out and pass before the next curve
An added lane that opens on the left
A no-passing zone on your side of the road
questions.explanation: The pennant is the no-passing warning placed on the left at the start of the zone. It tells you not to move left to pass, even when the vehicle ahead is slow.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Rounding a crest, you meet a circular yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR. What should you prepare for?
options: A railroad crossing ahead
A crossroad where the other drivers must stop for you
A freeway split marked with an X pattern
A closed work-zone lane identified by the X
questions.explanation: The round yellow sign is the advance warning for a railroad crossing. It is not the crossing itself, but it gives you time to slow and scan the tracks before you reach them. A railroad crossing ahead, so slow and look both ways along the tracks.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Children are near a five-sided sign as you enter a neighborhood street during the day. What does that shape mark?
options: A mandatory stop at the sign even when no one is present
A school zone or school crossing
A county route marker with no special duty
A street that is closed to all traffic during the day
questions.explanation: The pentagon is reserved for school warnings. It tells you to watch for children and to obey a school-speed sign posted with it, rather than treating the shape as an ordinary route marker. A school area or school crossing that calls for extra scanning and any posted school speed.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Cones appear with an orange diamond as your lane begins to narrow for construction. What does the orange color add?
options: A recreational route through a park
A cancellation of every white regulatory sign for the rest of the drive
A warning about a temporary work-zone condition
A permanent curve warning that crews painted orange
questions.explanation: Orange is the color of temporary traffic control. The diamond warns about the work zone ahead. Permanent rules still come from the regulatory signs that face you inside and outside the zone.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A yellow diamond with a side-road symbol stands on a highway that has no signal at the junction. What is it asking of you?
options: Assume the side road stops and hold your speed
Turn onto the side road
Read the diamond as a keep-right command
Watch for cars entering from that road
questions.explanation: A yellow diamond warns. It does not promise that the entering driver will stop, and it does not order you to turn. Scan the side road because traffic may join. Watch for vehicles entering from that side road and be ready to slow.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The white rectangular sign over your lane reads LEFT TURN ONLY, but you wanted to go straight. The line beside you is already solid. What is the legal choice?
options: Turn left from this lane and reroute
Go straight because a white sign is only advice
Stop on the solid line and change lanes in the intersection
Use the lane as a through-passing lane
questions.explanation: A white rectangle is regulatory. LEFT TURN ONLY restricts that lane to the left turn. Once the line is solid you are committed, and a wish to go straight does not change the sign.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You want fuel and see a blue sign with a fuel symbol and an arrow at the next exit. How should you treat it?
options: Treat the arrow as a lower regulatory speed for every driver
Follow it only if you choose that service
Leave the freeway
Read it as a warning that the exit ramp is closed
questions.explanation: Blue marks motorist services such as fuel, food, lodging, or a hospital. The sign helps you decide. It is not a command to turn and not a warning of a hazard. It does not order the exit.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A brown sign names a state park at the interchange where you need the through highway. What kind of message is the brown color carrying?
options: A prohibition on entering the park road
A railroad warning for a crossing inside the park
Recreation or cultural guidance
A required detour off the through highway
questions.explanation: Brown identifies recreation and cultural-interest guidance. It does not assign a stop, a ban, or a detour. Use the green guide signs when you want the through route. Recreation or cultural guidance you follow only if that place is your destination.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A fluorescent yellow-green sign shows a pedestrian symbol beside a city crosswalk. Why is that color chosen instead of ordinary yellow?
options: To post a regulatory speed that applies only after dark
To mark a truck weight limit
To identify an interstate route
To make a pedestrian, school, or bicycle warning stand out
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green is a warning color for people walking, school areas, and bicycles. It is easier to see than ordinary yellow. It does not set a speed by itself and it is not a route marker.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Dry pavement and light traffic make the posted white speed sign feel slow. How should you read the number?
options: As the maximum under ideal conditions
As advice you may exceed when the road looks empty
As a required pace you must hold even if a storm arrives later
As a suggestion that applies only while an officer is visible
questions.explanation: A regulatory speed sign sets the highest legal speed when conditions are good. It is not a target and not a suggestion to go faster. When conditions worsen you go slower.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Heavy rain cuts visibility while a white regulatory speed sign is still in force. What does that sign allow in the storm?
options: A faster pace so you spend less time on the wet pavement
Up to the maximum, but slower if needed
The posted maximum
Any pace as long as the headlights are on
questions.explanation: The regulatory number is a ceiling for ideal conditions. Rain means the safe speed can be lower. The sign does not raise the ceiling and it does not require you to drive the maximum. No more than the posted maximum, and less if a lower speed is what keeps control.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A yellow plaque under a curve warning shows a speed lower than the white regulatory sign you passed on the highway. What is the plaque's job?
options: It sets a minimum you must hold through the bend
It cancels the curve warning once you have driven the road before
It advises a safe speed for that curve
It replaces the white regulatory sign for the entire highway
questions.explanation: An advisory speed on a yellow plaque is guidance for a curve, exit, or ramp. It does not by itself create a regulatory limit, and it does not erase a white speed sign posted for the roadway.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Navigation says to turn left, but the corner sign shows a left-turn arrow inside a red circle and slash. The circular signal is green. What may you do?
options: Go straight or take another legal movement, but do not turn left
Turn left because the green light outranks the sign
Turn left after yielding
Use the oncoming lane briefly to make the left turn
questions.explanation: A red circle and slash prohibit the movement shown. A green light for other traffic does not cancel a posted left-turn ban.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are in the right lane and a sign bans right turns during the hours printed on its plaque. Those hours are in effect. What is required?
options: Stop in the through lane and turn when the restriction feels inconvenient
Choose a movement the signs still allow instead of turning right
Turn right because the plaque is aimed only at delivery vehicles
Turn right if the corner crosswalk is empty
questions.explanation: A time-limited turn ban is still a ban while the posted hours are in effect. Your lane and a short wait do not create an exception the plaque does not give.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A median opening looks wide enough for a U-turn, but a sign at the opening prohibits U-turns. Traffic is light. What is the legal move?
options: Cross the median and stop facing the side street
Back along the arterial until you are facing the other way
Skip this opening and turn around only where U-turns are allowed
Make the U-turn
questions.explanation: NO U-TURN is regulatory. Geometry and light traffic do not override it. A wide opening can still be an unsafe or forbidden place to turn around.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You start onto a ramp and the sign facing you reads DO NOT ENTER. Headlights are not yet visible. What is the immediate action?
options: Yield, then enter if the ramp still looks empty
Enter slowly because the message applies only at the opposite peak hour
Treat the red legend as a merge warning
Stop before entering that roadway and find a route that faces the right way
questions.explanation: DO NOT ENTER means you are about to join opposing traffic or a closed direction. Yielding is not enough. Empty pavement does not make the ramp yours.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A KEEP RIGHT sign stands at the nose of a median where the road splits. Which path is legal?
options: Stop and back down the approach if you wanted the other road
Pass to the right of the sign and the median
Pass to the left
Straddle the median until you pick a direction
questions.explanation: KEEP RIGHT is a regulatory command at an island or median. Passing on the left would put you into opposing traffic the island was built to separate.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Roadwork has placed a KEEP LEFT sign before a temporary island, and your usual lane is to the right of it. What do you do?
options: Drive between the sign and the island
Ignore it if some pavement remains on the right
Move left of the sign and follow the open path
Stay right because the sign applies only to oversized loads
questions.explanation: KEEP LEFT means the obstruction must be passed on the left. In a work zone that channel keeps you out of the closed side, even if the old pavement is still visible.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You want to turn onto a street where the ONE WAY sign points away from your intended turn. What does the arrow require?
options: Enter against the arrow for a single block
Treat the street as two-way
Use the street as a pocket to turn around
Travel only in the arrow's direction
questions.explanation: ONE WAY means every vehicle on that street travels with the arrow. Turning against it puts you head-on into legal traffic, no matter how short the block is. Enter only if you will travel in the direction of the arrow.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A TWO WAY TRAFFIC sign appears as you leave a divided section and the median ends. What should change?
options: Expect opposing vehicles nearby and stay to the right
Move to the left half
Use the center of the road as a shared passing lane
Assume every driveway on the left has a stop facing the other driver
questions.explanation: The sign tells you the buffer between directions is gone. Position yourself on the right and pass only where sight distance and markings allow.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: DIVIDED HIGHWAY ENDS is posted as the median narrows away. What conflict is the sign preparing you for?
options: You must stop at the sign and turn around
Passing becomes required once the median disappears
Oncoming traffic with no median between
The road is becoming a one-way freeway
questions.explanation: When the divided highway ends, the physical gap between you and oncoming traffic disappears. The warning is there so you adjust before the two-way conflict is beside you. Opposing traffic will be closer, so tighten your lane position and scanning.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A lane-ends warning is posted over your lane and the through lane beside you is busy. How should you merge?
options: Accelerate and force a gap at the last cone
Stop in the ending lane until the through lane yields
Drive the shoulder past the taper and merge later
Signal and take a gap before the taper
questions.explanation: Your lane does not continue, so you must find a gap. The through lane is not required to stop for you, and the shoulder is not a substitute travel lane. Signal and take a gap in the continuing lane before the taper runs out.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An added-lane sign shows your ramp continuing as its own lane beside the freeway. Must you merge left immediately?
options: No; stay in the new lane and let freeway traffic keep its lane
Yes; stop at the ramp end until a freeway driver signals you over
Yes; the sign means your lane is ending at the gore
You must cross two lanes before the next overhead sign
questions.explanation: An added lane means a lane is joining, not ending. Forcing a left merge when your lane continues creates the conflict the sign was meant to prevent.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A merge warning is posted where your ramp and the mainline must share one lane. How do you join?
options: Use the shoulder to pass the merge point
Adjust speed and blend into an existing gap
Stop on the ramp until the mainline is completely empty
Enter at mainline pace and expect others to brake for you
questions.explanation: A merge means two streams become one. Small speed changes that fit a gap are safer than stopping dead on the ramp or forcing the mainline to absorb you.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The pavement is dark after a shower and a slippery-when-wet warning stands before a curve. What should you change before the bend?
options: Move onto the shoulder
Treat the warning as a closure until the pavement dries
Slow before the curve and steer smoothly
Hold speed and brake only after the car begins to slide
questions.explanation: The warning means the surface loses friction when wet, especially where you must turn. Reducing speed before the bend leaves tire grip for steering instead of spending it on a slide. Slow before the slick stretch and avoid sudden steering or braking in the curve.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A winding-road symbol is posted at the mouth of a canyon you have not driven. Why slow before the first bend?
options: The symbol marks a straight passing zone through the canyon
The sign requires a full stop at every curve
The road becomes one-way until the symbol repeats
Several curves are coming, and the first can hide the next
questions.explanation: The winding-road warning means a series of bends, not a single gentle curve. Speed you carry into the first bend is still with you when the next one appears.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A sharp-left curve warning stands before a bend you cannot see through. What is the correct path?
options: Slow before the curve and stay in your lane through the bend
Cut into the opposing lane
Brake hard only after you are halfway around
Read the symbol as a required left turn into a driveway
questions.explanation: The warning means the roadway itself bends sharply. Speed has to come off before the bend so you can track your lane instead of drifting across the center.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A sharp-right curve warning is ahead and a slow truck is already braking in your lane. What is the safe choice?
options: Accelerate so you finish the curve ahead of the truck
Slow behind the truck and stay in your lane through the bend
Pass the truck on the left inside the curve
Use the right shoulder to go around the truck
questions.explanation: Sight distance and room are limited inside a sharp curve. Passing a slowing truck there puts you in the opposing lane or off the pavement. Match the slower speed until the road straightens.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A reverse-curve warning shows the road bending one way and then the other. How should you steer it?
options: Stop between the curves and reverse direction
Treat the second bend as an intersection where you must turn off
Slow once and track your lane through both bends without drifting wide
Straighten the first bend by crossing the centerline
questions.explanation: A reverse curve is two bends in opposite directions. Speed left over from the first bend is what carries you wide on the second. One smooth, slower path keeps you in lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Black chevrons on yellow signs trace a tight bend at night. How do you use them?
options: Read them as the boundary of a bicycle lane
Treat the row of chevrons as a no-passing pennant
Aim the car at the signs
Slow enough to follow the chevrons while remaining in your lane
questions.explanation: Chevron alignment signs show how sharply the road bends. The point of each chevron follows the path. Hitting a chevron means you have left the roadway.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A narrow-bridge warning appears and an oncoming car is already on the span. What should you do?
options: Slow and let the bridge clear first
Race the oncoming car so you reach the bridge first
Pass that car on the bridge if it is centered in the span
Stop on the bridge until a flagger arrives
questions.explanation: A narrow bridge is tighter than the road that feeds it, so two vehicles have less room and passing is unsafe. If someone is already on the span, give them the space by slowing before you enter. Slow on the approach and let the bridge clear rather than passing on the span.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A low-clearance warning and a height plaque stand before an underpass, and you are unsure your roof cargo will fit. What is the right decision?
options: Use the oncoming lane where the arch looks taller
Enter only if you know the cargo clears
Enter slowly and back out if you hear a scrape
Ignore the plaque
questions.explanation: The structure will not move for your vehicle. If the loaded height may exceed the posting, another route is safer than backing out of a low underpass or guessing from the shape of the arch. Do not enter unless you know the vehicle, including cargo, will clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A steep-hill warning is posted as the road drops away in front of you. What should you do before the grade?
options: Treat the hill as a passing zone
Accelerate on the crest so momentum carries you down
Slow to a controlled speed before the grade
Shift to neutral and coast
questions.explanation: On a downgrade the hill adds speed whether you ask for it or not. The warning tells you to choose a speed and a gear before gravity does it halfway down. Set a controlled speed before the downhill so the grade does not build it for you.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A deer-crossing warning stands along a wooded highway at dusk and no animals are in sight. What does the sign still ask?
options: Stop at the sign until you see a deer
Speed up to spend less time in the signed stretch
Move to the center of the road and stay there
Scan the shoulders and be ready to slow
questions.explanation: Animal warnings do not require a stop at the sign. They mark a stretch where animals enter. At dusk, scanning the shoulders gives you time to slow instead of swerving blindly.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A bicycle-crossing warning is posted where a path meets the road, and a rider is approaching that crossing. What do you owe the rider?
options: Slow and yield so the rider can cross or enter safely
Hold speed because bicycles must always yield to cars
Honk so the rider waits on the path
Pass the crossing in the opposing lane
questions.explanation: The warning means people on bicycles may cross or enter. A rider already nearing the road should not have to guess whether you will slow. Yielding prevents a side impact.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A pedestrian-crossing warning stands ahead of a marked crosswalk and a person has stepped off the curb. What is your duty?
options: Change lanes inside the crosswalk to go around
Slow or stop so the person can finish crossing your lane
Continue if you think you can pass close behind them
Expect them to return to the curb
questions.explanation: A person already in the crosswalk has started across. Your arrival does not move them back to the curb, and using the crosswalk as a passing lane is still driving through their path.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A warning shows a person using a wheelchair at a crossing that looks empty as you approach. How do you pass it?
options: Stop and wait a full signal cycle even though no one is there
Use the empty crossing as a turn pocket
Cover the brake and look
Treat the symbol as a truck-route marker
questions.explanation: The symbol warns that someone who may move more slowly uses this crossing. An empty view is not a reason for a needless stop, but it is a reason to be able to yield. A person using a mobility device may still enter.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A farm-machinery warning is posted on a rural highway in harvest season. What should you be ready to meet?
options: Only emergency vehicles
A vehicle that will pull off at the sign and wait for you
Traffic that matches your speed
A slow farm vehicle on the road
questions.explanation: The warning means slow agricultural equipment may be on the road and cannot match ordinary highway pace. Slowing early prevents a closing-speed surprise. A slow farm vehicle you may need to approach well below the pace of other traffic.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A stop-ahead warning appears while you are still at highway speed and a hill hides the stop sign. What should you do at the warning?
options: Begin slowing so you can stop at the sign
Stop at the warning sign and then proceed
Hold speed until the stop sign is actually visible
Treat the warning as the stop and roll the intersection
questions.explanation: Stop-ahead gives braking distance before the regulatory stop. Stopping at the warning leaves you in the travel lane too early. Waiting to brake until you see the sign can leave you too fast.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A signal-ahead warning sits before a curve that hides the intersection, and you cannot see the indication yet. What is the prudent assumption?
options: Stop on the curve until a green is guaranteed
It may be red, so be ready to stop
The hidden signal is flashing yellow, so hold speed
A signal behind a curve is green for the larger road
questions.explanation: The warning exists because the indication is not visible in time. Prepare to stop. Do not assume a color or a flash mode you have not seen. The signal may be red or yellow, so be ready to stop as the curve opens.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A yield-ahead warning is posted on a ramp that later joins a busy road. Where does the yield duty apply?
options: Nowhere, because the warning replaces the yield sign
Only when an officer is standing at the merge
At the yield sign ahead, after you have used the warning to adjust speed
At the warning sign, where a full stop is always required
questions.explanation: The advance warning buys time to slow. The legal yield is at the yield sign. You do not stop at the warning as if it were the yield, and you do not skip the yield because you saw the warning.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A school-speed sign is paired with a fluorescent yellow-green school warning, and children are on the sidewalk. What combination fits?
options: Hold highway pace
Stop in the travel lane until every child goes indoors
Use the opposing lane to give the sidewalk more room
Obey the school speed and watch the children
questions.explanation: The school warning says children may be present. The regulatory school-speed sign, when it applies, is the legal maximum. Children on a sidewalk can still step out, so the speed and the scanning go together. Obey the school-speed sign and watch the children, including those not yet in the street.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A school-bus-stop-ahead warning is posted on a two-lane road and a hill blocks your view. What should you prepare to do?
options: Slow and be ready to stop for a bus
Pass any stopped bus
Stop at the warning even if no bus is present
Drive the center of the road to see over the hill
questions.explanation: The warning means a bus stop is hidden by the hill. You slow so a bus that is actually there, with its stop devices operating, does not surprise you. The warning itself is not a stop sign.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A flagger-ahead sign is posted and, around the bend, a person holds a paddle toward you while a signal beyond them is green. Whom do you obey?
options: The driver behind you if that driver sounds the horn
The flagger holding the paddle
The green signal
Neither, if the workers are only on the shoulder
questions.explanation: A flagger directing traffic overrides the signal. The advance sign exists so you slow enough to obey the paddle instead of discovering the flagger at the last moment.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An orange road-work-ahead sign appears well before any cones, and traffic is still moving quickly. What should change now?
options: Stop at the orange sign until the zone ends
Move to the shoulder and pass the line of cars
Ease off and watch for workers and closures
Keep pace until a worker is standing in your lane
questions.explanation: The advance warning gives you distance before the conflict. Workers and closures may still be out of sight. Waiting until someone is in your lane leaves no room to stop. Ease off and look for workers, equipment, and a lane that may close.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Orange detour signs send you off the highway you usually take, and you know a shortcut across the closed section. What is the legal route?
options: Use the shortcut
Ignore an orange detour when you are driving a passenger car
Stop on the closed road until it reopens
Follow the detour signs in the order they are posted
questions.explanation: A detour is the temporary legal path around a closure. Familiarity with the old road does not reopen it, and the orange signs apply to passenger cars as well as other vehicles.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A lane-closed-ahead sign is posted over the right lane you occupy, and the left lane is flowing. When should you move?
options: Merge left at the first safe gap instead of riding to the taper
Stay put and merge at the final cone
Stop in the closing lane so the open lane must let you in
Use the right shoulder as a continuing lane
questions.explanation: An early, signaled merge is more predictable than a last-second squeeze. The closing lane is not a passing lane, and stopping in it blocks the drivers behind you.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A road-closed sign and barricades stand across your intended street, with a gap wide enough for a car. What do you do?
options: Park against the barricade until someone moves it
Turn around or follow the posted detour
Slip through the gap if no workers are visible
Treat the closure as applying only to trucks
questions.explanation: Road closed means the street is not open, even if a physical gap remains. The closure may hide workers, a drop-off, or a surface that will not carry a car. Do not drive through the gap.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A soft-shoulder warning is posted and you want to pull off there to check a map. What does the sign say about that shoulder?
options: It is signed as a standing area for short visits
It is the required path around the next curve
It may not support the car's weight
It is an extra travel lane during busy hours
questions.explanation: A soft shoulder can rut or give way under a tire. Using it for a convenience stop can leave you stuck or pull you back onto the road at a sharp angle. It may not support the car, so do not drive on it for a convenience stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A pavement-ends warning is posted as the smooth surface changes color ahead. What should you do before the change?
options: Speed up so the transition takes less time
Stop on the change until a new route sign appears
Move into the opposing lane where the surface looks newer
Slow down before the surface changes
questions.explanation: When the pavement ends, grip, dust, and steering can change suddenly. Slowing before the joint keeps the car stable. The sign is not a stop and not a reason to use the opposing lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A bump warning is posted and you can see a raised strip in your lane. How should you take it?
options: Slow before the bump so the car stays settled and steerable
Speed up so the tires skim over it
Swerve into the next lane without a mirror check
Stop on top of the bump and then creep off
questions.explanation: A bump hit at speed can unload the tires and tug the wheel. Slowing first keeps the suspension in its working range. Speeding up makes the impact harder.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A dip warning appears at night and your headlights fall into a dark low spot. What is the right response?
options: Accelerate so the car jumps the low spot
Slow so the low spot does not bottom the car or hide a hazard
Brake hard only after you are inside the dip
Treat the dip as a place where a stop is required
questions.explanation: A dip can hide water, roughness, or an oncoming vehicle until late. Slowing on the approach keeps the car from striking the far lip and gives you a moment to see what is in it.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A rough-road warning is posted and the surface ahead is patched and uneven. How should you handle the wheel?
options: Change lanes repeatedly to hunt for smoother pavement without looking
Stop in the lane and wait for a smoother hour
Slow and hold the wheel firmly so the patches do not steer you
Loosen your grip so the wheel can kick freely
questions.explanation: Uneven pavement can tug the steering. A firm grip and a lower speed keep the car tracking. Unsignaled lane changes on that surface add a conflict with the cars beside you.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A shoulder-drop-off warning is posted and your right tires slip off the pavement edge. What is the controlled recovery?
options: Yank the wheel left at once while still at highway pace
Brake hard with the right tires still off the edge
Accelerate so the tires climb the lip
Ease off, slow, then steer gently back
questions.explanation: A sharp edge can grab a tire. Jerking the wheel can launch you across the center once the tire finally climbs. Slowing and returning gently keeps the recovery inside your lane. Ease off the accelerator, slow, and steer gently back when the edge will let the tire climb.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A crossroad-warning symbol is posted on a rural highway with no stop sign facing you. What conflict is ahead?
options: The symbol marks a railroad crossing
A road crossing yours
Your road ends and you must turn
Cross traffic always has a stop
questions.explanation: The crossroad symbol warns of an intersection. It does not promise that the other road stops. If nothing controls your approach, you still look for a vehicle that fails to yield. A road crosses yours, so scan for traffic even though you have no stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A side-road symbol shows a road entering from the right, and a car is nosing out of it. What should you do?
options: Turn right because the symbol directs you onto that road
Cross the centerline to pass the nose of the car
Be ready to slow
Hold speed and expect the car to wait no matter how it is positioned
questions.explanation: A side-road warning means traffic may enter. A vehicle already at the edge of your lane is a reason to slow rather than to assume that driver judged your speed correctly. That driver may pull into your path.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A T-intersection symbol warns that the road you are on is about to end. What should you prepare for?
options: A short bridge you can cross at highway pace
A through lane that continues past the junction
An added lane joining from the left
A required turn or stop
questions.explanation: At a T, your road ends at the cross street. The warning gives you time to slow and make the turn the signs require instead of discovering the end of the pavement too late. The pavement does not continue straight.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A roundabout-ahead warning is posted and you can see the circulating roadway. How should you enter?
options: Slow and yield to traffic already in the circle
Enter at speed
Stop inside the circle if you are unsure of the exit
Use the center island to turn around if you miss the exit
questions.explanation: The advance warning gives you time to slow. Entering drivers yield to people already circulating. The center island is not a place to stop or to make a U-turn.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)
