questions.q: You stop at an octagonal sign with an ALL WAY plaque. Two drivers on the cross street stopped before you did. Who should move before you?
options: You, because the plaque gives your approach priority
Whoever sounds the horn first
The largest vehicle, regardless of who stopped first
Those drivers, in the order they arrived
questions.explanation: ALL WAY means every approach stops. After the stops, drivers go in arrival order. Arriving last means you wait. The plaque is not a green light for your leg.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are below the flow on a multi-lane road signed SLOWER TRAFFIC KEEP RIGHT, and the right lane is open. What should you do?
options: Move right so faster traffic can pass on your left
Stay in the left lane
Exceed the regulatory maximum so you can match the left lane
Stop in the left lane until the faster cars go by
questions.explanation: The sign tells slower drivers to leave the left lanes for passing. Moving right does that. It does not authorize a speed above the regulatory maximum just to hold a left-lane position.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A NO TRUCKS sign stands at a parkway entrance you are approaching in an ordinary passenger car. What does it mean for you?
options: The sign is a weight suggestion any driver may ignore
Your car may enter
Passenger cars are banned and trucks may enter
Every motor vehicle must turn around
questions.explanation: A truck prohibition keeps heavy vehicles off a road that cannot take them. Reading it as a ban on cars would keep you off a road you may use.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A bridge carries a weight-limit sign and you are driving a passenger car with no trailer, clearly under that weight. What does the sign require?
options: Stop on the bridge so the car can be weighed
Treat the limit as optional when the bridge looks empty
You may cross
Read the figure on the sign as a speed you must not exceed
questions.explanation: A weight-limit sign regulates weight, not speed. A car that is under the posting may proceed. An over-limit vehicle does not get an exception because the span looks quiet. A vehicle over the posted weight must use another route.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The freeway shoulder is signed for emergency stopping only, and you want to stop there to check a map. What is that shoulder for?
options: Any stop that feels shorter than a rest break
A scenic overlook you may use at will
A travel lane when the freeway is busy
True emergencies, not convenience stops
questions.explanation: The sign reserves the shoulder for breakdowns and similar emergencies. A convenience stop puts a parked car where traffic does not expect one and blocks space a disabled driver may need.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The only open curb space shows the access symbol and a reserved-parking message. You do not have the required credential. May you wait there with the engine running?
options: No; it stays reserved without the credential
Yes, if you remain in the car with the engine running
Yes, if the errand will be brief
Yes, if every other space on the block is taken
questions.explanation: The access symbol reserves the space for a vehicle displaying the required credential. Occupying it while you wait is still occupying it. The aisle beside it is part of that reservation.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An overhead sign marks your freeway lane EXIT ONLY, and you do not want that exit. The lane line ahead is about to become solid. What must you do?
options: Cross the gore paint to return to the freeway
Move to a through lane while the line is broken
Take the ramp and merge back onto the freeway from it
Stop in the exit lane until a through gap appears
questions.explanation: EXIT ONLY means that lane must leave. After the line turns solid, climbing back through the gore is illegal and dangerous. Pick the through lane while a lane change is still legal.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A blue hospital symbol with an arrow appears at a decision point, and you are not going to the hospital. What should you do with the sign?
options: Stop beside the sign until you can confirm the route
Read the arrow as a warning that your road is closed
Treat it as guidance and continue on your own route
Turn, because a service sign is a mandatory detour
questions.explanation: Hospital signs are blue service guidance. They help a driver who needs the hospital. They do not order every driver to turn and they are not closure warnings.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You pass a rest-area exit and then realize you wanted it. What is the safe correction?
options: Back down the ramp against traffic
Stop on the shoulder and walk back to the ramp
Make a U-turn through the gore area
Continue to the next exit
questions.explanation: A rest-area sign is guidance, not an order to stop. Missing the exit is fixed at the next legal exit. Backing or using the gore puts you against traffic that is still moving at highway speed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: On a rural highway you close on a vehicle displaying an orange triangular slow-moving emblem. What should you expect?
options: A vehicle that is exempt from keeping to the right
A vehicle built to travel well below ordinary highway pace, so slow early
A vehicle that is stopped permanently and has left the road system
A vehicle that will accelerate to highway pace when you close the gap
questions.explanation: The slow-moving emblem identifies equipment that usually cannot keep up with other traffic. Slowing early avoids a closing-speed crash. Pass only in a legal zone with enough sight distance.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A reduced-speed-ahead warning is posted before a town. Where does the lower regulatory speed begin?
options: At the warning sign you are passing now
Only after an officer repeats the lower limit
Nowhere, because the warning cancels the lower limit
At the speed limit sign ahead
questions.explanation: The warning gives you distance to lose speed. The new legal maximum starts at the regulatory sign, not at the warning. Reaching that sign still over the limit means you entered the zone too fast.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A dead-end sign stands at a side street you hoped to use as a through route. What does it tell you?
options: The street does not go through
The street is one-way toward you
The street is closed to passenger cars at this hour
You must enter
questions.explanation: Dead end means there is no through connection. It is not a one-way sign and not a temporary closure. Enter only with a legal way to turn around.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The sign over your lane shows a straight arrow and a right-turn arrow together. You want to turn left. What may you do from this lane?
options: Make a U-turn in addition to every other movement
Go straight or turn right, but not left
Make any movement
Turn left only, because the sign is read as a mirror image
questions.explanation: Lane-use signs list the only movements that lane allows. Straight and right do not include left. If you need left, change lanes before the line becomes solid.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You want to travel several blocks in the center lane signed for two-way left turns only. Is that lane available for through travel?
options: Yes; it is a passing lane for both directions
Yes, if you stay exactly between the painted lines
No; enter it only to turn left, then leave it
Yes; it is a high-occupancy through lane
questions.explanation: A center two-way left-turn lane is for slowing and turning left from either direction. Driving through it or passing in it puts you head-on into someone using it correctly.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A bike-lane sign and a solid white line separate a bicycle lane from yours, and you need a right turn at the next corner. How may you use that lane?
options: Use it as a travel lane whenever it looks empty
Use it as a parking lane if you stay with the car
Never cross it, even where the line is dashed for the turn
Do not drive or park in it
questions.explanation: The bicycle lane is reserved for bicycles. Driving or parking in it is not allowed. A dashed segment near a corner may let you merge across for a turn, and a rider already there still goes first. Cross it for the turn only where the markings allow, yielding to any rider.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A diamond symbol and a sign restrict a lane to a stated occupancy during the hours shown. You are alone during those hours. May you use the lane to pass a slow truck?
options: No; the occupancy and the hours on the sign still apply
Yes, whenever the general lanes are crowded
Yes, because a diamond marking is only advice at rush hour
Yes, if you leave the lane within a few blocks
questions.explanation: A managed or high-occupancy lane is regulatory for the occupancy and the times posted. Congestion beside it does not open it to a driver who does not qualify.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A no-parking sign covers an unpainted curb where you want to leave the car and step inside a store. What controls?
options: The lack of a meter
The sign; do not park there even though the curb has no paint
The bare curb, which allows a short visit
Your hazard lights, which turn the space into a loading zone
questions.explanation: A no-parking sign is enough by itself. Paint and meters are extra cues, not the only way a restriction is posted. Leaving the car for an errand is parking.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A no-standing sign is posted where you hoped to wait at the curb for a passenger. What may you do?
options: Stand for loading for as long as the passenger needs
Idle there because you are not inside a marked travel lane
Keep moving, except for a stop the sign itself still allows
Wait as long as you remain at the wheel
questions.explanation: No standing is stricter than no parking. Waiting at the curb, even with a driver in the seat, is what the sign limits. Only an exception written on the sign would allow the wait.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A no-stopping sign lines a busy curb and a passenger asks you to pull over there. When may you stop?
options: Whenever the hazard lights are on
For a passenger exchange if it is quick
If the nearest moving car is still a block away
Only to avoid a conflict or to follow a traffic direction
questions.explanation: No stopping forbids voluntary stops, including a quick passenger drop. The usual exceptions are avoiding a conflict and obeying a direction, not convenience.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You find yourself in a right-turn-only lane, you need the next block, and the light is green. What is the lawful movement?
options: Turn from the left half of the lane and go straight from the right half
Turn right and reroute
Go straight because the circular light is green
Stop in the lane and reverse into a through lane
questions.explanation: A green light permits the movements the lane sign allows. Right turn only does not include straight. Going straight conflicts with the turn other drivers expect from that lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A sign beside a left-turn lane reads that the turn yields on green. The circular light is green and oncoming cars are close. What does the sign add?
options: Left turns are forbidden for as long as the sign is posted
You should turn without a yield
You may turn left only after yielding to those cars and to pedestrians
The green is protected and oncoming traffic is held on red
questions.explanation: The sign tells you the circular green does not protect the left turn. Oncoming traffic can still have a green. You wait for a gap and for people in the crosswalk.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A sign beside the signal reads NO TURN ON RED. The circular light is red and the cross street looks empty. What may you do?
options: Turn after a full stop
Turn without stopping if you creep forward first
Treat the sign as an instruction that the turn on red is required
Wait for a green indication that allows the movement
questions.explanation: Where a no-turn-on-red sign is posted, that turn is forbidden while the signal is red. An open-looking street does not cancel the sign.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A yield-to-pedestrians sign faces you at a crosswalk where two people are halfway across. What is the correct response?
options: Stop and let them finish before you enter the crosswalk
Honk so they hurry to the far curb
Pass behind them if you leave a single step of room
Go first because the sign is addressed to the people walking
questions.explanation: The sign assigns you the duty to yield to people in the crosswalk. Sounding the horn does not transfer that duty. They have already started, so you wait until your path is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A sign shows a bicycle and a pedestrian side by side where a path crosses the street you are turning across. People are approaching on the path. What should you do?
options: Turn through them
Use the path itself as a shortcut to the next street
Yield to the people using the crossing before you finish the turn
Treat the sign as a freeway-entrance marker
questions.explanation: The combined symbol marks a crossing used by people walking and riding. Your turn crosses their path, so when they are using the crossing they go first.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A warning shows a truck on a downgrade as you start down a long hill behind a heavy truck. What extra room should you give it?
options: Less space, so you can follow in its draft
A pass along the right shoulder if it is in a low gear
No extra space
More space in front
questions.explanation: The downgrade warning tells you heavy vehicles may move slowly or may be controlling speed in a low gear. Cutting in front of them leaves no room if their speed builds. The truck may be slow or holding a low gear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Inside a work zone you see an orange warning diamond and, separately, a white regulatory speed sign. Which one sets the legal maximum?
options: The white regulatory speed sign
The orange diamond
Whichever message you find more comfortable
Neither, because a work zone has no enforceable maximum
questions.explanation: Orange diamonds warn about the temporary condition. The legal maximum is the regulatory speed sign. Do not treat a warning diamond as the speed law.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A large green overhead sign names the next city and an exit you do not want. How do you use it?
options: As a regulatory lane closure
As guidance only; stay with your route if this exit is not yours
As an order to take the named exit
As a warning to stop on the shoulder under the sign
questions.explanation: Green is the guide color for direction, destination, and distance. It helps you choose. It does not by itself require an exit, a stop, or a lane change.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The freeway's regulatory speed sign is well above the yellow advisory plaque on the exit ramp you are taking. What governs the bend in the ramp?
options: Ignore both, because leaving the freeway cancels speed messages
Hold the advisory figure as a minimum even if the ramp is sharper than it looks
Heed the yellow plaque and any limit posted on the ramp
Keep the freeway regulatory speed all the way through the ramp curve
questions.explanation: The mainline regulatory speed governs the mainline. A ramp curve carries its own advisory so you slow for the bend. A white regulatory sign on the ramp, if there is one, is the legal maximum there. Use the yellow plaque as a warning for the ramp curve, and obey any regulatory sign posted on the ramp itself.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A white DO NOT PASS sign stands where the centerline on your side turns solid, and the short straight stretch looks clear. What controls?
options: Your view of the gap
The broken line you remember from the previous block
The lack of oncoming headlights at this moment
Both the sign and the solid line
questions.explanation: Do not pass is regulatory, and a solid yellow line on your side says the same thing in paint. A clear-looking stretch does not reopen a zone the sign just closed.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A KEEP RIGHT EXCEPT TO PASS sign is posted and you are not overtaking anyone. Where should you drive?
options: Straddling the center so you can see farther ahead
In the right lane except when passing
In the left lane
On the shoulder, so faster cars can use both lanes
questions.explanation: The sign keeps ordinary travel on the right so the left side stays available for a legal pass. Sitting in the left lane when you are not passing sets up a head-on conflict.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A yellow warning and pavement arrows show your lane tapering into the next one, and a car is even with your door in that lane. What is the orderly move?
options: Stop in the taper until the other lane is empty
Move onto the shoulder and pass the taper there
Adjust speed to drop behind that car, or ahead of it only if a real gap opens
Hold your bumper even with their door and expect them to drop back
questions.explanation: The warning and the arrows describe a lane that is ending. The driver beside you already occupies the lane you need. A small speed change creates a gap; crowding their door does not.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A fluorescent yellow-green children-crossing sign stands by a park on a weekend, and no school bell is ringing. Do you still treat it as a warning?
options: No; that color applies only on weekday mornings
No; a park crossing is decorative on weekends
Only when a crossing guard is standing in the street
Yes; people may cross at any time
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green pedestrian warnings mark a place people cross. A weekend at a park is a time children are likely to be there. The color does not switch off because a school bell is silent. Yes; people may be crossing whether or not a school schedule is running.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A falling-rock warning is posted along a steep cut. What should you do through that stretch?
options: Watch the lane and the slope, and do not stop under the cut
Stop under the steepest face to look up the slope
Drive in the opposing lane
Accelerate and change lanes inside the cut without looking
questions.explanation: The warning means debris may already be in the lane or may come off the slope. Stopping under the cut increases your time in the hazard. Scan and continue through steadily.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A warning says the bridge decks ice before the rest of the road, and the approach you are on looks dry on a cold morning. How do you treat the bridge?
options: Use the bridge shoulder, where any ice would be thinner
Slow before the bridge
Hold speed, because a dry approach proves the deck is dry
Stop on the bridge to test the surface with a brake
questions.explanation: Bridge decks lose heat from above and below, so they freeze first. The warning tells you the approach can look clear while the span is slick. Slowing before the bridge leaves a margin. The deck can be icy when the road is not.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A fire-station warning is ahead and the station doors are opening. What should you prepare to do?
options: Stop in the station driveway so the truck cannot leave
Ignore the warning until a siren is already behind you
Slow and yield if apparatus enters the road
Speed up to clear the driveway before a truck moves
questions.explanation: The warning marks a driveway where emergency vehicles enter, sometimes before you hear a siren. Open doors are a reason to be ready to yield rather than to race the driveway.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: At the end of your road a large double-headed arrow points left and right, and the pavement does not continue. What is the sign telling you?
options: You may continue straight between the two arrowheads
Both directions are closed
The sign is a curve warning you can take at highway pace
You must turn left or right
questions.explanation: A two-direction large arrow at the end of a road marks the T and shows the two legal turns. It is not a gap to drive through. There is no road straight ahead.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: NO OUTLET is posted at a cluster of streets that only reconnect to the road you are on. How should you use that entrance?
options: Enter only for a destination inside
Treat the streets as one-way toward a freeway
Read the sign as a detour onto a freeway
Assume the streets are closed beyond the sign
questions.explanation: No outlet means the street system does not connect to another through road. It is not a closure and not a one-way pattern. Enter only if you mean to come back out.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A diamond-lane sign lists the hours of its restriction, and those hours have ended. No other restriction is printed. May a solo driver use the lane now?
options: No; the diamond symbol alone bans passenger cars
Yes, if nothing else on the sign is still in effect
No; a diamond lane is restricted at every hour
Only by crossing a solid line at once
questions.explanation: Many managed lanes are limited only during the hours and occupancies the sign lists. When that restriction is over and no other regulatory message remains, the lane may be used with the general lanes.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You miss a freeway exit, see DO NOT ENTER facing the ramp you almost took, and can still stay on the mainline. What is the correction?
options: Stop on the mainline and back up to the exit you missed
Cross the gore to reach the ramp
Stay on the mainline and leave at the next exit
Take the ramp anyway
questions.explanation: Do not enter on that ramp means the ramp serves opposing traffic. A missed exit is corrected at the next exit. The gore and a backup are not substitute ramps.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Overhead green signs place your destination over the left lanes, while the right lane you occupy is signed for a different destination. The lines are still dashed. What should you do?
options: Stay, assuming every lane reaches every destination
Stop under the sign until the left lanes empty
Follow the right-lane destination and turn around on the freeway
Move into a lane signed for your destination
questions.explanation: Green lane-assignment signs tell you which lanes serve which places. They are guidance to follow before the split. Waiting until the lanes divide forces a late, illegal movement.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are low on fuel and a blue sign shows a fuel symbol for the next exit. What decision is that sign supporting?
options: A choice to take the exit if you want the service
A requirement that every driver leave the freeway
A warning that the exit ramp is closed to cars
A minimum pace you must hold on the ramp
questions.explanation: Blue service signs locate fuel and similar services. They help you decide to exit. They do not order every driver off the freeway and they do not describe a ramp hazard.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You need the through highway. A brown sign names a park and a green sign names the highway. Which sign continues the highway?
options: The brown sign if its panel is larger
The green guide sign
The brown sign
Neither, because both colors are warnings
questions.explanation: Green carries route and destination guidance. Brown points to a recreation or cultural site that may leave the through route. Panel size does not change the color code.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Orange detour arrows through a downtown closure point left, then right, then left. You are unsure the second arrow fits your mental map. What is the reliable method?
options: Return to the closed street once you are past the first workers
Treat later arrows as optional when traffic is light
Follow each detour sign in sequence instead of guessing a straight line
Ignore any arrow that disagrees with the first one
questions.explanation: Detours change direction as they follow open streets. Each arrow is one piece of a single path. Skipping an arrow that seems odd is how drivers re-enter a closure.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A flagger's paddle is turned to the SLOW side while workers are still in the lane beside the open path. How do you pass?
options: Accelerate, because the slow side means the zone is already clear
Remain stopped until the paddle is flipped even though it says slow
Drive around the workers on the unpaved side
Move slowly on the path the flagger gives you and watch the workers
questions.explanation: The slow face means you may move, but people are still exposed. The path the flagger indicates is the open path. Speed stays low until you are past the work.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A flagger turns the paddle to STOP while you still have room to halt short of the paddle. What is required?
options: Stop and stay stopped until the flagger directs you to go
Creep forward so the flagger can see you more clearly
Go if a worker looks up and meets your eyes
Treat the paddle as advice on a one-lane temporary layout
questions.explanation: The stop face is a stop. Eye contact is not permission to roll. You wait because the opposite direction may be using the single open lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An orange temporary stop sign is placed where your lane meets the single lane through a work zone. You cannot yet see cross traffic. What do you do?
options: Stop only after you see the other direction coming
Make a full stop, then go only when that open lane is clear
Roll through because an orange stop is only a warning
Ignore it if a permanent signal farther ahead is green
questions.explanation: A temporary stop sign is still a stop sign. Orange tells you the control belongs to the work zone. It does not downgrade the octagon into a warning you may roll.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A no-parking sign includes a plaque making the restriction effective at all times. You want to unload a passenger there at midday. What is allowed?
options: Unload, because midday falls outside a typical night restriction
Park if someone remains in the vehicle
Use the curb if you will be gone only briefly
Do not leave the vehicle there at midday or at any other time
questions.explanation: A plaque that makes parking prohibited at all times removes any guess about hours. Leaving the vehicle to unload is still parking. The sign does not open a midday exception.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An overhead white sign says your left lane must turn left, and you wanted to go straight to the next light. What is your lawful path?
options: Turn left, or leave the lane while you can still do so safely
Go straight because the must-turn message is only a warning
Go straight if the signal shows a green ball
Stop past the stop line and change lanes inside the intersection
questions.explanation: A must-turn-left sign is regulatory for that lane. A green ball allows the turn; it does not allow a different movement. Changing lanes inside the intersection is not the repair.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You reach a yield sign, look both ways, and see no traffic and no pedestrians. Is a full stop required?
options: No; you may go even if a vehicle is in your path
No; you may proceed without stopping
Yes; every yield sign requires a full stop
Yes; you must stop and count before any yield
questions.explanation: Yield demands the right-of-way, not a stop on every approach. If the way is clear you continue. If only a stop will let you give way, you stop. You never take a gap that is not there.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A stop sign stands beyond a painted stop line, and a crosswalk lies between the line and the sign. Where do you stop?
options: Inside the intersection where the view is better
A full vehicle length past the sign
At the stop line, before the crosswalk
Beside the sign, even if that puts you in the crosswalk
questions.explanation: When a stop line is present, that line is where the stop is measured. Stopping at the sign instead can leave you blocking the crosswalk. Creep for a view only after the stop, and only if people are clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A stop sign faces you, but there is no painted line and no marked crosswalk at the city corner. Where should you stop?
options: In the middle of the intersection
Even with the far curb
Wherever the car coasts after you release the pedal
Before entering the intersection or the unmarked place people walk
questions.explanation: Without a line you still stop at the near side, short of the intersection and the path people use to cross. Rolling in blocks pedestrians and puts the car in cross traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At an all-way stop you and the driver on your right stop at the same moment. No one else is waiting. Who should go first?
options: The driver on your right
You, because you are going straight
Whichever driver is turning left
The driver who signals first
questions.explanation: When two drivers arrive together at an all-way stop, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. Going straight does not outrank that tie-breaker.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You stopped first at an all-way stop. A driver on your right arrives and stops a moment later. Who has the next turn?
options: Neither driver, until a third vehicle arrives
You, because you arrived and stopped first
The driver on your right, even though you were already stopped
Whoever is on the busier street
questions.explanation: Arrival order runs an all-way stop. Yielding to the right breaks a tie when two drivers arrive together. It does not let a later arrival cut off someone who already stopped.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Rain is falling as you approach a curve that has both a white speed sign and a yellow advisory plaque. How do the two messages work together?
options: Treat the yellow plaque as the new legal maximum for the whole highway
Ignore both because rain replaces posted signs
Stay under the white limit and slow more for the curve
Follow whichever message is higher and ignore the other
questions.explanation: The white sign is the legal maximum in ideal conditions, so rain already calls for less. The yellow plaque warns about the curve. Neither sign is permission to choose the faster figure.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A large one-direction arrow board points left at the outside of a curve you are entering too fast to track comfortably. What is the arrow for?
options: Ordering a left turn off the road at a hidden driveway
Marking a passing zone on the outside of the curve
Closing the curve to passenger cars
Showing the direction the road bends
questions.explanation: A large arrow warning sign shows which way a sharp curve goes. It is not a turn bay and not a closure. If you are already too fast, the remaining useful act is to slow as much as you safely can and stay in lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You see a route shield for the highway you want and, beside it, a yellow diamond for a curve. Which sign tells you the hazard, and which tells you the route?
options: The yellow diamond warns of the curve
The shield warns of the curve and the diamond names the route
Both are regulatory speed signs
Both are service signs for the next exit
questions.explanation: Route shields guide you onto a numbered highway. A yellow diamond warns of a condition such as a curve. Mixing the two jobs leads drivers to treat a warning as a route or a route as a hazard.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A work-zone speed sign is a regulatory panel, and a separate orange diamond shows a lane shift. You are still on the approach. What should you change first?
options: Stop at the diamond until the shift is removed
Start slowing to the work-zone speed
Ignore the regulatory panel until you see a worker
Make the lane shift at the last moment without slowing
questions.explanation: The regulatory panel sets the maximum in the zone. The diamond warns that the lane will move. Using the warning distance to slow makes the shift a smooth lane change instead of a swerve. Begin slowing toward the regulatory work-zone speed and prepare for the lane shift.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are first at a steady circular red light and the cross street has an opening. Before any question of a turn, what does the red require?
options: The same duty as a yield sign, with no need to halt
A stop only when a pedestrian is already in the roadway
A full stop until green or a legal turn
A slow roll if the cross street happens to be empty
questions.explanation: A steady circular red is a stop, not a yield and not a suggestion. Any turn while it is red exists only where state law and the signal posting both allow it, and only after that full stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The light turns yellow while you are far enough from the stop line to halt smoothly, and the driver behind is not closing fast. What should you do?
options: Accelerate so you can still claim the green
Stop only if a pedestrian signal is also changing
Treat the yellow as a flashing caution and hold your pace
Stop before the line instead of speeding up to beat the red
questions.explanation: Yellow is clearance time so the intersection can empty. When a smooth stop is still possible, taking that stop keeps you from being in the junction when the conflicting green begins.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The light turns yellow when you are so close to the line that a hard stop would risk a rear impact. What is the safer choice?
options: Continue and clear the intersection rather than stopping past the line
Brake so hard that you finish the stop inside the crosswalk
Back up to the near side of the line
Swing into the neighboring lane to buy stopping distance
questions.explanation: If you cannot stop safely before the line, the yellow interval is for finishing the crossing, not for parking in the crosswalk or reversing. Clearing is how you stay out of the next green's path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your signal is a steady green and a person is still walking in the crosswalk you must cross. What does the green allow?
options: A horn tap that transfers the right-of-way to you
Movement only after that person has cleared your path
An immediate go
A pass behind the person if you leave them one step
questions.explanation: Green permits you to go when the intersection is clear. It does not cancel a person who is already in the crosswalk. Waiting until your path is empty is part of what the green requires.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The light turns green, but cars ahead are stopped so you cannot reach the far side of the intersection. Where should you wait?
options: In the crosswalk, where you can see the queue better
Beside the stopped cars, using the turn lane as a bypass
Behind the stop line until there is room beyond the intersection
In the middle of the intersection until the queue creeps forward
questions.explanation: Entering on green when you cannot clear the far side is how a junction locks up. The green does not order you into a box you cannot leave. Wait behind the line for space.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The left-turn signal shows a steady red arrow while the through lanes beside you show a green ball. You are in the turn lane. What may you do?
options: Turn with the through traffic
Turn after yielding, the way a flashing yellow arrow would allow
Make a U-turn on the red arrow if the median looks open
Wait; the red arrow forbids that turn until it changes
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow controls the movement it points to. The green ball on the through lanes is not your indication. The arrow forbids the turn until an indication that allows it is shown.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are waiting to turn and the steady green arrow becomes a steady yellow arrow. You can still stop before the line. What does the yellow arrow mean?
options: The protected phase is ending, so do not start the turn
You must finish the turn now at whatever pace you have
The arrow has become a permanent ban on the turn
Oncoming traffic has just received a green arrow too
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow clears the protected or permissive phase. If you can stop before entering, you leave the intersection empty for the next movement instead of starting a turn that is already ending.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A steady green arrow has just come on for your left turn and the opposing lanes appear held. What extra check still matters?
options: Change lanes while you are inside the intersection
Look for anyone who has not yet cleared the intersection or the crosswalk
Close your eyes briefly to avoid headlight glare and then go
Accelerate to highway pace inside the intersection
questions.explanation: A green arrow protects the movement by stopping conflicting traffic. It does not prove the junction is empty. A late runner or a person still in the crosswalk is still your conflict.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Your left-turn signal is a flashing yellow arrow and oncoming cars are approaching on a green. When may you turn?
options: Never; a flashing yellow arrow bans the left turn
Only by making a U-turn instead of a left turn
Only after you yield to those oncoming cars and to any pedestrians
Immediately, because a yellow arrow is always protected
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow is a permissive turn, not a protected one. Oncoming traffic and people in the crosswalk still have the right-of-way, so you turn only when their path is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The signal facing you is flashing circular red at a small crossing with no officer present. What is the maneuver?
options: Treat the flash as a broken green and continue
Slow and go without stopping if you see no headlights
Wait there until a green ball appears
Stop completely, then go when the intersection is clear
questions.explanation: A flashing circular red carries the same idea as a stop sign. The stop is required every time. You proceed only after the stop, when cross traffic and pedestrians leave you a gap.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The only indication facing your approach is a flashing circular yellow, and cross traffic is moving cautiously. How should you enter?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop and wait as though the flash were red
Take the intersection at full pace
Treat the flash as a closed road
questions.explanation: A flashing circular yellow warns you to proceed carefully. It is not a stop and it is not a protected green. The caution is there because other traffic may also be moving. Slow down and go through only when you can do it with caution.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A storm has left the signal dark, no officer is directing, and no temporary sign is posted. How do you treat the intersection?
options: As a reason to sound the horn and continue without stopping
As an all-way stop, with each driver stopping and then taking a turn
As a green light for the wider of the two streets
As a yield that lets everyone enter at the same moment
questions.explanation: A dark signal assigns no one a green. Unless a temporary sign says otherwise, each approach stops and proceeds in turn. Guessing that the larger street still has a green is how the dark junction crashes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A red X is lit over the reversible lane you are about to enter. The lane itself is empty. May you use it?
options: Yes, if no other car is using it at the moment
Yes, because an empty lane is always a passing lane
Yes, but only long enough to pass one vehicle
No; the red X means you must not drive in that lane
questions.explanation: A red X is a lane-control stop for that lane. Emptiness does not open it. The X may mean the lane is about to serve the opposite direction or is closed.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are traveling under a lane signal that changes from a green downward arrow to a yellow X. What should you do?
options: Move to a green-arrow lane when safe
Stay, because a yellow X confirms the lane is yours
Stop in that lane until the X turns green again
Back up to the previous block to find another lane
questions.explanation: A yellow X tells you to leave the lane because it is closing or about to reverse. Moving while a gap exists is safer than waiting until the indication becomes a red X over your roof. Move into a lane that still shows a green arrow as soon as you safely can.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A green downward arrow is lit over your freeway lane and a red X is lit over the lane on your left. Which lane is open to you?
options: Both lanes, because freeway lane signals are advisory
The lane under the green downward arrow
The lane under the red X
Neither lane, until a turn arrow appears
questions.explanation: On a lane-control signal, a green downward arrow means that lane is open for travel. A red X over the neighboring lane means that lane is not. The arrows are commands for each lane, not suggestions.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A person facing a walking-person signal steps off the curb as you prepare a turn that crosses them. What does their indication mean for you?
options: They are being told to run across ahead of you
Their indication is a don't-walk
They may cross, and you must yield
They must wait until every turning car has passed
questions.explanation: The walking person is the indication that lets a pedestrian start. A turn that crosses that crosswalk yields to the person who has a walk, rather than racing the first step. They are allowed to start, and you must yield if your path crosses theirs.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The pedestrian signal changes to a flashing upraised hand while a person is already beyond the curb in the crosswalk. What should happen?
options: The person should turn back to the curb they left
The flash is a fresh walk, so more people should start
You may turn
They should finish, and you let them clear
questions.explanation: A flashing upraised hand means do not start. Someone already in the crosswalk uses the flashing interval to finish. Turning through them treats a clearance interval as a brand-new walk for cars.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A person is waiting on the curb facing a steady upraised hand, and your turn would pass in front of that curb. What does the steady hand mean?
options: They must not step into the crossing on that indication
They may start if the nearest car is a block away
The steady hand means the same thing as a walking person
They should cross on a diagonal while the hand is steady
questions.explanation: A steady upraised hand is a do-not-enter indication. It keeps a new pedestrian out of the street so vehicular movements can go. It is not a walk and not permission to start if the street looks quiet.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The pedestrian countdown shows only a few seconds left and the person beside you has not stepped off the curb. Should that countdown be treated as a fresh walk?
options: Yes; the number counts lanes the pedestrian must sprint
No; the numbers are clearance time for people already crossing
Yes; any remaining number is a new walk indication
Yes; the number is a speed the turning driver must reach
questions.explanation: The countdown runs during the flashing don't-walk clearance. It tells people already in the street how much time remains. A person still on the curb who starts on a short count may still be there when traffic is released.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You approach a pedestrian hybrid beacon that is completely dark, and the crosswalk is empty. Is that dark beacon a red light?
options: Yes; darkness means pedestrians have a protected walk
Yes; the crosswalk is closed to drivers at every hour
No; a dark hybrid beacon is inactive
Yes; a dark hybrid beacon is a continuous red
questions.explanation: A hybrid beacon stops traffic only after a pedestrian activates its sequence. While it is dark it is not displaying red. Treating every dark beacon as a red light is not how the device operates. No; a dark hybrid beacon is inactive and does not by itself require a stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A hybrid beacon begins flashing yellow after a person pushes the button. What driver indications should you expect next?
options: An immediate green for your lane
A green turn arrow aimed across the crosswalk
The beacon going dark again without a red
Steady yellow, steady red, then flashing red
questions.explanation: The sequence warns, then clears, then stops traffic for the crossing, then requires a stop-and-go at the flashing red before it returns to dark. The first flash is not the end of the message. A steady yellow, then a steady red while people cross, then a flashing red.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The hybrid beacon facing you is flashing red and the people who crossed are now on the far sidewalk. What do you do?
options: Stop, then go when you have confirmed the crosswalk is clear
Drive through, because a flashing red is only a warning
Wait for a green ball that this beacon does not show
Sound the horn so anyone nearby will hurry off the curb
questions.explanation: Flashing red on a hybrid beacon is a stop, followed by permission to go only when the crossing is clear. It is not a rolling caution and it does not hold you for a green that will not come.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The hybrid beacon is showing a steady red and people are in the crosswalk. What is required of you?
options: Treat the steady red as a yield if you nudge forward first
Remain stopped until the red phase ends and the people have cleared
Creep through the crossing between the people
Turn around in the lane and find another street
questions.explanation: Steady red on a hybrid beacon holds traffic so people can cross. Moving while they are in the crosswalk defeats the red phase. You wait for both the indication and a clear path.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A ramp meter shows red for your lane and green for the lane beside you. The sign allows one vehicle each green. What do you do?
options: Treat the red as a closure of the ramp for the day
Ignore the meter if the freeway looks open
Wait for your green, then go one car
Follow the beside lane's green
questions.explanation: A ramp meter releases lanes one indication at a time. The other lane's green is not yours. One vehicle per green, unless the sign says otherwise, is what keeps the merge from dumping a platoon onto the freeway. Wait for the green on your own signal, then go as a single vehicle.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The ramp meter at the freeway entrance is dark, and no sign says the ramp is closed. How should you use the ramp?
options: Stop at the dark meter until a green appears
Back down the ramp
Use the meter stop line as a parking spot
Merge in the ordinary way
questions.explanation: When a ramp meter is not operating it is dark, and drivers merge normally. A dark meter is not a red indication and not a ramp closure. A dark meter is not holding you at the stop line.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An officer in the intersection waves you through while your signal is a steady red. What controls your movement?
options: The officer's direction to go
The red light, which you must wait out anyway
The horn of the driver behind you
A rule that an officer may only reinforce the signal, never override it
questions.explanation: A traffic officer directing you overrides the signal. The officer can see a conflict, a closure, or an emergency the light is not handling. Waiting for green against that direction blocks the movement the officer is clearing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your signal is green, but an officer facing you holds up a palm and keeps you in place. What do you do?
options: Turn around in the intersection without being directed
Stop and wait for the officer even though the light is green
Go, because a green light outranks a hand signal from an officer
Edge forward until the officer steps aside
questions.explanation: When an officer is directing, that direction replaces the signal, including a green. The palm is a stop. Proceeding on the green drives into whatever the officer is holding the lane for.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your light has just changed to green and a cross-street driver is still inside the intersection. What do you do first?
options: Sound the horn until the driver accelerates
Steer around them through the crosswalk
Let that driver clear before you move
Launch at once
questions.explanation: A fresh green is a common moment for someone from the previous phase to still be clearing. Green means go when the intersection is clear, so the late vehicle finishes first.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The circular signal is red, no sign prohibits a turn on red, and the state you are in allows that movement. What must still happen before you turn right?
options: A rolling turn
A turn without looking
A wait for a green arrow even though the movement is legally open
A full stop, then the turn only if the gap and the crosswalk are clear
questions.explanation: Where state law and the posting both allow a turn on a circular red, the turn is still a stop first. After the stop you go only if pedestrians and cross traffic leave a gap. The allowance is not a rolling green.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Your state generally allows a turn on a circular red, but this signal is posted NO TURN ON RED. The light is red and the street looks empty. What is legal?
options: Waiting for a green indication that permits the turn
Turning after a stop
Turning without a stop if the street stays empty
Treating the sign as a command that the turn must be made on red
questions.explanation: A no-turn-on-red sign removes the movement at that approach even in a state that otherwise allows it. An empty street does not replace the sign. Wait for an indication that actually permits the turn.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A steady red arrow points the way you want to turn, and your state sometimes allows a turn on a circular red. What does the red arrow do?
options: It means the turn is required on this phase
It forbids that movement while the red arrow is displayed
It allows the turn after a stop, the same as a circular red
It protects the turn against oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow does not behave like a circular red that might allow a turn. It tells you not to make the movement the arrow shows until a different indication permits it.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The left-turn indication changes from a steady red arrow to a flashing red arrow. How has the turn changed?
options: The turn is forbidden for the rest of the day
You may turn without stopping
You now stop and may turn only when the gap is clear and the turn is allowed
The turn has become protected and oncoming traffic is stopped
questions.explanation: A flashing red arrow is a stop for that movement, then a go when it is safe, similar to a stop sign for the turn. It is not a protected arrow and it is not permission to roll the line.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The signal shows a green right-turn arrow together with a steady red ball. You want to go straight. What is allowed?
options: Straight travel, because any green arrow releases the whole approach
A U-turn from the through lane
A stop for the arrow and a go for the red ball
Only the right turn
questions.explanation: Each indication does its own job. The green arrow permits the turn it shows. The red ball still holds every movement the arrow does not cover, including straight. The through movement stays stopped.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You want to turn left. The display shows a green ball and a flashing yellow arrow, and oncoming traffic is moving. What protects your turn?
options: Nothing; you must yield on the flashing yellow arrow before you turn
The green ball, which stops oncoming traffic for you
The arrow, which is protected whenever the ball is green
A red arrow that you should wait to see
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow is permissive even beside a green ball. Oncoming drivers can still have a green. The ball lets through traffic go; it does not clear your left turn.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You have a green left arrow, and a pedestrian who started legally is still in the crosswalk you must cross. What do you do?
options: Use the crosswalk as part of your turning lane
Wait until that pedestrian is out of your turning path
Turn behind them as closely as the arrow allows
Sound the horn and complete the protected turn
questions.explanation: Protected does not mean you may cut through a person. The arrow stops conflicting vehicles. A person already in the crosswalk is still a reason to hold the turn.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A yellow X appears over your lane and the lane to the right shows a green downward arrow, but a car is beside you in that lane. How do you leave?
options: Signal and move when that open lane has a gap, without stopping dead under the X
Stop under the yellow X until the car beside you leaves the road
Accelerate and stay under the X
Swerve right without a gap and without a signal
questions.explanation: The yellow X means the lane must be vacated. A stop in the closing lane traps everyone behind you. A gap in the lane that still shows a green arrow is the exit the signal is pointing you toward.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You look up and the signal over the lane you are already driving in has become a red X. What is the priority?
options: Treat the red X as a pedestrian don't-walk aimed at you
Move out of that lane as soon as you can do it safely
Finish the next several blocks under the red X
Stop in the lane and wait for a downward arrow
questions.explanation: A red X means do not drive in that lane. If you are already in it when the X appears, the safe priority is to leave into an open lane, not to keep traveling or to stop under the closed indication.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Inside a work zone the signal ahead is green, but the flagger at the tape holds the STOP face toward you. Which control do you obey?
options: Whichever device the driver behind you follows
Neither, until a second flagger repeats the message
The flagger
The green signal
questions.explanation: A flagger directing traffic overrides the signal. The green may be for a movement the flagger is holding because workers or oncoming traffic are in the one open lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A school crossing guard steps into the crosswalk with a stop paddle while your light is green. What is required?
options: Continue, because the green light includes the crosswalk
Drive around the guard if a gap remains at the curb
Sound the horn so the guard will finish faster
Stop for the guard until the paddle and the guard release you
questions.explanation: A crossing guard directing the street overrides the signal. The paddle is a stop for the children in the crossing. The green does not authorize a path through the guard.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Red lights begin flashing alternately at a railroad crossing as you approach, and the gate is still fully raised. What do you do?
options: Stop until the lights stop and tracks clear
Cross at a reduced pace
Stop only if you can already see the train
Treat the lights as a yield and roll the nearest rail
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights at a crossing are a stop by themselves. A gate that has not yet moved does not make the lights optional. Trains can be closer than they look, and a second track may still be occupied. Stop and wait until the lights quit and you have checked that the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The railroad gate is lowering across your half of the road and a gap remains near the center. What is the legal action?
options: Follow a vehicle that has already slipped past the arm
Stop and wait
Squeeze through the remaining gap before the gate settles
Drive around the gate arm on the shoulder
questions.explanation: A lowering or lowered gate is a physical stop, not a suggestion to hurry. Going around or under it puts you on the tracks in front of the train the gate is closing for. Wait on the near side.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The railroad gate has risen, but the red lights are still flashing. Why is it too early to cross?
options: A raised gate cancels the lights even while they flash
You should cross and stop on the tracks to look
Another train can be approaching while those lights continue
The lights are only a lane-control signal for the road beside the tracks
questions.explanation: Gates can rise between trains on a multi-track crossing or before the warning has fully timed out. Flashing red lights still mean stop. Cross only after the lights stop and you have looked both ways.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: This crossing has flashing red lights but no gate at all. The lights start as you near the rails. Does the missing gate let you continue?
options: Yes; without a gate the lights are only a courtesy
Yes, if you are driving a passenger car rather than a bus
Yes, whenever you cannot yet see a locomotive
No; the flashing lights still require a stop
questions.explanation: Many crossings warn with lights and a crossbuck and no gate. The lights are the stop. The absence of an arm does not downgrade them to a caution you may roll. No; the flashing red lights require a stop even where no gate was installed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A painted stop line sits before the railroad tracks and the crossing lights are flashing. Where do you stop?
options: Behind that line, short of the tracks
On the rails, where the view down the tracks is better
Past the line but ahead of the gate mechanism
In the opposing lane so you can see around a waiting truck
questions.explanation: The stop line is placed to keep you off the tracks and clear of a descending gate. Stopping on the rails to improve your view traps you in the train's path.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Traffic is stopped on the far side of a railroad crossing and the crossing lights are dark. Where do you wait if you cannot clear the tracks?
options: In the oncoming lane around the queue
On the near side, until there is room to cross completely
On the tracks
Halfway across, with the rear of the car still over a rail
questions.explanation: A dark crossing is not a promise the queue will move before a train arrives. If you cannot clear the far side, you wait short of the tracks so a train does not meet a car that has nowhere to go.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in a left-turn lane facing a circular green, a sign says the turn yields on green, and no arrow is lit. An oncoming car is close. What do you do?
options: Turn at once
Wait for a red arrow before you consider the turn
Move into the oncoming lane to shorten the turn
Wait for the car and pedestrians, then turn
questions.explanation: Without an arrow, and with a sign that the turn yields on green, the circular green is permissive. Oncoming traffic is still moving on its own green. You take the turn only after it yields a real gap. Wait for that car and for pedestrians, then turn when the path is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Your green arrow and the steady yellow arrow have both ended, and you now see a flashing yellow arrow. You have not entered the intersection. How has the turn changed?
options: It is no longer protected
It is now forbidden until the next day
It is still protected
It must be made immediately, without a yield
questions.explanation: The flashing yellow arrow that follows a protected phase is the permissive phase. Oncoming traffic may be released. Staying behind the line until you can yield keeps you out of that new conflict. Turn only after yielding.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You entered the intersection on a green to wait for a left-turn gap. The light then turns yellow and oncoming traffic stops. What should you do?
options: Abandon the turn and park across the crosswalk
Finish the turn and clear the intersection
Back out of the intersection to the stop line
Stay stopped in the intersection through the next red
questions.explanation: Once you are past the line and committed, the job is to clear when the gap appears. Backing out or sitting through the red leaves you in the path of the next green. Finish the turn as oncoming traffic stops.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are turning right while the pedestrian countdown and a flashing hand are showing, and a person is already in that crosswalk. What do you do?
options: Pass on the left side of the person inside the crosswalk
Stop in the crosswalk so the person will walk around the car
Yield until that person finishes clearing your path
Turn now, because the flashing hand ended their right to be there
questions.explanation: The flashing hand tells a new pedestrian not to start. It does not erase someone who is already crossing. Your turn waits for the path they still occupy.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The pedestrian indication is a flashing hand, nobody has left the curb, and you are turning right on a green ball. What should you still watch?
options: Only the signal mast
The car behind you, which decides whether the turn is safe
A point a block away
The curb, because you must yield if someone steps into the crosswalk
questions.explanation: A flashing hand reduces the chance of a new pedestrian, but it does not repeal your duty if someone steps off. A right turn on a green ball still yields to a person in the crossing.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You need to go straight, but the only green indication is a right-turn arrow and the circular signal is red. What is your movement?
options: Turn left from the right-turn lane
Treat the red ball as green
Wait for a green to go straight
Go straight on the arrow
questions.explanation: A green arrow releases only the movement it shows. Straight traffic remains on the red ball. Using the arrow for a different movement puts you in a lane and a phase that are not yours. Wait; the arrow does not permit straight travel.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A sign permits U-turns, but the signal governing the left side of the intersection shows a steady red arrow. May you make the U-turn on that arrow?
options: Yes; a U-turn sign overrides every red arrow
Yes, if you complete the U-turn without stopping
Yes, because a red arrow applies only to right turns
No; the red arrow forbids the leftward movement until it changes
questions.explanation: A regulatory sign that allows U-turns does not defeat a red arrow aimed at that movement. The arrow holds the turn until a permissive or protected indication replaces it.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A beacon above a school-speed sign is flashing yellow as you approach in daylight. What is the beacon telling you?
options: The school-speed regulation posted with the beacon is in effect
The school zone has ended
You must stop and wait for a guard who is not there
The beacon is a railroad signal for a crossing you cannot see
questions.explanation: When a school-speed sign is tied to a flashing beacon, the flash is what turns that special limit on. Read the sign that the beacon is lighting. The flash is not a stop by itself and not a railroad warning.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The school-speed beacon is dark, and the sign says the special speed applies when the beacon flashes. No children are present. What does the dark beacon mean?
options: You must stop at the dark beacon as at a red light
The special school speed tied to that beacon is not active
The special speed is active all day whether or not the beacon flashes
The road is closed until the beacon is repaired
questions.explanation: A beacon that the sign itself ties to the school speed is the on-switch for that limit. Dark means that particular restriction is not in effect. You still obey any other regulatory speed and you still watch for people.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Your light is green and an emergency vehicle with lights and a siren is approaching from your left on the cross street. What should you do?
options: Stop in the middle of the intersection and wait
Ignore it, because a green light cancels the duty to yield
Do not enter, or clear quickly if you are already inside
Take the green at full pace and race the emergency vehicle
questions.explanation: A green light does not outrank an approaching emergency vehicle. Staying out of the intersection, or clearing it if you are already in, leaves the path the emergency vehicle needs.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You cross the stop line as the light turns yellow and then wish you had waited. May you back out of the intersection?
options: No; continue through and clear rather than reversing
Yes; backing to the line is the preferred correction
Yes, if the car behind you leaves a gap
Yes, because yellow requires every driver to return to the line
questions.explanation: Reversing out of an intersection puts you into the driver behind you and into the crosswalk. Once you are committed on yellow, the safe finish is to clear the far side.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Late at night your busy-street signal is flashing yellow and the side street you can see is flashing red. What is your indication telling you?
options: Stop, because any flash at night is an all-way stop
Take a protected turn across the side street without looking
Treat your direction as a steady green with no caution
Slow and proceed with caution
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow on the major approach warns you while the side street, on flashing red, must stop. You still watch the side street, because the caution exists for drivers who may not stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are on the side street facing a flashing red while the main street has a flashing yellow. What must you do?
options: Stop, and go only when main-street traffic leaves a gap
Go with the main street
Enter without stopping if the main street looks slow
Wait until the flash becomes a steady green
questions.explanation: Your flashing red is a stop. The main street's flashing yellow does not stop those drivers. After your stop you use a gap they actually give you.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: After a power glitch every approach you can see is flashing red, and no officer is present. How should the intersection operate?
options: Your direction treats the flash as a green
As an all-way stop
The wider street goes without stopping
Everyone yields and enters together
questions.explanation: All-way flashing red is an all-way stop. No approach has a flashing yellow or a green to claim priority. Arrival order, and the right-hand tie-breaker, sort out who goes. As an all-way stop, with drivers taking turns after each stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A technician has set every approach to flashing yellow. How is that different from flashing red on every approach?
options: Flashing yellow on every approach closes the intersection
Flashing yellow gives the larger street a protected turn
Flashing yellow calls for caution without a required stop
They mean the same thing and both require a stop
questions.explanation: Color still matters in flash mode. Yellow flash is caution and proceed when you can do it carefully. Red flash is stop, and red on every leg is an all-way stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Your green arrow has just come on, but a cross-street car looks as if it will not stop for its red. What should you do with the protected arrow?
options: Take the arrow at once and require the other car to avoid you
Turn into the opposing lanes to dodge the car
Leave the car in the intersection and walk away
Delay the turn until that car clears, even though your arrow is green
questions.explanation: A green arrow stops conflicting traffic only if those drivers obey. A vehicle that is clearly running the red is already in the intersection. Waiting a moment prevents a protected turn from becoming a collision.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You want to turn left on a green ball. The street you would enter is jammed, and the turn would leave you stopped in the intersection. What should you do?
options: Use the oncoming lane to get around the jam
Wait behind the line until you can finish the turn and clear
Enter and block the intersection until the jam moves
Make the turn and stop in the crosswalk on the far side
questions.explanation: A permissive green does not require you to occupy the intersection. If the far side cannot take your car, you stay behind the line so through traffic and cross traffic still have the junction.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have a green ball for a right turn, and the pedestrian signal for the street you are turning into shows a walking person. People are stepping off the curb. What is your duty?
options: Turn between them if you do it slowly
Wave them back and use the crosswalk
Yield to those pedestrians before you turn
Turn first, because a vehicular green beats a walk indication
questions.explanation: People who have a walking-person indication are supposed to start. A right turn on a green ball crosses their path, so they go first. The green allows the turn only when that path is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A yellow X is showing over a reversible lane you have not yet entered. Why stay out?
options: The yellow X requires you to enter and stop in the lane
The yellow X means that lane is closing or about to change direction
The yellow X means the lane is open only for passing
The yellow X is a pedestrian signal for the sidewalk
questions.explanation: Yellow X is the clearance for a lane-control signal. Drivers already in the lane are supposed to leave. A driver still outside it has no reason to enter a lane that is being shut or reversed.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A bus ahead of you enters the intersection as the light turns yellow. You are still at the stop line and can stop smoothly. What should you do?
options: Pass the bus on the right inside the intersection
Sound the horn and close the gap before the red
Stop at the line
Follow the bus
questions.explanation: The bus may have been too close to stop. You are not. Yellow does not extend to every vehicle behind one that was committed. Stopping at the line is the decision the distance allows. Stop at the line instead of following the bus into the clearance interval.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An officer points at you and motions you to turn left while the signal for that turn is a red arrow. What do you do?
options: Stay for the red arrow and ignore the officer
Turn right instead, as a compromise with the arrow
Wait until the officer leaves and the arrow turns green
Make the left turn as the officer directs
questions.explanation: An officer's direction overrides the red arrow. The officer may be clearing a crash, a motorcade, or a failed signal. Refusing the directed turn blocks the path the officer is managing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: No arrow is shown, the circular light is green, and you are turning left across oncoming lanes that are still moving. Why is this turn not protected?
options: A circular green does not stop oncoming traffic
A circular green always stops oncoming traffic for a left turn
Oncoming traffic is required to yield to every left turn on green
The missing arrow means left turns are prohibited
questions.explanation: Protection comes from a green arrow that holds the opposing movement. A circular green usually releases both directions at once. Your left turn waits for a gap in traffic that still has the right to go straight. You must yield to it.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The light is a steady red and a pedestrian is approaching the crosswalk but has not entered it. Where do you wait?
options: Beside the signal pole, blocking the curb ramp
Behind the stop line
In the crosswalk, to see the signal better
Past the crosswalk, with the front of the car in the intersection
questions.explanation: The stop line keeps your car out of the pedestrian path during red. Creeping into the crosswalk forces the person off their route and can put your bumper into cross traffic. The crosswalk stays open.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: After a full stop at a red light, a right turn is legal here, but a parked van blocks your view of the cross street. How do you find the gap?
options: Turn from behind the van without a view
Use the oncoming lane of the cross street for a better angle
Creep forward just enough to see, then yield
Launch onto the cross street and look as you turn
questions.explanation: Where a turn on red is actually allowed, the stop comes first and the gap comes second. A limited creep to see is not a rolling start. Pedestrians at the corner and traffic on the cross street still have priority.
