provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A flashing yellow arrow allows your left turn, and a pedestrian facing the street you will enter has a walking-person signal. Who goes first?
options: You, because any arrow outranks a pedestrian indication
Whoever entered the intersection first, including a rolling start
The pedestrian only if a crossing guard is also present
The pedestrian; the flashing yellow arrow requires you to yield
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow is permissive. A person who has a walk indication is one of the conflicts you must yield to. The arrow does not clear the crosswalk the way a fully protected phase might.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Oncoming traffic has a yellow and is stopping, you have a flashing yellow arrow, and a gap is opening that you can finish. May you use it?
options: Yes, without looking
Yes, by turning from the through lane instead of the turn lane
Yes, after you confirm every oncoming lane you must cross is stopping and the crosswalk is clear
No; a flashing yellow arrow forbids the turn once the oncoming light is yellow
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows the turn when the conflict is actually gone. Oncoming yellow helps only if those vehicles are truly stopping in every lane you cross. The crosswalk still has to be clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Railroad lights start flashing while you still have room to stop before the line, and the driver behind you is impatient. What do you do?
options: Cross so the driver behind is not delayed
Stop on the tracks where the driver behind can see you
Go around the gate arm if it has started to move
Stop before the line and wait, regardless of the driver behind you
questions.explanation: The flashing red is your stop, not the following driver's. Stopping short of the tracks leaves room for the gate and for the train. Pressure from behind does not open a crossing that the lights have closed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The first train passes a crossing marked for more than one track, and the red lights keep flashing. Why do you keep waiting?
options: A second train may be coming on another track
The lights are stuck and you should go around the gate
The first train's passing cancels the lights at once
Multi-track signs are decorative once one train has gone
questions.explanation: A second train can be hidden by the first. As long as the lights flash, the stop remains. Crossing because one train has passed is how drivers meet the train on the other track.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: One railroad gate is stuck partly down, the lights are dark, and you do not see a train. What is the cautious legal choice?
options: Cross and stop on the tracks to look farther down the line
Do not go around the lowered gate
Drive around the arm
Nudge the gate with the car until it rises
questions.explanation: A gate across the lane is a stop even if the lights appear dark. Going around it assumes there is no train and assumes the gate failed in a safe position. Neither assumption is yours to make. Wait or use another route.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A green downward arrow over a freeway lane is easy to confuse with a turn arrow at a corner. What does the downward arrow mean?
options: The lane is closed to passenger cars
You must turn left from the freeway lane
That lane is open for travel
You must exit at the next ramp
questions.explanation: Lane-control arrows point down to mark an open lane. A turn arrow at an intersection points the way of a protected movement. Reading a downward arrow as a turn sends you out of a lane that is actually open for through travel.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A red X is lit over your lane and the shoulder beside it looks clear. May you use the shoulder to get past the closed lane?
options: Yes; a shoulder becomes a lane whenever a red X is nearby
Yes, if you use the hazard lamps
Yes, for as long as the shoulder paint is unbroken
No; move only into a lane that shows an open indication
questions.explanation: The red X closes the lane it hangs over. The shoulder is not an open lane-control indication. The legal move is into a lane showing a green downward arrow, when a gap lets you get there.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: People receive a walking-person signal and enter the crosswalk several seconds before your light turns green. Your light then turns green. What do you do?
options: Turn through the crosswalk
Yield to the people already crossing
Take the new green immediately and expect them to stop
Honk so they return to the curb they left
questions.explanation: A leading pedestrian interval lets people start before vehicles are released. When your green arrives they may already be in the street. The green still requires a clear path, so they finish first.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You have a green right-turn arrow and the pedestrian signal for the conflicting crosswalk shows a steady hand. A person is still standing on the curb, not in the street. What may you do?
options: Wave the person out against the steady hand
Turn without looking
Turn with the arrow while watching the curb, and yield if that person enters
Refuse the arrow until the person leaves the corner entirely
questions.explanation: A green arrow permits the turn, and a steady hand tells the pedestrian not to start. You may turn. You still watch, because a person who steps in anyway must not be hit, arrow or not.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Both a stop sign and a flashing red signal face the same approach. What do they require together?
options: Only a yield
A stop for the sign and a nonstop roll for the flasher
A wait until the flash becomes a steady green
A full stop before you go, when the way is clear
questions.explanation: A stop sign and a flashing red agree with each other. Both mean stop, then go when it is clear. Neither one downgrades the other into a rolling yield.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are waiting to turn left on a circular green. The light turns yellow, the near oncoming lane is stopping, and a second oncoming lane is hard to see. What is the careful action?
options: Turn only when every oncoming lane you must cross is stopping or empty
Turn as soon as the first lane stops, without checking the second
Turn from the through lane to improve the view
Back up so the second lane can be ignored
questions.explanation: A permissive left turn on yellow is safe only if the entire conflicting flow is actually stopping. One lane braking does not speak for a lane you cannot see. Wait until each lane you cross has given you the gap.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A bicycle signal shows a green bicycle symbol while the circular signal facing your car is red. You are in the general lane. What do you obey?
options: Neither device, until a pedestrian signal agrees
The bicycle signal if no bicycle is present
The red circular signal facing your lane
The green bicycle
questions.explanation: A bicycle signal controls bicycles on the movement it faces. A red ball facing the general lane still holds cars. Using the bicycle green pulls a car into a phase that was not timed for it.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The light is red, a pedestrian is about to use the crosswalk, and the only better view of traffic is from inside that crosswalk. What do you do?
options: Take the crosswalk now so you can see past the corner
Wave the pedestrian into a path around your bumper
Move past the line and stop with the car broadside in the intersection
Stay behind the line until the pedestrian passes
questions.explanation: Seeing better is not a reason to occupy the crosswalk while someone is about to use it. The stop on red is behind the line. Any creep for a view comes after the person is clear, and it still yields to cross traffic. Stay behind the line until the pedestrian has passed, then creep only if the crossing is empty and you still need the view.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A green left arrow is lit and a sign allows U-turns. Oncoming traffic is held. What extra place do you still look?
options: The crosswalk and new lanes
Only the arrow housing
The shoulder behind you
A point straight ahead
questions.explanation: A green arrow and a U-turn sign can make the movement legal and protected from opposing through traffic. People in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the lanes you will enter are still reasons to look before you commit. The arrow does not erase every conflict.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The flashing yellow arrow is on, but the only gap in oncoming traffic is shorter than the time you need to finish the turn. What should you do?
options: Stop in the oncoming lane halfway through the turn
Keep yielding until a gap is long enough to complete the turn
Take the short gap and hope oncoming traffic brakes
Turn from the adjacent through lane to shorten the distance
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows the turn only when you can yield completely. A gap you cannot finish is not a gap. Waiting for a longer one keeps you from stopping broadside in front of oncoming traffic.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The through lanes show a steady green while the left-turn arrow over your lane has just become a steady yellow. You can still stop. Why is the through green not your signal?
options: A yellow arrow means the turn has just become protected
You should switch into a through lane inside the intersection
Each lane follows its own signal; yours is ending
The through green extends your turn for as long as it lasts
questions.explanation: Turn arrows and through balls are separate indications. A green for the through lanes does not lengthen a turn phase that is already on yellow. If you can stop, you do not start a turn the arrow is clearing.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Traffic in your lane is slow and the reversible lane beside you is empty under a red X. May you use that empty lane to get around the queue?
options: Yes; an unused reversible lane is a passing lane by default
Yes, if you return to your lane within sight of the X
Yes, because a red X applies only to trucks
No; a red X closes the lane even when it looks unused
questions.explanation: The red X is the closure. The lane can be empty because opposing traffic has not reached it yet or because it is shut for a reason you cannot see. Using it to pass the queue is driving in a closed lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Lights set into the pavement at a crosswalk begin to flash as a person steps from the curb. You have no red signal. What do the flashers require?
options: Yield to the person who is crossing
Maintain speed, because in-pavement lights are only decorative
Stop and wait for a green ball that is not part of this crossing
Pass the person on the left if the flash is yellow
questions.explanation: In-roadway lights at a crosswalk highlight a person who is entering. They do not give you a vehicular green and they do not replace the duty to yield. The flash means look and give the person the crossing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A rectangular beacon beside a marked crosswalk flashes in a rapid stutter pattern and a pedestrian is in the roadway. What should you do?
options: Drive around the pedestrian through the opposing lane
Stop or slow enough to let that pedestrian finish crossing
Treat the stutter flash as a protected green for your lane
Honk and continue
questions.explanation: A rapid-flashing beacon is there to make the pedestrian conspicuous. It is not a green and not a device the pedestrian must yield to. If the person is in the crossing, you give them the space to finish.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You can still stop safely as a hybrid beacon changes from flashing yellow to steady yellow. What should you do?
options: Treat the steady yellow as a fresh green
Stop in the crosswalk so you are ready for the red
Stop, because the steady yellow is about to become a red for the crossing
Accelerate to clear the crosswalk before anyone steps off
questions.explanation: On a hybrid beacon the steady yellow is the last warning before steady red. If you can stop safely, you do, short of the crosswalk, so the pedestrian phase does not begin with you still rolling through it.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You stopped for a hybrid beacon's flashing red, the crosswalk is now empty, and the beacon goes dark. What does the dark display mean?
options: Dark means the beacon has failed and you must keep stopping
Dark means pedestrians now have a protected walk
Dark means the crosswalk is closed for the rest of the day
The sequence is over and you may go
questions.explanation: After the flashing red, a hybrid beacon returns to dark on purpose. Darkness is the inactive state, not a steady red and not a failure by itself. With the crosswalk empty, you go.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A ramp meter gives you a green, and the freeway lane beside the acceleration area is crowded. What does that green allow?
options: Release from the meter, after which you still need a safe gap to merge
An absolute right to force the freeway lane to brake
Permission to stop on the freeway gore until a hole appears
A requirement to enter the freeway shoulder instead of merging
questions.explanation: The meter green lets you leave the stop line. It does not pre-empt the freeway. You still match speed and join a gap rather than expecting the mainline to absorb you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A slower car is ahead, a broken white line is on your left, and the next lane has a long open gap. How do you use that marking?
options: Slide left without a signal
Signal, check the mirrors and blind spot, then move left only into the open gap
Cross at once
Treat the broken white line as a median you are forbidden to cross
questions.explanation: Broken white lines separate lanes moving the same way and allow a lane change when it is safe. The marking permits the move; it does not require it or replace a mirror and blind-spot check.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The driver beside your rear door is in the left lane while the line between you is broken white. Should you move over now?
options: Yes. Drift left gradually so the other driver is forced to brake
Yes. The line is yellow in function at night, so passing on the left is required
No. Wait until that car is out of the conflict space
Yes. A broken white line gives you the lane over any car already beside you
questions.explanation: Permission to cross a broken white line exists only when the move is safe. A vehicle already beside you means there is no gap, so the marking does not authorize the change. No. Wait, even though a broken white line allows a change, until that car is no longer in the conflict space.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You need the next driveway on the left, but a solid white line separates you from the lane that reaches it. What does the line require?
options: Cross the solid white line immediately so you do not miss the driveway
Straddle the solid white line while you look for the driveway opening
Stop on the solid white line and wait for someone to make a gap
Stay in your lane until a broken line or other legal opening lets you move left
questions.explanation: A solid white line means stay in your lane. Missing a driveway is not a reason to weave across it. Continue to a place where the line is broken or a movement is otherwise allowed.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Solid white lines border both sides of your lane inside a tunnel, and traffic in the next lane is moving faster. What lane choice fits the marking?
options: Hold your lane through the tunnel instead of crossing the solid white lines
Cross the solid white line to join the faster lane
Use the narrow shoulder inside the tunnel as a passing lane
Ride the solid line so you can claim either lane at the exit
questions.explanation: Solid white lines tell you not to change lanes, and a tunnel is a common place that restriction is firm. Faster traffic next to you does not turn the solid line into a broken one.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An express lane is separated from you by double solid white lines, and your exit is coming up on the far side of those lines. What should you do?
options: Treat double solid white lines as a two-way left-turn lane and turn from them
Do not cross the double solid white lines
Cross the double white lines
Drive between the two white lines as if that gap were a lane
questions.explanation: Double solid white lines prohibit lane changes. The gap between them is not a travel lane and not a turn lane. Take a later legal exit rather than cut across. Leave at the next opening that the pavement allows.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You realize you entered the express lanes by mistake and double solid white lines now separate you from the general lanes. How do you correct course?
options: Stop in the express lane and reverse back to the opening you passed
Straddle both white lines until a general-lane driver lets you in
Continue until a signed or broken-line opening
Cross anywhere once you have signaled for several seconds
questions.explanation: A wrong entrance is fixed at the next legal opening. Double solid white lines are a hard lane barrier, so reversing or cutting across them creates a conflict the marking is there to prevent.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: On a rural two-lane road the centerline is broken yellow, a slow truck is ahead, and you can see the opposing lane is empty through the passing zone. What may you do?
options: Pass even if an oncoming car is already close
Stay forever behind the truck
Treat the broken yellow line as proof the road is one-way
Pass if you can return before oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means opposing traffic is on the other side and passing is allowed only when the way is clear. The marking lets you consider a pass; sight distance still decides whether to go. Pass if you can finish and return to your lane before any oncoming vehicle conflicts.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The centerline is broken yellow, but an oncoming car is approaching and you are not sure you can return before meeting it. What is the safe reading of the line?
options: Do not pass. A broken yellow line allows a pass only when the opposing lane is clear
Pass and rely on the oncoming driver to move onto the shoulder
Pass because a broken line removes any duty to judge the gap
Cross the centerline and stop beside the slow car until the oncoming car passes
questions.explanation: Broken yellow is not a guarantee. It allows passing only when you can see far enough to complete the pass without conflicting with opposing traffic.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A solid yellow line is on your side of the center and a broken yellow line is on the oncoming side. A slow car is ahead and the road looks open. May you pass?
options: Yes, the solid line restricts only drivers who are turning left
No. You may not cross the solid yellow line on your side to pass
Yes, because the oncoming side has a broken yellow line
Yes, if you sound the horn before leaving your lane
questions.explanation: The line on your side is the one that governs you. A solid yellow line on your side prohibits your pass even when oncoming drivers have a broken line.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Your side of the centerline is broken yellow and the oncoming side is solid yellow. The opposing lane is empty for a long stretch. What does that pattern mean for you?
options: You must pass
You should move into the opposing lane and remain there behind the solid line
You may pass a slower vehicle if you can complete the pass while the way stays clear
You may not pass
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass if the pass can be completed safely. The solid line on the other side restricts oncoming drivers, not you.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Double solid yellow lines run down the middle of a two-lane highway ahead of a hill. A car in front of you is traveling slowly. What passing choice is legal?
options: You may pass if no oncoming headlights are visible over the hill
The paved space between the two yellow lines is a passing lane
You may pass on the right by using the shoulder beside the double lines
Neither direction may cross the double solid yellow lines to pass
questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines close passing for both directions. A hill hides oncoming traffic, which is why the marking is solid. Wait for a zone where passing is allowed.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Double solid yellow lines are in the center, and the driveway you need is on the left. No sign bans the turn, and oncoming traffic is absent. How should you enter?
options: Turn left carefully across the lines into the driveway after yielding to opposing traffic
Never cross double solid yellow lines, so continue until you can find a different road
Use the opposing lane to pass the car ahead and then dive into the driveway
Back up in your lane until the driveway lines up with your bumper
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines forbid passing, but a careful left turn into a driveway is allowed where turns themselves are allowed. Yield, turn, and do not use the opening as a passing lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A divided highway has a solid yellow line along the left side of your lanes, next to the median. What does that edge line tell you?
options: It separates same-direction lanes, so change lanes across it freely
It marks the right shoulder and you should steer toward it
It is the left edge
It invites you to pass slower traffic by moving left of the line
questions.explanation: Yellow on the left edge of a divided road keeps you out of the median. Crossing it puts you on the wrong side of the separation the paint is marking.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are on a one-way street and a yellow line runs along the left curb. A bus stop is on that side. Where should your car stay?
options: Drive left of the yellow line
Treat the yellow left-edge line as a bike-only stripe you must straddle
Use the area left of the yellow line as a passing lane around stopped cars
Keep right of the yellow left-edge line and do not drive in the space beside the left curb
questions.explanation: On a one-way road, yellow marks the left edge. That paint is not a passing lane. Staying to the right of it keeps you in the traveled lanes.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The right edge of your lane is a solid white line and the paved shoulder is empty. A slow truck is ahead in your lane. How should you respond?
options: Do not cross the white edge line to pass
Pass the truck on the shoulder
Drive with your right tires on the shoulder whenever the lane feels narrow
Treat the white edge line as a centerline that separates opposing traffic
questions.explanation: The white right-edge line marks the boundary of the travel lane. The shoulder is for emergencies and legal stops, not for passing a slow truck.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your right tires begin to drop onto the shoulder beyond the white edge line, and you hear the change in surface. What steering response matches the marking?
options: Brake hard and stop broadside across the edge line
Ease back into the lane gently instead of jerking across the white edge line
Yank the wheel left immediately so you jump back over the edge line
Accelerate and continue on the shoulder until the next driveway
questions.explanation: The white edge line is the lane boundary you just left. A sudden yank can throw you across the lane or into another driver. Recover smoothly and return fully to the travel lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A wide white stop line is painted before a crosswalk at a red signal. Where should you stop?
options: Pull into the crosswalk so you can see past the corner building
Ignore the stop line and stop beside the signal pole in the intersection
Stop with your vehicle behind the stop line, short of the crosswalk
Stop with your front wheels on top of the stop line for a better view
questions.explanation: The stop line is the legal stopping position when a stop is required. Stopping on it or beyond it puts your car into the crosswalk where people walk.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The light turns green, but people are still in the crosswalk beyond the stop line. What should you do with the painted crosswalk?
options: Enter the crosswalk and nudge forward so the people move aside
Drive around the people by using the painted crosswalk as a lane
Stop in the middle of the crosswalk and wait for the next green
Remain behind the stop line until the crosswalk is clear, then go
questions.explanation: A marked crosswalk is for people on foot. A green light does not let you occupy it or cut them off. Wait behind the line, then proceed when they are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Traffic is backed up through an intersection and the only open pavement is the painted crosswalk on your side. Where do you wait?
options: Wait behind the stop line so you are not stopped inside the crosswalk
Stop in the crosswalk
Block the crosswalk and wave people around your bumper
Park across the crosswalk until the queue ahead moves a full car length
questions.explanation: You must not stop in a crosswalk. If moving forward would leave you sitting in it, stay behind the stop line so people can still cross.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are approaching an intersection with sidewalks but no painted crosswalk lines. A person is stepping off the curb to cross your path. What is true?
options: Honk and keep your speed
An unmarked crosswalk still exists at the intersection, so yield and let the person cross
No paint means the person must wait until every car has passed
Unmarked intersections never have a crossing, so continue without slowing
questions.explanation: Paint does not create the crosswalk at an ordinary intersection. People may still cross there, and you must yield rather than treating the lack of paint as permission to continue.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A dotted white line still separates your through lane from an exit lane, and the striped gore has not started. You want the exit. What does the dotted line allow?
options: The dotted line is a stop line
You may move into the exit lane across the dotted line while it is still dotted, if the gap is safe
You may also drive through the striped gore if you change your mind a moment later
The dots mean the exit is closed and you must stop on them
questions.explanation: While the line is dotted you may still choose the exit or the through lane. That permission ends when the line becomes solid and the gore begins. Never drive through the striped wedge.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The lane line beside an exit has changed from dotted white to solid white, and the gore stripes are starting. You are still in the through lane. What should you do?
options: Use the gore if you keep two tires outside the stripes
Stop on the solid line and wait for a gap in the exit lane
Stay on the through road
Cross the solid line
questions.explanation: The change from dots to a solid line is the point of no return. After that, crossing into the exit means driving through the gore or a prohibited line. Take the next exit.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A center lane is marked with yellow lines and two-way left-turn arrows. You need to turn left into a driveway a short distance ahead. How do you use the lane?
options: Enter the lane several blocks early and drive in it as a through lane
Use the center lane to pass the line of cars on your right
Treat the arrows as a reversible express lane for any movement
Enter the two-way left-turn lane close to the driveway, then turn left out of it
questions.explanation: A two-way left-turn lane is only for left turns from either direction. Enter near your turn, make the turn, and do not travel through it or use it as a passing lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Traffic is stopped in both through lanes, and the center two-way left-turn lane is empty for a long stretch. Can you use it to get to the front?
options: No. Do not use the two-way left-turn lane to pass stopped traffic or to drive through
Yes. An empty center lane is a passing lane whenever the through lanes are slow
Yes. The yellow arrows mean either direction may travel any distance in that lane
Yes, if you put on the hazard lights while you pass in the center lane
questions.explanation: The center lane exists so drivers can get out of the through lanes to turn left. Using it to pass or to skip a queue turns a turn bay into a head-on conflict.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You have turned left into a two-way left-turn lane and now want to go straight for the next half mile because your lane is crowded. Is that use allowed?
options: Yes, because two-way arrows reserve the lane for passing slow trucks
No. Leave the two-way left-turn lane by completing a left turn; do not travel through it
Yes. Once you have entered, you may use it as an ordinary through lane
Yes. You may accelerate in it and merge right wherever you like
questions.explanation: The lane is storage for a left turn, not a commuting lane. After you enter, finish the turn rather than driving along the center and conflicting with drivers entering from the other direction.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A bike-lane symbol and a solid white line mark the lane on your right. Cars are stopped in your lane near a corner. May you drive in the bike lane to get around them?
options: Yes. The symbol is decoration and the lane is for right turns at any speed
Yes, if you tap the horn so any rider still in the lane moves away
No. Do not drive in the bike lane to pass or to reach the corner sooner
Yes. A bike lane is a spare car lane whenever bicycles are not visible
questions.explanation: The bike-lane marking reserves that space for bicycles. Stopped cars do not convert it into a passing lane. Wait in the travel lane instead of driving in the bike lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You need to turn right and a bike lane lies between your lane and the curb. A rider is approaching in that lane and would reach the corner with you. What should you do?
options: Yield and turn across the bike lane only after the rider has cleared your path
Turn immediately and let the rider brake
Move into the bike lane early and block it so the rider cannot pass you
Swing wide into the left lane, then turn right across both lanes at once
questions.explanation: You may cross a bike lane to turn only when the lane is clear. The rider already approaching has the space. Turning across them is the conflict the marking is warning you about.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A shared-lane marking, a bicycle symbol with chevrons, is painted in the middle of the travel lane you are using. What does that sharrow mean?
options: The marking prohibits bicycles from using this street
The chevrons are a lane-drop arrow and your lane is about to end
Bikes and cars share this lane
The marking makes the lane a bike-only lane and you must leave it at once
questions.explanation: A sharrow shows that bicyclists may use the travel lane and that drivers should expect them there. It does not create a bike-only lane and it is not a no-bike symbol.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A rider is traveling on a sharrow in the center of a narrow lane, and there is not enough room to pass inside the lane. What should you do?
options: Pass within the same lane anyway
Honk until the rider leaves the lane
Use the opposing lane without looking
Slow and wait until you can pass safely
questions.explanation: A shared-lane marking means the rider may take the lane. If there is no safe room to pass, the correct decision is to wait, not to squeeze past or to treat the symbol as a ban. Slow and wait behind the rider until you can pass with enough clearance.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A white diamond is painted in a lane, and the sign beside it says the lane is reserved for two or more occupants during the hours printed on the sign. You are alone during those hours. May you enter?
options: No. During the posted hours you must meet the posted occupancy, so stay out
Yes. The diamond by itself is permission for any car to use the lane
Yes. Occupancy rules apply only to buses, not to passenger cars
Yes, if you drive faster than the cars in the general lanes
questions.explanation: A diamond marks a restricted lane, but the sign states the rule. Alone, during the hours the sign restricts, you do not qualify. The symbol is not a substitute for reading the occupancy and the hours.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A diamond lane is separated from you by a solid white line, and you qualify to use it. The next broken-line opening is still ahead. Where may you enter?
options: Cross the solid white line anywhere
Enter by driving through the striped buffer between the lines
Stop beside the solid line until the lane's users wave you over
Enter only where the line is broken or a signed opening is provided
questions.explanation: Meeting the occupancy rule lets you use the lane; it does not let you cross a solid white line. Wait for the break in the line so you enter at the place the pavement provides. Across the solid segment.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: White triangles point toward your car at the entrance to a roundabout, and a yield sign stands at the same point. Circulating cars are close. Where do you give way?
options: Yield at the triangle line so circulating traffic does not have to brake for you
Drive past the triangles and stop inside the circle if you dislike the gap
Ignore the triangles
Treat the triangles as a stop line that always requires a counted stop even with nobody near
questions.explanation: The row of white triangles is a yield line. You give way at that line. Entering and then stopping in the circle blocks the people who already have the circulating roadway.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The same style of white yield triangles faces you on a ramp, and you can see the road you are joining is empty. What should you do at the line?
options: Treat the triangles as a railroad marking and abandon the ramp
Proceed without stopping, ready to stop
Stop and remain stopped at the triangles until another car arrives
Ignore the line and accelerate as if it were a lane-drop arrow
questions.explanation: A yield line requires you to give way, not to stop when there is nothing to give way to. Keep enough control to stop at the triangles if a vehicle or person appears. Proceed without a needless full stop, still at a speed that lets you stop if a conflict appears.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: KEEP CLEAR is painted across the mouth of a fire-station driveway, and the traffic light ahead has stopped the queue. If you pull forward you will sit on those words. What should you do?
options: Stop before the KEEP CLEAR marking so the driveway stays open
Stop on the words
Park on the marking while you wait for the station doors to open
Treat KEEP CLEAR as a decoration and stop wherever the car ahead stops
questions.explanation: KEEP CLEAR means do not stop there. Blocking that pavement traps the driveway or cross street the words are protecting. Leave a gap even if the light ahead is holding traffic.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A side street crosses through a KEEP CLEAR legend, and you are tempted to stop there so you can see farther down the main road. What is the correct stop?
options: Use the painted words as a short-term parking space
Do not stop on the KEEP CLEAR words
Stop on the legend
Stop there only if you keep the engine running
questions.explanation: Those words mark pavement that must stay empty so cross traffic can get through. A better view is not a reason to block the opening the marking reserves. Choose a position that leaves the crossing open.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The letters RXR and a pair of large Xs are painted in your lane as you approach a slight rise. What must you prepare for?
options: The letters mark a freeway entrance and you should speed up
RXR means the lane is ending and you must change lanes at once
A railroad crossing is immediately ahead
A school zone is ending
questions.explanation: The RXR pavement marking is the last warning before the rails. You slow and search for a train because the crossing can be on you as soon as you crest the rise. Slow, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You see an RXR marking, then notice a train is approaching the crossing ahead. What does the pavement symbol tell you to do now?
options: Race the train
Stop on the rails so you can see the train better
Swerve into the oncoming lane to go around the lowered gate area
Stop before the crossing
questions.explanation: RXR tells you the crossing is right in front of you. Once a train is coming, the only safe response is to stop short of the tracks, not to hurry over them. The RXR mark means the railroad is immediately ahead and the train has the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Lane arrows in your lane showed a straight-or-left choice upstream, but near the intersection the arrow now reads ONLY for a left turn and the line beside you is solid. You wanted to go straight. What should you do?
options: Go straight from the ONLY lane if the signal is a green circle
Cross the solid line at the last moment into the through lane
Stop in the ONLY lane and reverse back to the shared arrows
Turn left. Once the lane is marked ONLY, do not go straight from it
questions.explanation: The shared arrows were the place to choose. Near the intersection the ONLY marking commits that lane to the turn. Going straight or diving across the solid line blocks the turn the lane was assigned.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You need to turn left, and the pavement arrow in your current lane is straight only, while the lane to your left shows a left-turn arrow and the dividing line is still broken. What should you do?
options: Change into the left-turn lane now
Stay in the straight-only lane and turn left from it at the corner
Wait until the line becomes solid, then cross it into the turn lane
Use the shoulder to reach the turn lane after the solid line starts
questions.explanation: Lane arrows become more restrictive as you approach the intersection. Make the lane change while the broken line still allows it, before the turn lane is walled off by a solid line.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Crosshatch markings fill the middle of the intersection, and the light is green, but traffic on the far side is stopped. What should you do with the hatched area?
options: Drive around the hatching by using the crosswalk
Stay behind the line
Enter and stop on the crosshatch so you keep your place in the queue
Park on the hatching if the light is long
questions.explanation: Crosshatch inside an intersection must stay clear. If you cannot get all the way through it, you wait. Stopping on it traps the cross traffic the open box is meant to serve. Do not enter if you would have to stop on the crosshatch.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A dotted white line continues your lane's path through a wide intersection, bending slightly toward the lane you should finish in. What are the dots for?
options: Ignore the dots and drift into whichever lane looks faster
Stop on the dots until the lane on the far side is empty
Follow the dotted path of your own lane
Change lanes along the dots
questions.explanation: Dotted lines through an intersection show the path of your lane so you do not drift into the next one. They are guidance, not a new weaving area in the middle of the crossing. Do not use the dots as a place to change lanes.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Yellow raised pavement markers follow a solid yellow centerline on a dark, wet road. You want to pass a slow car. What do the markers repeat?
options: They mark a bike lane you may enter to pass
They replace the solid line and turn the zone into a broken-yellow passing area
They separate same-direction lanes
They repeat the solid yellow centerline
questions.explanation: Raised markers match the line they supplement. Yellow markers on a solid centerline still mean opposing traffic and no passing. Feel and color do not loosen the solid line. You still may not cross them to pass.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: White raised markers sit along a broken white lane line between two same-direction lanes at night. The lane to your left is empty. How should you treat the markers?
options: You may change lanes if the painted line is broken and the gap is safe
White markers are a centerline, so crossing them means you are driving toward oncoming cars
The markers prohibit every lane change, day or night
The markers are a stop line
questions.explanation: White raised markers repeat white lane lines between lanes traveling the same way. They do not create a new prohibition. If the painted line is broken and the move is safe, you may change lanes.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Green paint fills a bike lane where it crosses your intended right-turn path, and a rider is in that green area. What does the color change about your turn?
options: Use the green paint as a car queue while you wait to turn
Honk and turn
Wait for the rider to clear the green area
Go. Green paint means your turn is protected and the rider must stop
questions.explanation: Green paint makes the conflict visible. It does not give cars a protected turn and it does not cancel the rider. Turn across that space only when it is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have started to enter a roundabout, and a wide white yield line and triangles are behind you. A driver on the next leg hesitates. Should you stop inside the circle?
options: Cut across the painted apron to leave room, then stop
No. Keep moving through the circle
Stop beside the center island so the waiting driver can enter
Back up to the wide white line and yield again
questions.explanation: The wide white line at a roundabout entry is where you yield, before you enter. Once you are in the circle you keep moving, except to avoid a crash. Stopping inside blocks circulating traffic. No. You already passed the yield line. Continue in the circle rather than stopping to let them in.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A stop line and a crosswalk sit back from a roundabout entry, and a pedestrian is in that crosswalk. Circulating traffic is also present. Whom do you yield to first?
options: Enter the circle and stop on the crosswalk while you wait for a gap
Wave the pedestrian back so you can take the gap in the circle
The pedestrian first, then circulating traffic
Ignore the crosswalk
questions.explanation: The set-back crosswalk is the first conflict. People on foot are yielded to before you take a gap in circulating traffic. Do not trade the pedestrian for a gap in the cars.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The line on your left is solid white and the line on your right is broken white. You want a faster lane. Which move matches the two lines?
options: Cross the solid line on the left
Cross either line
Straddle the solid line until the broken line ends
You may move right across the broken line when it is safe
questions.explanation: The line you intend to cross is the one that matters. A broken white line on the right allows a safe lane change that way. A solid white line on the left means you stay out of that lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A solid white line has separated a right-turn lane from your through lane, and the through lane is stopped at a red light. The turn lane is empty. May you use it to pass the queue?
options: Yes, if you merge back across the solid line before the intersection
No. Do not use the turn lane as a passing lane once the solid line has assigned it to turns
Yes. An empty turn lane is a legal passing lane whenever the through lane is stopped
Yes. Go straight from the turn lane when the light changes
questions.explanation: Once the line is solid, the turn lane is not a through lane and not a place to pass stopped traffic. Be in the correct lane before that solid segment, or stay where you are.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A pavement arrow in your lane bends and shortens, and a sign says this lane must exit. You do not want the exit, and a gap exists in the lane to your left while the line is still broken. What should you do?
options: Wait until the gore, then squeeze left through the stripes
Stop in the exit lane and back up to a place where the arrow is not painted
Change out of the exiting lane while the gap and the broken line still let you
Ignore the lane-drop arrow and continue straight from the exit lane
questions.explanation: A lane-drop arrow means the lane is ending or must leave. Merge or exit while you still have a legal gap. The arrow is not a suggestion that the lane continues past the split.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: STOP HERE ON RED is signed beside a stop line set well back from the corner, and the signal facing you is red. Where do you stop?
options: Creep forward to the crosswalk anyway so you can see cross traffic
Stop beside the cross street inside the intersection
Ignore the set-back line if it looks farther back than a normal stop
Stop at the set-back line the sign identifies
questions.explanation: A set-back stop line keeps the intersection open, often so turns or large vehicles can get through. On red you stop at that line rather than creeping to the corner.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A dashed bike lane runs through the area where you want to turn right, and a rider is going straight in those dashes. What do the dashes mean for your turn?
options: Yield to the through rider
Turn across the rider
The dashes require the rider to leave the road for your turn
Use the dashed area as a car lane and force the rider to the curb
questions.explanation: Dashed bike-lane markings show where right-turning drivers and through bicycles cross paths. They do not erase the rider. You yield, then turn when the lane is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in a queue and the car ahead stops short of a KEEP CLEAR legend at a busy driveway, leaving you the choice to close the gap. Why should you leave the same gap?
options: The words are a suggestion you may cover if traffic is heavy
Closing it would stop you on KEEP CLEAR and block the driveway the words protect
You should close every gap so the queue looks orderly, including on KEEP CLEAR
KEEP CLEAR applies only when a police officer is parked in the driveway
questions.explanation: KEEP CLEAR is a do-not-stop marking. Leaving the gap is the point. If you fill it, cross traffic or the driveway cannot get out, which is the problem the paint prevents.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: On a bridge the lane lines are solid white, traffic is moderate, and you would like the lane to your left because it is moving a little faster. What should you do?
options: Pass on the bridge shoulder if the solid line is inconvenient
Straddle the solid line across the whole bridge
Hold your lane until you are off the bridge and a broken line allows a change
Cross the solid line on the bridge
questions.explanation: Solid lane lines on a bridge or in a tunnel mean you should not change lanes there. Tight clearances are why the line is solid. Wait until the marking and the roadway open up.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are preparing to turn left across a solid yellow centerline into a driveway. An oncoming bicyclist is close in the opposing lane. What should the yellow line and the gap tell you?
options: Honk and turn
Wait until you can turn without conflict
Turn at once
Use the solid yellow line as a shield and turn from the opposing lane
questions.explanation: A careful left turn across a solid or double yellow line still yields to traffic that is already in the opposing lane. The marking allows the turn; it does not let you take a gap that is not there.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: White triangles are painted across a lane that joins a busier road, and a line of cars is passing on that road with no usable gap. Where do you wait?
options: Treat the triangles as a merge sign that requires the other road to yield
Drive around the triangles on the shoulder and enter beside the moving line
Wait before the yield-line triangles until a gap lets you join without forcing those cars to brake
Pull past the triangles and stop in the busier lane until someone lets you in
questions.explanation: The triangles point at the driver who must yield, which is you. Waiting past the line means you are already in the road you were supposed to join only when it was clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A two-way left-turn lane sits in the center, and you want to turn left into a driveway. A car coming toward you has also entered that center lane to turn. How should you both use it?
options: Race the oncoming driver for the longer stretch of the center lane
Use the lane to pass each other and then continue straight
Stop side by side in the center lane and trade the through movements
Each uses it only for your own left turn
questions.explanation: The center lane can hold opposing drivers who are both turning left, but it is not a through lane. You enter near your own driveway, watch for the other turning driver, and complete the turn rather than traveling toward them. Each of you uses the lane only to finish your own left turn, yielding so you do not meet in the middle of it.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Your lane's pavement marking changes from a shared straight-and-right arrow to a right-turn ONLY arrow, and a solid white line now walls off the through lane. You wanted to go straight. What is the lawful movement?
options: Turn right from the ONLY lane
Go straight from the right-turn ONLY lane
Stop and back up to the shared arrow you passed
Turn right from the through lane instead, across the solid line
questions.explanation: The shared arrow was the decision point. After the marking becomes ONLY and the line is solid, that lane must turn. Late corrections across the solid line are how turn lanes get blocked. Do not cross the solid line to recover a through movement.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Raised white markers and a solid white line separate your lane from a shoulder-side lane that is ending. You want to move right before the lane ends. What should you do?
options: Treat white markers as yellow and pass opposing traffic on the right
Do not cross the solid white line and the markers
Cross the solid white markers
Drive over the markers and use the ending lane to pass
questions.explanation: White markers repeat the white line beside them. When that line is solid, the markers are not a broken-line opening. Wait for a marking that allows the lane change. Stay left until a broken line allows the move.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A sharrow is painted in the right lane of a multi-lane street, and a rider is in that lane while the lane to your left is empty and the line is broken white. How do you pass?
options: Change lanes to pass when it is safe
Squeeze past the rider inside the shared lane
Honk and stay in the shared lane, forcing the rider onto the sidewalk
Treat the sharrow as a bike-only lane you must not pass in any lane
questions.explanation: The sharrow means you share; it does not forbid a normal pass from another lane. Use the broken white line for a real lane change, and do not skim past the rider inside the shared lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An RXR marking is in your lane, the crossing ahead has no flashing lights and no gate, and you cannot see far down the tracks because of a building. What should you do?
options: Treat RXR as a lane-ends symbol and change lanes on the tracks
Slow at the RXR marking, look and listen, and be prepared to stop before the rails
Maintain speed because the absence of a gate means no train can come
Stop on the tracks to get a better view past the building
questions.explanation: RXR means the railroad is immediately ahead even when the crossing hardware is quiet. Limited sight distance is a reason to slow and be able to stop, not a reason to roll across blind.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A solid yellow line is on your side as you follow a farm vehicle, and a broken yellow segment begins well ahead. What is the legal plan?
options: Wait until your side is broken and clear
Cross the solid yellow segment now and finish the pass in the broken segment
Pass on the right shoulder while the yellow line is solid
The farm vehicle must pull over
questions.explanation: The solid yellow line on your side is your prohibition for as long as it lasts. You begin a pass only where your line allows it, and only when the way is clear. Wait behind the vehicle until your side of the line is broken, then pass only if the opposing lane is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Double solid white lines separate a toll lane from the free lanes, and you do not want the toll lane. A friend in the toll lane is waving. How do you join them?
options: Stop across the double lines so your friend can fall in behind you
You do not cross the double solid white lines
Cross the double lines slowly
Drive between the double white lines until a booth attendant directs you
questions.explanation: Another driver's gesture does not cancel double solid white lines. Those lines prohibit the lane change. Enter only where the roadway provides an opening. Stay in the free lanes until a legal entrance.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A white edge line and a rumble strip mark the right side of a freeway-style lane, and an exit ramp has not started. You want to let a tailgater pass. What should you avoid?
options: Stop across the white edge line so the tailgater has to choose a side
Treat the edge line as a broken line you may cross to make a new lane
Do not move onto the shoulder beyond the white edge line to let the tailgater by
Leave the lane across the edge line and drive the shoulder until the tailgater passes
questions.explanation: The white edge line is the lane boundary. Creating a shoulder lane for someone else's impatience is not an emergency stop and not a legal pass. Hold the travel lane or change lanes where the markings allow.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Green conflict paint covers a bike crossing straight ahead, and no rider is in it or approaching. Your signal is green for a right turn. How do you treat the paint?
options: Avoid the turn forever
Stop on the green paint and wait even though no one is coming
Treat the green paint as a signal that your turn is protected from all traffic
Scan the green area, then turn through it
questions.explanation: Green paint highlights where bicycles cross. It does not forbid the turn when no rider is in the conflict, and it does not protect you from one. You turn only after you see the space is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: An unmarked intersection has no stop line and no crosswalk paint, and a pedestrian has already begun to cross from your left. Where should you stop?
options: Stop only if the pedestrian is inside a painted line, which there is not
Stop before the unmarked crossing and let the pedestrian finish, even though no lines are painted
Continue, because the lack of a stop line means the pedestrian is jaywalking with no protection
Pass the pedestrian on the right inside the intersection
questions.explanation: The absence of paint does not erase the intersection crosswalk. Once the person is crossing, you stop short of their path and wait until they are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in a two-way left-turn lane waiting to turn into a driveway, and through traffic in your direction is moving past you on the right. A gap in oncoming traffic appears. What do you do with the center lane?
options: Accelerate straight in the center lane now that oncoming traffic has a gap
Use the gap to pass the through traffic on their left
Back out of the center lane into the through lane you came from
Complete the left turn through the gap
questions.explanation: You entered the two-way left-turn lane for the driveway turn. When the gap appears, you finish that turn. The gap is not permission to convert the center lane into a through or passing lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A diamond symbol is in a lane whose sign requires two occupants, and you have a passenger, but the line into the lane is solid white until a gap a quarter mile ahead. When may you move over?
options: At the gap where the line is broken
Across the solid line now
Never, because a diamond lane cannot be used by an ordinary passenger car even with two people
Only by stopping in your lane and backing up to a broken section you already passed
questions.explanation: Occupancy lets you use the lane during the restriction; the solid line still tells you where you may enter. Qualify and enter at the opening, rather than crossing the solid segment. You meet the occupancy rule and that is the legal opening.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The word ONLY and a straight arrow are painted in your lane, and the lanes to either side are turn lanes walled off by solid white lines. A navigation prompt says to turn right now. What can you legally do?
options: Cross the solid white line into the turn lane at the stop line
Stop in the straight lane and reverse into a turn lane
Continue straight as the lane requires
Turn right from the straight ONLY lane
questions.explanation: ONLY means the lane may be used only for the movement shown. A navigation prompt does not repaint the arrow or make a solid white line legal to cross. Continue straight. The ONLY arrow assigns this lane, and the solid lines forbid a last-second change.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Yellow raised markers continue through a work area where the painted yellow line is faded, and they sit on what is still the center of a two-way road. How should you use them at night?
options: Drive to the left of the yellow markers
Treat yellow markers as a same-direction lane line you may cross to pass at will
Straddle the markers so following drivers can see them better
Keep to the right of the yellow markers, just as you would keep to the right of a yellow centerline
questions.explanation: Raised yellow markers repeat the centerline that separates opposing traffic. Faded paint does not change their color or their meaning. Stay on your side of them.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A wide driveway crosses a sidewalk, and KEEP CLEAR is painted on the street across that driveway. You are on the street and the signal ahead is green, but cars are stopped on the far side. Where do you wait?
options: Wait before KEEP CLEAR
Enter and stop on KEEP CLEAR
Stop on the sidewalk instead
Park in the driveway mouth until the far side clears
questions.explanation: A green light does not authorize you to stop on KEEP CLEAR. If you cannot clear the marking, you wait before it so the driveway stays usable.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are approaching a railroad crossing marked RXR, the lights are not flashing, and a bus ahead has stopped before the tracks and is still there. What should the marking lead you to do?
options: Use the opposing lane to go around the bus across the rails
Slow and be prepared to stop behind the bus
Pass the bus and stop on the tracks so you do not lose your place
Ignore RXR because dark lights mean the crossing has been closed
questions.explanation: RXR tells you the rails are immediately ahead. A stopped bus at that crossing is a reason to wait behind it, not to occupy the tracks or pass into the crossing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The line between a through lane and a right-turn lane is still broken white, you need the turn, and no one is beside you in the turn lane. What should you do before the line becomes solid?
options: Wait for the solid line
Enter the turn lane by crossing the solid segment at the crosswalk
Signal and move into the turn lane while the broken white line still allows the change
Stay in the through lane and turn right from it after the line turns solid
questions.explanation: A broken white line is the legal place to choose the turn lane when the move is safe. Waiting until the line is solid leaves you in the wrong lane with no lawful last-second correction.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A painted left-turn arrow is in the lane to your left, your lane has a through arrow, and you are alongside a car in that turn lane. The signal is a green circle. May you turn left from your lane?
options: Yes. A green circle lets any lane turn left regardless of the arrows
Yes, if the car in the turn lane is slower than you
Yes. Pavement arrows are suggestions you may ignore when the light is green
No. Your lane is for through traffic only
questions.explanation: Lane arrows assign the movement. A green circle allows traffic to go, but it does not let a through lane make the turn that the arrow gave to the lane beside you.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Double solid yellow lines divide the road, and a vehicle ahead is stopped in your lane with its hazard lights on. The opposing lane is empty. What passing decision fits the lines?
options: Do not cross the double solid yellow lines to pass the stopped vehicle
Pass in the opposing lane
Use the space between the double lines as a narrow passing lane
Pass on the left and stay in the opposing lane until the next intersection
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines still forbid the pass. A stopped vehicle with hazard lights is not the driveway-turn exception. You wait or go around only where the law and the markings allow, without turning the opposing lane into a passing lane.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A shared-lane sharrow is in your lane and no bicyclist is present. The lane continues, and you are not turning. How should the marking change your trip?
options: Treat the chevrons as a wrong-way warning and turn around
Keep driving in the lane
Leave the lane immediately
Stop on the sharrow until a bicycle arrives to use it
questions.explanation: A sharrow marks a shared lane. Cars may use it, and bicycles are not banned from it. With no rider present you simply continue, ready to share if one appears. A sharrow does not close the lane to cars and does not make it bike-only.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You drifted and both right tires are now right of the white edge line, with rumble strips chattering and a guardrail close on the right. What recovery fits both warnings?
options: Accelerate along the shoulder between the edge line and the guardrail
Brake hard and stop angled across the edge line and the lane
Ease left just enough to return to the lane
Yank left across two lanes to escape the rumble quickly
questions.explanation: The edge line and the shoulder rumbles both say you have left the lane. A small smooth correction puts you back. A hard yank risks a spin or a sweep across the lane; staying on the shoulder risks the guardrail.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: White yield triangles are at a channelized right turn, and a pedestrian is about to step into the crosswalk just beyond those triangles. What do you do at the line?
options: Roll past the triangles and stop in the crosswalk
Take the turn without slowing
Use the opposing side of the channel to avoid yielding
Yield and let the pedestrian cross first
questions.explanation: The yield line is where you give way, including to a person using the crosswalk at that turn. Passing the triangles and stopping in the crosswalk blocks the person you were supposed to yield to.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A buffered bike lane ends at an intersection approach where the buffer markings stop and a dashed bike lane continues toward the corner you will turn past. A rider is beside you in the dashes. What is the right sequence?
options: Let the rider pass, then turn
Cut in front of the rider where the buffer ends
Stop in the dashed lane and motion the rider onto the sidewalk
Turn from the buffer itself while the rider is beside you
questions.explanation: The end of the hashed buffer does not end the rider's right to go through. Dashes mark the place your turn crosses them. You yield first, then cross when the lane is clear. Let the rider proceed, then turn across the dashed bike lane only after it is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At an all-way stop you came to a complete stop clearly before the car on your left, and your paths cross. Who should move first?
options: You both enter together and sort it out inside the intersection
You go first, after your own stop
The car on your left goes first
The faster car goes first even if it arrived later
questions.explanation: At an all-way stop the first driver to arrive goes first after stopping. Arriving earlier than the car on your left gives you the turn; it does not let you skip the stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Another driver reached the all-way stop well before you and is already stopped. You have just stopped. What is your turn?
options: Edge into the intersection beside them so you leave together
Honk until the earlier driver gives up the turn they already have
Wait. The driver who arrived first goes before you
Go immediately because a later arrival can claim the intersection
questions.explanation: Arrival order is the rule. If they were there first and your paths conflict, you wait until they have taken their turn. Being ready to be impatient does not reorder the stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You and a driver on your right stop at an all-way stop at the same moment, and your paths cross. Who yields?
options: You go first
The driver who flashes the headlights goes first
The driver turning left always takes a tie over the driver on the right
You yield. A tie goes to the driver on your right
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive together, the tie-breaker is position, not size or nerve. The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You stop at the same instant as the driver on your left at an all-way stop, and both of you intend to go straight through crossing paths. What should you do?
options: Go first after the stop
Yield because the driver farther from the curb always waits
Wait for the left-side driver
Enter together side by side through the crossing
questions.explanation: A simultaneous arrival is settled by the right-hand rule. From their seat you are on the right, so they yield and you take the open turn after you have stopped. You are the driver on their right, so the tie favors you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Three cars have stopped at an all-way stop. Two of them were already there when you arrived. How do you order your start?
options: Take the first gap
You go last, after the two drivers who arrived before you have gone
Go when the first car goes so two cars can leave side by side
Go second because three-car stops ignore the last arrival
questions.explanation: Count the arrivals. If two drivers were already stopped when you got there, both of them have a turn before yours. Do not pair yourself with a car that arrived earlier.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You stopped first at an all-way stop and you are going straight. A driver who arrived after you wants to turn left across your path. Who goes?
options: Left turns always outrank straight movements at an all-way stop
You must wave the turning driver through before a straight car may go
You go first
The left turn goes first
questions.explanation: At an all-way stop, who arrived first matters more than who is turning. You were first and you are going straight, so you take your turn. The later left turn waits. Arrival order outranks the fact that the other driver is turning.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You arrived second at an all-way stop and you want to turn left. The first driver is going straight across your turn. What should you do?
options: Turn first because a left turn has priority over a later straight movement
Turn with them so both of you occupy the intersection together
Back away from the stop and approach again to become first
Let the first driver go straight
questions.explanation: Being the turning driver does not jump the queue. The driver who arrived first goes first. You make the left turn only after that straight movement is out of the way.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You reached an all-way stop first, you have completed your stop, and your plan is a left turn. A straight-through driver arrives while you are still the only one waiting. What is your move?
options: Take your left turn first
Yield the first turn
Wait until two more cars arrive so the stop becomes busier
Turn from the right lane instead of waiting for your own gap
questions.explanation: Arrival decides the order. A left turn does not surrender a turn you already earned by getting there first. Stop, then make the turn while the intersection is yours.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You and the driver opposite you arrive together at an all-way stop. You want to turn left and that driver is going straight through the path you would cross. Who yields?
options: Both of you turn into the same lane at the same time
The straight driver must wait
You yield the conflicting path
You go first
questions.explanation: A tie at an all-way stop does not let a left turn cut across an opposite driver who is going straight. Your paths conflict, so the left turn yields even though you arrived together.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pedestrian steps off the curb to cross at an all-way stop just as you finish your stop. Two other cars arrived after you. What is the order?
options: Take the car queue first
Go with the later cars and let the pedestrian fit in afterward
Honk so the pedestrian waits until every car has cleared
Yield to the pedestrian first, then take your turn among the cars
questions.explanation: People crossing are not last in the vehicle queue. Even if you were the first car, a pedestrian who is starting to cross goes before any of the cars take the intersection.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are first in line at an all-way stop, but you have not quite stopped rolling. The intersection is empty. What must you still do?
options: Come to a full stop, then go
Continue through without stopping
Stop in the middle of the intersection instead of at the line
Only slow down
questions.explanation: First to arrive is first to go only after the required stop. Rolling through wastes the rule that makes the order predictable for everyone else.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The signal shows a green ball, you are turning left, and oncoming cars are approaching in the lane you must cross. What is required of your turn?
options: Turn wide into the oncoming lanes so you finish faster
Yield. Wait for a gap in the oncoming traffic before you turn left on the green ball
Turn immediately because a green ball protects a left turn from oncoming cars
Expect the oncoming cars to stop
questions.explanation: A circular green lets you turn left only after you yield to oncoming traffic. It is not a protected arrow. If those cars are close, you wait.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your left turn faces a green ball, oncoming lanes are open, and people are still walking in the crosswalk you would drive through. What do you do?
options: Honk so the people hurry out of the protected green ball
Turn into the oncoming lane to avoid the crosswalk entirely
Wait for the people to clear the crosswalk, then turn left
Turn behind the people as closely as you can so you keep the green
questions.explanation: A green ball does not let a left turn cut through pedestrians. Oncoming cars are not the only yield. The people in the turn path go first.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are turning left on a green ball. Oncoming traffic has a large gap and the crosswalk you will enter is empty. What should you do?
options: Wait for a green arrow even though the ball is green and the way is open
Turn now and assume any pedestrian who steps out will stop
Swing into the far lane of the new street as you complete the turn
Make the left turn through that gap while the crosswalk stays clear
questions.explanation: When the green ball's yields are satisfied, a large gap and an empty crosswalk, you should take the turn. Sitting through a clear gap is not what the yield rule requires.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A green arrow faces your left-turn lane, oncoming traffic has a red light, and the crosswalk on your turn is empty. How do you use the arrow?
options: Turn left; the arrow holds oncoming cars
Yield to oncoming cars anyway, as if the signal were only a green ball
Wait in the intersection until the arrow turns red before you turn
Ignore the empty crosswalk and watch only the arrow lamp
