questions.explanation: A green arrow protects the turn from oncoming traffic that is being held. It does not excuse skipping a look at the crosswalk. With people clear and oncoming held, you turn. Turn left. The arrow holds the oncoming cars, and you still checked that the crosswalk is empty.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your left-turn signal is a green arrow, but a person is still in the crosswalk that the turn crosses. Oncoming cars are stopped. What should you do?
options: Honk and complete the turn beside the person
Wait until the person is clear
Turn through the crosswalk
Follow an oncoming car that is running the red light
questions.explanation: The arrow stops oncoming vehicles. It does not remove a person who is already in the crosswalk. Protected from cars is not the same thing as an empty crossing. Wait until the person is clear of your turn path, even though the arrow protects you from oncoming cars.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are going straight on a green light and an oncoming driver starts a left turn across your lane. Who has the right-of-way?
options: Swerve left into their lane so they have room to finish the turn
Stop in your lane and back up to give them the intersection
You do. Continue straight, covering the brake in case that driver turns anyway
You must stop and let every oncoming left turn go in front of you
questions.explanation: On a green ball the through movement has priority over an oncoming left turn. Do not give the lane away, and do not assume they will always finish the yield. Cover the brake.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have started to creep into a left turn on a green ball and you now see an oncoming car that is closer than you first thought. What is the better decision?
options: Floor the throttle and finish the turn in front of the oncoming car
Complete the turn
Flash your lights so the oncoming car takes the shoulder
Hold the turn and wait
questions.explanation: Creeping forward does not lock in the turn. If the gap has closed, you stop the turn and keep yielding. A circular green never forces the oncoming driver to brake for you. A green ball still requires you to yield to that oncoming car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are turning left from a two-way street onto another two-way street, and nothing assigns you a different lane. Which lane should you finish in?
options: Turn into any lane you like if you signal during the arc
Turn into the nearest lane that is lawfully moving your direction
Swing wide into a lane of oncoming traffic on the street you are entering
Finish in the far left lane of opposing traffic so the turn is smoother
questions.explanation: A left turn should end in the nearest proper lane for your direction. A wide swing puts you into a lane someone else is using, including an oncoming lane on the new street.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are making a right turn from a wide road onto a multi-lane street. No sign tells you to finish in a different lane. Where should the turn end?
options: Turn from the left lane of your road without checking a bike lane on your right
Finish the turn stopped across a crosswalk
End in the right lane of the road you are entering
Arc into the left lane of the new road as a habit
questions.explanation: A right turn belongs in the right lane unless markings say otherwise. Swinging into the left lane, or turning from the wrong lane across a bike lane you have not checked, takes someone else's space.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The light is a green ball for your right turn, and a pedestrian is in the crosswalk you would use. What is the order?
options: Turn in front of the pedestrian
Pass behind the pedestrian as closely as the bumper allows
Use the crosswalk as part of your turning lane
The pedestrian goes first
questions.explanation: Green permits the turn. It does not authorize driving through a person. The pedestrian already in the crosswalk has the right-of-way over your right turn. You turn only after the crosswalk is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are about to turn right onto a street that has a bike lane, and a bicyclist is riding in that lane toward the space you would enter. What must you yield to?
options: Yield to the bicyclist in the bike lane as well as to any car you are joining
Expect the rider to leave the bike lane
Turn across the rider if you reach the corner first by a small margin
Honk so the rider stops while you take the lane
questions.explanation: A bike lane is traffic you are joining or crossing, not an empty stripe. The rider who is there has the lane. You turn only when that lane and the street are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A sign beside the signal says NO TURN ON RED. Your signal is a steady red, and the cross street happens to have a gap. What is the lawful choice?
options: Creep into the crosswalk and turn from there during the red
Wait for a signal that allows the turn
Turn now because a gap in traffic overrides the sign
Turn if you stop first
questions.explanation: A sign that prohibits the turn on red is controlling. A gap does not erase it. Right turn on red is not something you take whenever the street looks open; here it is forbidden. Wait. The sign removes this turn on red, so you need an indication that allows the turn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: No sign at this intersection prohibits a right turn on red. You have stopped, the crosswalk is empty, and there is a clear gap in cross traffic. What may you do?
options: Refuse the turn forever
Turn and require a pedestrian who then steps out to wait for you
Turn right after the stop, still yielding
Turn without stopping
questions.explanation: Where no sign prohibits the movement, a right turn on red still starts with a full stop and a yield to people and cross traffic. It is not automatic, and it is not forbidden merely because the signal is red.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are leaving a driveway, and several people are walking on the sidewalk you must cross before you reach the road. Who goes first?
options: Honk so the sidewalk clears, then enter the road in the first small gap
The driveway has priority over both the sidewalk and the road
Enter the road first and let the people walk behind your car
The people on the sidewalk go first
questions.explanation: Driveway traffic is the movement that is joining. The sidewalk and the road are already there. You stop for people on the sidewalk before you even compete for a gap in the street.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The sidewalk across your driveway is empty, but cars are passing on the road you want to enter. What is the right-of-way order?
options: Yield to the road
Pull out and expect the road traffic to slow
Block the nearest lane so the next car has to change lanes around you
Enter if you think the closest driver can slow a little without stopping
questions.explanation: Once the sidewalk is clear, you still yield to the road. A driveway does not become the through movement. Their speed should stay steady; you take a real gap. Enter only into a gap that does not force those cars to brake.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are at the end of a driveway, the sidewalk is empty, and the road you are entering has a long gap both ways. What should you do?
options: Stop in the sidewalk after you enter so you can watch the road from there
Check the sidewalk again and the road, then enter
Wait until a car appears so someone can assign you a turn
Drive out without looking
questions.explanation: Yielding means giving way to traffic that is there. An empty sidewalk and a real gap mean you go. You still look, because the duty is to yield, not to wait for a conflict that does not exist. You do not sit there when nothing is using either one.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An alley meets the street in front of you, and you are the driver coming out of the alley. People are on the sidewalk and cars are on the street. What do you yield to?
options: Yield only to cars
Honk and take the first small opening in the curb lane
Yield to people and vehicles first
The alley has the right-of-way over the street
questions.explanation: An alley is not a through road. Leaving it is the same kind of join as leaving a driveway: sidewalk users first, then street traffic, and only then your entry. Yield to the people on the sidewalk and to the vehicles on the street before you enter.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child is riding a bicycle along the sidewalk across the driveway you are exiting. The road beyond is open. What do you do?
options: Cross the sidewalk now
Nose into the sidewalk and let the child steer around your bumper
Honk as a signal that the child should stop and walk the bike
Wait until the child has cleared the sidewalk
questions.explanation: The sidewalk is not a car lane, and a child on a bicycle there has priority over an exiting car. An open road does not let you occupy the sidewalk to reach it. Wait until the sidewalk is clear of the child before you cross it, even though the road is open.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are backing out of a driveway and the sidewalk behind the car is your first conflict. A person is walking toward your path. What is the order?
options: Stop the back-up and yield until the person has passed
Continue backing and expect the person to pause for a reversing car
Honk and keep rolling so the person knows you are coming
Back into the street first and deal with the sidewalk on the way
questions.explanation: Backing out does not reverse the yield. The person already on the sidewalk has the crossing. You wait, then look for street traffic before you enter the road. Do not continue across the sidewalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An emergency vehicle is approaching from behind with lights and a siren on a multi-lane city street. You are not in an intersection. What should you do?
options: Stop in the lane you are in, even if that lane is the left lane
Pull to the right and stop until it has passed
Speed up so you stay ahead of it and clear its path that way
Follow it closely once it passes so the cars ahead keep moving
questions.explanation: Lights and a siren mean you give the emergency vehicle the road. Pulling right and stopping is the way to do that. Racing it or drafting behind it keeps you in its way.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in the middle of an intersection when you hear a siren and see emergency lights approaching. What should you do first?
options: Back out of the intersection toward the stop line
Finish your trip at the same speed and pull over several blocks later
Clear the intersection, then pull right and stop
Stop immediately in the intersection so the emergency vehicle can choose a way around you
questions.explanation: Stopping inside the intersection blocks the very space the emergency vehicle needs. Clear it, then move right and stop. The pull-over rule does not mean freeze wherever you are.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: After an emergency vehicle with lights and a siren passes you, the lane ahead of it is open. What should you avoid?
options: Follow a few feet behind so other drivers keep the lane open
Pass it on the right while its lights are still on
Race it to the next signal so you are not delayed
Do not follow closely behind it
questions.explanation: The emergency vehicle's right-of-way continues while it is using the road with lights and siren. Following closely is the same conflict as failing to pull over. Let it go, then drive normally. Stay pulled over until it has passed, then resume without tailing it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A fire truck with lights and siren is coming toward you in the opposing lanes of an undivided street. What should you do?
options: Pull right and stop until it has passed
Hold your lane and speed
Turn left across its path so you clear the street sooner
Stop beside a parked car in a way that leaves you sticking toward the center
questions.explanation: An approaching emergency vehicle gets the road in both directions on a street where your position could block it. Pull right and stop rather than betting that it will thread past you. Do not assume the opposing lane is enough if you are still in its way.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your road ends at a T intersection and the cross road continues both ways. No signal gives you a turn. What must you do?
options: Enter and expect the through road to stop for a driver at the stem of the T
Use the through road's lanes as a place to wait while you choose a direction
Yield to traffic on the road that continues, and turn only into a gap
Go first because you are the driver who has to turn
questions.explanation: At a T, the ending road yields to the road that continues. Your need to turn does not create priority. Look both ways and go only when you will not force through traffic to brake.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are driving on the through road at a T intersection. A driver on the ending stem is waiting to turn. Who has the right-of-way?
options: You must stop and give every waiting stem-road driver your lane
The driver who wants to turn left from the stem goes before through traffic
You should pull onto the shoulder whenever a car is waiting at a T
You do. The ending road yields, so you continue rather than stopping in the through lane
questions.explanation: The through road keeps moving. The driver whose road ends is the one who waits for a gap. Stopping on the through road without a reason just moves the conflict into a lane that has the right-of-way.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The road you are on ends at a T, and both directions of the through road are busy with no usable gap. What is the correct wait?
options: Stay on the ending road and wait for a gap long enough for your turn
Nose into the through lane and make the nearest driver slow down
Turn left across a short gap
Block the nearest through lane so the far lane becomes easier
questions.explanation: A T does not give the ending road a turn just because the wait is long. You yield until a gap lets you enter without forcing through traffic to change speed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are about to enter a roundabout, and two cars are already circulating in the circle beside the entry. What do you do?
options: Use the truck apron or the center island to squeeze past the circulating cars
Yield to the traffic already in the circle, and enter only when you will not make those cars brake
Enter beside them
Stop inside the circle once you have entered so another car can follow you in
questions.explanation: Traffic in the roundabout has the right-of-way over traffic that is entering. You wait for a gap on the approach. You do not stop later inside the circle to fix a late entry.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The circulating lanes of a roundabout are empty, but a pedestrian is in the crosswalk at your entry. What is the first yield?
options: Stop in the crosswalk while you look for a gap that is already there
Honk so the pedestrian waits on the splitter island
Yield to the pedestrian and do not enter until that crosswalk is clear
Enter the circle
questions.explanation: Roundabout rules require a yield to pedestrians as well as to circulating traffic. An empty circle does not let you take the crosswalk. People first, then the gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The roundabout entry is clear of people and of circulating cars. How should you enter?
options: Stop inside the circle at the first exit to be sure the entry was legal
Wait at the yield line until another car arrives behind you
Enter and then stop broadside so a waiting driver can pull out
Enter without an unnecessary stop, and do not stop inside the circle once you have joined it
questions.explanation: Yield means give way when someone is there. When the crosswalk and the circle are clear, you enter and keep moving. Stopping inside the circle is for avoiding a crash, not for politeness.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are already circulating in a roundabout, and a driver is waiting at the next entry with a small gap behind you. Should you stop in the circle?
options: No. Do not stop inside the circle to let that driver enter
Stop beside the central island and wave that driver into your lane
Slow to a crawl in the circle whenever an entry has a waiting car
Leave the circle by crossing the splitter island so they have room
questions.explanation: Once you are in the roundabout you have the circulating right-of-way. Stopping to be helpful traps the drivers behind you. The waiting driver yields until a real gap appears.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Signs on a two-lane roundabout approach show that the exit you need is served by the left lane only. Where do you choose that lane?
options: Ignore the lane sign and take whichever lane is moving
Stop inside the circle and back up to the correct approach lane
Choose the left lane on the approach, before you enter
Enter in the right lane and change lanes inside the circle near your exit
questions.explanation: Lane choice in a multi-lane roundabout is made before entry. The signs are the map. Changing lanes beside the island or stopping to correct the choice breaks the circulating flow.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You missed your exit inside a roundabout and you are still moving in the circle. How do you correct it?
options: Stop and reverse to the exit you just passed
Turn across the center island as soon as you see the exit
Leave by the next driveway cut in the splitter
Continue around to the exit again
questions.explanation: Missing the exit is fixed by going around. The circle is one-way. Stopping and backing, or cutting the island, puts you into drivers who are circulating correctly. Do not stop, back up, or cut across the island.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are ready to leave a roundabout, and a pedestrian is in the crosswalk at that exit. Circulating traffic is behind you. What do you do?
options: Yield to the pedestrian at the exit crosswalk before you leave the circle
Exit through the crosswalk
Stop in the middle of the circle rather than at the exit crossing
Honk and complete the exit beside the pedestrian
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are part of the roundabout yield, including at the exit. You do not trade a person in the crosswalk for the convenience of the car behind you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your light is green, but the lanes beyond the intersection are full and you would have to stop in the middle of the box. What should you do?
options: Use the cross street's lanes to get around the stopped queue
Wait behind the line
Enter and block the box so you keep your place in the queue
Enter and stop on the crosswalk on the far side
questions.explanation: A green light is not a right-of-way to occupy the intersection. If you cannot clear the far side, you stay behind the line so cross traffic and people can still move. Do not enter if you would be stuck in the intersection.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The light has just turned green for you, and a car that entered from the cross street is still in the intersection. What should you do?
options: Honk and move into its path so it finishes faster
Go around it through the crosswalk
Wait and let that car clear
Enter beside it
questions.explanation: A vehicle already in the intersection may clear. Your green starts your turn only after that movement is out. Entering beside it is how the box gets blocked.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You entered the intersection on green, and the signal turned red before you finished the movement. What should you do now?
options: Stop on the crosswalk now that the light is red
Back through the crosswalk to the stop line you came from
Park in the intersection until the next green for your direction
Finish the movement and clear the intersection
questions.explanation: The mistake would have been entering if you could not clear. Once you are in, the correction is to finish and get out. Reversing through people or freezing in the box makes the blockage worse. Do not sit in the box and do not back up.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A fresh green light has just appeared, the intersection looks open, and a cross-street driver is still close to the box. How should you start?
options: Look and let anyone already entering finish clearing before you move into their path
Launch immediately because a fresh green is always an empty intersection
Wait through the entire green to be sure no one else is coming
Honk and move without looking at the cross street
questions.explanation: A new green is a common moment for a late driver to still be in the intersection. Your green gives you the next turn. It does not erase someone who has not cleared.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A traffic officer in the intersection points you through a red signal. The lamp and the officer disagree. Whom do you obey?
options: Wait until the officer and the signal show the same thing, however long that takes
Obey the officer
Stay stopped for the red light and ignore the officer's direction
Follow the signal and also try to follow the officer at the same time
questions.explanation: Hands and the whistle override the lamp. When an officer is directing you, the signal does not cancel that direction. Do what the officer signals.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The signal facing you is green, and the officer directing the same intersection is holding you with a raised palm. What should you do?
options: Creep forward until the officer steps aside
Turn around in the intersection
Obey the officer and stay stopped
Go on the green
questions.explanation: The officer is the traffic control when the officer is directing. A green light does not give you permission to roll past a palm that is holding your approach. Stop and stay stopped while the officer holds you, even though the lamp is green.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A school crossing guard is in the crosswalk holding a stop paddle toward you, and your signal is green. What should you do?
options: Stop and remain stopped while the guard's paddle holds you, green light or not
Go on the green and drive slowly around the guard
Honk so the children hurry in front of the paddle
Turn into the nearest driveway to avoid the guard's direction
questions.explanation: The guard is the traffic control at that crossing. A green signal does not let you pass a stop paddle or drive around a guard who is holding children in the street.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A highway flagger is holding a paddle that says STOP toward your lane in a work zone. A permanent sign farther back shows a higher usual flow. What do you obey?
options: Drive around the flagger on the shoulder
Stop only if the paddle is also a red signal lamp
Stop for the paddle
Continue, because a permanent sign outranks a flagger
questions.explanation: Temporary direction from a flagger replaces the permanent sign it is controlling. The paddle is the right-of-way assignment. You stop when it says stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The same flagger has turned the paddle from STOP to a slow or proceed face and is motioning your lane forward. What should you do?
options: Stay stopped until the permanent signal returns, ignoring the new paddle face
Accelerate past the flagger to recover the delay
Use the closed lane beside the flagger
Move forward as the flagger directs, slowly enough to follow that direction
questions.explanation: A flagger assigns both the stop and the release. When the paddle and the motion tell your lane to go, you go as directed. Sitting there blocks the one-lane pattern the flagger is running.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The car ahead of you has stopped at a marked crosswalk, and you cannot see the far side of that crossing. May you pass?
options: No; someone may be crossing
Pass on the left if the adjacent lane is open
Pass on the right between that car and the curb
Honk and pass
questions.explanation: A stop at a crosswalk is often a yield to a person hidden by the stopped car. Passing it, in either lane, is how pedestrians are hit. Wait until you can see the crossing is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A car in the lane to your left is stopped at a crosswalk while your lane is empty beside it. You still cannot see who is in front of that car. What should you do?
options: Change lanes into the space the stopped car is protecting
Do not pass it until the crosswalk is clear
Use your empty lane to go around the stop
Accelerate so you clear the crosswalk before anyone steps out
questions.explanation: The ban on passing a car stopped at a crosswalk is not limited to your own lane. The empty lane beside them can still be the pedestrian's path. Hold back until you can see.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pedestrian has started across your lane against the signal. You have a green light and the legal turn. What should you do?
options: Honk and continue at the same speed through the person
Drive around the person by using the opposing lane
Wait until that person is out of your vehicle's path
Proceed because the signal makes the pedestrian the one who must stop
questions.explanation: Being right does not include driving through a person. A pedestrian who started against the signal is still in your path, and you wait until they are clear. Do not hit them because they are wrong.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pedestrian with a white cane is stepping off the curb into the crossing in front of your car. How should you respond?
options: Honk once as the instruction for them to start walking
Drive slowly around the cane
Call out directions and keep creeping forward
Stop and stay stopped until the pedestrian is clear
questions.explanation: A white cane means you yield. Honking is not a safe signal for when a blind pedestrian should move. You stop and remain stopped until they have finished crossing. Do not honk as a signal for them to go or to hurry.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs, you want to turn left and an oncoming vehicle is going straight. You would cross that vehicle's path. Who yields?
options: Neither yields, because no sign means no rule
You yield to the straight vehicle
The straight vehicle yields
The left turn goes first
questions.explanation: No sign does not mean no rule. At an uncontrolled intersection the through movement beats the left turn. If you are turning left across their path, you wait. You yield. The left turn waits for the vehicle that is going straight.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection together, and the other driver is on your right. Your paths cross. What is the tie-breaker?
options: The driver who honks first takes the intersection
The larger vehicle goes first
Yield to the driver on your right
The driver who is going faster goes first
questions.explanation: When no sign assigns the road and both of you arrive together, the ordinary tie-breaker is the driver on the right. Speed and size do not reorder that rule.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You and a driver on your left reach an uncontrolled intersection together. You are going straight and your paths cross. What should you do?
options: Stop and let the left-side driver go
Both of you stop and wait until a third car arrives
Turn right instead so you do not have to use the right-hand rule
Proceed; you are on their right
questions.explanation: The right-hand rule works both ways. If you are the driver on the right and you arrived together, the other driver yields. You still watch them in case they do not. Proceed. You are the driver on their right, so the tie-breaker gives you the first movement.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You entered an uncontrolled intersection clearly before the car on the cross street reached it. That car is now approaching the edge. What should you do?
options: Continue and clear
Stop in the box and back up
Yield now even though you were already crossing
Turn around inside the intersection to give them a straight path
questions.explanation: Once you are already in the intersection, you clear it. The later driver yields to the vehicle that is already crossing. Stopping or backing up recreates the conflict.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are approaching an uncontrolled intersection just beyond a crest, and you cannot see the cross street yet. What right-of-way should you assume?
options: Drive in the center of the road so both directions can see you sooner
Do not assume you have the right-of-way
Hold your speed and honk
Accelerate so you cross before a hidden car can arrive
questions.explanation: A blind intersection is a reason to cover the brake. Moving first is not the same as having the right-of-way over a driver you have not seen. You are moving. Slow enough that you can stop for traffic you cannot yet see.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You face a stop sign and the cross street has no stop sign. You arrived at your sign before a cross-street car reached the intersection. Who must yield?
options: You go together
The first driver to arrive always goes, and the signs are only warnings
You must. Your stop sign assigns the duty, so you wait until the cross street is clear
The cross street should stop
questions.explanation: A stop sign assigns the yield. The cross street's lack of a sign means they are the through road. Your earlier arrival does not move their duty onto them.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The cross street has a stop sign and your road does not. A driver is waiting at that sign. How should you treat your own approach?
options: You must stop
You must yield
Stop in the through lane and trade turns as if it were an all-way stop
Continue, but watch that driver
questions.explanation: Only the approaches with a stop sign must stop. You keep the through movement, and you do not convert the intersection into an all-way stop. Cover the brake if the waiting driver starts into your lane. You are on the through road and may continue, while still watching in case that driver pulls out.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A yield sign faces you, and cross traffic is close enough that your entry would make those drivers brake. What should you do?
options: Slow or stop at the yield so their speed can stay steady
Enter if you think they can slow a little without a real stop
Enter and expect them to change lanes around you
Ignore the yield
questions.explanation: Yield means the other traffic does not have to brake or swerve for you. If the only way in is to force that change, you wait for a different gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You face a yield sign, you can see the crossing and the sidewalk are empty, and no one is approaching. What does the sign require right now?
options: Treat the yield as a green light that cancels any later conflict
You may continue without a full stop, at a speed that still lets you stop if someone appears
You must always stop and count before you enter, even when nothing is coming
You may accelerate through without being able to stop
questions.explanation: A yield sign is not a stop sign when the way is empty. It remains a duty to give way. You keep a speed that lets you stop at the line if a vehicle or a person appears.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to change lanes, and the car in that lane is even with your door. Your signal is on. Do you have the right-of-way to move over?
options: Yes. The signal requires that car to brake and let you in
Yes, if you drift toward them slowly enough that they notice
Yes. The car beside you must yield because you decided first
No. A signal asks for the lane. Wait until you are clearly ahead or drop back
questions.explanation: A turn signal does not grant a lane that another car is already occupying beside you. You move only when you are clear of that car, ahead or behind, after mirrors and a blind-spot check.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are clearly ahead of the car in the lane you want, your signal is on, and the blind spot is empty. What does that position allow?
options: You may change lanes
You must keep waiting
You should brake and fall back beside their door before you move
You may move over without signaling
questions.explanation: The other driver does not own space you have already cleared. A lane change is allowed when you are ahead, the signal is on, and the mirrors and blind spot show the gap. The signal still has to be used.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are merging from an acceleration lane onto a freeway, and freeway traffic is beside the ramp. Who has the right-of-way?
options: You should stop at the nose of the ramp whenever a car is anywhere in sight
Freeway traffic has the right-of-way
Ramp traffic has the right-of-way
Whichever driver honks owns the merge
questions.explanation: The ramp joins a road that is already moving. Freeway drivers have the right-of-way. Your job is to match their speed and use a gap, not to make them slow down for your entry.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A usable gap is opening in the freeway lane next to your acceleration lane. What is the right use of that gap?
options: Enter at a much lower speed and let the freeway driver close the gap
Use the shoulder beyond the gore if you dislike the gap's size
Match speed and move into the gap
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait even though the gap is there
questions.explanation: Stopping at the nose is not the plan when a gap exists. The acceleration lane is for matching speed. Take the gap that does not force freeway traffic to brake.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have used the acceleration lane and still see no gap that you can enter without forcing a freeway driver to brake. What should you do?
options: Force the merge and require the freeway lane to open
Stop at the beginning of a long acceleration lane and wait there
Cross the gore and enter downstream of the merge
Do not barge in
questions.explanation: Freeway traffic does not have to brake for you. If there is truly no gap, you do not invent one by cutting someone off. You keep looking and avoid making a habit of stopping at the nose when the lane still lets you match speed. Wait for a real gap rather than pushing into the lane; a stop at the nose is only a last resort.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A funeral procession marked with flags or lights is passing through the intersection you want to cross, where that procession is being kept together. What should you do?
options: Honk and turn through the line
Pass the procession on the shoulder and rejoin beyond it
Do not cut through the procession
Insert your car into a small gap so you are not delayed
questions.explanation: A gap in a marked procession is supposed to stay closed. Cutting through forces cars apart and into cross traffic. Wait for the procession to pass, and follow any officer who is directing it. Wait until it has passed, then go.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pedestrian is already walking across an unmarked intersection crosswalk in front of you. No lines are painted. What right-of-way applies?
options: Continue, because no paint means the pedestrian has no right-of-way
Pass on the right if part of the roadway is open
Honk so the pedestrian returns to the curb they left
Yield and let the pedestrian finish
questions.explanation: Ordinary intersections have crosswalks whether or not they are painted. A person already crossing has the right-of-way. Lack of paint is not a reason to take their path. The crossing exists even though it is not painted.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are turning left on a green ball, and the oncoming vehicle in the lane you must cross is a motorcycle with a rider close to the intersection. How do you treat that rider?
options: Yield, just as you would to a car
Turn because a motorcycle should yield to any left turn on a green ball
Turn in front of the motorcycle if you think it can brake harder than a car
Use the oncoming lane so the motorcycle can pass on your left
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a vehicle. A green ball still requires your left turn to yield to oncoming traffic, and a smaller vehicle is easier to misjudge, not easier to turn in front of. Wait until the motorcycle has passed before you turn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You and a bicyclist arrive at an all-way stop together. The rider is on your right and your paths cross. Who goes first?
options: Both of you go, with the bicycle using the crosswalk as a lane
The rider on your right goes first, the same as a driver on your right would
You go first
The rider must dismount and walk so you can take the tie
questions.explanation: A bicycle is a vehicle at the stop sign. The tie still goes to the road user on the right. The rider's size does not move that user to the back of the line.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: People are in a marked crosswalk and you are waiting to turn. One of them is moving slowly. What should you not do?
options: Inch forward so your bumper encourages a faster walk
Drive behind them inside the crosswalk lines
Do not honk or creep into the crosswalk
Honk in a steady tone until the crosswalk clears
questions.explanation: The crosswalk is their space while they are in it. Horn and bumper pressure do not transfer the right-of-way to your turn. You wait until they are clear, then go. Do not honk at them to hurry, and do not creep into the crosswalk while they finish.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are driving on a street, and a car is nosing out of a driveway toward your lane. Who has the right-of-way?
options: The driveway car goes first
You must stop in your lane whenever a driveway car appears
You should change lanes into oncoming traffic to make their entry easier
You do; driveway traffic must yield
questions.explanation: The road you are already on has priority over a driveway. You do not have to give the lane away, and you also do not aim at a driver who is failing to yield. Cover the brake.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A driver is edging out of an alley toward the sidewalk and the street you are traveling. What should that alley driver do, and what should you expect?
options: The alley driver must yield to the sidewalk and to you
Alley traffic has priority over both the sidewalk and the street
You must reverse so the alley can empty
The alley may enter first if its driver honks
questions.explanation: An alley is not a through road. Its driver yields to people and to street traffic. Your through movement continues, with enough attention to stop if they pull out anyway.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The signals at an intersection are dark, with no officer directing. What right-of-way pattern should you use?
options: Treat the dark signal as a green for the larger road only
Continue at speed
The driver who enters last has priority so the box does not empty
Treat it as an all-way stop
questions.explanation: A dark signal is handled as a stop on every approach. After stopping, the all-way order applies: first to arrive goes first, and a tie goes to the driver on the right.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An oncoming driver is already in the intersection turning left as your light turns green for a straight movement. What do you allow them to do?
options: Allow them to clear
Enter because a new green cancels any turn that started on the previous phase
Pass on the right of their turn through the crosswalk
Stop beside them and wait for the next cycle
questions.explanation: A vehicle already in the intersection may finish. Your new green is the next movement, not a license to meet them in the box. Wait, then go. Do not enter until that turn is out of your path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are leaving a stop sign for a right turn, and a pedestrian is approaching in the crosswalk from your left, about to enter your turn. What do you do?
options: Use the crosswalk as the start of your acceleration
Yield to that pedestrian before you complete the right turn
Turn in front of the pedestrian
Turn into the left lane of the new street to avoid the crosswalk
questions.explanation: Stopping at the sign satisfies the sign. It does not buy the crosswalk. If a person is about to use the crossing your turn needs, you yield and turn after they are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to turn left across a solid centerline area into a driveway, and an oncoming bicyclist is close. The signal is not what is controlling this mid-block turn. Who yields?
options: You both move, with the bicycle taking the shoulder at the last second
Honk and turn
You yield. The left turn waits until the oncoming bicyclist has passed
The bicyclist yields
questions.explanation: A left turn, including a mid-block turn into a driveway, yields to oncoming traffic. A bicycle in that oncoming lane is oncoming traffic. You wait for it to pass.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: One waiting driver flashes headlights as if offering you a gap out of a driveway, while other cars are still approaching in the lane you must cross. What should you do?
options: Go at once because one driver's flash assigns you the road
Enter and let the approaching cars solve the second half of the crossing
Stop in the first lane you reach and wait there
Do not take a gap that is not really there
questions.explanation: A single driver's courtesy does not cancel everyone else on the through road. You yield to the traffic that is actually coming, not only to the driver who flashed. Other through traffic still has the right-of-way.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You qualify for an HOV lane, but a solid white line separates you from it and the next opening is ahead. Does qualifying give you the right-of-way to cross now?
options: Yes. The lane's users must brake and open a gap wherever you choose
No. You enter only at the broken line or signed opening, not across the solid line
Yes. Meeting the occupancy rule lets you cross a solid line anywhere
Yes, if you signal for several seconds first
questions.explanation: Qualifying to use the lane is not a right-of-way to cross a solid line. The opening is part of the rule. You wait for the break, then move if the gap is safe.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A divided highway has a median, and an emergency vehicle with lights and a siren is approaching on your side from behind. Where do you pull over?
options: Stop in the left lane next to the median
Accelerate until you reach an exit, then decide
Pull to the right on your own roadway and stop
Cross the median so you leave the entire side of the highway empty
questions.explanation: You give the emergency vehicle your side of the road by pulling right and stopping. Crossing a median puts you into opposing traffic, which is a new crash rather than a clear path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A bystander on the sidewalk is gesturing for you to roll through the crosswalk, while the school crossing guard's paddle is still facing you. Whom do you obey?
options: Turn through the children
Obey the guard's paddle
Obey the bystander
Split the difference and creep while both are signaling
questions.explanation: The guard is the assigned traffic control. Another person's gesture does not give you the crosswalk. You wait until the guard, not the bystander, releases you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your green arrow is on for a left turn, and an oncoming driver is still finishing a movement that started before your arrow. What should you do with the protected turn?
options: Honk and turn into the space they have not left
Abandon the turn and go straight from the turn lane
Let that driver clear, then use the arrow
Take the arrow at once
questions.explanation: A green arrow holds new oncoming traffic. It does not erase a vehicle that is already in the intersection. You let them finish, check the crosswalk, and then turn. Protection does not mean you hit someone already in the box.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are going straight through an all-way stop, and the only other driver arrived with you from your left and also wants to go straight. Your paths cross. Who yields?
options: You yield because straight movements from the left go first
You both enter and turn slightly right to miss each other
The driver who stops farthest past the stop line goes first
The driver on your left yields
questions.explanation: This tie is the right-hand rule in its simplest form. Same arrival, crossing paths, and you are on the right. The left-side driver waits. You go after your stop, not before it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A channelized right-turn lane has a yield sign, and a pedestrian is in the crosswalk that crosses that channel. The main street looks busy behind you. What is the yield?
options: Yield to the pedestrian at the channel before you enter the street they are crossing
Take the turn
Stop in the crosswalk so you can see the street better
Treat the yield sign as applying only to cars on the road you are joining
questions.explanation: The yield at a channelized turn includes the person in its crosswalk, not only the cars on the street. Pressure from behind does not move the pedestrian out of the right-of-way.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have stopped at an all-way stop a moment later than the driver on your right. That driver is going straight across your straight path. What is your action?
options: Turn left from the stop so you do not have to yield
Wait for the driver on your right
Go first because two rules cannot apply to the same pair of cars
Go together and let the faster start win
questions.explanation: Both the arrival rule and the right-hand rule point the same way here. They were first and they are on your right. You have no basis to take the intersection before they do.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are at a four-way stop in a line of cars, you are first, and the pedestrian who started from the right curb is still in your half of the road. The car on your right arrived after you. What happens?
options: The pedestrian must return to the curb
Wait for the pedestrian, then go in turn
The later car on the right goes first
You and the later car go together around the pedestrian
questions.explanation: People who are already crossing are not rearranged behind a car that arrived later. You yield to the person, then you go before the car that came after you. The pedestrian finishes before you go, and the later car on your right does not jump ahead of that order.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A long acceleration lane is beside you, a gap is opening in the freeway lane, and your speed is still below the flow. How should you use the lane?
options: Merge at once from a slow speed and let the freeway lane brake
Drive past the gap and stop at the gore
Use the acceleration lane to match the freeway's speed, then move into the gap
Stop at the beginning of the acceleration lane and wait for a wave of empty pavement
questions.explanation: The acceleration lane exists so you can match speed before you join. A gap is useful only if you enter it at the flow of traffic. Stopping early or merging slowly pushes the yield onto drivers who already have the freeway.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have just left the meter and a long acceleration lane is still ahead of you. Freeway traffic is heavy but moving. Where should you gain speed?
options: Stop where the ramp straightens and wait for the freeway to empty
Enter the freeway immediately at ramp speed
Use the shoulder past the gore as your acceleration lane
Gain speed along the acceleration lane
questions.explanation: An acceleration lane is wasted if you stop at the top of it. You build speed on the lane you were given, then take a gap. The freeway does not owe you a full stop at the nose. Do not stop at the start of that lane when it still gives you room to match traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At the end of the acceleration lane a freeway car is beside your door and there is space behind that car. How should you merge?
options: Do not move into the car beside you
Move over now
Stop beside that car and wait at the gore
Swing onto the shoulder and pass the car before you merge
questions.explanation: Freeway traffic has the right-of-way, including the car already beside you. The end of the ramp is not a command for them to brake. You fit the gap that is actually open. Adjust to the gap behind that car instead of forcing the nose of the ramp.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are about to leave the acceleration lane for a gap you have matched. What checks belong with that move?
options: Change lanes inside the gore if the mirror looks busy
Signal, mirrors, and a blind-spot check
Move over on mirrors alone
Signal after you are already in the freeway lane
questions.explanation: Matching speed is only half of the merge. A car can sit in the blind spot the mirrors miss. Signal first, then mirrors and a shoulder check, then move if the gap is still there.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You realize the exit you wanted is the one you are passing, and you are still in a through lane. What is the correction?
options: Cut across the diagonal gore stripes to reach the ramp
Stop in the through lane and wait for a gap to back into the exit
Continue to the next exit
Stop and reverse on the freeway to the ramp you missed
questions.explanation: A missed exit is fixed at the next exit. Backing up or driving through the gore turns a small mistake into a high-speed conflict. The through lane stays a through lane. Do not back up, and do not cross the gore.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The striped gore for your exit is already beside you and you are in the through lane. Navigation is insisting that you leave. What do you do?
options: Stay in the through lane and take the next exit
Cross the stripes if you signal first
Stop on the gore and inch down it onto the ramp
Use two tires on the stripes so you are only partly in the gore
questions.explanation: Once the gore is beside you, the exit is gone. Diagonal stripes are not a lane. Crossing them puts you into the side of drivers who took the ramp correctly.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have passed the last broken line before an exit and a solid line plus the gore now separate you from the ramp. May you still change your mind?
options: Yes, if you stop first and then cross when the ramp looks clear
No. Do not cross the solid line or the gore. Continue and leave at a later exit
Yes, if you missed the decision by only a car length
Yes, because a solid line at an exit is only a guide
questions.explanation: The broken line was the decision zone. A solid line and the gore are the point of no return. A late change there is a sideswipe, not a merge.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have finished passing a slower car on a multi-lane freeway, and the lane to your right has room. Why should you leave the left lane?
options: Remain left because the left lane is the traveling lane on a freeway
Stop in the left lane while you decide whether the pass is finished
The left lane is for passing
Stay in the left lane so you do not have to pass anyone else later
questions.explanation: The left lane is a passing lane, not a place to cruise after the pass is over. Moving right opens it for the next passing driver and puts you back in the through flow. Once the pass is done, move right.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in the left lane of a freeway and you are not overtaking anyone. A line of cars is building behind you. What should you do?
options: Stay left and match the slowest speed you prefer
Move right without a signal or a blind-spot check
Brake in the left lane so the line behind you has to pass on the right
Move right when you can do it safely
questions.explanation: Camping in the left lane blocks the passing movement that lane is for. You move right when a safe gap exists, using a signal, mirrors, and a blind-spot check. You do not brake to make a point.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You need a lane change on the freeway to line up for an exit that is still well ahead. Traffic is moderate. What is the full check?
options: Rely on a quick mirror glance and skip the blind spot
Change lanes across a solid line if the exit is the next one
Signal, check mirrors and blind spot, then move
Drift over when the dashed line appears, without a signal
questions.explanation: A freeway lane change is the same disciplined move as any other: signal, mirrors, blind spot, gap. An upcoming exit is a reason to start early, not a reason to skip the check or cross a solid line.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want the next lane, and the only opening you see would take you across a striped gore. What is forbidden?
options: Use the gore as a short lane-change lane if you signal
Stop on the stripes until the next lane clears
Cross the gore
Do not change lanes through the gore
questions.explanation: A gore is not a lane, even when you are only using it to change lanes rather than to reach a ramp. Same-direction stripes are still closed pavement.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are following a large truck so closely that you cannot see its side mirrors. What does that tell you?
options: The truck is about to change lanes
The truck has a camera that shows you
The truck driver cannot see you
You are at a safe following distance
questions.explanation: If you cannot see the truck's side mirrors, the truck driver cannot see you. Drop back out of the blind spot (the No Zone).

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have been driving beside the left side of a long truck for some time instead of completing the pass. Why is that a problem?
options: Move closer to the trailer so you spend less time in the wind
The left side of a truck is a no-zone
The left side is the one place a truck can always see a car
Lingering on the left is required so the truck knows you are passing
questions.explanation: No-zones include both sides, not only the rear and the front. A long stay beside the trailer is time the truck driver may not see you. Complete the pass on the left or fall behind. Finish the pass or drop back; do not linger there.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The right side of a truck is open and you are tempted to cruise there because your exit is eventually on the right. What should you know?
options: Stay on the right for the whole exit so the truck can turn around you
The right-side no-zone applies only on city streets
The truck's right side is a no-zone
The right side is safe
questions.explanation: Both sides of a truck hide cars, and the right side is worse when the truck turns right and swings wide. Exit behind it or complete a pass, rather than living in that blind spot.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are close behind a truck in the same freeway lane and you cannot see the road beyond its trailer. What should change?
options: Move closer, because the rear of a truck is outside its no-zones
Pass on the right from that close position without a gap
Tailgate until the truck changes lanes for you
Drop back out of the rear no-zone so you can see past the truck and it can see you
questions.explanation: The rear of a truck is a no-zone, and a close follow also leaves you blind to the traffic the truck is reacting to. More space restores your view and the truck driver's view of you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A truck ahead in the lane to your left is starting a right turn or a right exit that will swing toward the lane you are in. Where should you not be?
options: Do not sit on the truck's right while it turns right
Accelerate along the truck's right side so you clear the turn first
Hold your position beside the trailer until the turn is over
Move into the space the trailer is swinging through
questions.explanation: A right-turning truck needs room to the right and often cannot see a car there. Sitting on its right is how cars get crushed against the turn. Fall back and let the truck use the space. Drop back and let the swing finish.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are already on the right of a truck that begins to move right toward an exit. A gap has opened behind the truck. What is the escape?
options: Move right onto the shoulder and pass the turning truck there
Drop back into the gap behind it
Speed up and shoot past on the right before the trailer swings
Brake and stop beside the drive wheels
questions.explanation: Once the truck starts right, the forward space on its right is closing. The gap behind it is the escape. Squeezing ahead bets that the trailer will not swing into you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are passing a truck on the left and you are only halfway along the trailer. The lane ahead of the truck is open. What should you do?
options: Cut right in front of the truck as soon as your mirror shows any part of it
Move right while your rear bumper is still beside the truck's cab
Finish the pass, then return when clear
Drop back to the middle of the trailer and match the truck's speed
questions.explanation: A pass beside a truck should be completed, not parked in the side no-zone. You return right only after you are far enough ahead that you are out of the front no-zone, not at the first glimpse of the cab. Finish passing on the left without lingering, then return right only when you are clear of the front no-zone.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your exit ramp leaves from the right and you are already fully in the exit lane. Where should you slow down?
options: Slow on the exit ramp
Brake hard in the through lane before you reach the exit lane
Slow in a through lane and then jump the gore into the ramp
Keep freeway speed all the way down a curving ramp
questions.explanation: Through lanes are for through speed. Once you are in the exit lane or on the ramp, that is where you decelerate to a speed the ramp can accept. Braking in the through lane surprises the drivers behind you. In the through lanes you have already left.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your car fails on the freeway and it will still roll. A right shoulder is available. Where do you stop, and what lights do you use?
options: Stop in a through lane if the shoulder looks dirty
Park on the gore between an exit and the through lane
Get as far onto the right shoulder as you can and turn on the hazard lights
Stop in the left lane and leave the hazard lights off so you do not confuse anyone
questions.explanation: A stop on a freeway belongs as far from moving lanes as the shoulder allows, with hazard lights on so approaching drivers can see you. A travel lane and a gore are not parking places.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have stopped correctly on the freeway shoulder and you need help. How should you and your passengers leave the vehicle?
options: Walk down the travel lane to the next exit for help
Stand behind the car in the lane so drivers will move over
Cross the freeway on foot to reach the opposite shoulder
Exit on the side away from traffic and do not walk on the travel lanes
questions.explanation: Hazard lights and a far shoulder still leave the travel lanes lethal. You get out away from traffic and you stay off those lanes. Help comes to you, or you use a path that is not the roadway.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The right shoulder is narrow because of a guardrail, and the car will not run. How far should you get the vehicle from the lanes?
options: As far onto the shoulder as it goes
Leave it in the right travel lane
Angle it across two lanes so it is more visible
Push it into the gore if an exit is nearby
questions.explanation: The rule is to get as far onto the shoulder as you can, not to occupy a lane because the shoulder is imperfect. Hazards stay on. You still do not walk in the travel lanes. As far onto the shoulder as it will go, hazard lights on, even if the remaining space is tight.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in an EXIT ONLY lane, the line on your left has become solid, and the gore has started. You did not want this exit. What now?
options: Take the exit
Cross the solid line
Stop and reverse to the last broken line
Drive through the gore and rejoin beyond it
questions.explanation: Once the line is solid and the gore has started, the lane is committed to the exit. Missing your preferred route is repaired at the next place you can re-enter, not by crossing closed pavement.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The exit ramp curves away and you are fully on it, still near freeway speed. Where do you lose that speed?
options: Stop on the ramp and then start again at the bottom
Lose it on the ramp, before the curve tightens
Return to the through lane and slow there
Brake only after you are already in the tightest part of the curve
questions.explanation: The ramp is the deceleration lane. You slow before the curve demands it. Going back to the freeway to slow down, or waiting until the curve has you, are both the wrong place to shed speed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You had to stop on the right shoulder and now the car will run again. How do you re-enter the freeway?
options: Pull straight into the travel lane from a stop without looking
Back up on the shoulder until you find a gap you like
Enter at a crawl and expect the lane to brake
Signal, build speed, and yield before joining
questions.explanation: The shoulder can be a short acceleration area. Freeway traffic still has the right-of-way. You build speed, signal, look, and take a gap. You do not reverse, and you do not enter from a dead stop in front of a live lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The meter has released you, and the freeway lane beside the remaining acceleration lane has no gap that you can take without a forced brake. What do you do?
options: Enter immediately because the meter assigned you the lane
Stop on the gore until a driver brakes
Cross two lanes at once from the nose of the ramp
Do not treat the green meter as the freeway's permission
questions.explanation: The meter spaces the ramp. It does not transfer right-of-way. After the release you still match speed and take a gap that freeway traffic does not have to surrender with a panic brake. Keep looking for a real gap instead of barging in.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A diamond lane runs along the freeway, and the sign says two or more occupants are required during the hours you are driving. You are alone. May you use it to pass?
options: No. During the posted hours you must meet the posted occupancy. Use a general lane
Yes, because a freeway diamond lane is a passing lane for any solo driver
Yes, if you enter across the solid buffer for only a moment
Yes, because the symbol itself is permission
questions.explanation: The diamond does not by itself let you in. The sign sets occupancy and hours. Alone, during the restricted hours, you stay in a lane you are allowed to use.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You meet the HOV occupancy rule, and a solid white buffer separates you from that lane until a broken opening ahead. Where do you enter?
options: Enter anywhere if you are faster than the HOV traffic
Enter at the broken opening, after a signal and a blind-spot check
Cross the solid buffer now
Drive on the striped buffer until the opening
questions.explanation: Qualifying for the lane and having a legal opening are both required. A solid buffer is not a place to cross, and the stripes are not a lane. Wait for the break.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your exit from the freeway is on the left, and you are still in the right lane with time and a broken line to move. What is the early choice?
options: Use the right shoulder to reach the left exit
Stop in the right lane and wait for the left lanes to empty
Move left one lane at a time, well before it
Stay right until the gore, then cross every lane at once
questions.explanation: A left exit is planned early. Each lane change gets a signal, mirrors, and a blind spot. A last-second slash across the gore is the move the markings are there to prevent.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A car is passing you on the left and is partly alongside. You had been about to move left. What should you do?
options: Accelerate so the pass takes longer
Move left because you signaled before they arrived
Brake hard so they pass you on the shoulder
Hold your lane and let the pass finish
questions.explanation: When you are the vehicle being passed, you do not defend the lane. Speeding up or moving over into the passer creates the conflict. Hold your lane until they are clear, then make your own move if you still need it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to pass a slower car and the lane to its left is open. The right shoulder is also empty. Which path is the pass?
options: Pass on the left, then move back right
Pass on the right shoulder
Pass on the left and stay in the left lane for the rest of the trip
Pass between the slower car and the shoulder stripe without a full lane
questions.explanation: The left lane is the passing lane. The shoulder is not. After the pass you return right instead of treating the left lane as a new cruising lane. Pass on the left in the open lane, using a signal and a blind-spot check, then move right when you are done.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A tire has failed while you are in a freeway through lane, and the car is still controllable. A right shoulder is a short distance ahead. What is the priority?
options: Get out and walk down the lane while the car rolls
Hold steady and ease onto that shoulder
Brake hard and stop in the through lane
Yank the wheel toward the shoulder
questions.explanation: A sudden yank or a stop in the lane is worse than a controlled move to the shoulder. You keep steering smooth, leave the travel lane as far as you can, use the hazards, and you do not walk on the lanes. Hold the wheel steady, ease toward that shoulder, and put the hazard lights on when you are as far off the lane as you can get.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An entrance and an exit share a short weave beside the freeway, and you are entering from the ramp. Through traffic is in the main lanes. What is your duty in the weave?
options: Stop in the weave until every freeway lane is empty
Enter the through lane at ramp speed and require a brake from the freeway
Use the gore in the middle of the weave as a waiting spot
Match speed and yield to freeway traffic
questions.explanation: A weave is still a freeway merge. Stopping in it stacks both the entrance and the exit, and freeway traffic keeps the right-of-way. You match speed and take a gap. Do not stop in the weave lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The HOV sign says the occupancy restriction is off at this hour and general traffic may use the lane. You are alone, and a broken opening is beside you with a gap. May you enter?
options: Yes. Drive on the buffer stripes until you feel settled in the lane
Yes, at that legal opening if the gap is safe
No. A diamond lane can never be used by a solo driver at any hour
Yes, but only by crossing the solid buffer instead of the opening
questions.explanation: Hours are part of the posted rule. When the sign says the restriction is not in effect, a solo driver may use the lane. The entry still has to be at a break in the line, with a real gap. Yes. Outside the restricted hours stated on the sign, you may enter at that legal opening if the gap is safe.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the right shoulder with its lights flashing, and the lane to your left has a safe gap. What should you do as you approach?
options: Stop in the travel lane next to the emergency vehicle
Pull onto the shoulder behind it and block the remaining shoulder
Move left without checking the blind spot
Change left into that gap if you can do it safely
questions.explanation: A stopped emergency vehicle needs space. If a lane change is safely available, take it with a signal and a blind-spot check. Stopping in the travel lane creates a second incident at freeway speed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The only gap in the freeway lane is behind the car that is now beside your front door on the acceleration lane. How do you use the rest of the lane?
options: Accelerate and cut in front of the car from the blind spot
Ease off enough to fall into the gap behind that car
Turn into the car's door
Brake to a stop at the gore and start from there
questions.explanation: A gap behind you is still a gap. A small speed adjustment on the acceleration lane lets you join behind the freeway car. Joining beside them, or stopping at the gore, ignores the lane you were given. Do not move over while you are still beside it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your mirror shows a gap for a freeway lane change, and a vehicle may be riding just behind your shoulder. What check settles that doubt?
options: Honk and move, using the horn as the blind-spot check
Change lanes first and look over your shoulder afterward
Look over your shoulder at the blind spot before you leave your lane
Move over if the inside mirror looks empty, without a shoulder check
questions.explanation: Freeway mirrors do not cover the quarter beside your rear door. The shoulder check is what finds a car the mirror missed. You look before the wheel turns, not after. Do not trust the mirror alone.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are fully on an exit ramp and you can see that you took the wrong exit. The freeway is running beside you beyond a gore. How do you get back?
options: Stay on the ramp and find another way back
Cross the gore back to the freeway if you signal
Stop on the ramp and reverse to the through lane
Drive the striped wedge between the ramp and the freeway
questions.explanation: A wrong exit is corrected off the freeway, not by re-entering through the gore. That wedge is closed pavement. Reversing on the ramp is the same class of mistake as backing up on the freeway.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are on the freeway in the right lane, and a truck on the entrance ramp is beside you, matching neither a gap ahead nor a gap behind. Who must solve that merge?
options: Accelerate into the truck's door so it cannot enter
The truck must find a gap
You must leave the freeway lane for the shoulder so the truck can enter
You must stop in the right lane
questions.explanation: Freeway traffic, including you, has the right-of-way over the ramp. A hard brake to rescue a late ramp entry is not required. You also do not steer into the truck. Hold a steady course.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are following a truck up a long freeway grade and you cannot see around it. The left lane is crowded. What following position is wrong?
options: The correct position is as close as possible so the grade does not separate you
Move alongside the trailer and stay there for the whole grade
Pass on the right shoulder while the truck is slow on the grade
Clinging in the truck's rear no-zone is wrong
