questions.explanation: A grade makes the rear no-zone more tempting and more dangerous, because you cannot see slowed traffic beyond the trailer. Space, not a close draft, is what gives you time to stop. Drop back until you can see past it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Wind from a passing truck is pushing your car as you travel beside its trailer. What is the lane decision?
options: Do not linger in that side no-zone
Match the trailer's speed and ride out the wind beside it
Move closer to the trailer so the wind has less leverage
Pass on the right from inside the wind blast
questions.explanation: Side no-zones and truck wind are the same neighborhood. Staying there makes both problems last. A completed pass or a drop-back puts you where the driver can see you and the push fades.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Two ramp lanes are separated by a solid white line as they reach the freeway, and you are in the right one wishing you were in the left. What is left to you?
options: Stop and trade places with the car on your left
Drive between the two ramp lanes on the paint
Stay in the right ramp lane and merge from it
Cross the solid line in the gore area
questions.explanation: A solid line at the end of a ramp means the lane choice is over. Crossing it puts you into the neighboring ramp lane at the worst point. Merge from the lane you have, then change on the freeway where the markings allow.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Construction barrels and a taper are closing the right lane, and the devices continue along a forbidden strip. Traffic is slow. May you drive beyond the barrels to save a place in line?
options: Yes. Barrels are suggestions when traffic is slow
Yes, if you put on the hazard lights first
Drive through the taper and re-enter at the front
No. Merge at the taper into an open lane
questions.explanation: Channelizing devices close the pavement they surround. Slow traffic does not reopen it. You stay in the open lane pattern and zipper at the taper instead of breaking the line of barrels. No. Do not drive through the barrels or the closed strip. Use the open lanes and take a turn at the taper.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Freeway traffic is congested, and the right shoulder is clear all the way to your exit. May you use that shoulder to get to the ramp?
options: Yes. A clear shoulder is a legal extra lane whenever speeds are low
Yes, if you use the hazard lights while you drive it
Yes, until you reach the gore, which you may also drive
No. The shoulder is not a travel lane and not a path around a jam to the exit
questions.explanation: Congestion does not convert the shoulder into a lane. Driving it to an exit mixes a stopped-car refuge with moving traffic and often ends in the gore. Stay in the travel lanes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A tire fails while you are in a middle freeway lane, the car is controllable, and you can reach the right shoulder by crossing one open lane. How do you get there?
options: Yank across two lanes at once
Leave the car in the middle lane and walk to the shoulder
Signal, check the blind spot, and ease across that lane to the shoulder
Stop in the middle lane and wait for a tow in place
questions.explanation: A controllable car belongs on the shoulder, not abandoned in a middle lane. You change lanes the normal way, smoothly, then get as far onto the shoulder as you can and use the hazards.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are re-entering from the shoulder and the gap you want is real, but it would leave you beside a car's rear door for a long time. What should you do instead?
options: Ride beside the rear door until the driver notices you
Enter halfway and straddle the shoulder line
Stop on the shoulder inside that blind spot
Take a gap that lets you fully enter and move clear
questions.explanation: A merge is finished only when you are in the lane and out of the other driver's blind spot. Hanging beside a door, on the freeway or from the shoulder, recreates the no-zone problem you just avoided.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are passing a truck and you can see you will be beside the trailer for several seconds. Both side no-zones matter. How should the pass be shaped?
options: Pass briskly and return when you see its front
Pause at the trailer's midpoint to let the wind settle
Pass on the right if the right no-zone looks shorter
Cut in as soon as your hood passes the truck's bumper
questions.explanation: Both sides of a truck are no-zones, so the time beside it should be short. The left side is the passing side. You re-enter in front only after the whole front of the truck is in your mirror, which means you have left the front no-zone.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You missed a left-side exit and you are now past its gore in a through lane. The next exit is a mile ahead on the right. What is the route correction?
options: Make a U-turn through the median opening
Continue to that next exit
Cross the left gore backward onto the ramp
Stop in the left lane and back up to the exit
questions.explanation: Left exits and right exits share the missed-exit rule. You go forward to the next one. The gore, a reverse, and a median turn are all closed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in the left of two exit lanes, and a solid white line now separates you from the right exit lane that your ramp split requires. The split is at the gore. What should you do?
options: Cross the solid line in the gore to reach the other ramp
Stop between the exit lanes and change after the gore
Use the striped wedge to move from one ramp to the other
Stay in the left exit lane and take the path it serves
questions.explanation: Exit-lane choice ends when the line becomes solid. The gore is the wrong place to correct it. Follow the lane you are in and return another way if it was not the ramp you wanted.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are already inside a queued exit lane, separated from the through lanes by a solid line. The queue is moving slowly onto the ramp. What should you do?
options: Leave the queue by driving through the gore
Stay in the exit lane and creep with that queue
Cross the solid line back to the freeway
Reverse down the exit lane to the last broken line
questions.explanation: Once you are committed to the exit lane, you leave on that lane even if it is slow. Returning across a solid line or the gore puts you into freeway traffic that is still moving.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Every through lane is crowded and moving at the same slow speed, and you are not overtaking anyone in the left lane. Which lane should you favor?
options: Move right when you safely can
Stay left because slow traffic cancels the passing-lane rule
Weave from lane to lane for any one-car advantage
Use the left shoulder to get ahead of the equal speeds
questions.explanation: Equal slow speeds are not a pass. If you are not overtaking, the left lane is the wrong place to cruise. You move right without endless weaving, and you leave the shoulder alone. The left lane remains the passing lane even when the whole freeway is slow.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Small gaps keep appearing in the lanes beside you, each one worth about a car length of progress. What freeway habit should you reject?
options: Use the shoulder between weaves
Reject continuous weaving for tiny gains
Change lanes at every gap so you are always in the fastest momentary lane
Weave without signaling if each change is short
questions.explanation: Lane changes are for a purpose, and each one needs a signal and a blind-spot check. Hopping for a car length multiplies the chances to miss a car beside you. Hold a lane when the speeds are nearly the same. Change lanes only for a real pass, an exit, or another genuine need.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with lights and a siren is coming up behind you on the freeway. A right shoulder is available. Where do you go?
options: Follow it down the shoulder after it passes
Accelerate in the left lane until it can go around you on the right
Move to the right and stop on the shoulder until it passes
Stop in the left lane so the emergency vehicle can use the right lane
questions.explanation: On a freeway the pull-right-and-stop rule uses the shoulder when there is one. Stopping in a through lane, especially the left lane, leaves you in the path you were supposed to clear. Do not chase the emergency vehicle afterward.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The emergency vehicle has passed and is well ahead. You are stopped on the shoulder. How do you resume?
options: Pull into the lane from a stop
Drive the shoulder until you catch the emergency vehicle
Back up to a wider part of the shoulder before you enter
Signal, build speed on the shoulder, and yield into a gap
questions.explanation: After you pull over, re-entry is an ordinary yield to freeway traffic. You accelerate on the shoulder and take a gap. You do not launch from a stop, follow the emergency vehicle, or reverse. The emergency vehicle's passing did not give you the travel lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You do not meet the posted HOV occupancy, and the restricted hours are in effect. The general lanes are slower than the diamond lane. What is the legal pass?
options: Pass in a general lane you are allowed to use
Enter the HOV lane for the length of the pass only
Enter the HOV lane
Drive the buffer until the general lanes speed up
questions.explanation: A faster restricted lane is not a passing lane for a driver who does not qualify. Hours and occupancy still apply. You pass, if you pass, in a lane the sign allows you to use. Do not enter the HOV lane as a shortcut.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in a freeway through lane, and a driver is entering from a ramp into a gap ahead of you that they can reach without forcing you to brake. What should you avoid doing?
options: Move onto the shoulder to forbid the merge
Avoid accelerating just to close that gap
Accelerate so they have to brake back onto the ramp
Stop so they can enter sideways across your bumper
questions.explanation: You do not have to brake for ramp traffic, and you also should not speed up solely to punish a merge that fits a gap. Holding speed lets a safe gap work. Closing it on purpose creates the conflict. Your right-of-way does not require you to shut a gap they can use safely.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your exit is two miles ahead on the right, you are in the left lane, and a broken line plus a gap let you move right now. Why move early?
options: Stay left until the exit gore, then cross all the lanes
Move right across a solid line if you start the signal now
Wait in the left lane and stop when you see the exit sign
Move right early, one safe lane change at a time
questions.explanation: Early lane changes are how exits stay smooth. Each one still gets a signal and a blind-spot check. Saving every change for the gore is how drivers end up crossing closed pavement. You are not forced into a last-second dive at the exit.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in the exit lane, the ramp is clear, and drivers behind you in that lane are close. Where do you reduce speed?
options: Reduce speed on the ramp itself, smoothly, after you are out of the through lanes
Brake sharply while your rear wheels are still in the through lane
Keep through-lane speed until the ramp curve starts to break the tires loose
Stop at the top of the ramp as a habit before you look
questions.explanation: The exit lane and the ramp are where speed comes off. A sharp brake that begins in the through lane hits the drivers who are not exiting. A late brake on the curve is the other mistake.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A slower vehicle is in the middle lane, the left lane is open, and you intend to pass one vehicle and return. What is the complete passing sequence?
options: Pass without a signal
Signal, check, pass on the left, then return
Pass on the left and remain in the left lane afterward for convenience
Pass on the right shoulder and return in front of the vehicle
questions.explanation: A freeway pass is a pair of lane changes: out and back. Both need a signal and a look. Staying left after one vehicle, or using the shoulder, violates the passing-lane and shoulder rules. Signal left, check the blind spot, pass on the left, then signal right and return once you are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Fog is thinning, the freeway is moving, and you are in the left lane behind a vehicle you are not gaining on. A right-lane gap is available. What lane belongs to you?
options: The left lane
Either shoulder, because fog changes lane rules
The left lane until the vehicle ahead exceeds your preferred speed
The right lane
questions.explanation: Visibility does not turn the left lane into a cruising lane. If you are not overtaking, you move right into the gap. You still signal and check the blind spot before you go. Move there when the gap allows, because you are not passing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are on the acceleration lane, a freeway driver is beside your rear quarter, and another gap is opening ahead of that driver if you accelerate smoothly. What is the better gap?
options: Pull in beside the driver's quarter panel
Leave the acceleration lane across the gore to reach the forward gap
Ease into the gap ahead without cutting off
Stop and let both gaps go by
questions.explanation: Acceleration lanes are for acceleration. If a forward gap can be reached by matching speed, that is the merge. Stopping, riding in the blind spot, or cutting the gore are the three ways to waste the lane. Do not brake to a stop. Accelerate smoothly toward the gap ahead if you can enter it without cutting the driver off.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You took the wrong fork of a freeway split and the two routes are now separated by a gore you have already passed. How do you recover the route?
options: Cross the gore back to the other fork
Stop and reverse to the decision point
Use a median turnaround meant for emergency vehicles
Continue on the fork you have and leave at the next exit
questions.explanation: A wrong fork is the same problem as a missed exit. Forward to the next exit is the correction. The gore you passed is behind you for a reason: it is not a place to change your mind. Do not cross the gore or reverse to the split.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Night has fallen, the exit you wanted is behind you, and traffic ahead is light. Does darkness change the missed-exit rule?
options: No. Go to the next exit. Darkness does not allow backing up or crossing the gore
Yes. At night you may reverse with the hazard lights on
Yes. A quiet freeway lets you use the gore
Yes. You may turn around on the shoulder if you see no headlights
questions.explanation: Light traffic and darkness make a wrong-way or reverse movement harder to see, not more legal. The next exit still works, and the gore is still closed pavement.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are merging from the acceleration lane and a car is in your blind spot on the freeway side. Another gap is forming behind that car if you ease off slightly. What is the decision?
options: Stop at the nose with the blind-spot car beside you
Leave the ramp across the gore in front of that car
Ease off and merge into the gap behind it
Merge now and let the blind-spot car brake
questions.explanation: A blind-spot car is not a gap. The acceleration lane still lets you adjust backward into space the car is not using. Merging into the blind spot is the crash the shoulder check is meant to prevent. Do not merge while it is beside you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The right lane will become an exit-only lane at the next sign, you want the freeway, and you are beside a gap in the lane to your left with a broken line under your wheels. What do you do with that information?
options: Wait until the EXIT ONLY arrow is under the car, then leave across a solid line
Continue and use the gore as the last opening
Stop in the future exit lane to force a gap later
Take the left gap now so you are not still in the lane when it becomes exit only
questions.explanation: The useful message of an upcoming exit-only lane is to leave it early. A broken line and a gap are the opening. Arrows, solid lines, and gores are what you see if you ignored that opening.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A truck is in the right lane, you are behind it in the same lane, and your exit is the next ramp, which the truck may also be taking. Where should you avoid arriving as the ramp starts?
options: Stay out of its right side and front no-zone
Pull up on the truck's right so you reach the ramp first
Cut in front of the truck at the ramp nose
Pass the truck on the ramp shoulder
questions.explanation: Exit ramps are where trucks swing and where the right-side and front no-zones get small. If you cannot finish a pass on the left with room to spare, you follow the truck down the ramp instead of sitting where it turns. Stay back and exit behind it if you cannot complete a left pass in time.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have a clear left lane, you are not preparing for an upcoming exit, and a slow line occupies the right lane. What is the lawful way to get ahead of that line?
options: Weave into every small hole inside the slow line
Pass on the left, then return right
Pass the line on the right shoulder
Stay left after the line is behind you
questions.explanation: The left lane is there so a slow line can be passed. The shoulder is not. When the line is behind you, you return right instead of converting the passing lane into your permanent lane. Pass the line on the left, then move right once you are past it and a gap lets you return.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Flashing red lights start at a crossing just as you reach the stop line, and you still do not see a train. What should you do?
options: Stop on the rails so you can see farther down the line
Go around the signal post by using the shoulder
Stop at the line until the tracks are clear
Roll through if no locomotive is visible yet
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mean stop even before a train is visible, because a train can be closer than it looks and a second train may follow. Stop at the line and wait until the lights are out and the tracks are clearly empty.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A crossing gate is already down when you arrive, and the red lights are flashing. What is required of you?
options: Slip around the gate if the track looks empty right now
Nudge the gate with the bumper until the arm rises
Cross after one horn blast even though the arm is down
Stop and remain stopped
questions.explanation: A down gate with flashing lights closes the crossing, because a train you cannot see yet, or a second train, may be about to use the rails. Never drive around a lowered gate.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You stopped for a train, the gate began to rise, and the lights started flashing again before you moved. What should you do?
options: Stay stopped until the lights go off
Accelerate while the gate is still only partly up
Treat the second flash as a glitch and go at once
Pull onto the tracks and wait there for the cycle to end
questions.explanation: If the lights start again before you move, you wait, because another train may be coming on a second track. Stay where you are until the lights stop and you can see that the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: After the first train passes, freight cars still block your view of a parallel track and the lights are flashing. What should you do?
options: Follow the car that is weaving past the gate arm
Wait until you see the second track is clear
Cross the moment the first train clears your hood
Drive between the two tracks and pause there to look
questions.explanation: A second train may be hidden behind the first, so you do not start until the lights are out, the gate is up, and every track is clear. Wait until you can see the second track is empty and the lights have stopped.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A crossbuck is the only control at this crossing, with no lights, no gate, and no stop sign. What does it require?
options: Ignore it unless a gate is also installed at the site
Treat it as a milepost and hold your approach speed
Yield to any train
Stop with your car sitting on the rails and then look
questions.explanation: A crossbuck marks a grade crossing and means yield to trains, because the lack of lights does not close the railroad. The crossing is real even though it has no flashing lights.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A stop sign is mounted beside the crossbuck at a rural crossing, and no train is visible. What should you do?
options: Roll through because the railroad lights are dark
Stop with your car sitting across the rails
Treat the stop sign as something only a bus must obey
Stop fully, look both ways, then cross
questions.explanation: A posted stop sign still requires a full stop, and after that stop you yield to trains and move only when you can clear the far side. Come to a full stop at the line, look both ways, and go only when you can clear the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Cars are backed up on the far side of the tracks, and there is no gap big enough for your car. What should you do?
options: Wait before the crossing until the far side has room for your whole vehicle
Enter and stop on the tracks so you keep your place in line
Block the crossing halfway and inch forward with the queue
Use the opposing lane across the rails to skip the queue
questions.explanation: Never start across unless you can clear the far side completely, because a car stopped on the tracks cannot escape an approaching train.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You see a round yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR well before the rails. The crossing ahead looks empty. What should you do?
options: Speed up so you spend less time near the crossing
Slow down and be ready to stop
Stop beside the yellow sign and wait there for a train
Ignore the sign until your tires are already on the rails
questions.explanation: The circular yellow sign is an advance warning, so you slow and prepare to stop, but you do not stop at the sign itself when the uncontrolled crossing is empty.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The letters RXR are painted in your lane ahead of a grade crossing. How should you respond to that marking?
options: Read the letters as a county route number
Change lanes after you are already on the rails
Recognize that the crossing is ahead, reduce speed, and be prepared to stop
Stop on the painted letters every time, even far from the rails
questions.explanation: RXR pavement markings warn that the rails are close. They tell you to slow and be ready to stop; they are not a command to stop on the paint when nothing is coming.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A gate has stayed down, the lights are dark, and several minutes have passed with no train in sight. What should you do?
options: Zigzag through the gate arms
Lift the arm by hand and then drive through
Duck under the arm if the car roof looks low enough
Wait or take another route
questions.explanation: A gate that seems stuck is not permission to drive around it, because a train may still be coming. You wait, reroute, or follow posted instructions.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are driving a passenger car behind a school bus that stops at a dark railroad crossing. What should you do?
options: Wait behind the bus
Pass the bus over the rails
Ignore both the bus and the crossbuck and keep going
Pull beside the bus and stop with your car on the tracks
questions.explanation: Buses sometimes must stop when a car might not, but that extra rule does not let you pass them on the crossing or drive onto the rails. Do not swing around it and onto the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Railroad lights are flashing, and someone says passenger cars may go because only buses must stop. What should you do?
options: Stop on the tracks to show you considered the advice
Stop; the lights apply to your car too
Go around the gate
Follow that advice and cross while the lights still flash
questions.explanation: Extra stop rules for buses and trucks do not exempt a car when the red lights flash or a gate is down. Those devices stop every driver.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A painted stop line sits before the crossing gate, and the red lights begin to flash. Where should your car stop?
options: In the opposing lane beside the gate housing
At the stop line, short of the gate
Past the line, with the bumper under the gate arm
On the near rail so you can see farther down the track
questions.explanation: The stop line is the safe waiting place. Stopping beyond it can put you into the gate or the train, so you wait there until the crossing is released and clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: At night you hear a train horn near a crossbuck, but the crossing has no lights of its own. What should you do?
options: Drive onto the rails and then look for the headlight
Turn around on the tracks to get away from the horn
Slow, look both directions, and be ready to stop
Keep speed because an unlit crossing is out of service
questions.explanation: A crossbuck crossing is live even without flashing lights. A horn means you should slow, look, and stop if you cannot clear before the train.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A stopped freight train is blocking the crossing and the gates remain down. What should you do?
options: Use the shoulder to slip past the end of the train
Drive through if two rail cars separate enough to make a gap
Follow any car that is already going around the lowered gate
Wait until the train moves and the gates rise
questions.explanation: A train on the crossing with the gates down still owns the road. Going around it or between cars can put you in front of equipment that starts to move.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You notice a blue emergency-notification placard with a crossing identifier and a phone number. What is that placard for?
options: Reporting a stall, a track blockage, or trouble with the warning devices
Asking permission to ignore flashing red lights
Marking a scenic spur you are welcome to drive along
Telling passenger cars they are excused from the crossbuck
questions.explanation: The emergency notification sign is how you reach the railroad quickly if a vehicle is stuck, the crossing is blocked, or the lights or gates are damaged.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A train is visible far down a straight track at a crossbuck-only crossing, and you think you can beat it. What should you do?
options: Straddle the rails while you decide whether to finish
Stop and let the train pass
Accelerate because the train still looks distant
Cross if a passenger agrees you can make the gap
questions.explanation: Trains are faster and closer than they appear and cannot swerve, so yielding at the crossbuck means waiting rather than racing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Several lanes approach a crossing, the lights are flashing, and the lane beside you has already stopped. What should you do?
options: Use the right shoulder to get around the line and the gate
Change lanes on the tracks and then brake
Stop in your own lane and wait
Pass those cars and cross while the lights still flash
questions.explanation: Every lane must stop for flashing railroad lights, because passing cars that have already stopped drives you into the path the signals are protecting. Do not pass the stopped traffic to reach the rails.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A police officer at the crossing directs you to stop even though the gate is fully raised. What should you do?
options: Go, because a raised gate always cancels an officer
Drive around both the officer and the crossbuck
Stop on the rails until the officer walks away
Stop and follow the officer
questions.explanation: A police officer directing traffic controls your movement. An open gate does not make it safe to disobey a stop direction at the crossing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to turn left just past a crossing, but the space between the rails and the queue is shorter than your car. What should you do?
options: Use the oncoming lane on the tracks to jump the line
Wait until you can clear the tracks
Stop on the tracks while you wait for a gap to turn
Shift gears on the rails during the turn
questions.explanation: Short storage past the rails is not usable space. You start across only when the far side can hold your whole vehicle through the move you need to make. Wait until you can cross and complete the turn without stopping on the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The gate on your side is down, while the gate facing oncoming traffic is still up. What should you do?
options: Drive down the centerline between the two gate arms
Loop on the tracks and head back the other way
Stop for the gate on your side
Cross in the opposing lanes
questions.explanation: A lowered gate closes your approach. Using the other direction is still driving around a gate, and the train may already be entering the crossing. Stop for the gate on your side and do not use the opposing lanes to go around it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The lights have gone out, the gate is fully up, both tracks look empty, and the far side has room. What may you do?
options: Wait for a railroad employee to walk the lane and escort you
Cross only by driving around the raised gate arm
Stay until you have watched two trains go by
Cross, since you can clear the far side
questions.explanation: You are released when the lights are out, the gate is up, and the tracks look clear, and you still go only if the whole vehicle will fit beyond the rails.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: This rural crossing has a crossbuck and nothing else, and you have never seen a train here. How should you treat it today?
options: Approach ready to yield
Skip looking because this route has always seemed empty
Stop on the tracks as a ritual even when you can see they are clear
Treat a quiet history as a reason to add speed
questions.explanation: Familiarity does not close a railroad. A crossbuck means yield to trains every time, even at a crossing that usually looks quiet.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A plaque under the crossbuck says two tracks are present, and a train has just cleared the nearer one. What should you do?
options: Stop between the two tracks to study the far one
Check the farther track and any lights before you move
Go as soon as the near track looks empty
Watch only the rail closest to your front bumper
questions.explanation: A multiple-track plaque warns that a second train can approach on another track, so you wait until every track is clear and the lights have stopped.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Stored rail cars on a siding block your view down the tracks at a crossbuck crossing. What should you do?
options: Stop on the rails at the spot where the view finally opens
Assume the crossing is abandoned
Slow, look until you can see, then cross
Hold speed because parked rail cars cannot be a hazard
questions.explanation: A blocked view is a reason to approach slowly and be ready to stop. You cross only after you can see the tracks are clear and the far side has room. Slow enough to stop, look until you can see, and cross only when the route is clear and you can finish.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your traffic signal turns green at the same moment the railroad lights begin to flash. Which control do you obey?
options: The green signal, and drive onto the tracks
Neither one; stop squarely on the rails and wait
The green signal, if the gate has not started down yet
The railroad lights
questions.explanation: Flashing railroad lights override a green traffic signal, because the green light does not let you enter a crossing the railroad has closed. Stay stopped until they quit and the tracks look clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The gate arm is broken and hanging beside the road, but the red lights are still flashing. What should you do?
options: Stop until the lights go out and it is clear
Go, because a damaged arm cancels the flashing lights
Drive around the broken arm without stopping
Stop on the tracks while you look for someone to tell
questions.explanation: A damaged gate does not turn flashing red lights into a suggestion. You stop, you do not drive around the equipment, and you wait until the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A passenger asks why you are still waiting when the lights flash and no train has appeared. What is the sound reason?
options: Passenger cars may go whenever the track looks empty
A train may be out of sight, and another train can come on a second track
The lights are only scenery unless a locomotive is already in view
A short wait always cancels railroad red lights
questions.explanation: You wait because the warning can start before you can see the train, and leaving early can put you in front of that train or a second one.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The only way to finish a pass of a slow car would put you on the railroad crossing. What should you do?
options: Pass on the shoulder through the crossing
Straddle the center line on the tracks to get by
Drop back and wait
Finish the pass on the rails if you see no train
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing is a place where you need your own lane. A pass that ends on the tracks can leave you stuck in front of a train.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are still a short distance from the rails when you pass the circular yellow railroad warning. What should you do right then?
options: Make a full stop at the circular sign every time
Treat the sign as the place to shift gears on the rails
Ignore it because only a gate is a real warning
Begin slowing and prepare to stop nearer the crossing if you need to
questions.explanation: Advance warning signs are placed before the crossing so you can slow down. The sign itself is not a stop line when the crossing ahead is empty and uncontrolled.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: There is room beyond the tracks, the lights are dark, and a train is approaching a crossbuck crossing quickly. What should you do?
options: Yield and wait for the train
Go if the train has not yet reached the edge of the pavement
Cross and stop just past the rails to watch it pass
Drop a gear and race the train to the far side
questions.explanation: Room on the far side is not enough if the train will reach you first. At a crossbuck you yield whenever you might not clear in time. Yield and wait if you are not sure you can clear completely before the train arrives.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The lights never went dark between two trains coming from opposite directions. What should you do?
options: Shoot the gap you think you see between the two trains
Go as soon as the first train's last car passes your bumper
Turn onto the tracks and drive away from both trains
Keep waiting until the lights stop and both tracks are empty
questions.explanation: Lights that stay on mean the crossing is still in use. A second train is a common reason, so you wait until every track is visibly clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You creep forward after a gate rises, then see that stopping would leave your car on the rails behind a stopped car. What should you do?
options: Stop before the rails if you still can, and do not sit on the tracks
Enter and hope the car ahead moves before a train comes
Stop on the tracks and shift into park
Use the shoulder across the rails to pass that car
questions.explanation: If the far side cannot hold your car, you do not enter, because a vehicle on the tracks cannot clear if the lights come back on.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Fog hides the distance down the tracks beyond a crossbuck, and no signals are installed. What should you do?
options: Follow the taillights ahead even if they halt on the crossing
Slow, listen, and cross only when sure
Hold your speed so you spend less time in the fog on the rails
Stop on the tracks where the fog looks thinner
questions.explanation: Fog shortens your view but does not cancel the crossbuck. You approach slowly enough to stop, and you enter only when you can clear the far side. Slow down, listen, and cross only when you are sure no train is near and you can finish.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Both an early RXR pavement legend and a stop line are visible, and the crossing lights begin to flash. Where do you stop?
options: On the RXR letters even though the rails are still well ahead
On top of the nearest rail
Beside the circular warning sign you already passed
At the stop line nearer the rails
questions.explanation: The painted RXR is an early warning. When the lights flash, the stop line is the place to wait, well short of the rails. On the advance pavement letters.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: This city crossing has flashing red lights but no gates, and the lights are on. What should you do?
options: Stop until the lights quit
Slow and roll through
Stop only if the locomotive is already in sight
Go if a traffic light beyond the tracks is green
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are a stop even when the crossing has no gates, because the train may not be visible yet. Stop and remain stopped until the lights quit and the tracks look clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Traffic is crawling, and entering the crossing now would leave you stopped on the tracks at the far red signal. What should you do?
options: Shift gears on the tracks while the far signal is red
Wait behind the line until there is room
Follow the car ahead onto the tracks and wait there
Block the crossing so the drivers behind you can close ranks
questions.explanation: A gap you cannot finish is not a reason to enter. A car left on the tracks sits in the path of the next train the signals release. Stay behind the stop line until there is room for your whole car beyond the rails.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An ambulance with lights and a siren is behind you as you reach flashing railroad lights. What should you do?
options: Go around the gate
Stop on the rails and let the ambulance go around you
Stop short of the tracks
Drive onto the tracks so the ambulance can get past you
questions.explanation: Railroad flashing lights still close the crossing. Moving onto the tracks to yield to an ambulance can put both of you in front of a train. Stop short of the tracks for the railroad lights, and do not pull onto the rails to make room.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The crossbuck is faded and slightly twisted, but the rails still cross the pavement. What should you do?
options: Treat the crossing as active and yield to any train
Ignore the sign
Stop on the rails to see whether they shine from use
Cross in the opposing lane at a sharper angle
questions.explanation: If the rails still cross the road, the crossing exists. A weathered crossbuck still means yield, so you look and go only when you can clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: While you wait at a lowered gate, the car beside you drives around the arm. What should you do?
options: Back into the cross street and then sprint the tracks
Stay stopped
Follow the car around the gate so you are not delayed
Go around on the opposite side of the same arm
questions.explanation: Never drive around a lowered gate, even if another driver does, because that driver may be heading toward a train you have not seen. Stay stopped; that driver's choice does not open the crossing for you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are running late as you pass the round yellow railroad warning, with the rails still ahead. What should you do?
options: Stop at the yellow warning sign and wait there for a train
Treat lateness as an exception to the advance warning
Ease off and be ready to stop
Add speed so you reach the rails before any lights can start
questions.explanation: Being in a hurry does not change the advance warning. You slow and prepare to stop, and you do not make a required stop at the warning sign itself. Ease off now and be ready to stop if the crossing is active or a train is coming.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A quiet-zone notice tells you trains may not routinely sound the horn at this city crossing. How should that change your approach?
options: Do not listen for a horn as your only warning
Assume no routine horn means no trains use this crossing
Cross whenever the area is quiet, even if the lights flash
Stop on the tracks so you can hear a distant engine
questions.explanation: A quiet zone limits routine horn use. It does not close the railroad, so you still stop when the lights flash or the gate comes down.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are towing a small utility trailer behind your passenger car as you approach the tracks. What must you confirm before you start across?
options: That a short trailer lets you drive around a lowered gate
That car and trailer both clear the far side
That only the car's front bumper clears
That you can shift gears while the trailer is on the tracks
questions.explanation: The whole combination must clear, not just the tow vehicle. If the trailer would still be on the rails, you wait for more room. That the car and the trailer together can clear the far side without stopping on the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The crossing is on a hill, and entering now would leave you stopped partway up with the car on the tracks. What should you do?
options: Shift gears halfway across the hill while you are on the tracks
Back down the rails if the climb feels steep
Wait on the near side until you can climb all the way clear in one move
Start up and stop on the rails if the car ahead slows
questions.explanation: A hill does not change the clearance rule. You start across only when you can reach the far side without a stop or a shift on the rails.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are already on the tracks when the railroad lights begin to flash. What should you do?
options: Keep going and clear the far side
Stop at once even though the car is sitting on the rails
Back up along the rails toward the lowering gate
Shift into neutral and wait on the crossing
questions.explanation: Once you are on the crossing, stopping is the danger. You continue until you are completely clear of the rails. Do not stop on the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The gate is lowering toward your hood as you approach the stop line. What should you do?
options: Swerve into the opposing lane and cross there
Stop at the line and wait
Accelerate and slip under the arm before it drops
Hit the gate so it cannot come down on the roof
questions.explanation: A gate that is coming down means the crossing is closing now, so you stop short and wait until the lights are out, the gate is up, and the tracks are clear. Do not try to beat the lowering gate.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: No stop sign is posted, the lights are dark, the gate is up, and you can see a long empty single track with room beyond. What should you do?
options: Drive around the raised gate as a formality
Ignore the crossbuck
Cross, still looking until you are through
Stop on the rails to prove the track is empty
questions.explanation: When an uncontrolled crossing is empty and you can clear it, you do not stop at the advance warning. You still look, and you go only because the tracks are clear. Cross without stopping at the advance sign, still looking until you are through.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A train is approaching from your right at a signed two-track crossing, and the lights are flashing. What should you do about the left-hand track?
options: Cross after the right-hand train passes even if the lights stay on
Stop between the two tracks so you are closer to the exit
Watch only the train you can see and ignore the other rails
Wait through the whole warning
questions.explanation: Flashing lights cover the whole crossing, not just the train you happen to see. You stay back until the lights are out and every track is clear. The other track may still be used by a second train.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to turn right immediately after the tracks, but the turn lane beyond the rails is full. What should you do?
options: Hold short of the crossing until that turn lane has room for your whole car
Stop on the tracks while you wait to enter the turn lane
Enter the crossing and inch through the turn from the rails
Use the shoulder on the far rail as your waiting spot
questions.explanation: A full lane beyond the tracks means you cannot clear the far side, so you wait before the crossing instead of stopping on the rails.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The pavement marking before the crossing includes a large X, and a train horn sounds as you reach it. What should you do?
options: Treat the X as a school crossing and scan only for children
Be ready to stop short of the rails and yield to the train you hear
Stop on the painted X even when it is far from the rails and no train is near
Speed across so the horn is behind you
questions.explanation: The X marking is an advance warning on the pavement. A horn means a train may be close, so you slow and stop short of the rails if you cannot clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You see tracks embedded in the street ahead of a crossbuck. Your signal is green, the railroad lights are dark, and no train is near. What should you do?
options: Treat the embedded rails as a harmless groove you may stop on at will
Shift gears while you are stopped on those embedded rails
Proceed on the green only if you will not have to stop with the car sitting on the rails
Stop on the street tracks and hold there through the whole green light
questions.explanation: Street tracks are still tracks. A green light lets you go only when you can clear them, and the rails are not a place you choose to stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Another driver says the flashing lights have misfired all week, so you should go around the lowered gate. What should you do?
options: Go around the gate
Zigzag between the arms if you are impatient
Follow that driver around the gate
Refuse and keep waiting
questions.explanation: Even if a gate seems faulty, you do not go around it. You wait, pick another route, or follow posted instructions, because a train may still be coming.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You approach a crossing where the gate is down, the lights are flashing, and people are waiting on the sidewalk too. What should you do?
options: Honk so someone on the sidewalk will tell you when to sprint
Stop your car and keep the crossing closed to you
Inch forward through the gate
Use the sidewalk opening to drive around the arm
questions.explanation: A lowered gate and flashing lights stop your car whether or not people are waiting nearby. You stay back until the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A side-road turn puts a crossbuck directly in the path you are about to take. How should you finish that turn?
options: Whip through the turn
Shift gears as your wheels meet the rails
Turn only if you will not stop on the tracks
Turn and stop on the rails while you look both ways
questions.explanation: A crossing just beyond a turn still requires a clear far side. You do not commit if the turn would leave you stopped or shifting on the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are on a one-way street that crosses the railroad, and the red lights facing you begin to flash. What should you do?
options: Stop; a one-way street does not exempt you from flashing railroad lights
Go, because one-way streets are excused from railroad gates
Stop on the tracks so one-way traffic can sort itself out
Use the sidewalk to bypass the flashing lights
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights apply on a one-way street the same way. You stop short and wait until they are out and the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A line of cars is using the shoulder to get around a lowered gate while horns blow. What should you do?
options: Cross because many horns mean the train has already stopped
Straddle the gate arm along with the other cars
Stay stopped behind the gate
Join the line on the shoulder and go around the arm
questions.explanation: Other drivers going around a gate are not a sign that it is safe. You wait until the lights are out, the gate is up, and the tracks look clear. Pressure from other drivers does not open the crossing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The active lights on a cantilever over your lane start to flash, while another set faces a side road. What should you do?
options: Stop for the lights that face you and wait until they stop flashing
Go if you are mostly watching the lights that face the side street
Stop under the cantilever with your car on the rails
Treat overhead railroad lights as a hint to slow
questions.explanation: Lights aimed at your approach are your stop signal. You wait until they are out and the tracks look clear, even if other heads face another road.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in the right lane, and the crossing gates lower across every lane including yours. What should you do?
options: Stop with the arm on your hood and then creep forward
Stop in your lane before the gate
Move left at the last moment and beat the neighboring gate
Drive the shoulder around your own gate arm
questions.explanation: When the gates come down across the lanes, every approach stops. A last-second lane change or a shoulder run is still driving around a gate. Do not change lanes to slip past the end of an arm.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The tracks cross a gravel road that has a crossbuck and no signals, and loose gravel lies before the rails. What should you do?
options: Hit the rails at speed so the car does not bog down
Stop on the rails where the gravel ends
Ignore the crossbuck
Slow on the gravel and cross only if clear
questions.explanation: Gravel lengthens your stop, so you slow early, yield at the crossbuck, and you do not use the rails as the place to test your brakes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You see a disabled car already stopped on the crossing with the hood up, and the lights are not flashing. What should you do?
options: Do not enter behind it
Push that car farther along the rails with your bumper
Drive around it on the tracks and continue your trip
Sit behind it on the rails until it moves
questions.explanation: A stalled vehicle on the tracks is an emergency. You do not add your own car to the rails, and the notification sign is how the railroad can warn trains. When you can do so safely, help get word to the emergency notification number.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The gate rises fully and the lights go out, but a second train horn sounds from a track you cannot see well. What should you do?
options: Race the sound so you are not delayed at the crossing
Wait and look
Go, because an up gate means every horn can be ignored
Cross and stop on the hidden track to locate the horn
questions.explanation: A horn after the gate rises can mean another train. You yield until you can see the tracks are clear, because an up gate is not a dare to beat a train you hear. Do not start across if that train may reach you before you can clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your side of the road is a solid line of stopped vehicles at flashing crossing lights, and you want a driveway before the rails. What should you do?
options: Use the shoulder to reach that driveway across the rails
Pass the line on the left while the lights flash
Wait in line
Cut through the driveway by crossing the tracks ahead of the line
questions.explanation: A driveway before the rails does not let you pass stopped traffic into a closed crossing. You wait until the lights are out and the tracks are clear. Do not leave the line and cross in front of the stopped cars.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The crossing warning activates while you are still in a driveway that opens directly toward the tracks. What should you do?
options: Back onto the tracks so you are ready to leave quickly
Back out and stop with the trunk hanging over the rails
Follow the gate arm around as it lowers across the mouth
Stay in the driveway until the lights stop and the tracks are clear
questions.explanation: A driveway at the rails is not a head start. If the lights are flashing or the gate is down, you stay off the tracks until the warning ends and the way is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are approaching an unsignalized crossbuck at dusk, and a single bright light is moving along the rails. What should you do?
options: Yield to that approaching train and wait well short of the tracks
Go if the light might belong to something smaller than a train
Meet the light by driving onto the rails for a better view
Dim your headlights and cross without looking again
questions.explanation: A light moving on the rails at dusk is a train until you know otherwise. The crossbuck requires you to yield short of the tracks instead of guessing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You stopped for flashing lights. They go dark, but the gate arm is still rising and still blocks part of your lane. What should you do?
options: Drive under the rising arm
Go around the arm while it is still moving
Stop on the tracks as soon as the arm clears the roof
Wait until the gate is fully up
questions.explanation: Dark lights are only part of the release. If the gate still blocks you, you wait until it is fully up and the tracks look clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A second gate at the far side of a wide multi-track crossing is still down, even though the near gate has risen. What should you do?
options: Do not enter
Enter and stop between the tracks beside the far gate
Drive around the far gate
Treat the far gate as a device that faces only the other direction
questions.explanation: The crossing is not clear while a gate still blocks the way out. Entering would leave you stopped among the tracks. Wait until the path all the way across is open and the tracks look clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The crossing is marked only by a crossbuck, the view is long and empty, and no train is coming. What should you do?
options: Cross without looking
Treat the missing light mast as proof the railroad is closed
Proceed when you can clear
Stop on the tracks and count slowly even though you can see a long empty distance
questions.explanation: The crossbuck itself is the yield message. When no train is coming and you can clear the far side, you do not stop on an empty uncontrolled crossing, but you still look.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A truck with a hazardous-materials placard is stopped ahead of you at a dark crossing, as some trucks must. You are in a car. What should you do?
options: Pass the truck on the rails
Assume the crossing is out of service
Pull beside the truck and stop on the tracks
Wait behind it rather than passing it on the crossing
questions.explanation: Some trucks must stop even when the signals are dark. You do not use that stop as a chance to pass on the tracks. Its extra stop is not a cue to ignore the rails.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A train is already occupying the crossing when you arrive, and the lights have not started flashing yet. What should you do?
options: Stop short of the tracks and wait
Go around the train
Try to cross ahead of the next rail car
Stop beside the moving cars while you are on the rails
questions.explanation: Lights and gates warn you, but a train already on the crossing is the hazard itself. You stop short and you never drive around it. The train controls the road even if the lights are late.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The lights flash at a gateless crossing, and traffic in another direction still seems to be moving. What should you do?
options: Treat the lack of a gate as permission to roll through the flashing red
Stop for the lights that face you
Go, because the other direction did not appear to stop
Stop on the tracks so both directions can see you
questions.explanation: Your flashing red lights are a stop for your approach. Another lane's movement does not cancel them, and a missing gate does not either. The other direction does not release your lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are first in line, the gate is up, and the lights are out, but a truck trailer is still finishing its crossing. What should you do?
options: Go around the trailer on the shoulder of the crossing
Move up beside the trailer in the space between the rails
Wait until the trailer is off the tracks and you can clear behind it
Start across and stop inches behind the trailer while you are still on the rails
questions.explanation: A rising gate does not erase a vehicle that is still on the tracks. You start only when the crossing and the space beyond it can hold your car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A temporary stop sign and a flagger are working a crossing where the automatic lights are covered. What should you do?
options: Go, because covered lights mean the railroad is closed
Drive around the flagger and the temporary stop sign
Stop on the tracks and ask the flagger from the driver's seat
Obey the flagger and the temporary stop
questions.explanation: When automatic lights are covered, the flagger is the protection. You do not drive around the stop, and you still clear the far side completely. Obey the flagger and the temporary stop, and cross only when directed and the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You approach a crossbuck while an oncoming car is waiting too, and a train is coming. What should you do?
options: Wait until the train passes and it is clear
Race the oncoming car across in front of the train
Use the pause to pass the oncoming car on the tracks
Stop side by side on the rails while the train approaches
questions.explanation: A train gets the crossing over both directions. You wait it out rather than using the other car as a reason to rush the rails. Wait until the train passes and the tracks are clear before either of you moves onto the rails.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The road curves sharply just after the tracks, and you cannot see whether that curve is blocked until you would be on the rails. What should you do?
options: Shift gears in the curve while your car is on the tracks
Go slowly and commit only to a clear path
Enter and stop in the curve while you are still on the rails
Cross at speed so the hidden curve does not matter
questions.explanation: A curve just past the rails can hide a stopped vehicle. You need to know you can clear the far side before you start, and you do not stop or shift on the tracks. Approach slowly and commit only when you can see a clear path all the way off the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are stopped at the line, the lights are flashing, the gate is down, and a gap opens between rail cars. What should you do?
options: Drive through the gap between the rail cars
Nose into the gap and wait there for more space
Follow a person who walks through that gap with your car
Stay stopped; a gap between cars is not an opening for your vehicle
questions.explanation: Rail cars can start moving, and another train can be on a different track. A gap is not a road, so you wait until the crossing is fully clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are behind the stop line, the warning has ended, and debris on the rails might force you to stop halfway across. What should you do?
options: Swerve around the debris after you are already on the tracks
Ignore the debris and also ignore a train horn
Cross only if you can do it without stopping on the tracks
Stop on the rails and clear the debris while the car sits there
questions.explanation: Debris does not cancel the clearance rule. If you cannot cross without stopping on the rails, you do not start. Otherwise wait or choose another route.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The railroad lights flash beside a highway signal that is showing a green left arrow toward the tracks. What should you do?
options: Take the green arrow onto the tracks
Turn under a lowering gate
Stop on the tracks so you do not lose the arrow
Cancel the turn and wait
questions.explanation: A green arrow does not let you enter a crossing protected by flashing red lights. You wait until those lights are out and you can clear the far side.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have never used this crossing. There is no gate and no light, and vines half cover a crossbuck beside empty rails. What should you do?
options: Treat it as a yield sign and look both ways
Skip the stop-and-look
Stop on the rails while you clear the vines from the sign
Use the opposing lane so the sign is easier to read
questions.explanation: A hard-to-see crossbuck still marks the crossing. You yield to trains, and when the rails are empty and you can finish, you cross without stopping on them. Treat the hard-to-see crossbuck as a live yield sign, look both ways, and cross only when you can clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The crossing lights are flashing in an industrial area, and you see rail cars being pushed with no engine at the front. What should you do?
options: Drive around the gate to beat the shoved cars
Stop on the near rail for a closer look at the cars
Stay stopped; pushed cars can still arrive
Go, because there is no locomotive leading the movement
questions.explanation: A shoving move can hide the engine at the rear. Flashing lights mean you wait until they are out, any gate is up, and the tracks are clear. Stay stopped; cars being pushed can reach the crossing before an engine comes into view.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A multi-track crossing is long, and a slow truck just past the far rail may make you stop among the tracks. What should you do before you enter?
options: Enter and plan to pause on a middle track if the truck is slow
Follow the truck onto the first rail and shift gears there
Pass the truck while both of you are on the tracks
Wait, because you may not clear every track before you catch that truck
questions.explanation: A long crossing needs more room on the far side. If the truck would force you to stop among the tracks, you wait until you can clear them in one move.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An oncoming driver flashes headlights as if offering you the crossing, and a train is also visible. What should you do?
options: Ignore the flash and wait for the train
Take the flash as permission to beat the train
Meet the oncoming car on the tracks and then look
Cross, because headlight flashes override a crossbuck
questions.explanation: Another driver's courtesy does not outrank a train. You yield at the crossbuck until the train is gone and you can clear the far side. Ignore the courtesy flash and wait until the train has passed and the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The gate is down and the lights are flashing on a line you believe carries only a few trains a day. What should you do?
options: Stop on the tracks until the usual train time has passed
Stop and wait out the warning
Go around the gate
Cross if your watch says a train is not due
questions.explanation: Schedules do not open a closed crossing. Extra trains run, and a second train may follow, so you wait until the lights are out and the tracks look clear. A light schedule is not a reason to go around the gate.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You can see the far side is clear, the lights are out, and the gate is up, but a passenger wants you to stop on the tracks for a photo. What should you do?
options: Park between two tracks so the background looks better
Back onto the tracks if the first angle is poor
Cross and clear the tracks
Stop on the rails for a moment
questions.explanation: Dark signals are not permission to use the rails as a parking spot, because a train or a new warning can arrive while you are stopped there. Never stop on them for a photo or any other pause.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A railroad crossing lies in the middle of a busy intersection, and you cannot clear both the tracks and the intersection. What should you do?
options: Enter the crossing and stop in the intersection on the rails
Block the tracks so you can claim a place in the intersection
Shift gears on the rails while you sort out the turn
Wait behind the stop line until you can clear
questions.explanation: You do not start across unless you can clear the far side completely. An intersection you cannot finish is a reason to wait, not a reason to occupy the tracks. Wait behind the near stop line until one move will carry you fully off the tracks.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The lights at the crossing flash, go dark, and start again before your wheels move. Why should you remain stopped?
options: Because a following train or a continuing movement may still be using the crossing
Because the round yellow advance sign is a mandatory stop on every trip
Because a passenger car must wait there until a school bus arrives
Because a dark signal mast means the tracks are closed for the day
questions.explanation: Restarting lights mean the warning is not finished. You stay put until the lights stay off, any gate is up, and you can see the tracks are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are coaching a new driver at a passive crossing that has only a crossbuck. Which instruction matches that sign?
options: Drive around any gate that is down
Yield to trains and be ready to stop
Always stop on the rails and then look around
Go without looking if no lights are installed
questions.explanation: A crossbuck means yield, and the round yellow sign or RXR marking is only the advance warning. You stop for a train, a stop sign, flashing lights, or a gate, not merely because the warning sign exists. Yield to trains and be ready to stop, and do not treat the earlier round warning as a required stop when the tracks are empty.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The vehicle ahead is slow on a two-lane road, the yellow line on your side is broken, and no traffic is coming. What should you do before you pass?
options: Stay in the oncoming lane until the next town
Pass with no signal
Signal, check, and pass only if you can return
Pull onto the shoulder and pass on the right
questions.explanation: A broken line on your side can allow a left-side pass only when the way ahead is clear and you can get back before oncoming traffic arrives. Signal, check the mirror and blind spot, and start only if you can return before the oncoming lane fills.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The line on your side of the center is solid yellow, and the line on the other side is broken. May you pass the slow car?
options: No; a solid yellow line on your side forbids the pass
Yes, because the other side's broken line is the one that matters
Yes, if you sound the horn first
Yes, by using the right shoulder
questions.explanation: Your side of the center line controls your pass. A solid yellow on your side means do not cross it, even when the opposing line is broken.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Both center lines are solid yellow on a two-lane road, and the car ahead is slow. What should you do?
options: Use a driveway apron to swing around the car
Stay behind it until passing is legal
Cross both solid lines
Pass on the right shoulder
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean neither direction passes here. A slow leader is not an exception to that marking. Stay behind it until a legal passing place and a clear road let you pass on the left.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A yellow pennant stands on the left as the center line on your side becomes solid. What does that pennant mean?
options: This is the best place on the road to pass
Children are boarding a bus on the left shoulder
A no-passing zone is beginning
A passing lane is opening on the left
questions.explanation: The no-passing pennant is placed on the left at the start of the zone, and together with the solid line it tells you not to start a pass.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are beside a slow car in the oncoming lane, and you can now see its front in your inside mirror. What should you do?
options: Stay in the oncoming lane until the next intersection
Cut back only after the other car honks
Return without a signal
Signal, return to your lane smoothly, and then cancel the signal
questions.explanation: You complete the pass and come back when you can see the passed vehicle in your mirror, so you do not cut it off, and then you cancel the signal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A driver is passing you on a two-lane road and is already alongside your door. What should you do?
options: Stop dead in your lane with no warning
Hold your speed or ease off so the driver can finish
Accelerate so the passer cannot get back into the lane
Move left into the passer
questions.explanation: When someone passes you, speeding up traps them in the oncoming lane. Holding speed or easing off lets them finish.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The car ahead is stopped at a marked crosswalk, and the yellow line on your side is broken. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right shoulder to save time
Honk and go around through the crosswalk
Do not pass that stopped car
Pass on the left
questions.explanation: A vehicle stopped at a crosswalk is a reason to stop, because someone may be crossing where you cannot see them yet. Do not pass; a person may be crossing in front of that stopped car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are approaching a hill crest, and you cannot see the oncoming lane beyond it. A slow car is ahead. What should you do?
options: Pass quickly before the crest
Use the right shoulder over the crest
Straddle the center line at the crest to see farther
Stay back until you can see past the crest
questions.explanation: A hill hides oncoming traffic, so you pass on the left only when you can see that the way is clear through your return to the lane. Stay back; do not pass on a hill when your view of the far side is limited.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A sharp curve hides the road ahead, and the yellow line on your side is broken. May you pass the slow tractor now?
options: No; you cannot see far enough on the curve
Yes, because a broken line always means pass immediately
Yes, by using the inside shoulder of the curve
Yes, if you honk all the way through the bend
questions.explanation: Markings are not the only test. You do not pass on a curve when you cannot see far enough to finish before oncoming traffic. No; limited sight on a curve forbids the pass even if the paint might otherwise allow it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)
