questions.q: The slow car ahead is inside an intersection, and you would need the oncoming lane to get around it. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right through the crosswalk
Do not pass in the intersection
Pass in the intersection if the light facing you is green
Use the cross street as a slingshot around the car
questions.explanation: Intersections hide cross traffic and turning vehicles, so a green light is not permission to pass there. Wait until you are through it and a legal gap is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A railroad crossing is just ahead, and the only gap for a pass would put you on the tracks beside a slow truck. What should you do?
options: Pass on the shoulder across the rails
Straddle the center line while you are on the crossing
Wait; do not pass at a railroad crossing
Pass on the tracks if the crossing lights are dark
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing is a forbidden passing place, because you may end up in the oncoming lane or on the tracks in front of a train.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A narrow bridge is ahead, you cannot see the far end clearly, and a slow car is on the approach. What should you do?
options: Pass on the bridge if the leading car is slow enough
Use the pedestrian walkway of the bridge to get by
Cross the center line on the bridge
Do not pass on a bridge when the sight distance is limited
questions.explanation: A bridge with a limited view can hide an oncoming vehicle and leaves little room to escape, so you wait until you can see a legal pass.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The car ahead signals a left turn and moves into a left-turn lane. Your through lane to its right is open. May you go by?
options: Yes, you may pass on the right in that real lane
No, because passing on the right is forbidden in every situation nationwide
Yes, by using the right shoulder beside the turn lane
Yes, by squeezing between the turning car and the curb where no lane exists
questions.explanation: Passing on the right is not the normal pass. It can be legal when the vehicle ahead is turning left and you have an actual lane, never the shoulder. The car is turning left, and you still stay off the shoulder.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A slower car is in the right lane of a multi-lane highway, and the left lane is clear for a long stretch. How should you pass?
options: Ride beside it in the left lane for a long distance
Signal, pass on the left, then return
Pass it on the right shoulder of the highway
Move left without a signal and cut back at once
questions.explanation: The ordinary pass is on the left in a clear lane. You return only after the mirror shows the vehicle you passed, and then you cancel the signal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The right shoulder is paved and empty, and a slow car is ahead on a two-lane road with a solid yellow line on your side. What should you do?
options: Cross the solid yellow line
Straddle the edge line and pass half on the shoulder
Stay behind the car
Pass on the paved shoulder
questions.explanation: The shoulder is not a lane, and a solid yellow line on your side also forbids a left-side pass at this spot.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to pass, but a solid yellow line will begin before you could get back into your lane. What should you do?
options: Start and cross the solid line for only a moment
Pass on the right to avoid the solid line
Honk and pass anyway
Do not start
questions.explanation: You pass on the left only when the markings allow the whole maneuver. If you cannot return before the solid line, you wait. You must be able to return before the no-passing marking and before oncoming traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An oncoming truck is visible, the line on your side is broken, and you are not sure the gap is long enough. What should you do?
options: Stay back until you are sure of the gap
Go now and expect the truck to move onto the shoulder
Pass and then travel beside the truck in the oncoming lane
Pass on the right
questions.explanation: If you are unsure about oncoming traffic, the way ahead is not clear, so you wait for a gap you can finish. Stay back until you are sure you can finish and return before the truck arrives.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A car is stopped in your lane at an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection, and people are waiting at the corner. What should you do?
options: Stop behind that car
Pass on the left through the intersection
Use the right curb to slip past the stopped car
Honk so the people stay on the corner while you pass
questions.explanation: An unmarked crosswalk at an intersection still protects people on foot, and passing a car stopped there can hide you from them. Do not pass a vehicle that has stopped for a crosswalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are about to enter a short underpass, you cannot see out the far end, and a slow car is inside. What should you do?
options: Cross the center line at the darkest point
Do not pass while the far side is hidden
Pass inside the underpass
Use the narrow ledge beside the lane to get around the car
questions.explanation: Limited sight is a reason to wait, the same idea as a hill, a curve, or a bridge you cannot see across. Wait until you can see enough road to return safely.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A farm tractor is ahead, the line on your side is broken, and the oncoming lane is empty as far as you can see. What may you do?
options: Stay in the oncoming lane after the tractor to save time
Pass inside the next intersection if one is closer than the straight stretch
Pass on the left if you can return well before any oncoming vehicle appears
Pass on the right shoulder
questions.explanation: A slow tractor may be passed on the left when your marking allows it and the oncoming lane stays clear long enough for you to return.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: On a one-way street with two lanes, the car in the left lane is stopped to turn left, and your right lane goes straight and is clear. What may you do?
options: Stop in the intersection until the left turn is finished
Continue in your lane past the left-turning car
Wait behind that turning car even though your own lane is open
Use the right shoulder even though the through lane is clear
questions.explanation: When a vehicle ahead is turning left and you already have a clear through lane, you may go past on the right in that lane, not on a shoulder.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A car is signaling a left turn on a two-lane road, and the only pavement to its right is a gravel shoulder. Oncoming traffic is coming. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right with two wheels on the sidewalk
Go around on the left through the oncoming traffic in the intersection
Wait behind it
Use the gravel shoulder to pass on the right
questions.explanation: There is no lane for a right-side pass, and the oncoming lane is occupied, so the shoulder is not a legal substitute.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A solid yellow line is on your side as you near a slow truck, while the oncoming side has a broken line. A passenger says you may pass. What should you do?
options: Accept the advice and cross your solid line
Pass on the right
Honk until the truck leaves the travel lane
Refuse the pass
questions.explanation: The broken line on the other side governs the other direction. Your solid yellow line still forbids your pass.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A two-way left-turn lane occupies the center, and you want to use it to get around the car ahead. What should you do?
options: Do not use that center lane for passing
Accelerate down the center lane and complete a pass
Drive the center lane for several blocks to get ahead
Treat the empty center lane as an ordinary passing lane
questions.explanation: A shared center turn lane is for leaving the road to the left, not for overtaking through traffic.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You have just reached a no-passing zone marked by a pennant on the left, and the car ahead is far below the pace of other traffic. What should you do?
options: Cross the solid line until the pennant is behind you
Stay behind it until the zone ends
Pass anyway, because the pennant is only advice
Pass on the right
questions.explanation: The pennant on the left marks the start of the no-passing zone, and a slow car does not cancel that restriction. Stay behind the car until you leave the zone and the road ahead is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A vehicle is stopped at a crosswalk on a multi-lane road, and the lane beside it looks open. What should you do?
options: Use the open lane to go around the stopped vehicle
Pass on the shoulder beside the crosswalk
Change lanes inside the crosswalk markings
Do not pass in the next lane
questions.explanation: You do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, even in the next lane, because a person can step out from in front of it. Stop and wait until the person has finished crossing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to pass two slow vehicles at once on a two-lane road, but the broken line and the clear gap are short. What should you do?
options: Pass only what you can finish before the clear gap or the broken line runs out
Pass both even if you will still be on the wrong side at the solid line
Pass both vehicles on the shoulder
Pass them inside the upcoming intersection
questions.explanation: You may pass on the left only when you can return before oncoming traffic and before the marking forbids it, so a short zone may fit one vehicle and not two.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: On a multi-lane highway a slower car is in the middle lane and the left lane is empty. How should you pass it?
options: Signal, pass on the left, then return
Pass on the right shoulder of the highway
Weave right, then left, then right again around the car
Travel for a long time in the blind area beside the car
questions.explanation: You signal, use the clear left lane, and come back only when the mirror shows you have cleared the car, then cancel the signal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A broken yellow line is on your side, a solid yellow line is on the oncoming side, and the oncoming lane is empty. May you pass a slow car?
options: Yes, and you may remain in the oncoming lane afterward
Yes, but only by using the right shoulder
Yes, if you can complete the pass and return before any oncoming vehicle arrives
No, because any solid yellow line anywhere on the road forbids you
questions.explanation: The line on your side governs you. Your broken line can allow a left pass when the road is clear, while the other solid line restricts the other direction.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are approaching an intersection, the car ahead is going straight and slow, and your line was broken just before the crossroad. What should you do?
options: Pass in the intersection
Pass on the right through the cross street
Use the left-turn lane of the cross street as a passing lane
Do not pass in the intersection
questions.explanation: A broken line nearby does not make an intersection a passing place, because cross traffic and turns conflict with you there. Wait until you are past it and can see a clear legal gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A hill blocks your view, you know the road well, and you doubt anyone is coming. The car ahead is slow. What should you do?
options: Do not pass from memory
Pass, because you drive this hill every day
Pass on the shoulder on the downhill side
Straddle the center line over the crest
questions.explanation: Familiarity is not sight distance. You need to see that the oncoming lane will stay clear until you are back on your side.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Someone is passing you, and you want to accelerate so you will not end up behind them. What should you do?
options: Match them and travel side by side for a while
Move into the oncoming lane beside them
Hold your speed or ease off
Accelerate and deny them room to return
questions.explanation: When you are being passed you do not speed up, because holding speed or easing off is what lets the other driver finish. Hold your speed or ease off until they have returned to the lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child is in the crosswalk, and the car ahead has stopped for that child. Your yellow line is broken. What should you do?
options: Pass on the left through the crosswalk
Pass on the right between the stopped car and the child
Honk so the child hurries out of the way
Stop and wait
questions.explanation: You do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A broken line cannot override a child who is already crossing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You see the no-passing pennant on the left and then a solid yellow line, before a straight section you cannot yet see. What should you do now?
options: Treat the pennant as the start of the zone and stay in your lane
Pass at the pennant
Ignore a pennant that looks small next to the car ahead
Pass on the right at the pennant
questions.explanation: The pennant is installed on the left where the no-passing zone begins, so you do not pass there and hope the view opens later.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The bridge ahead is arched, you cannot see over the arch, and a truck is moving slowly toward it. What should you do?
options: Pass on the side nearest the bridge rail
Cross the center line before the arch so you can see better
Stay behind it until past the bridge
Pass on the arch
questions.explanation: An arched bridge hides oncoming traffic. Limited sight on a bridge means you do not pass, even when the truck is slow. Stay behind the truck until you are off the bridge and can see a legal opening.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: After a pass you can see the other vehicle in the center mirror, and you have already signaled right. What is the last step?
options: Move back and cancel the signal
Stay in the left lane with the signal still on
Cancel the signal before you ever check the mirror
Cut back before the vehicle appears in the mirror
questions.explanation: Seeing the vehicle in the mirror tells you the lane is yours again. You return smoothly and then cancel the signal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A line of cars is stopped at a crosswalk, and the opposing lane looks empty. What should you do?
options: Honk and move forward into the crosswalk
Stop with the line
Pass the whole line by moving into the opposing lane
Use the shoulder to get around the stopped line
questions.explanation: Those drivers may be stopped for a person you cannot see, so passing them is how people on foot get hit. Do not use the opposing lane to pass cars that have stopped for the crosswalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A curve warning is posted, you cannot see through the bend, and a slow car is ahead on a broken yellow line. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right between the roadside mailboxes and the car
Cut the curve by using the oncoming lane
Follow the car through the curve
Pass in the curve
questions.explanation: A broken line cannot turn a blind curve into a passing zone, because you cannot see whether the oncoming lane will stay empty. Do not pass where the bend limits your view.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The car in front stops for a person who is stepping off the curb at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Pass on the left before the person finishes stepping down
Pass on the right between the car and the curb
Honk so the person waits on the curb while you pass
Stop behind that car and wait
questions.explanation: A car stopped for someone at a crosswalk is not an obstacle you may pass, because going around it puts you in that person's path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A solid white line separates your lane from a car-pool lane on the left, and a slow truck is ahead of you. What should you do?
options: Pass the truck on the right shoulder
Straddle the solid white line for the length of the pass
Do not cross the solid white line to pass
Cross the solid white line
questions.explanation: A solid white line tells you to stay in your lane, and the shoulder is not a substitute passing lane. Wait for a broken line or another legal opening.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Your light is green, yet the car ahead stops at the intersection crosswalk and you cannot see why. What should you do?
options: Pass it on the left inside the intersection
Pass it on the right through the crosswalk
Honk and go around
Stop behind it and do not pass
questions.explanation: A green light does not let you pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, because that driver may see a person you have not seen.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The center line is broken and then turns solid well before a hilltop, and a slow motor home is ahead. What should you do?
options: Pass only if you are back before the solid line
Carry the pass over the hilltop on the solid line
Pass the motor home on the right shoulder before the hill
Start the pass at the hilltop where the line is solid
questions.explanation: You need both a legal line and a view. If either the solid line or the hill will arrive before you can return, you do not start.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A motorist behind you pulls out to pass, and you are already holding the pace you intend. What should you do?
options: Move left as the passer comes alongside
Keep that pace or ease off slightly
Increase speed so the passer has to pick someone else
Brake suddenly so the passer is forced to drop back
questions.explanation: When another driver starts to pass you, speeding up removes the room they need to return to the lane. Do not increase speed while the pass is underway.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to pass a car that is stopped with brake lights on at a railroad crossing, and the oncoming lane looks empty. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right shoulder across the tracks
Pull alongside the car while both of you are on the rails
Do not pass at the railroad crossing
Pass on the left across the tracks
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are not passing zones. The stopped car may be waiting for a train or for room beyond the tracks. Stay behind and see why that car has stopped.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A curve to the right limits your view, and the slow vehicle ahead is towing a small trailer. Your line is broken. What should you do?
options: Pass in the curve
Pass between the trailer and the right edge of the pavement
Use the oncoming lane through the entire curve
Wait until the curve opens up
questions.explanation: The trailer makes the pass longer, and the curve already hides oncoming traffic, so you wait until you can see the return.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are on a narrow bridge behind a slow car, and an oncoming vehicle is already on the bridge. What should you do?
options: Do not pass; the limited room and the oncoming vehicle mean you wait
Squeeze past both vehicles while you are on the bridge
Use the bridge rail to get around the slow car
Back up quickly and then rush a pass
questions.explanation: A bridge that is already occupied and offers little room is not a passing place, so you wait until you can see a legal gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your broken passing segment is short, and a car is oncoming at a distance you would meet during the pass. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right so the oncoming car does not matter
Start and plan to finish beyond the broken segment
Do not start the pass
Start and make the oncoming car slow down for you
questions.explanation: A broken line allows a pass only when the way ahead is clear. If you would still be over the center when that car arrives, you wait.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A slow truck is in the right lane of a freeway, and several cars are behind you in the left lane. What is the safer way past the truck?
options: Wait for a gap, signal, pass, and return
Pass the truck on the right shoulder
Squeeze between the truck and the left-lane traffic with no gap
Move in front of the truck before you can see it in the mirror
questions.explanation: On a multi-lane road you still pass to the left in a clear lane, return only after the mirror shows room, and never use the shoulder. Wait for a real gap in the left lane, signal, pass, and return when the truck appears in your mirror.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The oncoming lane is busy, your yellow line is broken, and the car ahead holds a steady pace. What should you do?
options: Tailgate until the driver ahead leaves the road
Stay behind until the oncoming lane clears
Pass because the line is broken, regardless of the oncoming cars
Pass on the shoulder while the oncoming lane is busy
questions.explanation: Markings allow a pass only together with a clear road. Busy oncoming traffic means you cannot return in time. Stay behind; a broken line is not a command to pass when oncoming traffic fills the other lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Where is the no-passing pennant placed for the drivers who must obey it?
options: In the center of the next intersection
Only beside freeway entrance ramps
On the left side at the start of the zone
On the right shoulder at the end of the zone
questions.explanation: The pennant is posted on the left at the start of the no-passing zone so it faces the drivers who are about to lose sight distance.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A solid yellow line runs on your side through a winding stretch, and a passenger urges one quick pass. What should you do?
options: Make the quick pass across the solid line
Use the right shoulder for that quick pass
Pass at the tightest bend
Decline and keep following
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side prohibits the pass, and a winding view makes starting one even less reasonable. Decline, and follow the vehicle ahead until your line is broken and the view is open.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The car ahead stops at a crosswalk on the far side of an intersection you are entering. What should you do?
options: Go around on the right at the crosswalk
Honk and creep forward beside the stopped car
Stop behind it
Pass it while you are still inside the intersection
questions.explanation: The stopped car is protecting a crossing. Passing it inside the intersection can strike a person stepping out. Stop behind it, and do not swing into another lane to pass at that crosswalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are considering a pass just as you reach an intersection where a vehicle is waiting on the side road. What should you do?
options: Do not pass in the intersection
Pass through the intersection before the waiting driver pulls out
Use the side road itself as your passing lane
Honk and pass on the right at the corner
questions.explanation: Intersections are no-passing places because vehicles enter from the side and conflict with a driver who is in the oncoming lane. Let the side-road driver and the car ahead finish their moves first.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A slow car is bouncing over a railroad crossing, no train is in sight, and your yellow line is broken. What should you do?
options: Pull alongside on the tracks and decide there
Wait until you both clear the crossing
Pass the car while it is still on the rails
Pass on the shoulder at the crossbuck
questions.explanation: You do not pass at a railroad crossing, even when no train is visible, because the oncoming lane on the tracks is the wrong place to be. Wait until both of you are past the crossing before you even consider a pass.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A wide paved shoulder runs for a long distance beside slow traffic, and your center line is solid yellow. What should you do?
options: Pass the line of cars on the shoulder
Alternate between the shoulder and the oncoming lane
Drive the shoulder until the solid line ends
Remain in line
questions.explanation: Shoulder passing is not a legal right-side pass. A right-side pass needs a real lane and a situation such as a left-turning vehicle beside that lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A vehicle ahead is turning left, a marked through lane is open on its right, and a person is in that lane's crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Go around the person by using the left side of the turning car
Stop for the person
Pass on the right through the occupied crosswalk
Honk and pass anyway
questions.explanation: A lane beside a left-turning vehicle can allow a right-side pass, but not through someone in the crosswalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The oncoming lane looks clear and your line is broken, but a sign shows the passing zone ends before you could finish. What should you do?
options: Pass on the shoulder to avoid the sign
Ignore the sign if you do not also see a pennant in the mirror
Do not start a pass you cannot finish before the zone ends
Start and complete the pass on the solid segment
questions.explanation: You need room to return while the pass is still legal. If the zone will end first, you wait.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have passed a car, you can see it in the side mirror, and you have not yet signaled the return. What should you do?
options: Return with no signal
Wait until the car disappears from every mirror and then swerve
Stay in the left lane indefinitely
Signal right, return when that lane is yours, and then cancel the signal
questions.explanation: The mirror tells you that you have cleared the vehicle. You still signal the move back, make it smoothly, and then cancel the signal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A truck is climbing a long hill, the oncoming lane is visibly open, and the broken line on your side covers the whole distance you would need. What may you do?
options: Pass on the left if no oncoming vehicle will reach you before you return
Pass on the right shoulder of the hill
Follow the truck over the crest while you remain in the oncoming lane
Refuse every hill pass even when the view and the line are both clear
questions.explanation: A hill forbids the pass when it limits sight. When you can see a clear oncoming lane and your line stays broken long enough, a left-side pass is allowed.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are close behind a slow car as a curve with a limited view begins, and the center line on your side is broken. What should you do?
options: Move into the oncoming lane before the curve starts
Back off and follow through the curve instead of passing
Pass immediately so the curve cannot interfere
Use the shoulder through the curve
questions.explanation: Limited sight on a curve is a no-pass condition. Being close to the slow car is a reason to open a gap, not a reason to swing out blind.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: On a street with two lanes in your direction, the car to your left is slowing to turn left, and you are in the clear right through lane. What should you do?
options: Move onto the right shoulder to pass
Stop in the through lane even though your path and the crosswalk are clear
Swing left around the turning car
Continue straight in your lane
questions.explanation: Passing on the right is not the usual move, but a real through lane beside a left-turning vehicle is the situation where going ahead can be legal. The shoulder is not. The allowed way past that left-turning car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A solid yellow line and a left-side pennant begin while you are still behind the vehicle you hoped to pass. What should you do?
options: Ignore the pennant
Stay behind until the zone ends
Cross at the pennant if you accelerate hard
Pass on the right at the pennant
questions.explanation: The pennant and the solid line on your side start the prohibition. An earlier plan does not let you begin a pass you cannot legally finish. Cancel the idea and remain behind until the zone ends and the road is clear.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: At night during a pass, the headlights of the car you are passing show in your mirror, so its front is behind you. What should you do?
options: Cut back before any light appears in the mirror
Switch off your own lights and then return
Signal your return, move back to your lane, and cancel the signal
Stay out until those headlights disappear completely
questions.explanation: Seeing the passed vehicle in the mirror means you have cleared it, so you signal, return, and cancel the signal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person is still finishing the crosswalk, and the car that stopped for them has not moved. What should you do?
options: Pass as soon as the person nears the far curb but is still in the roadway
Use another lane to go around the stopped car
Honk so the car and the person both hurry
Wait behind that car until the person is clear
questions.explanation: You do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk while the person is still crossing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your side of the road has a broken yellow line, but completing a pass would take you through a marked railroad crossing. What should you do?
options: Wait until you are past the crossing
Complete the pass on the crossing
Pass on the shoulder over the rails
Stop on the rails and then pull out to pass
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing interrupts any pass, even on a broken line, because you must not occupy the oncoming side on the tracks. Wait until you are beyond the crossing and still have a legal, clear gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A crest and a curve come together ahead of a slow car you would like to pass. What should you do?
options: Use the center of the road at the crest to see farther
Follow the car until the view opens
Pass before the crest
Pass on the shoulder around the outside of the curve
questions.explanation: A hill and a curve each hide oncoming traffic, and together they mean you cannot see the whole return. Treat the hidden road as a no-pass and follow the car until the view opens.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A solid yellow line on your side lasts a short distance and then becomes a long broken segment. Where may you begin a pass?
options: Only after your own line becomes broken, and only if the oncoming lane is clear
During the solid stretch, if you expect to finish on the broken part
On the shoulder beside the solid line
At the solid line whenever no pennant is posted
questions.explanation: You may not cross a solid yellow line on your side to begin a pass. You wait until your line is broken and you can still return in time.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A second through lane is open to the right of a left-turning car, and that lane's crosswalk is empty. What may you do?
options: Stop in the clear through lane until the turn is fully done
Pass by driving through the turning car's own lane
Use the through lane to go past the left-turning car
Use the shoulder even though the through lane is open
questions.explanation: This is a case where a right-side pass can be legal: the vehicle ahead is turning left and you have a real lane. You still wait if a person is in the crosswalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are late, traffic is slow, and the yellow line on your side is solid. What should you do?
options: Cross the solid line
Pass the line of cars on the shoulder
Use the center turn lane as a fast lane
Accept the delay and stay in line
questions.explanation: Being late does not change a solid yellow line or turn the shoulder into a lane. Accept the delay and stay in line until a pass is both legal and safe.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A slow car is ahead, your line is broken, and a school bus in the oncoming lane has flashing red lights and the stop arm out. What should you do?
options: Pass the bus on the right shoulder
Go around both vehicles while the red lights flash
Do not pass; stop for the bus
Pass the slow car
questions.explanation: The bus warning closes the oncoming lane you would need, and you must stop rather than pass.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Traffic in your lane has stopped for a person in a crosswalk, and a driver behind you pulls left to go around that line. What should you do?
options: Stay stopped behind the line
Follow them around the stopped cars
Pass on the right while they pass on the left
Move up into the crosswalk so you are first when it clears
questions.explanation: Passing cars that have stopped for a person in a crosswalk is dangerous, so you do not copy that move. Stay stopped; do not follow that driver around the line or into the crosswalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You can see far down an empty oncoming lane, your yellow line is broken for the full distance, and a slow car is ahead on open pavement. What should you do?
options: Pass without signaling
Signal, pass on the left, then return
Pass on the right shoulder
Remain in the oncoming lane after the pass to stay ahead
questions.explanation: When the marking, the view, and the gap all allow it, the correct pass is still on the left, completed only after the mirror shows you are clear. Signal, pass on the left, return when the car appears in your mirror, and cancel the signal.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Yellow lights begin flashing on a school bus you are following. The red lights are not on yet. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right shoulder while the yellow lights flash
Ignore the yellow lights until a crossing guard appears
Slow down and prepare to stop
Accelerate and get past before the red lights start
questions.explanation: Amber or yellow lights mean the bus is about to stop. You slow and get ready to stop instead of trying to beat the change to red. Do not rush past the bus.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are meeting a school bus, and its yellow lights start flashing while the stop arm is still folded. What should you do?
options: Hold your speed
Move left and pass before the arm can extend
Honk so the driver keeps the arm folded
Slow down and prepare to stop
questions.explanation: Yellow lights facing you are the warning that a stop is coming. Rushing past is how drivers meet the stop arm too late. Slow down and prepare to stop rather than trying to pass before the red lights come on.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A school bus ahead of you has flashing red lights and the stop arm extended. What should you do?
options: Stop and stay stopped until the red lights quit and the arm is withdrawn
Stop, then go as soon as the last child steps toward the bus
Pass slowly on the left while the arm is out
Treat the arm as a request you may refuse if you are late
questions.explanation: Red lights and an extended stop arm mean you stop and remain stopped, because children may still be crossing until the warning is fully over.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are approaching an oncoming school bus on a two-lane road, and the red lights and stop arm are out. What should you do?
options: Stop beside the bus so the children can walk around your car
Stop and wait until the lights stop and the arm is withdrawn
Continue, because only traffic behind the bus must stop
Pass the bus in the opposing lane while the arm is out
questions.explanation: On an undivided road, traffic meeting the bus must stop too. Children often cross in front of the bus from either side.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The stop arm has been folded, yet the red lights on the school bus are still flashing. What should you do?
options: Go, because a folded arm always ends the stop
Creep forward beside the bus while the lights flash
Turn around in front of the bus
Remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing too
questions.explanation: The release requires both the lights to stop and the arm to be withdrawn. Flashing red lights alone still mean you stay stopped.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are behind a school bus in the right lane of a multi-lane road, and the bus shows red lights and an extended stop arm. What should you do?
options: Use the left lane to pass the bus while the arm is out
Pass on the right between the bus and the curb
Keep rolling because multi-lane roads cancel the stop arm
Stop and stay stopped
questions.explanation: Same-direction lanes still stop for the red lights and the stop arm. Children can come out in front of the bus into any lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A school speed sign shows a number you can read, and the zone is active. What speed do you use?
options: A faster number
The number printed on that school speed sign
Whatever pace feels comfortable with no children in sight
The speed you remember from a school zone in another town
questions.explanation: The national bank does not invent a school-zone speed. You obey the number posted on the school speed sign while that zone is in effect.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A crossing guard is in the crosswalk holding a stop paddle toward you, and your traffic signal is green. What should you do?
options: Honk so the guard clears the crosswalk
Drive around the guard through the opposing lane
Stop for the guard
Go, because a green signal outranks a guard
questions.explanation: A guard's stop paddle overrides the signal. Children are in the crossing on the guard's direction, not on the green light alone.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are about to turn right, and the crossing guard's paddle still faces you. What should you do?
options: Turn anyway, because a turn is shorter than going straight
Use the bike lane to sneak past the paddle
Honk and make the turn slowly
Wait through the turn until the guard no longer holds you
questions.explanation: The paddle controls the intersection, including turns. You do not turn across children the guard is holding traffic for.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The crossing guard has brought the children across and now directs your lane to move, while you are unsure of the signal. What should you do?
options: Follow the guard's direction
Ignore the guard and wait only for the signal
Motion the remaining children to run ahead of you
Turn through the crosswalk before the guard finishes
questions.explanation: The guard's direction overrides the signal. When the guard releases your lane and the children are clear, you follow that direction.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You see a fluorescent yellow-green pentagon showing two children walking. What does that sign mean?
options: Passing is required in the next block
A railroad crossing is the next control
A school area or a school crossing is ahead
The road is a numbered county route
questions.explanation: The school pentagon warns of a school or a school crossing so you can slow and scan. It does not identify a county highway. It is not a county route marker.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A fluorescent yellow-green sign with a school crossing symbol appears before you see any children. What should you do?
options: Treat it as a county route shield and hold your pace
Stop in the travel lane at the sign and wait for a bell
Speed up to clear the area before children arrive
Slow and start scanning for children and a guard
questions.explanation: The sign means the school crossing is ahead. You prepare early because children may enter the road before you expect them. The sign is a warning, not a route marker.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A beacon above a school speed sign is flashing. What does the flasher tell you?
options: The posted school speed on that sign is in effect
The school zone has ended for the day
You must ignore the number on the sign
The beacon is a railroad signal you may roll through
questions.explanation: A flashing beacon tied to the school speed sign means the special rule is active, so you obey the number printed on that sign.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The school speed sign says it applies when the beacon flashes, and the beacon is dark. What should you do?
options: Pass any car that is slowing near the crosswalk
Follow the sign
Ignore children because a dark beacon closes the school
Invent a slower number of your own and stop in the lane
questions.explanation: When the sign itself says the school speed applies while the beacon flashes, a dark beacon means you follow that instruction and you still expect unpredictable children.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The school speed sign says it applies when children are present, and children are on the sidewalk by the crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Honk so the children go back inside
Pass the car ahead that has already slowed
Obey the number on the school speed sign
Hold a higher pace
questions.explanation: Children present beside the crossing make the posted school speed apply. You use the number on the sign, not a pace you prefer.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The school bus yellow lights are on, and you believe you can beat them to a side street just past the bus. What should you do?
options: Honk and hold your speed
Do not rush past
Accelerate into the side street ahead of the bus
Pass on the right and turn at the same time
questions.explanation: Yellow lights mean the bus is about to stop. Trying to beat that change is how you meet an extending stop arm. Slow down and prepare to stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Red lights come on and the stop arm starts out before you have reached the school bus. What should you do?
options: Change lanes and pass
Stop only if a child is already in your lane
Stop before you reach the bus, and stay there until the warning ends
Accelerate so you are beside the bus before the arm locks
questions.explanation: If the red warning starts before you reach the bus, you stop. Speeding up to beat the arm puts you beside children leaving the bus.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have stopped for a school bus, and a child who crossed in front of it turns around and runs back. What should you do?
options: Stay stopped until the child is clear
Go, because the child already crossed once
Honk so the child freezes
Steer around the child while the arm is still out
questions.explanation: Children do not move in a straight plan. You remain stopped through the full warning and until that child is out of the road. Stay stopped until the red lights quit, the arm is withdrawn, and the child is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Several cars are stopped for a school bus with the stop arm out, and the left lane looks empty. What should you do?
options: Honk so the line starts moving
Join the stop
Use the empty lane to pass the line and the bus
Pass on the shoulder
questions.explanation: Those cars are stopped because children may be crossing. Passing them is the same mistake as passing the bus itself.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have been waiting and you want the school bus driver to fold the stop arm. What should you do?
options: Drive around the arm
Keep waiting for the driver
Honk until the driver folds the arm
Pull alongside the door and ask
questions.explanation: The driver folds the arm when the children are safe, not when traffic is impatient. Honking does not end the stop. Keep waiting until the lights stop and the arm is withdrawn on the driver's own timing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An intersection near a school has no painted crosswalk lines, and a child is stepping off the corner. What should you do?
options: Go, because only painted lines create a crosswalk
Honk and continue the turn
Pass the car that has already stopped
Yield; it is still a crosswalk
questions.explanation: Intersections have crosswalks even when they are not painted. A child stepping off the corner is a person you must yield to.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child is about to step into a marked school crosswalk as you approach. What should you do?
options: Stop and yield before the crosswalk
Speed up to pass the crosswalk first
Stop inside the crosswalk so the child walks behind you
Wave the child back and then go
questions.explanation: Someone about to enter a marked crosswalk has the crossing. You stop before it rather than entering the space the child needs.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The crossing guard raises the stop paddle and steps off the curb. Where should you stop?
options: You do not stop
Before the crosswalk, and stay there
Inside the crosswalk, close to the guard
Beside the guard in the opposing lane
questions.explanation: You stop short of the crosswalk so the guard and the children have the crossing. The paddle overrides a green signal. Before the crosswalk, and you stay there while the paddle faces you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your passenger says the light is green, so you should go while the guard's paddle is still up. What should you do?
options: Honk at the guard and proceed
Turn through the children on the green light
Refuse and remain stopped
Go, because a passenger and a green light agree
questions.explanation: The guard is controlling the crossing in person. A green light does not cancel a stop paddle held toward you. The paddle overrides the signal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: It is dark, a school event is letting out, and you see the fluorescent yellow-green school pentagon. What should you do?
options: Ignore it because school warnings apply only in daylight
Read it as a county route number
Speed up because the event is almost over
Treat it as a school warning and scan for children and a guard
questions.explanation: The pentagon means a school area or crossing is ahead at whatever hour you see it. Darkness makes the children harder to see, not less important.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Rain is falling in an active school zone, and children in hoods are near the crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Obey the school speed and expect surprises
Use a faster pace
Honk so they look up
Pass a slowing car beside the crosswalk
questions.explanation: Rain and hoods reduce what children can see and what you can see. The posted school speed and a covered brake are the right response. Obey the posted school speed and expect a child to move without looking.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are stopping for children at a school crosswalk. Where should the car be?
options: Stopped in the opposing lane to get a better view
Stopped before the crosswalk
Stopped with the front wheels inside the crosswalk
Stopped on the far crosswalk after rolling through
questions.explanation: Blocking the crosswalk forces children to walk around your car into live lanes, so you stop short of it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: On a narrow street the school bus stop arm reaches toward your lane, and the red lights are flashing. What should you do?
options: Drive around the arm in the oncoming lane
Stop with your bumper under the stop arm
Stop well back until the lights quit
Squeeze past the arm if your mirror can clear it
questions.explanation: The arm and the red lights close your lane. Stopping well back leaves room for children to cross in front of the bus. Stop well back and stay there until the lights quit and the arm is withdrawn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Two school buses are ahead. One shows red lights and a stop arm, and the other still shows yellow lights. What should you do?
options: Pass both, because they disagree with each other
Stop only for the yellow lights and pass the red lights
Pass the red-light bus on the right and watch the other one
Stop for the red-light bus
questions.explanation: Red lights and an extended arm require the stop. Yellow lights on the second bus mean another stop is about to happen, so you do not rush.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You stopped for the full school-bus warning. The lights then stop, the arm folds, and another child runs from the sidewalk. What should you do?
options: Wait for that child
Go at once, because the arm is the only thing that matters
Honk so the child stops running
Steer around the child in the opposing lane
questions.explanation: The lights and the arm tell you when the bus release happens, but a child who then enters the road is still a person you must not hit. Do not move just because the mechanical warning has ended.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You remember a school speed from your hometown and see a different number on this town's school speed sign. Which do you follow?
options: The number on the sign in front of you
The hometown number
Whichever number is faster
Neither number if no children are standing in the lane
questions.explanation: School speeds are posted locally. The sign you are looking at is the one that controls this zone.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A flashing yellow beacon is mounted with a school warning, not at a railroad, and the school speed plaque is visible. What should you do?
options: Pass cars that are slowing for the zone
Obey the posted school speed and watch for children
Stop on the rails that are not there and wait for a train
Ignore the plaque
questions.explanation: A school beacon activates the school warning or the posted school speed. It is not a railroad flashing red light, and it is not a reason to rush.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You can see alternating red lights on a yellow school bus, and glare hides the stop arm. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right while you look for the arm
Honk for a clearer view and keep moving
Stop and wait
Go until you can see the arm itself
questions.explanation: Alternating red lights on the school bus require you to stop even if glare hides the arm. You also wait until the arm, once seen, is withdrawn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are tempted to drive around a school bus stop arm because the oncoming lane looks empty. What should you do?
options: Use the empty lane to go around the arm
Use the shoulder on the bus's right side
Follow a driver who is already going around the arm
Stay stopped; do not drive around the stop arm
questions.explanation: An empty-looking lane can still hide a child in front of the bus. The stop arm closes the road until it is withdrawn and the lights stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to turn left across the front of a school bus that has the stop arm out. What should you do?
options: Wait until the arm is withdrawn
Turn quickly before a child steps off
Honk and turn in front of the bus
Use the oncoming lane to finish the turn
questions.explanation: A left turn across a loading bus cuts through the place children cross. You wait for the full release of the lights and the arm.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A driveway faces a school bus that is loading with red lights and the stop arm out. You are in that driveway. What should you do?
options: Turn the opposite way along the bus while the arm is out
Stay in the driveway until it ends
Enter the street between the children and the bus
Honk and edge out until the children move
questions.explanation: Leaving a driveway into a loading zone puts you in the children's path. You wait for the warning to end and for the path to be clear. Stay in the driveway until the lights stop, the arm is withdrawn, and no child is in your path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: No crossing guard is on duty, the sign says the school speed applies when children are present, and children are walking toward the school. What should you do?
options: Use any pace you like
Honk to move the group onto the grass
Pass vehicles that have slowed for the children
Obey the posted school speed and watch the crosswalk
questions.explanation: The sign, not the presence of a guard, tells you when the posted school speed applies. Children present means you obey that number.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: In summer the school beacons are dark, and the sign says the school speed applies only when the beacon flashes. No children are around. What should you do?
options: Follow the sign
Drive without looking
Stop in the lane until autumn
Treat the pentagon as a county route and add speed
questions.explanation: The sign tells you when the posted school speed applies. A dark beacon under a when-flashing legend means you do not invent a stop, and you still watch the road. The special school speed is not active, and you still remain attentive.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A school bus has not turned on its loading lights yet, but children are already crossing the street toward it. What should you do?
options: Yield to those children now
Go, because the red lights are still off
Honk so the children return to the curb
Pass the bus on the left while the children cross
questions.explanation: The lights and the arm are the bus rule, but a child already in the road is a person you must yield to immediately. Do not wait for a light that has not come on.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your signal is green at a school crossing, and a group of children is still in the crosswalk with the guard. What should you do?
options: Turn through the group
Stop and wait
Go on the green and let the children finish behind you
Honk and enter the crosswalk
questions.explanation: A green light never authorizes you to hit or crowd children. The guard and the occupied crosswalk keep you stopped.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You can see the school bus stop arm extended toward your side on a two-lane street. What does that arm require?
options: A stop only if you are behind the bus
Nothing, if you do not see a child at that exact moment
A full stop until the arm is withdrawn and the red lights have stopped
A tap of the brake and then a slow pass
questions.explanation: The extended arm is the stop device. You stay stopped through the lights and the arm because a child may appear at the last second.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are at a four-way stop, and beyond it a school bus has red lights and the stop arm out on your road. What should you do?
options: Treat the stop sign as a substitute for the bus warning and go
Use the intersection to pass the bus
Honk at the bus from the stop line and proceed
After the stop sign, still stop for the bus and wait out the lights and the arm
questions.explanation: A stop sign does not replace the school-bus rule. You still stop for the red lights and the extended arm.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are following a school bus in traffic, and its yellow lights are still off. How should you follow?
options: Assume the bus will never stop on this road
Leave enough space to slow and stop when the yellow lights come on
Ride the rear of the bus so other drivers cannot pull in
Pass on the right at every block
questions.explanation: Yellow lights can come on with little notice. A tight gap leaves you no room to prepare for the stop that follows.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are going downhill toward a school bus that has just started its yellow lights. What should you do?
options: Pass now while the lights are only yellow
Shift up and hold your pace down the hill
Begin slowing now
Wait to brake until you see the red lights
questions.explanation: A downhill approach takes longer to stop, and yellow lights mean the bus is about to stop. You slow at once. Begin slowing immediately so you can stop if the red lights and the arm come out.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You thought a fluorescent yellow-green pentagon was a county route marker. What is it really?
options: A county highway number you may follow at any pace
A railroad advance sign
A sign that the school zone has ended
A warning that a school or a school crossing is ahead
questions.explanation: The pentagon shape and the fluorescent yellow-green color are for schools, not for county route numbers.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A rectangular county route marker and a school pentagon are both visible. Which one warns of children?
options: The school pentagon
The county route marker
Neither one; only a crossing guard warns of children
Both signs mean you must pass other cars
questions.explanation: County route markers identify a road. The pentagon identifies a school area or crossing so you can slow and look.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A crossing guard holds a stop paddle and also uses a whistle. What controls your car?
options: The pace of the cars that are going around the guard
The guard's stop paddle, which overrides the traffic signal
Only the whistle, and only if you feel like stopping
The green signal, if it conflicts with the paddle
questions.explanation: The paddle is the instruction to stop, and it overrides the signal even when a whistle is also used.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A line of cars has stopped for a school bus with red lights, and you are approaching from behind. What should you do?
options: Pass the line on the left
Pass the line on the shoulder
Stop beside the bus in the opposing lane
Stop with the line and do not pass it
questions.explanation: The line is stopped for children. Passing those cars can put you in front of a child leaving the bus.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The school bus is in the right lane with the stop arm out, and you are in the left lane going the same way. What should you do?
options: Move to the shoulder and pass on the right
Stop in the left lane too
Keep the left lane moving so traffic does not stack
Pass quickly before a child reaches the left lane
questions.explanation: Same-direction lanes stop together. A child can run past the front of the bus into the left lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person is about to enter a school-zone crosswalk, and you think you can clear it first. What should you do?
options: Honk so they wait
Wave them back and take the gap
Yield and let the person enter
Accelerate and clear the crosswalk first
questions.explanation: Someone about to enter the crosswalk should not have to race you. You yield because children misjudge closing cars. Do not try to beat them to the crossing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The crossing guard faces you with an open palm while standing in the crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Stop while the guard holds you
Go if your signal is green
Edge forward until the guard steps aside
Turn behind the guard through the crosswalk
questions.explanation: A guard standing in the crosswalk and holding you overrides the signal. You stop short and wait. Stop and stay stopped while the guard holds you, even if your signal is green.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The guard lowers the stop paddle, the crosswalk is empty, and the guard motions your lane ahead while your signal allows the move. What should you do?
options: Wave a waiting child to cross in front of you first
Go when the guard releases you and the crosswalk is empty
Stay stopped until the next school day
Honk before you move
questions.explanation: When the paddle is down, the crosswalk is empty, and the guard releases you, you may go. You still do not wave a child into the street.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A school bus is stopped on the shoulder with red lights flashing and the stop arm out. What should you do?
options: Pass on the left without slowing
Stop only if children are outside the bus at that second
Stop and wait until the lights stop and the arm is withdrawn
Pass, because a bus on the shoulder is off the road
questions.explanation: Red lights and an extended arm require the stop even when the bus is on the shoulder, because children cross from the shoulder to the other side.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A school bus on the shoulder has only the yellow lights flashing. What should you do?
options: Pass at pace
Stop in the opposing lane beside the bus
Honk so the driver skips the red lights
Slow down and prepare to stop
questions.explanation: Yellow lights mean the stop is about to happen. Passing now only races the moment the red lights and the arm come on. Do not rush past.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: From a hill you can see red lights flashing on a school bus you have not yet reached. What should you do?
options: Slow at once and be ready to stop before you reach the bus
Hold your pace until you can read the fleet number
Pass as you arrive if the arm is hard to see
Use the hill to coast past the bus
questions.explanation: Seeing the red lights early is a gift of time. You use it to slow, because the stop is required before you reach the bus.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A rider on a motorcycle passes a school bus that has the stop arm out. What should you do?
options: Honk and then follow
Do not follow
Follow the motorcycle around the bus
Pass on the other side from the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Another driver's illegal pass does not open the road. The red lights and the stop arm still require you to stop. Stop for the bus until the lights quit and the arm is withdrawn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The school speed sign lists hours, and you are inside those posted hours. What should you do?
options: Use a number you prefer during those hours
Treat the hours plaque as a parking rule only
Obey the posted school speed
Ignore the sign if you do not see a child in the lane
questions.explanation: When the sign gives hours, those hours are part of the rule. You follow the posted school speed rather than deciding the zone looks empty.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You are outside the hours printed on the school speed sign, the beacons are dark, and no children are present. What should you do?
options: Ignore the road
Stop and block the lane until the hours return
Pass any pedestrian who steps toward the corner
Follow the sign
questions.explanation: The sign's own hours tell you when the school speed applies. Outside them you do not invent the restriction, and you still yield to any person who enters the road. The special school speed is not what the sign is requiring right now, and still watch the roadside.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You would rather drive faster than the number shown on the active school speed sign. What should you do?
options: Use the number on the sign anyway
Add a little to the posted number if traffic is light
Match the fastest car in the zone
Ignore the sign when no guard is present
questions.explanation: The posted school speed is the limit while the zone is active. A preference for going faster does not change the sign.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: A school warning tells you the reduced speed is ahead, and you can already see the school speed sign. What should you do?
options: Pass the cars that are already easing off
Ease off to the school speed
Brake hard inside the crosswalk
Wait until a child appears and then slow down
questions.explanation: The advance warning exists so you arrive at the posted school speed instead of braking late where children cross. Ease off so you are at the posted school speed when you reach the zone.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Children are running from the right toward a school bus that has just extended the stop arm. What should you do?
options: Honk so they stop running
Turn in front of them to leave the street
Stop until the children are clear
Continue if you can clear before they reach your lane
questions.explanation: Running children and an extended arm are the reason the stop exists. You wait out both the device and the children. Stop and stay stopped until the lights quit, the arm is withdrawn, and the children are out of the road.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The oncoming lane is empty, and a school bus ahead of you in your lane has the stop arm out. What should you do?
options: Stop behind the bus
Pass in the oncoming lane
Pass on the right
Stop beside the loading door
questions.explanation: You do not pass a bus that is displaying the stop arm, even when the other lane looks empty.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A narrow undivided street has a school bus facing you with red lights and the arm out. What should you do?
options: Meet the bus in the middle of the street
Stop; this street is not a divided highway with a far-side exception
Continue, because narrow streets are too tight for the bus rule
Climb the curb to get around the arm
questions.explanation: An undivided street gives you no far-side exception to guess about. You stop until the lights quit and the arm is withdrawn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You planned a right turn on a green light, and the crossing guard is still holding the stop paddle for children. What should you do?
options: Delay the turn until the guard releases traffic
Turn on the green in front of the children
Use the crosswalk as part of the turn
Honk and turn behind the guard
questions.explanation: The paddle overrides the green light, including a turn you already planned.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A fluorescent yellow-green pentagon stands beside an active school speed plaque. What do the two signs tell you together?
options: You may choose either sign and ignore the other
The plaque ends the school zone
Obey the plaque speed in the school area
The pentagon is a county route and the plaque is optional scenery
questions.explanation: The pentagon is the school warning, not a route marker, and the plaque is the posted school speed you obey when the zone is active. A school area is ahead, and you obey the number on the school speed plaque while it is in effect.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: The stop arm is out and you have stopped. A driver behind you pulls onto the shoulder to go around. What should you do?
options: Stay stopped; do not follow that driver around the bus
Follow on the shoulder so you are not left behind
Move left and pass together
Honk and then follow
questions.explanation: Another driver going around a stop arm does not make a safe path. You stay stopped until the lights quit and the arm is withdrawn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Yellow lights are flashing on the bus, and a solid line of children is walking toward it from a school driveway. What should you do?
options: Honk so the line waits
Slow down and prepare to stop
Pass the children before the red lights start
Turn into the school driveway through the group
questions.explanation: Yellow lights plus children approaching the bus mean the stop is imminent. You slow now instead of racing the group.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are unsure whether the red lights you see belong to a school bus or to some other vehicle, and you then see the school bus stop arm. What should you do?
options: Pass while you identify the vehicle
Stop on the crosswalk and then decide
Stop for the school bus
Go, because you were unsure at first
questions.explanation: Once you recognize the school bus warning, the stop is required. Early doubt is not a reason to be beside the bus when the arm is out.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A school crossing guard is substituting for a broken walk signal and is holding traffic with the paddle. What should you do?
options: Go, because a dark walk signal means the crossing is closed to the guard
Follow only the cars that ignore the paddle
Treat the paddle as a yield and roll through
Obey the paddle even though the walk signal is dark
questions.explanation: The guard's paddle overrides the signal equipment, including a signal that is dark. You stop while the paddle faces you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The school zone crosswalk is occupied, and the car beside you starts to roll. What should you do?
options: Honk at the children and follow
Stay stopped until it is clear
Roll with the other car
Pass that car inside the crosswalk
questions.explanation: Another car's impatience does not clear a crosswalk. You remain stopped because the children are still in it. Stay stopped until the crosswalk is clear, even if the other car rolls.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You see the school pentagon, then a crossing guard at the next intersection. What should you do as you approach?
options: Pass traffic before the guard looks up
Honk to announce that you will not stop
Slow to the posted school speed and be prepared to stop for the guard's paddle
Treat the pentagon as a route marker and the guard as optional
questions.explanation: The pentagon is your early warning, and the guard's paddle is the control that can override the signal when you arrive.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A school bus turns on yellow lights, then red lights, while you are still a short distance behind it. What is the right sequence for you?
options: Pass on the yellow lights and ignore the red lights
Stop only after the bus starts moving again
Honk on the yellow lights and pass on the red lights
Slow on yellow, then stop on red
questions.explanation: Yellow means prepare to stop. Red lights and the arm mean the stop has started and continues until both are finished.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The active school speed sign is posted, and a friend in the car says no one enforces this block. What should you do?
options: Treat enforcement as the thing that creates the rule
Obey the number on the school speed sign anyway
Follow the friend's advice and choose your own pace
Pass cars that are obeying the sign
questions.explanation: The posted school speed applies because children are unpredictable, not because you expect a citation. You obey the number on the sign.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You have stopped for the stop arm. The lights go out and the arm folds, but a crossing guard beyond the bus now faces you with a stop paddle. What should you do?
options: Honk at the guard and proceed
Pass the guard in the next lane
Remain stopped for the guard
Go, because the bus warning has ended
questions.explanation: The end of the bus warning does not cancel a guard's stop paddle. You stay stopped until the guard releases you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child on foot and a child on a bicycle both approach a school crosswalk from the sidewalk. What should you do?
options: Wave both of them into the street so you can turn
Yield only to the child on foot
Honk and take the gap in front of them
Yield to both children
questions.explanation: Both children are unpredictable. You obey the posted school speed, you yield, and you do not wave either child into the street.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The school bus is loading on your side of an undivided road, and you are late for work. What should you do?
options: Stop and wait anyway
Pass because being late is an exception
Use the shoulder to save time
Honk so loading goes faster
