questions.explanation: Being late does not cancel red lights or an extended stop arm. You wait because a hurried pass is how children are struck.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are teaching a new driver who asks whether a school pentagon means the road is a county highway. What do you say?
options: No; it means a railroad crossing is immediately under the car
No; it means a school area or a school crossing is ahead
Yes; pentagons are county route markers
Yes, but only after the school day ends
questions.explanation: The fluorescent yellow-green pentagon is a school warning. County routes use a different marker, so you slow and look for children.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: Before the school speed sign, you see children near the curb and the beacon for the zone is already flashing. What should you do?
options: Pass the children before the sign
Honk to move them off the curb
Be at the school speed, ready to stop
Wait until you are inside the crosswalk to slow down
questions.explanation: A flashing beacon means the posted school speed is in effect, and children at the curb may step out before you reach the sign.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A motorcycle is riding in the left portion of your lane, with open pavement on its right. What should you do?
options: Share the lane side by side
Honk until the rider moves onto the edge line
Pass the rider inside the same lane
Leave the rider the whole lane
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane. Riding to one side is for the rider's view and escape space, not an invitation to share the lane. Do not pull up beside them.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You want to move forward beside a motorcycle that is already using your lane. What should you do?
options: Stay behind in your lane and do not crowd the rider
Pull up level with the rider to save space
Use the shoulder to pair up beside the motorcycle
Honk so the rider makes room for two
questions.explanation: You do not share a lane side by side with a motorcycle. Crowding removes the space the rider needs to avoid a hazard.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are turning left at an intersection, and a single headlight is approaching in the oncoming lane. What should you do?
options: Honk and turn
Turn and leave the motorcycle to brake
Wait; it may be a motorcycle
Turn in front of it
questions.explanation: A single headlight is often a motorcycle, and it is easy to misjudge. You wait rather than turning left across the rider.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are following a motorcycle in the same lane on dry pavement. What gap should you keep?
options: A gap small enough that other drivers cannot pull in
No extra gap
A gap that puts your bumper beside the rider's saddle
A generous gap, larger than you would use to crowd the rider
questions.explanation: A motorcycle can be hidden by your hood if you follow too closely, and a short gap leaves you no room if the rider brakes for a hazard you do not see. You can stop without hitting them.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At night an oncoming vehicle shows one headlight in the through lane. How should you read it?
options: Treat it as a possible motorcycle and give it a full lane
Assume it is a car with a burned-out lamp that is still far away
Move toward the center so you can see past the light
Flash and hold the center line
questions.explanation: One headlight may be a motorcycle that is closer than a distant car. You keep your lane and do not turn or crowd across its path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are about to pass a motorcycle on a multi-lane road, and the left lane is open. What should you do?
options: Squeeze past in the same lane
Pass on the right shoulder
Stay beside the rider for a long time
Change lanes fully to pass
questions.explanation: The safe pass gives the rider a full lane by changing lanes. You do not share the lane during the pass, and you return only when the mirror shows you are clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You looked once to the left at an intersection and are ready to turn across a gap. What should you do about motorcycles?
options: Look again for a motorcycle that a quick glance can miss
Turn, because one look is enough when the gap seems wide
Honk through the turn
Turn and correct later if a rider appears
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to hide behind a post or a mirror. A second look is what keeps you from turning across the rider.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Rain is falling, and a motorcycle is ahead in your lane. What should you change?
options: Honk so the rider moves to the shoulder
Open a larger gap and avoid passing in the same lane
Follow more closely so the rider blocks the spray
Pass in the same lane while the paint is wet
questions.explanation: Wet pavement reduces a motorcycle's grip. Extra space is how you avoid hitting the rider if a tire slips. The rider has less traction.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A motorcyclist is beside your front fender in the same lane as traffic starts to move. What should you do?
options: Move right until the rider has to leave the lane
Accelerate while you are still beside the rider
Drop back and give the rider the lane
Hold the side-by-side position to save a car length
questions.explanation: Side-by-side in one lane is not sharing the road correctly. You drop back so the motorcycle has the full lane. Drop back and give the rider the lane rather than staying beside them.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You can pass a bicyclist by moving into a clear left lane. What should you do?
options: Stay in the bicyclist's lane and pass with a small gap
Honk and pass without moving over
Pass on the right between the rider and the curb
Change lanes and pass from the other lane rather than squeezing by
questions.explanation: When a lane change is available, that is how you leave a wide gap. Squeezing past in the same lane crowds the rider.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The left lane is full, and the only way past a bicyclist is a tight move inside the same lane. What should you do?
options: Wait behind the rider
Squeeze through the same lane
Pass on the right along the curb
Honk until the rider moves off the road
questions.explanation: If you cannot leave a wide gap, you do not force the pass. Exact clearances are state rules, so the national practice is to wait or change lanes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are preparing to turn right, and a bicyclist is riding straight in the bike lane beside you. What should you do?
options: Use the bike lane to start the turn early
Yield to the through rider
Turn immediately across the bike lane
Honk so the rider waits while you turn
questions.explanation: The through rider has the bike lane. A right turn across that rider is a common crash, so you let them pass before you turn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A bike lane is marked along the curb on your route. What is the lane for?
options: A passing lane for cars in heavy traffic
A shoulder you may use whenever the travel lane is slow
Bicycles; do not drive in it and do not park in it
A temporary parking lane when the curb looks open
questions.explanation: A bike lane is reserved for bicycles. Driving or parking in it forces riders into the travel lane or into your doors.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You need to unload a passenger next to a marked bike lane. What should you do?
options: Stop in the bike lane
Park in the bike lane with the hazard lights on
Block the lane and let the passenger out on the left
Choose a legal stopping place outside the bike lane
questions.explanation: A short stop is still parking or standing in a lane that belongs to bicycles, so you find a legal place instead.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your car is beside a bike lane, and you are about to open the driver's door. What should you do first?
options: Look for a bicyclist and open the door only when the lane is clear
Open the door quickly and look afterward
Open the door without looking if you hear no bell
Leave the door open into the bike lane while you gather your things
questions.explanation: A door opened into a bike lane can throw a rider into traffic. You look first because the rider may be in the space the door will sweep.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A shared-lane marking, a sharrow, is painted in the travel lane with a bicyclist riding in the center of that lane. What should you do?
options: Pass inside the same lane
Pass only by changing lanes
Expect the rider to hug the curb
Honk until the rider moves right
questions.explanation: A sharrow means bicycles and cars share the lane and the rider may ride away from the curb. You do not squeeze them. Accept that the rider may use the full lane, and pass only by changing lanes or leaving a wide gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have just passed a bicyclist and you want to turn right at the next driveway. What should you do?
options: Turn only once the rider is clear
Turn right immediately across the rider's path
Brake and turn from inside the rider's lane
Honk and turn at the same time
questions.explanation: A pass that ends in an immediate right turn cuts the rider off. You turn only when you are no longer crossing their path. Finish the pass with a wide gap and turn only after the rider is not beside your turn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child on a bicycle wobbles away from the curb on a street with no extra lane. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right of the child
Wait behind the child until you can leave a wide gap
Squeeze past before the wobble gets wider
Honk so the child snaps back to the curb
questions.explanation: Children wobble. A tight pass in the same lane has no spare room if the bicycle moves sideways, so you wait.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You and a bicyclist arrive together at a stop sign, and the rider is on your right. Who goes first?
options: Whoever honks first
The bicycle, only if it is in a bike lane and never at a stop sign
The rider on the right, the same as another vehicle on your right
You, because a car outranks a bicycle
questions.explanation: A bicycle is a vehicle at a stop sign. The driver on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A buffered bike lane has a hashed strip between the bike lane and your lane. What is that buffer for?
options: A car passing lane when traffic is slow
A parking strip for short errands
A shoulder you may use to pass a truck
It is part of the bicycle space
questions.explanation: The buffer is not leftover pavement. It is part of the bike facility, so occupying it crowds the rider. Do not drive, stop, or park in the lane or the buffer.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are turning left, and a bicyclist is approaching straight toward you in the oncoming lane. What should you do?
options: Honk and turn
Turn into the bike lane on the far side ahead of the rider
Wait until the rider has passed
Turn if you think the rider can brake
questions.explanation: A left turn across a through rider is the same conflict as turning across a car, with a person who is harder to see. You wait.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person is in a marked crosswalk at mid-block. What should you do?
options: Go if the crosswalk is not at a corner
Honk so the person hurries
Pass another car that has stopped for the crosswalk
Stop and yield until that person has cleared your lane
questions.explanation: A marked crosswalk works mid-block as well as at a corner. You yield, and you do not pass a vehicle that has already stopped for the person.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An intersection has no painted crosswalk, and a person is stepping off your right-hand corner. What should you do?
options: Yield to the person
Go, because paint is what creates every crosswalk
Honk and complete your turn in front of the person
Wave the person back to the sidewalk
questions.explanation: Intersections have crosswalks even when the lines are missing. A person stepping off the corner is about to cross, so you yield.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person is standing at the curb of a marked crosswalk and looking to enter it as you approach. What should you do?
options: Stop inside the crosswalk and then discuss it
Yield and let them enter
Accelerate through before they step off
Honk so they stay on the curb
questions.explanation: The duty covers a person who is about to cross, not only a person already in the middle. You slow and yield. Yield and let them enter rather than trying to clear the crosswalk first.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The car ahead is stopped at a crosswalk, and you cannot see the far side of that car. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right between the car and the curb
Honk and move up beside the car
Stop behind it and do not pass
Pass on the left to see what is happening
questions.explanation: Never pass a car stopped for a pedestrian. The stopped car is often the only clue that a person is in the crosswalk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person with a white cane is at the corner and starting into the crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Honk so they know it is their turn
Wave them across and then roll forward
Drive around them through the opposing lane
Stop and yield
questions.explanation: A white cane means a blind pedestrian. You stop and yield. A horn is not a safe go signal, because they may not know which vehicle honked. Do not honk as a signal for them to go.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pedestrian is crossing with a guide dog, and you want them to know you are waiting. What should you do?
options: Stay stopped and quiet until they and the dog have crossed
Honk once as the signal for the dog to move
Call out and edge into the crosswalk
Pass on the left while the dog is in the lane
questions.explanation: A guide dog and a blind pedestrian need a predictable stopped car, not a horn telling them to go. You yield until they are clear. Do not honk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person using a wheelchair is entering a marked crosswalk from the sidewalk. What should you do?
options: Stop in the crosswalk ramp they are using
Yield the same as you would to any other person about to cross
Go, because a wheelchair should use a driveway instead
Honk so they speed up
questions.explanation: A wheelchair user in or entering a crosswalk is a pedestrian. You yield and you do not block the ramp.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are turning right on a red light, and a person is in the crosswalk you must cross. What should you do?
options: Honk and turn behind them while they are still in the crosswalk
Use the crosswalk as a second lane for the turn
Stay stopped and yield to the person before you turn
Turn on the red in front of the person
questions.explanation: A right turn on red still requires you to yield to people in the crosswalk. The red light's turn permission does not move them.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Traffic is stopped ahead, and the only place your car will fit is inside the crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Stop in the crosswalk and let people walk around the car
Creep into the crosswalk so you are ready
Block the crosswalk
Wait behind the crosswalk until there is room beyond it
questions.explanation: A car sitting in the crosswalk forces people into the travel lanes. You enter only when you can clear the crosswalk completely.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A large truck ahead of you swings left and then starts a right turn. What should you do?
options: Stay back and do not move into the open space on the truck's right
Use the gap on the truck's right to pass
Pull up beside the truck's rear wheels on the right
Honk and squeeze through the gap
questions.explanation: Large trucks need a wide path for right turns and often swing left first. The gap on their right is where the trailer will go, not a passing lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are beside the right side of a tractor-trailer that has its right turn signal on. What should you do?
options: Honk and hold your position
Drop back immediately so you are not in the space the trailer must use
Stay beside the trailer and accelerate through the turn
Move closer to the trailer so other cars can pass you
questions.explanation: The trailer will sweep the right side as the truck turns. Staying there traps you between the trailer and the curb.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are following a large truck and you cannot see either of its mirrors. What does that mean?
options: The driver can see you better than if the mirrors showed your car
You are in the safest place to follow
You should move closer so a mirror can pick you up
The driver cannot see you
questions.explanation: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you. Dropping back puts you out of the rear no-zone.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are passing a long truck and you have been beside its trailer for several seconds. What should you do?
options: Finish the pass and do not linger beside the trailer
Hold a position beside the trailer so you can draft
Drop into the right no-zone and stay there
Honk and remain alongside
questions.explanation: The side of a truck is a no-zone. Lingering there means the driver may not see you if the truck needs to move over.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A large truck is merging from an entrance ramp beside you. What should you do?
options: Move onto the shoulder so the truck can take your lane at once
Honk and hold the exact gap you have
Adjust speed so the truck can merge
Speed up and close the gap the truck needs
questions.explanation: Trucks need more room and more time to merge. Closing the gap traps a vehicle that cannot stop or swerve like a car. Adjust speed so the truck can finish the merge with space, instead of squeezing it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A truck is turning right from a position left of the curb, leaving a tempting opening near the sidewalk. What should you do?
options: Do not take that opening
Drive into the opening and turn right with the truck
Park in the opening until the truck leaves
Honk and claim the opening
questions.explanation: The truck offset itself to make the turn. Moving into the right-side gap puts you where the trailer must swing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You see a horse and rider on the right shoulder of a two-lane road as you approach from behind. What should you do first?
options: Pass at your current pace with little extra room
Slow early, and do not honk or rev the engine
Honk early so the horse knows you are there
Rev the engine and pass close
questions.explanation: Horses startle at noise and at cars that appear suddenly. Slowing early, without a horn or a rev, keeps the animal from jumping into your lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A tractor ahead is displaying a slow-moving-vehicle emblem. What should that emblem change in your driving?
options: Treat the emblem as a sign that the tractor will pull over immediately
Honk until the tractor leaves the pavement
Pass on the right shoulder at once
Slow early and pass without crowding it
questions.explanation: The emblem marks a vehicle that cannot keep the pace of traffic. You slow early and pass only when you can do it without crowding.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Three people are riding horses abreast of one another on a narrow road. What should you do?
options: Slow early and pass with a wide gap
Honk so they form a single file at once
Rev the engine as you pull alongside
Pass between two of the horses
questions.explanation: A group takes more width and more time. Noise or a pass through the middle can frighten more than one animal into your path. Slow early, stay back, and pass only when the whole group can be given a wide uncrowded gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A wide piece of farm equipment is moving slowly and taking part of your lane. What should you do?
options: Rev the engine and stay beside it
Use the ditch side to force a gap
Slow early and pass without crowding it
Honk and squeeze past on the right
questions.explanation: Farm equipment is wide and slow. Crowding it can catch a mirror, a wagon, or an oncoming vehicle, so you wait for a real gap. Slow early and pass only when you can do it without crowding the equipment.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are about to pass a horse and rider on a straight, empty road with a full lane available. What should you avoid during the pass?
options: Leaving a wide gap
Slowing before you start the pass
Returning only after you are well past the horse
Honking, revving, or cutting back in close to the animal
questions.explanation: Even on a straight road a horse can shy at a horn, a rev, or a car that dives back too soon. You pass quietly and with room.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An emergency vehicle is approaching from behind with flashing lights and a siren on an undivided road. What should you do?
options: Pull to the right and stop until it has passed
Speed up so you can turn off before it reaches you
Stop in the center of the lane
Follow it closely once it passes
questions.explanation: Lights and a siren mean you clear the way by pulling right and stopping. Speeding ahead or stopping in the lane blocks the response.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in the middle of an intersection when you hear a siren and see an emergency vehicle approaching behind you. What should you do?
options: Back up through the intersection
Turn left across the emergency vehicle's path
Clear the intersection, then pull right
Stop immediately and block the intersection
questions.explanation: Stopping inside the intersection boxes the emergency vehicle in. You clear the crossing if you can, and only then pull right and stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with lights and a siren is coming toward you on a two-lane road. What should you do?
options: Follow it after it passes by making a U-turn onto its path
Pull to the right and stop
Pull left so it can use the right shoulder
Hold the center line and slow only a little
questions.explanation: Oncoming emergency traffic still needs your side of a two-lane road clear. Pulling right and stopping gives that path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A curb and parked cars keep you from pulling fully onto the right shoulder as a siren approaches. What should you do?
options: Stop in the opposing lane
Drive onto the sidewalk at speed
Move as far right as you can
Keep driving at pace
questions.explanation: The goal is to open a path and stop. If the shoulder is blocked, you still get as far right as you can rather than continuing in the lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: After an ambulance passes, you see a fire truck with lights and a siren a short distance behind it. What should you do?
options: Pull out between the two vehicles
Follow the ambulance so you are ahead of the fire truck
Use the gap to turn left
Remain pulled to the right until the fire truck has also passed
questions.explanation: Emergency vehicles often travel in pairs. Pulling out between them puts you in the path of the second one.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A police car is stopped on the shoulder ahead with its emergency lights flashing, and the next lane is open. What should you do?
options: Move over one lane if you can do it safely
Stay in the lane next to the police car at your present pace
Stop beside the police car in the travel lane
Use the shoulder on the police car's side to squeeze by
questions.explanation: Move-over practice says you change lanes away from a stopped emergency vehicle when that move is safe, because people may be standing at the lane edge.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The lane beside you is full, so you cannot move over from a stopped ambulance on the shoulder. What should you do?
options: Pass partly on the shoulder
Slow down as you pass
Hold your pace
Stop in the travel lane next to the ambulance
questions.explanation: When a lane change is not safe, you slow down and give the stopped vehicle room. There is no single national speed to quote for that slowdown. Slow down as you pass, without inventing a special number, and do not crowd the shoulder.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A tow truck is working a disabled car on the shoulder with its warning lights on. What should you do?
options: Stop in the lane to watch the hookup
Use the shoulder to pass the tow truck
Move over a lane if you can do it safely
Pass close because a tow truck is not an emergency vehicle
questions.explanation: A service vehicle stopped on the shoulder with people beside it needs the same move-over response: change lanes if you can, and slow down if you cannot.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A highway service vehicle is stopped on the shoulder with lights flashing, and a worker is at the rear of a car. What should you do?
options: Pass at your present pace in the adjacent lane
Honk so the worker steps behind the car
Drive between the worker and the disabled car
Move over, or slow if you cannot
questions.explanation: The worker is standing where a mirror or a drift can reach them. Moving over or slowing is what creates room.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Two lanes are open to the left of a stopped fire truck on the right shoulder. What should you do?
options: Stop in the lane closest to the truck
Move over at least one lane if the move is safe
Stay in the lane next to the truck
Move right onto the shoulder in front of the truck
questions.explanation: With an open lane you use it. The lane beside a stopped emergency or service vehicle is where people step out.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your passenger is about to open the right door into an empty-looking bike lane. What should you do?
options: Let them open it quickly if you heard nothing
Open it yourself without looking to save time
Hold the door open until a rider passes around it
Have them wait and look
questions.explanation: Doors open into bike lanes from either seat. You look first because the rider is easy to miss in a mirror glance. A rider can be in the door's path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have parallel-parked next to a bike lane and are ready to leave the car. What should you do before the door opens?
options: Check the bike lane before opening
Open the door into the bike lane as you stand up
Leave the door open while you unload
Step out without looking
questions.explanation: A rider may arrive after you parked. Looking at the moment you open the door is what prevents a dooring crash. Check the bike lane and the mirror, then open the door only if it will not swing into a rider.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A bicyclist is in your right mirror and closing as a passenger reaches for the handle. What should you do?
options: Open the door halfway and hold it
Keep the door shut until the rider has passed
Open the door so the rider sees it and slows
Honk and open the door together
questions.explanation: An approaching rider owns the space the door would enter. You wait so the door never crosses their line.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are in a roundabout, and a bicyclist is already circulating in front of you. What should you do?
options: Honk and move up beside them
Use the truck apron to get around them
Stay behind the rider in the circle
Pass the rider on the left inside the circle
questions.explanation: The rider is already in the circle and may need the lane. Crowding them against the apron takes away their balance and their exit. Yield the lane and do not pass inside the roundabout by crowding the rider.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A motorcycle is in the blind spot over your left shoulder as you prepare to change lanes. What should you do?
options: Move left because the mirror was empty a moment ago
Honk and move together
Drift left and let the rider brake
Wait until the rider and lane are clear
questions.explanation: A motorcycle in the blind spot is easy to miss and impossible to share a lane line with. You wait until you can see the rider clear of the move. Cancel the lane change until the rider is visible and the lane is empty.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Two motorcycles are side by side in the lane ahead, riding as a pair. What should you do?
options: Honk until one of them leaves the lane
Give the pair the lane
Pull up between them
Pass between them and the center line with no extra room
questions.explanation: The pair is already using the full lane. Adding a car beside or between them leaves nobody an escape. Do not try to join them three abreast.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Dashed lines mark a bike lane as it approaches your right turn. A rider is coming straight through. What should you do?
options: Treat the dashes as the end of the rider's right to the lane
Turn across the dashes in front of the rider
Stop in the dashed lane and block the rider
Yield to that through rider and turn only when the lane is clear
questions.explanation: Dashes show the conflict. They do not erase the rider, so you yield instead of turning across them.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are leaving a driveway, and the sidewalk in front of you has a child on a bicycle. What should you do?
options: Wait until the sidewalk is clear before you cross it
Expect the child to stop
Honk and roll through the sidewalk
Block the sidewalk while you look for a gap in traffic
questions.explanation: The sidewalk is not a car lane. The child has the path you are about to cross, so you wait.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person with a white cane is walking in the roadway away from a corner, not in a painted crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Pass another stopped car that is waiting for them
Stop and yield
Honk so they return to the sidewalk
Drive around them without slowing
questions.explanation: A blind pedestrian in the road gets the yield whether or not paint is under their feet. A horn does not tell them where to go. Do not honk as a signal for them to move aside or to go.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A guide dog is leading a person across an unmarked intersection crosswalk. A driver beside you rolls forward. What should you do?
options: Honk so the dog team hurries
Pass the team on the left
Stay stopped until they are across
Roll forward with the other driver
questions.explanation: The guide dog team is a pedestrian movement in the crosswalk. Another driver's roll does not end your duty to wait. Stay stopped until the person and the dog are across.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are passing a bicyclist on a multi-lane street with an open lane. Which pass matches the national guidance?
options: A same-lane pass a few hand-widths from the handlebar
A pass that uses the bike lane
A pass on the right of the rider
A full lane change or a wide gap
questions.explanation: State laws differ about exact clearances, so you do not treat one distance as the national rule. You change lanes when you can, or you leave a wide gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A horse-drawn buggy is ahead on a rural road, and you can see a long empty oncoming lane. What should you do?
options: Slow early, stay quiet, pass wide
Honk from a long way back and pass close
Pass on the right between the buggy and the ditch
Rev as you pull alongside so the horse keeps moving
questions.explanation: A buggy is a slow farm vehicle with an animal that can shy. The pass is quiet, early-slowed, and wide. Slow early, avoid the horn and the engine rev, and pass only with a wide uncrowded gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person steps from a median toward your half of an unmarked intersection crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Honk and take your half
Wave them back to the median and proceed
Yield and let them finish crossing your side
Go, because they started on the median
questions.explanation: A person about to enter your half of the crosswalk is still crossing. You yield instead of making them retreat.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The truck on your right is signaling a right turn and creeping forward at a corner. You are in a car to its right rear. What should you do?
options: Move into the gap so you can turn first
Honk and hold the gap
Pass on the sidewalk side of the truck
Stay back out of the trailer's path
questions.explanation: That creep-and-swing is the start of a wide right turn. The empty-looking right side is the trailer's path. Stop back, out of the right-side gap the trailer needs.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You cannot see the front of a truck you are passing, and you also cannot see its mirrors. What should you do?
options: Stay out until the driver can see you
Return now, because the pass has taken long enough
Drop back along the truck's right side
Stop beside the cab
questions.explanation: If you cannot see the mirrors, the driver cannot see you. Returning early hides you in the front no-zone. Stay out of the return until you are far enough ahead to see that the driver can see you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A bicyclist is riding legally in the travel lane on a narrow road with no bike lane and no room to leave a wide gap. What should you do?
options: Pass on the right
Stay behind until there is room
Squeeze past at the narrowest point
Honk continuously until the rider leaves the road
questions.explanation: When the road is too narrow for a wide gap, the rider keeps the lane and you wait. Forcing the pass is the squeeze you are supposed to avoid. Stay behind the rider until a wider place lets you pass without squeezing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are parked at the curb, a bike lane is to your left, and you want to pull away. What should you do?
options: Honk and take the bike lane
Drive down the bike lane to the next gap
Yield to any rider in the bike lane
Pull out and make the rider brake
questions.explanation: The bike lane is not a launch lane. You yield to the through rider before you cross it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with lights and a siren is approaching while you are in the left lane of a multi-lane road. What should you do?
options: Stay in the left lane and slow only a little
Move farther left
Follow the emergency vehicle in the left lane
Move right, lane by lane as it is safe, and stop
questions.explanation: The clear path is usually to the right. You work right and stop rather than holding the left lane in front of the siren.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A stopped police car has its lights on, on the left shoulder of a divided highway, and you are in the left lane. What should you do?
options: Move right one lane if safe
Move left toward the police car
Stop in the left lane
Ignore it because it is on the left
questions.explanation: Move-over applies to a stopped emergency vehicle on the shoulder you are nearest. You change lanes away from it when you can, and you slow down when you cannot. Move one lane to the right if you can do it safely.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You see a white cane at the edge of your right-turn path and a guide dog in a harness. What should you do?
options: Wave the team into the turn
Stop the turn and yield to the pedestrian team
Honk so the dog leads the person faster
Complete the turn in front of the cane
questions.explanation: The cane and the guide dog both mark a blind pedestrian. You stop and yield, and a horn is not a go signal. Do not honk them forward.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are next to a large truck's cab, and the truck starts to drift toward your lane. What should you do?
options: Accelerate and hold the side of the cab
Honk and stay in the blind area
Move closer so the driver feels you there
Drop back out of the side no-zone
questions.explanation: If you cannot be seen in the mirror, the drift may be unintentional. Dropping back puts you where the driver can see you and where you have room. Drop back out of the side no-zone instead of racing the drift.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A bicyclist ahead signals a left turn from the center of the lane. What should you do?
options: Let the rider use the lane for the turn
Pass on the left during the turn
Honk so the rider returns to the curb and turns from there
Pass on the right and then turn left with them
questions.explanation: A rider who takes the lane to turn left is avoiding exactly the squeeze you would create by passing. You wait. Do not try to pass on their left as they turn.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Children are walking in a marked crosswalk, and the car in the lane beside you has stopped. What should you do?
options: Honk at the children and the stopped car
Stop too; do not pass that stopped car
Continue, because your lane was empty a moment ago
Pass the stopped car on the right
questions.explanation: A stopped neighbor lane often means a person is about to enter yours. Passing that car is forbidden for that reason.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are merging onto a freeway beside a motorcyclist who is already in the lane you want. What should you do?
options: Honk and move into their half of the lane
Use the shoulder to pass them during the merge
Yield and take a gap behind the rider
Merge beside the rider in the same lane
questions.explanation: The rider owns the full lane during your merge. You take a gap behind them rather than arriving side by side.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A person is about to cross at a corner with no paint, and you are turning right. What should you do?
options: Turn first because the crosswalk is not painted
Honk and turn
Wave the person through and turn at the same time
Yield to the person before the turn
questions.explanation: Right turns meet unmarked crosswalks at every corner. You yield to a person who is about to cross.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The emergency vehicle's siren is on, you have pulled right, and a driver behind you is still moving up in the lane. What should you do?
options: Stay stopped at the right
Pull out in front of the emergency vehicle with that driver
Move left to block the emergency vehicle
Back up along the shoulder
questions.explanation: Your stop is what keeps the lane clear. Following an impatient driver back into the path undoes the yield.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A service truck with flashing lights is picking up debris on the shoulder, and traffic beside you will not let you move over. What should you do?
options: Pass on the shoulder in front of the truck
Slow down and give it all the room you can
Hold your speed
Stop next to the workers
questions.explanation: The fallback when a lane change is unsafe is to slow down. You do not keep a highway pace beside people working on the shoulder. Slow down and give the truck as much room as the lane allows.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A bicyclist is passing a line of stopped cars on their right, in a bike lane, as you want to turn right across that lane. What should you do?
options: Turn across the bike lane between the rider and the curb
Block the bike lane with your car so the rider must stop
Sound the horn and turn across the rider
Wait; the through rider in the bike lane has the path you would cross
questions.explanation: Even when cars are stopped, a rider in the bike lane may be moving straight. You yield rather than turning across them.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You open your door a few inches and hear a bicycle brake behind you. What should you do?
options: Close the door and wait until the rider is past
Open the door the rest of the way so the rider has a warning
Step out and apologize in the bike lane
Hold the door half open
questions.explanation: The brake noise means the rider is already in the door zone. Closing the door is what gives the lane back.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A horse rider raises a hand asking drivers to slow, and you are approaching from the rear. What should you do?
options: Rev the engine as a reply
Slow early and stay quiet
Honk to answer the hand signal
Pass immediately beside the horse
questions.explanation: The rider is telling you the animal needs a calm car. You slow early and you do not answer with noise or a crowded pass. Slow early, skip the horn and the rev, and pass later only with a wide gap.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An ambulance is stopped in a through lane with lights flashing, treating someone, and a lane to the left is open. What should you do?
options: Honk for the crew to move
Use the sidewalk to pass
Move left if safe, or slow and go around
Squeeze between the ambulance and the people on the ground
questions.explanation: A working crew in the lane is unprotected. You move over when you can and you never drive through the space the crew is using. Move left into that open lane only if the move is safe, and otherwise slow and follow the path around them that does not crowd the crew.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pedestrian with a white cane hesitates at the curb. You are stopped. What should you not do?
options: You should not honk to hurry them
You should not remain stopped
You should not leave them the crosswalk
You should not watch for a second person
questions.explanation: A honk does not tell a blind pedestrian that the whole road is safe. You stay stopped and let them choose when to go. You should not honk as a signal for them to start walking.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The vehicle ahead is a motorcycle, the lane to the left is open, and you intend to pass. What is the correct shape of that pass?
options: Return before the rider appears in any mirror
Use the whole left lane, then return
Share the rider's lane for the length of the pass
Pass on the right shoulder
questions.explanation: The motorcycle keeps a full lane during the pass. You change lanes completely and come back only when the mirror says you are clear. Move fully into the left lane, give the rider their lane, and return only after you see them in the mirror.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Farm equipment ahead has a triangular slow-moving emblem and is straddling the center of a narrow road. What should you do?
options: Rev and ride the equipment's left side
Pass in the ditch
Slow early and wait for a safe pass
Honk and push through on the right
questions.explanation: The emblem means the equipment is much slower than you think, and its width leaves little room. You wait for a pass that does not crowd it. Slow early and wait for a chance to pass without crowding it or an oncoming car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are stopped for a person in a crosswalk, and the person has reached the far curb. What should you do?
options: Go while the person is still in the far lane if your lane looks free
Follow a car that is already passing you on the left
Honk to close the crossing
Go only when the crosswalk in front of you is clear
questions.explanation: Your lane may be clear a moment before the person is actually done, and another person may be behind them. You move when the crossing in front of you is clear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A large truck is stopped at a light, and you are alongside its trailer doors. The light is about to change. What should you do?
options: Do not stay beside the trailer
Stay beside the doors to be first through the intersection
Move closer to the trailer
Honk so the truck waits for you
questions.explanation: When the light changes the truck may need the lane you are hiding in. If you cannot see the mirrors, the driver cannot see you, so you leave the side no-zone. Drop back or finish a lane change so you are not in the no-zone when traffic moves.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Leaving any part of your car inside a marked crosswalk is a bad parking choice because
options: You may stand there if you stay in the car with the engine running
People on foot need that full path, and a parked car hides them from traffic
Faded crosswalk paint may be used as an extra stall when the street is quiet
A paid meter next to the stripes makes the crosswalk a legal stall
questions.explanation: A crosswalk exists so people can cross. A vehicle left in it blocks them and keeps other drivers from seeing them until they step out.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Stopping inside the intersection itself, even to wait for a passenger, is unsafe because
options: You may wait there as long as you are not actually parked and walking away
The box is available whenever the light facing you is green
You block cross traffic and can be trapped when the signal changes
An intersection is a legal loading zone if you activate the hazard lights
questions.explanation: Intersections must stay open for crossing vehicles and people. A stopped car there creates a gridlock and a blind conflict.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Using the sidewalk as a place to leave your car forces people to walk in the street because
options: Sidewalks may be used if the curb lane is already full of parked cars
Only the grass strip beside the sidewalk must be kept clear
A sidewalk is fair parking if all four wheels stay on the concrete
The sidewalk is a pedestrian path
questions.explanation: People, including those using wheelchairs or strollers, need the sidewalk. Parking there pushes them into moving traffic. A parking stall or a shoulder.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Blocking the mouth of a driveway, even by a bumper, is not an acceptable stop because
options: Residents and delivery drivers must be able to enter and leave that property
A driveway may be blocked if nobody is home and the lights are off
You may cover a driveway when you are only dropping off a package
Driveways are public loading space after the posted curb time expires
questions.explanation: A driveway is private access. Even a partial block traps the people who live or work there and invites a conflict in the lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Choosing the deck of a bridge as a parking place is prohibited because
options: Only the approach to a bridge is restricted
Bridges are narrow, have little escape room, and are not built as stalls
Bridge parking is allowed if you pull fully onto the painted line
You may park on a bridge when traffic behind you is light
questions.explanation: A bridge gives other drivers little room to pass or avoid you, and a stopped car there becomes a high-speed obstacle.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Leaving a car inside a tunnel creates a serious hazard because
options: You may stop in a tunnel to read a map if you hug the wall
Only commercial vehicles are kept out of tunnel walls and shoulders
Tunnels have limited width, poor escape paths, and confined sight lines
Tunnel parking is legal if your hazard lights are on and you stay inside
questions.explanation: A stopped car in a tunnel is hard to see in time and leaves almost no room for others to steer around it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Treating a marked bike lane as a temporary stall or standing zone is wrong because
options: Bike lanes may be used for parking whenever no bicycle is in sight
You may occupy a bike lane if your passenger door stays closed
A bike lane becomes a loading zone after dark automatically
That lane is travel space for people on bicycles
questions.explanation: People on bikes have little protection. A car in their lane forces them into faster traffic or into the door zone.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Waiting in a posted bus stop so a rider can run an errand blocks transit because
options: Bus stops must stay open so the bus can reach the curb for passengers
Bus stops are public parking whenever the next bus is not yet visible
You may use a bus stop if your own stop will last under a minute
A bus can always load from the travel lane while you hold the curb
questions.explanation: The bus needs the curb space to load and unload safely. Your car makes passengers board in the traffic lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Facing downhill beside a curb, you turn the front wheels toward the curb so that
options: The wheels should point straight ahead so the car can roll freely downhill
The front wheels should point away from the curb, the same as on an uphill curb
Wheel direction does not matter if the transmission is left in neutral
If the car rolls, the curb catches the front tire instead of releasing it into traffic
questions.explanation: Toward the curb means a roll brings the tire against the curb and stops the car from swinging into the lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Facing uphill beside a curb, you turn the front wheels away from the curb so that
options: A roll turns the front tire into the curb, which stops the car from entering the lane
The front wheels should point toward the curb, the same setting used when facing downhill
Wheels should stay straight so the car rolls back along the parking line
Uphill wheel position matters only for vehicles with manual transmissions
questions.explanation: Away from the curb lets the tire contact the curb if the car rolls backward, instead of rolling straight into traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Where a hill has no curb at all, you point the front wheels toward the right side so that
options: Wheel angle is optional on an uncurbed hill if the surface is level gravel
A roll takes the car off the traveled roadway rather than into a lane
You point the wheels left so the car stays centered if the brake slips
You leave the wheels straight
questions.explanation: Without a curb to catch a tire, the safe direction is toward the roadside, which is the right side, away from opposing traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Every time you leave a parked car, you set the parking brake because
options: Setting it wears the shoes
An automatic transmission in park makes the parking brake unnecessary
The brake is the reliable hold
The parking brake is only for steep hills and may be skipped on flat streets
questions.explanation: Transmissions can fail or be left in the wrong position. The parking brake is the habit that keeps the car from rolling. Gear position alone is not a substitute.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An automatic transmission, once you are finished parking, should be placed in park because
options: Neutral is the correct final position so the transmission does not bind
Drive is safer than park if you might need to pull out quickly
Low gear replaces park on every automatic and holds the car better
Park locks the driveline and, with the parking brake, resists a rollaway
questions.explanation: Park is the designed lock for an automatic. Neutral lets the car roll, and drive is not a parking position.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A car with a manual transmission should be left in gear when you park because
options: The engaged gear adds engine resistance that helps the parking brake hold the car
Neutral is safer so a bump cannot turn the engine over
You leave a manual in gear only when the nose points downhill
A manual should be left in park, the same lever position as an automatic
questions.explanation: There is no park lock on a typical manual. A gear plus the parking brake gives compression resistance against a roll.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Only a vehicle displaying the required credential may use an accessible parking space because
options: You may use the space if you move as soon as a person with a credential arrives
Those stalls exist for people whose disability credentials the space is reserved for
Any driver may use one if all the ordinary stalls are already taken
A credential is needed only when the space is next to a store entrance
questions.explanation: The space and its extra room are reserved. Using it without the required credential takes access away from someone who needs it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The striped access aisle beside an accessible space must stay empty because
options: You may stop in the aisle for a minute if your hazard lights are flashing
The aisle is overflow parking once the accessible stall itself is occupied
That strip is the room a ramp or wheelchair needs to enter and exit the vehicle
The stripes are a compact-car stall that anyone may use for a short errand
questions.explanation: Without the aisle, a person cannot deploy a lift or open a door wide enough. A car stopped there 'just for a minute' still blocks that room.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A one-minute stop in an accessible stall without the required credential is still wrong because
options: Short stops are allowed if the driver remains seated behind the wheel
The rule applies only after the stall has been empty for a long time
Hazard lights convert an accessible stall into a temporary loading zone
The reservation does not pause for quick errands, pickups, or running engines
questions.explanation: People who need the stall cannot use it while you occupy it. Duration and good intentions do not replace the credential.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Starting a parallel park, you signal and stop beside the open space so that
options: You nose in at once from the travel lane without lining up beside the space
You stop in the opposing lane and slide sideways across the center line
Signaling is optional if the space is the last one on the block
Drivers behind you understand the maneuver and you can back in on a controlled angle
questions.explanation: The setup position beside the space, announced with a signal, lets you reverse at a shallow angle instead of swinging wide.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: While you back into a parallel space, a controlled angle matters because
options: It lets you enter the stall without striking the cars ahead or behind or swinging into traffic
A sharp uncontrolled crank is faster and therefore safer in traffic
You should back straight in with the wheels locked fully to the right the whole way
Angle does not matter if a passenger watches only the front bumper
questions.explanation: Too much angle hits the car behind or blocks the lane; too little angle never gets you close to the curb. Control both.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Finishing a parallel park, you leave the car close to the curb with the wheels straight because
options: Touching or climbing the curb is required proof that you are close enough
A close, straight car neither sticks into the lane nor sits ready to roll on a turned wheel
You should finish with the wheels still cut hard so the car cannot be pushed
The ideal finish is several feet into the travel lane so doors can open wide
questions.explanation: Close to the curb keeps the lane clear. Straight wheels and a set brake finish the job. Hitting the curb is not the goal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Pulling away from the curb, the safe order begins with a signal, then mirrors and a shoulder check, because
options: You pull out first and signal only after the car is already in the travel lane
A shoulder check replaces the need to yield to any vehicle already approaching
Mirrors alone see every bicycle and motorcycle that is beside your rear quarter
The signal warns others, and the mirror plus shoulder check finds the blind spot before you move
questions.explanation: People in the lane, especially bikes in the blind spot, are easy to miss. Signal, look, check the shoulder, and yield before you enter.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your move from a curb space into traffic must yield because
options: Vehicles already traveling in the lane have the right of way over a car entering from the curb
The car leaving the curb has priority once the turn signal has been on
Yielding is required only when you leave a space on the left side of a one-way street
You may force a small gap if you have been waiting at the curb for a long time
questions.explanation: You are entering a lane that is already moving. The signal does not grant priority; you wait for a gap that does not make others brake hard.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Double-parking beside a car that is already at the curb is prohibited because
options: The lane beside a full curb is reserved for standing while you shop
Your car sits in a travel lane, blocks the parked car, and surprises moving traffic
Double-parking is allowed if the driver stays in the seat with the engine running
You may double-park in a two-way street if your hazard lights are on
questions.explanation: A second row of cars occupies the lane others need, traps the inside car, and creates a sudden obstacle.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: On a two-way street you park facing the same direction as traffic on your side because
options: Facing traffic is required at night so your headlights point toward oncoming cars
The rule about direction applies only on one-way streets
Parking against the flow puts your car where drivers do not expect a head-on shape at the curb
Either direction is legal on a two-way street if you are within a car length of the curb
questions.explanation: Drivers expect parked cars to point with the flow. A car facing the wrong way is confusing, harder to leave safely, and often illegal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child left in a closed car in the heat can die quickly because
options: The cabin temperature climbs far faster than the outside air, even with the windows cracked
A cracked window keeps a closed car at a safe temperature for a long errand
Children are safe inside if the car is parked in light shade
The risk begins only after the outside air feels uncomfortable to an adult
questions.explanation: A closed car becomes an oven. Cracked glass and shade do not make it safe. Never leave a child inside while you leave.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An animal left in a closed hot car faces the same cabin danger because
options: A pet may be left if you park where a passerby can see the car
Pets cannot escape the rising heat, and a short errand is still long enough to harm them
Animals tolerate closed cars better than children if water is left in a bowl
Leaving the fan on with the engine off keeps the cabin safe for a pet
questions.explanation: Heat buildup does not spare animals. Do not leave a pet in a closed car while you go inside, even for a supposedly quick stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If the car breaks down, you move it as far onto the shoulder as you can because
options: The shoulder is reserved for enforcement
A breakdown should be left where it died until a tow driver waves you over
The farther you are from the travel lanes, the less likely a passing driver hits you
You should stop in the lane so approaching drivers are forced to slow down
questions.explanation: Moving right, as far as the shoulder allows, gets you out of the stream of traffic before you tend to the car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: After you are off the roadway as far as possible, you turn on the hazard lights because
options: Headlights alone are the breakdown signal, and hazards are reserved for funeral processions
Hazards should stay off so drivers do not confuse you with a turn signal
You use the left turn signal only, even though you are not moving left
Flashing hazards tell approaching drivers your car is stopped and not traveling with them
questions.explanation: Hazards are the standard 'I am stopped' signal. They give others time to change lanes or slow before they reach you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You stay out of the travel lanes while you wait with a disabled car because
options: Standing or walking in a live lane puts you in the path of drivers who may not see you in time
The safest waiting spot is directly behind the bumper in the same lane
You should direct traffic from the center of the lane until help arrives
If the shoulder is narrow, sit on the lane line so you can watch both directions
questions.explanation: If you can wait from the shoulder side, away from traffic, do that. A person in the lane is harder to see than the car itself.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A passenger pickup that stops you in a live lane beside parked cars is still double-parking when
options: You pull fully into a legal curb space and the passenger walks to you
You use a signed loading zone for the time the sign actually allows
You stop at the curb with room ahead and behind and set the brake
You stand in the travel lane next to a car already occupying the curb
questions.explanation: The name of the errand does not matter. If a car is already at the curb and you stop beside it in the lane, you are double-parked.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A marked bike lane that continues to the corner is not a place to wait 'just to park' because
options: A bike lane may be used as a standing zone when no bike symbol is freshly painted
Riders still need that lane to reach the intersection without swerving into cars
Bike lanes expire near corners and become ordinary curb parking
You may occupy the lane if you are only unloading the trunk
questions.explanation: The lane remains a bike lane through the block. Waiting in it is the same conflict as parking in it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Tunnel shoulders and walkways are not backup parking when traffic stops moving because
options: You may park against the tunnel wall if you face the exit
Tunnels allow parking on the left walkway only
A stopped car traps others in a tunnel
Any flat pad inside a tunnel may be used once traffic speed drops
questions.explanation: Confined space, limited sight, and no real escape path make tunnel stops for parking unacceptable even in slow traffic. Even a wide spot inside a tunnel is not a stall, and a stopped car traps others in a confined space.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Bridge railings do not create a legal stall on the span, even when a shoulder looks wide, because
options: A wide bridge shoulder is designated long-term parking by default
You may park on a bridge if the railing is taller than your car
Parking is banned only on bridges that cross water
Parking on a bridge is prohibited
questions.explanation: The prohibition is about the bridge itself: narrow margin for error and no ordinary curb use. Do not treat the span as a lot. The span is still a bridge, where parking is prohibited and breakdowns should be moved off if possible.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The bus-stop zone marked by signs or paint is reserved even between scheduled buses because
options: Bus zones are suggestions unless a bench is bolted to the sidewalk
The next bus still needs the curb, and you cannot assume a long gap in service
Empty minutes between buses convert the zone into ordinary parking
You may use the zone if you can see that no bus is approaching
questions.explanation: Transit zones are kept clear continuously so the bus can curb properly whenever it arrives, not only when you happen to see one.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Sidewalk corners with curb ramps must be left clear when you park because
options: Curb ramps are vehicle loading ramps and may be blocked by your bumper
You may overhang a ramp if the sidewalk behind it remains wide
Ramps are only for construction equipment
The ramp is how people using wheels move between sidewalk and street
questions.explanation: A bumper over a curb ramp traps wheelchair users and others who cannot step off a high curb. Leave the ramp fully open.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When the curb is on your right and you face downhill, the wheel cue to remember is
options: Leave the wheels straight and rely on the transmission alone
Turn the wheels away from the curb
Turn the front wheels toward the curb so the curb can catch a rolling tire
Turn the front wheels toward the center of the street so you can pull out faster
questions.explanation: Downhill with a curb: toward the curb. That is the opposite of the uphill-with-curb setting, and the parking brake is still set.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When the curb is on your right and you face uphill, the wheel cue to remember is
options: Turn the front wheels toward the curb, using the downhill rule on every hill
Point the wheels left only if the street is one-way
Keep the wheels straight
Turn the front wheels away from the curb so a backward roll steers into the curb
questions.explanation: Uphill with a curb: away from the curb. If the car rolls back, the turned front tire meets the curb instead of the lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: On a hill with no curb, the roadside you aim the wheels toward is
options: The right side of the road
The left side, toward the centerline, on every uncurbed hill
Either side, because the lack of a curb cancels the wheel rule
Straight ahead, with the parking brake released so the wheels can be moved later
questions.explanation: No curb means there is nothing to catch a tire on the street side. Aim toward the right roadside and still set the brake. A roll leaves the traveled lanes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Setting the parking brake is part of parking on level ground, not only on hills, because
options: You set it only if you will be gone overnight
A bump, a worn park pawl, or a missed gear can still let a car move
Level ground cannot produce a roll
The brake is a cold-weather tool and is left off in warm months
questions.explanation: Most rollaways people cause are simple mistakes. The brake every time covers flat streets as well as hills.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Putting an automatic in neutral and relying on the curb alone is not enough because
options: The curb replaces both the parking brake and the park position
Neutral plus a turned wheel is required, and park is only for repairs
Neutral removes driveline resistance, and a tire can still climb or miss a low curb
Neutral is the manufacturer's parking position for automatics
questions.explanation: Use park and the parking brake. Neutral is for brief tows or special situations, not for leaving the car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Leaving a manual transmission in neutral on a hill is a rollaway risk because
options: Neutral is the strongest holding position on a manual car
A manual in neutral is equivalent to an automatic in park
You should leave the clutch pedal held down with a brick as the main brake
Neutral provides no engine braking to help the parking brake
questions.explanation: Select a gear, usually with the nose of the car considered by your state guidance, and always set the parking brake. Neutral will not hold the hill.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Someone borrowing your car still may not use an accessible space unless
options: That vehicle, as parked, displays the required credential for the person who needs it
The owner of the credential is somewhere in the same shopping district
The space has been empty for several minutes and ordinary stalls are scarce
The borrower promises to return before a credentialed driver arrives
questions.explanation: The credential has to entitle the use that is happening. A nearby owner or a short visit does not transfer the space to someone else.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Wheelchair users need the striped aisle clear on either side of the stall they are assigned because
options: The aisle is a walkway for any shopper pushing a cart during busy hours
The aisle is maneuvering room
The stripes mark motorcycle parking beside the accessible stall
You may park in the aisle if you leave your passenger door over the stripes only
questions.explanation: Ramps fold out into the striped aisle. A vehicle stopped there, even partly, can make the adjacent accessible stall unusable. A second parking space or a drop-off lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A driver with a disability credential still should not stop in the striped aisle itself because
options: The aisle is the preferred spot if your ramp is on the passenger side
Stripes are optional buffer paint with no keep-clear meaning
The credential authorizes the stall
The credential lets you park on the stripes whenever the stall is taken
questions.explanation: Even a credentialed vehicle belongs in the stall, not on the aisle. The stripes have to remain open for entry and exit.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When a sign prohibits parking during posted hours, the paint underneath does not open those hours because
options: Signs apply only to the first car and paint applies to the rest of the block
You may ignore a sign if the curb paint is worn out
The sign's words and times are the restriction you can verify on the spot
Painted curbs override signs during the middle of the day
questions.explanation: Follow the sign's times. Do not treat worn or unfamiliar paint as permission to ignore a clear regulatory sign.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Before you begin backing into a parallel space, stopping beside it lines you up so that
options: You should already be halfway into the space with the front bumper at the curb
The correct start is two lanes away so you can dive in nose-first at speed
You stop in the space ahead and then reverse along the curb without an angle
You can see the space and use a smooth reverse angle instead of a blind swing from the lane
questions.explanation: The beside-the-space start is the controlled setup. It gives you a reference for the angle and warns others with your signal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A shoulder check before you leave the curb catches what mirrors often miss, which is
options: Only the traffic signal color at the next intersection far ahead
The position of your front license plate relative to the bumper
Whether the parking brake warning lamp has burned out
A bicycle, motorcycle, or car sitting in the blind spot just behind your shoulder
