questions.explanation: Mirrors do not cover the quarter beside you. Turn and look before you pull out, then yield to whoever is already there.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If a vehicle is approaching in the lane you want to enter from the curb, you should
options: Edge out sideways until the other driver is forced to stop
Wait and yield, even though you have already signaled and checked the mirror
Enter immediately because the signal gives you the right of way
Honk and move out so the approaching driver has to slow
questions.explanation: Signaling announces intent; it does not clear the lane. The car already in the lane keeps priority until a real gap appears.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Standing in the travel lane to 'hold a spot' next to a full curb is double-parking because
options: The practice is allowed when you are saving the space for a friend
Double-parking refers only to stacking two cars in one metered stall
You are occupying the moving lane beside vehicles that are already parked
Holding a spot is legal courtesy if you stay under a minute
questions.explanation: Two abreast, with one car at the curb and yours in the lane, is double-parking regardless of the favor you are doing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Parking facing oncoming traffic on a two-way street confuses night drivers because
options: Facing traffic is safer at night
Direction does not matter at night if the street has a painted centerline
You must face traffic on a two-way street so plates can be read
Your reflectors and the shape of the car are not where they expect a parked vehicle to point
questions.explanation: Park with the flow of traffic on your side. A wrong-way car at the curb is unexpected and harder to pull out of safely.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Cracking the windows does not make a hot closed car safe for a child because
options: Children are safe if the car is white or light colored
A sunshade on the dash removes the heat danger entirely
The interior still heats rapidly, and a small opening does not keep the cabin at a survivable temperature
Two inches of open window equalizes the cabin with the outdoor air within a minute
questions.explanation: Heat stroke in a closed car happens fast. Window cracks and sunshades are not a childcare plan. Take the child with you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pet that seems comfortable when you leave can still be in danger minutes later because
options: Pets pant to stay completely safe no matter how hot the cabin gets
A water bowl prevents overheating for the length of a typical errand
If the outside temperature feels mild to you, the cabin cannot overheat
Cabin heat keeps rising after you walk away, and the animal cannot open a door
questions.explanation: Do not judge by the first minute. Closed cars heat up, and animals cannot escape. Never leave a pet inside in the heat.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Moving a disabled car even partway onto the shoulder is better than staying in the lane because
options: Each foot farther from moving traffic reduces the chance of a high-speed impact
The law prefers that you stop in the center of the lane to be more visible
You should never steer a limping car toward the shoulder if the engine has stalled
The shoulder is illegal to touch except for enforcement vehicles
questions.explanation: Get as far right as you safely can. A car fully or partly out of the lane is less exposed than one left in the stream.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If you cannot get completely off the road after a breakdown, you still should
options: Turn the hazards off so the battery is saved for the starter
Get as far onto the shoulder as you can
Abandon the car sideways across all lanes so traffic must stop
Stand in front of the car in the lane to warn drivers with hand motions only
questions.explanation: Partial refuge plus hazards is better than a sideways block. Keep yourself out of the travel lanes while you wait for help. Steer as far onto the shoulder as the car will go, use hazards, and keep people out of the lanes if you can.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Hazard lights on a shouldered car are a warning, not a substitute for getting over, because
options: Once hazards are on, you should move back into the lane to be closer to help
Hazard lights are used only while the car is being driven, never when stopped
Lights help you be seen, but they do not remove the car from the path of traffic
Hazards make it legal to stop in any travel lane for as long as you like
questions.explanation: First choice is distance from the lanes. Hazards then tell others you are stopped. One does not replace the other.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Waiting on the traffic side of a stalled car is more dangerous than the shoulder side because
options: The traffic side is the recommended place to stand so you can see oncoming cars
You should lean on the lane-side doors so your body adds brightness
Standing in the lane behind the car is the standard breakdown posture
Passing vehicles are inches away, and drivers may be looking at the car rather than at you
questions.explanation: If the shoulder side is available, wait there. Your body should not be the first object in the live lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A hydrant hidden by your tall vehicle is still blocked even if you can see the top fitting because
options: Fire crews need a clear approach to connect hoses
Seeing any part of the hydrant means the parking position is legal
Hydrants only need clearance on the sidewalk side
You may park in front if you leave the engine running for a quick move
questions.explanation: Do not park where the car would block use of the hydrant. Your state sets the clearance in feet; do not invent that distance here. A glimpse of the hydrant over your hood.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Crosswalks that are unmarked at a corner can still be a bad place to park because
options: You may park through an unmarked crossing if you honk before moving later
Only painted zebra markings create any duty to leave a corner open
People legally cross at many intersections, and a car at the corner hides them
Unmarked corners are preferred parking
questions.explanation: Do not park in a crosswalk, marked or where you would cover the path people use at the corner. Leave the crossing and the view open.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Stopping on a bridge to take a photo or a call is still parking or standing where it is forbidden because
options: The reason you stop does not change the lack of room and the surprise to other drivers
Photo stops are allowed on bridges if you stay inside the vehicle
Calls may be taken while stopped on a bridge as long as the engine is off
Bridges allow standing on the right edge during daylight
questions.explanation: Bridges are not pullouts. If you need to stop for a non-emergency, leave the bridge first and find a legal place.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An intersection that includes a crosswalk on each leg leaves no legal 'middle' for a quick park because
options: Only the crosswalk bars are restricted
The intersection interior and the crosswalks are both places you must not park
The center of an intersection is a turnaround stall if you signal
You may stop in the middle if all four crosswalks are occupied by people
questions.explanation: Neither the box nor the crosswalks are stalls. Keep the whole intersection clear for movement.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When signs mark a bus stop longer than a single car, the whole zone stays clear because
options: Only the painted tire spot under the sign is restricted, and the rest is public parking
You may fill the far end of a bus zone if the bus can nose in behind you
Long bus zones are park-and-ride stalls outside of commute hours automatically
Buses need the full length to align the doors with the boarding area
questions.explanation: If the zone is signed or painted as a bus stop, do not park in it. The length is there so the bus can reach the curb straight.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Parking across a sidewalk's continuation at a driveway cuts off people walking because
options: The sidewalk path crosses the driveway, and your car on that path blocks it
Driveway crossings are vehicle space, so people must walk around your car in the street
You may block the sidewalk portion if the driveway itself is private
Sidewalks end legally at every driveway and resume on the far side for parking purposes
questions.explanation: Do not park on a sidewalk, including the part that crosses a driveway. People should not have to step into the road to get around you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A parking space that requires you to leave the car hanging in a bike lane is not usable because
options: You may hang into the bike lane if your hazard lights remain on
You may not occupy the bike lane to complete an otherwise tight parking job
Bike lanes may be overlapped by any parked car's rear quarter
The lane is only a suggestion once parking stalls are striped nearby
questions.explanation: If the only way to 'fit' is to sit in the bike lane, that stall is not a legal option. Find a space that leaves the bike lane open.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Nose-in parking against traffic on a two-way street combines two errors when
options: Two-way streets require wrong-way parking so headlights face the curb
Direction rules apply only outside of business districts
You both face the wrong direction and leave the car where departure crosses a live lane unexpectedly
Facing the wrong way is corrected by turning the wheels toward the centerline
questions.explanation: On a two-way street, park with traffic. Wrong-way positioning makes leaving the curb a turn across surprise traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The parking brake should be set before you rely on a chock or a lucky curb stone because
options: A single stone behind a tire replaces the need for the brake and for park
Chocks are required equipment on passenger cars and the brake is optional
You set the brake only after someone else bumps your car
The brake is the primary habit every time, and a curb is only a backup on hills
questions.explanation: Set the parking brake every time you park. On a hill, add the correct wheel direction. Do not trust a random stone as the system.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Automatic transmissions left in drive at the curb can creep because
options: Drive is a moving gear, and idle power can push the car if the brake is not holding
Drive includes an internal parking lock similar to park
Creep is impossible once the wheels are turned toward a curb
Leaving an automatic in drive is the recommended winter parking method
questions.explanation: Select park and set the parking brake. Drive will try to move the car. It is not a substitute for park.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A manual car parked in gear can still roll if the parking brake is forgotten and the slope is enough because
options: Manuals cannot roll if the key is removed, regardless of gear and brake
Gear resistance helps but is not a reason to skip the parking brake
Any gear fully replaces the parking brake on every slope
You should leave the clutch disengaged with the pedal tied down instead of using the brake
questions.explanation: Use both: a gear and the parking brake. The gear is additional resistance, not permission to skip the brake.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Accessible parking vans often need extra room, which is why the striped aisle cannot be your trunk-loading zone because
options: Van stalls include the stripes as a second vehicle space
You may load groceries on the stripes if you finish quickly
Lift equipment deploys into that aisle, and your standing there blocks the lift
The aisle is specifically for shopping carts and trunk loading by any driver
questions.explanation: The aisle is operating space for the person using the credentialed vehicle. It is not a convenience strip for other errands.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A credential placard lying on the dashboard of a car that is not entitled to it does not legalize the stall because
options: Any blue paper on the dash converts an ordinary car into a legal user of the space
Placards are optional decorations once the international symbol is painted on the stall
You may share one placard across several cars that rotate through the stall
The space requires the credential that actually applies
questions.explanation: Use an accessible space only when the vehicle has the required credential for that use. A fake, expired, or misused display does not qualify. A look-alike or a borrowed display used improperly.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Stopping in the access aisle 'so the stall stays open for someone else' still blocks the person who needs it because
options: They need both the stall and the aisle, and your car in the aisle removes the aisle
Occupying the aisle is a courtesy that keeps the stall available
The aisle is the waiting lane for drivers who might be credentialed
Striped aisles are the correct place to wait for a passenger from the store
questions.explanation: Leaving the stall empty while you fill the aisle does not help. The person who arrives still cannot deploy a ramp.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Parallel parking on a street with moving traffic requires the signal before you slow sharply because
options: Signals are for turns at intersections only and are never used for parking
You tap the horn instead of signaling when you parallel park
Hazard lights replace a turn signal for the entire parallel-park maneuver
The driver behind you needs warning that you are about to stop beside a space and reverse
questions.explanation: A surprise stop and reverse causes rear-end crashes. Signal, stop beside the space, then back in with a controlled angle.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Once you are in the space, creeping forward and back to center the car is normal, but you still must
options: Finish close to the curb, avoid hitting it, straighten the wheels, and set the brake
End the creep with the car sticking well into the travel lane for easy exit
Leave the wheels fully turned and the transmission in neutral
Stop when you feel the tire bump solidly up onto the curb
questions.explanation: Adjustments are part of a careful park. The end state is still close, not striking the curb, wheels straight, brake on.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Yielding as you leave the curb includes yielding to bicyclists in the bike lane or at the edge because
options: You have priority over bikes once your turn signal is on
Bike riders are expected to stop behind parked cars until you exit
They are traffic, and they are easy to miss if you look only for cars in the mirror
Bicycles must always yield to any car that is leaving a parking space
questions.explanation: Look for bikes, signal, shoulder-check, and yield. A rider beside you has the lane space you are about to enter.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Mirrors are checked before the shoulder check, not instead of it, when you leave a curb because
options: A modern mirror replaces any need to turn your head
The shoulder check is only for freeway merges
You look over your shoulder first and never use the mirrors when parked
Mirrors show most of the scene, and the shoulder check covers the wedge they leave out
questions.explanation: Use both. The mirror sees distance; the shoulder check sees the rider or car tucked beside your rear corner.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Facing downhill with a curb, turning the wheels away from the curb is the wrong way around because
options: The front wheels should point at the centerline whenever the car faces downhill
That angle can let the car roll out into the traffic lane instead of into the curb
Away from the curb is the downhill rule, and toward the curb is only for uphill parking
Wheel direction is reversed at night for visibility
questions.explanation: Remember the pair: downhill with a curb, wheels toward the curb. The uphill-with-curb rule is the one that points wheels away.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Facing uphill with a curb, turning the wheels toward the curb is the wrong way around because
options: Uphill parking always uses straight wheels and neutral
The curb should be ignored uphill
A rolling car could steer into the street
Toward the curb is the uphill rule on every street in the country
questions.explanation: Uphill with a curb: wheels away, so a backward roll brings the front tire into the curb. Toward the curb is the downhill rule. If the car rolls back, that angle can steer it away from the curb and into the street.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: No-curb hill parking that aims the wheels toward the center of the road is dangerous because
options: The centerline direction is preferred so the car stays visible
Without a curb you must aim left on a two-way street
Wheel aim is irrelevant if you leave the car in neutral
A roll would carry the car into a traveled lane instead of off to the right side
questions.explanation: No curb: point the wheels to the right, toward the side of the road, and set the parking brake so a roll leaves the lanes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Children and animals are not safe 'just this once' in a hot closed car because
options: One exception is enough for heat injury, and there is no safe quick-errand exception
A single short stop is the situation the heat warning does not cover
The danger applies only on days when a heat advisory is posted
If you leave the radio on, the cabin stays cool enough for a child or a pet
questions.explanation: Never leave a child or an animal in a closed car in the heat. There is no 'just this once' that makes the cabin safe.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A breakdown on a curve or hill deserves even more effort to reach a visible shoulder because
options: Hills cancel the need for hazard lights if you are visible from the top
Approaching drivers have less time to see you, so distance from the lane matters more
Curves are the preferred place to stop in the lane
You should back up around the curve to the place the engine failed
questions.explanation: Get as far onto the shoulder as you can where sight distance is better if you can still do so safely, use hazards, and keep people out of the lanes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An automatic in park can still move if the parking pawl breaks or was never engaged, which is why
options: Park is fail-proof and the brake should stay released to avoid freeze-up
You should leave the car in neutral so the pawl cannot be stressed
Rocking the car after you walk away is the way to test the pawl
You set the parking brake every time instead of trusting the lever alone
questions.explanation: Redundancy is the point of the habit. Park plus the parking brake holds the car even if one system is not doing its job.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A striped aisle shared by two accessible stalls is keep-clear for both sides because
options: Either driver may need that same strip to open a door or deploy a ramp
The stripe belongs only to the stall on the left, and the right stall may overlap it
Shared aisles are public motorcycle parking between the two stalls
You may stop in a shared aisle if only one of the stalls is taken
questions.explanation: Do not occupy the stripes. They serve the accessible stalls beside them, including when one stall is empty.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A tunnel is a worse place than an open shoulder to sit with the engine idling because
options: Idling in a tunnel is safer
You should choose the tunnel over a shoulder so other drivers are forced to slow
Exhaust collects in a confined space, and the car remains an obstacle with nowhere to swerve
Tunnels are designed as climate-controlled parking structures
questions.explanation: Do not park in a tunnel. If you are disabled, get as far out of the travel path as possible and remember exhaust danger in enclosed space.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When you return to a car parked uphill against a curb, you should expect the wheels to have been left
options: Turned away from the curb, brake set
Turned toward the curb
Pointed straight, with the transmission in neutral and the brake released
Turned toward the center of the road even though a curb is present
questions.explanation: Uphill with a curb means wheels away from the curb, brake on, and the transmission in park or a gear. Check those before you release anything.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When you return to a car parked downhill against a curb, you should expect the wheels to have been left
options: Aimed at the opposing lane in case the curb is low
Turned toward the curb, with the parking brake set and the transmission holding as well
Turned away from the curb so the car can roll forward freely
Straight and in neutral so morning traffic can slide past if bumped
questions.explanation: Downhill with a curb means wheels toward the curb plus the parking brake and park or gear. That combination is what you undo carefully when you leave.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Opening a door into a bike lane after you have parked can still cause a crash, so you should
options: Open the door quickly so riders have to stop behind you
Bike lanes beside parking exist so doors can open into them at any time
Door position does not matter if you parked close to the curb
Park only where you are legally out of the bike lane and check before you open the door
questions.explanation: Being legally parked includes not occupying the bike lane. Look before opening a door so you do not send a rider into traffic or into the door.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A breakdown that leaves you partly in a lane still calls for people to exit away from traffic if they can because
options: The shoulder side, or a barrier side away from wheels, is safer than stepping out into the live lane
Everyone should exit on the traffic side so they can flag down help immediately
Passengers should stand between the car and passing traffic to add visibility
The correct gathering place is the lane directly behind the trunk
questions.explanation: Get the car as far over as possible, hazards on, and people off the travel lanes. Exit toward the safer side when that path exists.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Legal parking ends where the car, including bumpers, intrudes into a crosswalk, sidewalk, or driveway because
options: Driveway blocking requires the entire apron to be covered
Intrusion by any part of the vehicle is still blocking that space
Only the wheels count, so bumpers may cover a crosswalk or driveway
A sidewalk may be covered if pedestrians can squeeze sideways past the bumper
questions.explanation: If any part of the car blocks a crosswalk, sidewalk, driveway, bike lane, or similar forbidden area, you are not legally parked. Move.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The safe last acts after the car is aligned in a parallel space are
options: Front tire climbed onto the curb, hazards left on, engine running
Car left a full lane from the curb so others can park closer later
Wheels straightened, car close to the curb without hitting it, parking brake set, transmission in park or gear
Wheels left fully cut, transmission in neutral, brake released so the curb holds the car
questions.explanation: Finish the maneuver completely. Straight wheels, close but not striking the curb, brake set, and park or a gear are the closeout steps.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Re-entering traffic from the curb is a yield situation similar to entering from a driveway in one respect:
options: The curb gives you priority over every lane you enter
Driveways must yield but curb departures have the right of way by default
You may enter either place without looking if you signal for one second
You do not have priority over people already moving on the road you are joining
questions.explanation: Signal, use mirrors, shoulder-check, and yield. The fact that you were legally parked does not make your entry more important than moving traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A bus pulling toward a signed stop where you are tempted to wait should find that curb empty because
options: Bus stops are not short-term personal standing zones between arrivals
You may race the bus for the curb if you were there first in the travel lane
Personal cars have priority at bus stops during off-peak hours
The bus is required to go around any car that reached the sign first
questions.explanation: Do not park or stand in a bus stop. Leave the curb open so passengers can board without stepping into traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A hill without a curb still needs the parking brake even though the wheels point right because
options: The brake is used only when a curb is present to press against
Uncurbed hills are parked in neutral with the wheels straight
Wheel direction only helps if the car rolls
Pointing the wheels replaces the brake entirely on uncurbed hills
questions.explanation: No curb: wheels toward the right side, and the parking brake set every time. An automatic goes in park; a manual goes in gear. The brake is what you rely on to prevent the roll.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Accessible spaces next to building entrances are often closest for a reason, which is why
options: The closest stalls are first-come spaces for anyone in a hurry
You may use them for pickup if the building has no other curb space
Credential rules apply only to spaces far from the door
They are reserved for drivers with credentials
questions.explanation: Closeness is part of the access. Do not take that space, or its striped aisle, without the required credential, even for a minute. They are not extra convenient stalls for drivers who do not have the required credential.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If your car dies in a tunnel and will move, you should try to exit the tunnel rather than park inside because
options: A tunnel is not a place to park, and the open air beyond it gives others room to pass
The safest plan is to shut down in the middle lane and wait inside the car
Tunnels require you to park against the left wall and walk for help in the lane
You should reverse out of the tunnel against traffic
questions.explanation: If the car can still roll or creep, get it out of the tunnel and as far onto a shoulder as possible, then use hazards and stay out of the lanes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Double-parking while you 'keep the engine running so it is not really parked' is still prohibited because
options: Hazard lights plus a running engine create a mobile loading zone in any lane
The lane is blocked whether or not the transmission is in park
A running engine converts double-parking into a legal standing stop
The restriction applies only when the keys are removed
questions.explanation: Do not double-park. Leaving the engine on does not change the fact that you are stopped in the travel lane beside a parked car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The right-side aim on an uncurbed road assumes you are driving on the right, so the wheels point
options: Toward oncoming traffic so the car is seen sooner
Straight downhill so the car follows the pavement crown
Toward the right edge, away from the lanes that traffic uses
Toward the left edge
questions.explanation: Where there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the side of the road, the right side, so a roll moves off the traveled way rather than into it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A parallel park that ends with you far from the curb invites sideswipes because
options: Distance from the curb is the required national finish position
Farther out is safer
You should center the car between the curb and the centerline
The car occupies part of the lane and forces others to squeeze past
questions.explanation: Finish close to the curb without hitting it. A car left out in the lane is a moving-traffic hazard even though it is 'parked.'

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Before the parking brake is released to leave a hill space, you should already have
options: Signaled, checked mirrors, and prepared to shoulder-check and yield as you move
Released the brake first and then decided whether anyone was coming
Turned the wheels straight while still relying on gravity alone
Shifted to neutral and rolled off the curb to test the slope
questions.explanation: The departure routine does not start with a blind roll. Signal and look, keep control with the brake until you are ready, then yield your way into the lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A credential is required for the accessible stall nearest the door and equally for one farther down the row because
options: The symbol is informational and does not reserve the stall
Every accessible space is reserved
Only the closest accessible stall needs a credential, and farther ones are general parking
Far stalls with the access symbol are overflow for any vehicle after noon
questions.explanation: If the space is marked accessible, it requires the credential. Distance from the door does not turn it into an ordinary stall. Only the space with the shortest walk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When workers or a driveway gate need the full apron, a car parked just upstream can still be a problem if
options: Parking is always legal within a car length of any driveway
Only paint, not the physical driveway, can create a restriction
You may block the apron if the gate is closed for the day
The parked car blocks the driveway or the sidewalk path people use to reach it
questions.explanation: Do not park in front of a driveway. If your position blocks the apron, the sidewalk across it, or the view out, choose another space.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Checking that a manual is in gear and an automatic is in park is the transmission half of a habit whose other half is
options: Turning the wheels randomly so thieves cannot predict the direction
Parking against traffic so the car is harder to tow
Setting the parking brake every single time you leave the car
Leaving the engine idling so compression stays high
questions.explanation: Transmission position and the parking brake work together. Do both, on hills and on flat streets, every time you park.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A rider in a bike lane has nowhere to go if you stop there to read a sign, which is why
options: Brief reading stops are the intended use of a bike lane
You may stop in the lane if you pull your right mirror in
Bike lanes are standing zones whenever the adjacent sidewalk is busy
A bike lane is not a pause zone, a loading zone, or a parking stall
questions.explanation: Do not park or stand in a bike lane. Riders cannot 'just go around' without entering faster traffic or hitting your car.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Shoulder-checking over your right shoulder is part of leaving a typical right-side curb because
options: Shoulder checks are unnecessary if the passenger says the road looks clear
The blind spot on the side you are about to enter is where a passing rider or driver hides
The right shoulder check is only for cars parked on the left of a one-way street
You look over the left shoulder exclusively, even when entering the lane on your right
questions.explanation: Turn toward the lane you are entering. The mirror will not show a rider directly beside you. Then yield before you pull out.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An uphill park with a curb that also has no use of the parking brake is incomplete even with correct wheels because
options: Correct wheel direction is the only step that matters on an uphill curb
The brake is optional uphill
You should leave an uphill automatic in neutral so the wheels can work
The wheel angle is a backup if the car rolls
questions.explanation: Wheels away from the curb, parking brake set, automatic in park or manual in gear. Skip any one of those and the hill routine is incomplete. The brake is supposed to keep it from rolling at all.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A downhill park with correct wheels still needs park or a gear selected because
options: The transmission adds another hold beyond the curb and the parking brake
The curb fully replaces park, gear, and the brake on every downhill
Neutral is required downhill so the wheels can caster into the curb
Drive or first gear while the engine runs is the downhill parking method
questions.explanation: Turn wheels toward the curb, set the parking brake, and place an automatic in park or a manual in gear. All of those layers belong together.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Heat danger inside a parked car is a reason the engine-off, nobody-left-inside habit matters especially because
options: The danger applies only to vans and never to ordinary passenger cars
A closed stationary car heats up whether or not you intended to be gone only a minute
Heat injury requires the engine to be running with the heater on
A parked car stays near the outside temperature as long as it is locked
questions.explanation: Never leave a child or an animal in a closed car in the heat. Shut the car down, take passengers and pets with you, and do not treat idle time as safe.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: If you are broken down and a legal shoulder is available a short distance ahead, you should
options: Use the gore if it is closer than the shoulder
Park across the sidewalk so pedestrians can direct traffic for you
Move there if the car can
Stay in the lane
questions.explanation: The priority is as far onto the shoulder as possible, hazards on, people out of the travel lanes. Do not substitute a forbidden area because it is closer. Stop in a lane, a gore, or a bike lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A two-way street's right-hand curb is the normal parking side when signs allow, and your car should point
options: Toward oncoming traffic so you can see drivers' faces
Either direction as long as the wheels are turned toward the curb
Away from the nearest intersection regardless of traffic flow
In the same direction as traffic moving on that side of the street
questions.explanation: Do not park facing against traffic on a two-way street. Point with the flow, set the brake, and follow the hill rules if the street slopes.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The striped access aisle is not a valet lane, even at a busy entrance, because
options: Valet or casual standing there blocks the ramp space the accessible stall requires
Valet operations may store cars on the access stripes by default
The aisle is a through lane for cars circling the lot
Busy times suspend the keep-clear meaning of the stripes
questions.explanation: Only a vehicle with the required credential belongs in the accessible space, and nobody belongs in the striped aisle as a parking or standing spot.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When a sign permits parking but a driveway, hydrant, crosswalk, or bus stop falls inside that stretch, you still must
options: Block the crosswalk but not the hydrant, or the reverse, based on convenience
Keep those specific features clear
Park anywhere the general sign allows, including across driveways and hydrants
Ignore the feature if the sign does not repeat the word hydrant or driveway
questions.explanation: General permission to park along a curb does not let you block a driveway, hydrant, crosswalk, sidewalk, bike lane, or bus stop. The state sets hydrant feet; do not guess them.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Leaving the opposite wheels turned the wrong way on a curbed hill is not a small error because
options: Wrong-way wheels are safer
The hill rules are reversed from the usual teaching on purpose in most states
The curb then fails as a backstop and the car can roll into the travel lane
Any wheel angle is fine if you remembered to set the parking brake, so direction is trivia
questions.explanation: Downhill with a curb: toward the curb. Uphill with a curb: away from the curb. The 'wrong' way removes the curb's ability to catch a roll.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Choosing a space that opens only if you block a sidewalk forces pedestrians into the street, so you should
options: Block the sidewalk only with the front overhang, which does not count
Park there after dark when fewer people are walking
Reject that space and find one that leaves the sidewalk completely clear
Use the space if pedestrians can walk in the gutter pan
questions.explanation: Do not park on a sidewalk. An overhang that takes the walking path is still a sidewalk block, not a clever use of a short stall.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The departure sequence from a curb is incomplete if you signal but never turn your head because
options: Head checks are optional once the signal has been on for a moment
Mirrors are angled to remove blind spots entirely on every passenger car
You only shoulder-check when leaving a parallel space on a hill
The blind spot beside you is exactly where a person on a bike is likely to be
questions.explanation: Signal, mirrors, shoulder check, yield. Skipping the head check is how parked cars pull into riders they never saw.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Wheel direction, transmission, and brake are a three-part hill routine, and the part people skip most often is
options: The turn signal, which must stay on while the car is parked on a hill
Neutral, which should be selected on every grade before you walk away
A stone chock, which replaces the other steps on steep streets
The parking brake, which belongs on every park, hill or no hill, curb or no curb
questions.explanation: Set the parking brake every time. Add the correct wheel direction for the hill, and leave an automatic in park or a manual in gear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Correct curb parking on a two-way hill street means you are with traffic and the wheels match the slope, so downhill you
options: Point the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake
Point the front wheels away from the curb and leave the car in neutral
Park against traffic so the nose points uphill regardless of the side
Leave the wheels straight so either roll direction is equally likely
questions.explanation: Direction of parking follows traffic. Wheel direction follows the hill: downhill toward the curb, uphill away from the curb, always with the brake set.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Uphill on that same two-way street, still parked with traffic beside a curb, you
options: Ignore the curb and point the wheels at the opposing lane
Point the front wheels away from the curb, set the brake, and select park or a gear
Point the front wheels toward the curb and select neutral
Face downhill against traffic so you can reuse the downhill wheel rule
questions.explanation: Uphill with a curb means wheels away from the curb. You are still facing with traffic, not turned around to make the wheel rule feel familiar.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Without any curb on that hill, both the uphill and downhill nosing still share one wheel rule:
options: Use the curbed uphill rule even though no curb exists
Leave the wheels straight and the brake off so the car can settle
Turn the front wheels toward the right side of the road so a roll leaves the lanes
Turn the wheels toward the center on both headings
questions.explanation: No curb removes the 'catch the curb' tactic. Aim right, toward the roadside, and set the parking brake with the transmission in park or gear.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The national lesson on accessible parking can be stated without listing plate designs because
options: Without the required credential, you may not use it
Any state plate is a credential for every other state's accessible spaces
Accessible spaces are open to all cars built with more than two doors
The international symbol on the pavement invites every careful driver
questions.explanation: Only a vehicle with the required credential may park there. Do not stop in the space or the striped aisle for a minute without it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When you leave a parallel space, yielding continues until your car is fully in the lane and matched to traffic because
options: You may block the lane while you adjust the radio as long as the park was legal
Half-out is still an entry, and people already in the lane should not have to swerve around your nose
Once the front tire leaves the curb you have the right of way
Yielding ends when the turn signal is canceled
questions.explanation: Signal, mirrors, shoulder check, and yield through the whole entry. Do not take the lane until you can join without forcing others to brake hard or leave their path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: How do you measure a following gap on a dry road instead of guessing by car lengths?
options: Match the bumper ahead so closely that you can read the plate easily
Count only until you say the word one and then close the space
Count three seconds past a fixed landmark
Stay one car length back at any speed and treat that as plenty of room
questions.explanation: A following gap is time, not a hood-length guess. Choose a sign or a shadow, start counting when the vehicle ahead passes it, and do not arrive before a steady three-count on dry pavement. Pick a fixed landmark the lead car passes and count at least three seconds before you reach it.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Rain starts to film the lane while you are already using a dry-road three-second gap. What should change?
options: Keep the same three seconds
Shorten the gap so you can see the lead car through the spray
Turn the count into half a second and rely on a last-instant stop
Add more seconds to the gap
questions.explanation: Water reduces tire grip and lengthens braking. The dry three-second habit is a minimum, not the setting for rain. Drop back until the count is clearly longer.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Fog shortens the distance you can see while a car is still ahead of you. How should the gap change?
options: Increase your seconds of following time
Close up and use the lead car as a windshield you do not need space for
Hold the dry-road count
Drop the gap to a bumper length so their lights outline the lane for you
questions.explanation: In fog you may not see a stopped vehicle until it is close. A longer time gap is how you keep the stop inside the piece of road that is still visible. Increase the seconds of following time so you can stop inside the distance you can actually see.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A large truck fills the lane ahead and you cannot see past its trailer. What gap is the skillful choice?
options: Ride the blind area directly behind the doors where the mirrors show nothing
Pass on the shoulder if the truck will not speed up immediately
Drop back well beyond three seconds
Tuck close behind the trailer so the draft shortens your trip
questions.explanation: Trucks block your view and have deep blind zones. Extra seconds let you see trouble earlier and put your car where the truck driver can see you in the mirrors. Drop back well beyond a three-second count so you can see around the trailer and the driver can see you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Someone is crowding your rear bumper on a multi-lane road. How should you manage the space in front?
options: Speed up and weave so the tailgater has to match you
Brake-check them until they drop back a few feet
Move to a one-second gap in front
Open a longer gap ahead
questions.explanation: You cannot control the driver behind you, but you can avoid a sudden stop. Extra space ahead lets you slow gradually and gives the tailgater time to react. Open a longer gap ahead so you can brake gently instead of slamming to a stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: When you are stopped in a line of traffic, which front gap still gives you an escape path?
options: Where you see the car's rear tires on the road
Stop so your bumper touches the vehicle ahead and no space is wasted
Stop in the crosswalk if that is the only way to stay close
Leave so little room that you cannot pull around a stalled car
questions.explanation: Seeing the rear tires touch the road means you left room to steer around a stall and you are less likely to be pushed into that vehicle if you are hit from behind. Stop far enough back that you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead meet the pavement.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Wet leaves or loose gravel cover part of the lane you are following another vehicle through. What change is required?
options: Move closer so you can use the track the lead car already cleaned
Accelerate through the leaves to clear them from your tires
Increase the following seconds again
Keep a dry-pavement count
questions.explanation: Leaves and gravel slide under the tires and lengthen the stop. Treat them as a reason to add time, not as a reason to crowd the vehicle ahead. Those surfaces steal grip the way ice does.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The steering goes light as you cross a rain-filled stretch and the car begins to skate. What is the first control move?
options: Crank the wheel toward the shoulder while the car is still floating
Accelerate so the tires can cut through the water film
Ease off the accelerator, keep the wheel straight, and do not brake hard
Stab the brake pedal to force the tires back onto the pavement
questions.explanation: That light feeling is hydroplaning: the tires are riding water instead of pavement. Power off, a straight wheel, and no hard brake let the tread meet the road again.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You recognize standing water in the lane ahead and still have time to choose a path. What avoids a hydroplane?
options: Hold speed and aim at the deepest rut so momentum carries you through
Brake hard only after the tires have already lifted on the film
Add power in the middle of the puddle to keep the cruise setting
Slow before the water and pick a shallow path
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is easier to prevent than to fix. Shed speed before the water, and do not make a sharp turn at the last moment to dodge it. Slow before the water and choose a shallower path if you can do it without a sudden swerve.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The tires have just reconnected after a brief hydroplane and the wheel feels heavy again. What comes next?
options: Accelerate to highway pace immediately to dry the tread
Test the skid by braking to the lock point on purpose
Slow gently and keep the car pointed straight until speed matches the wet road
Yank the wheel to the shoulder now that you can feel the tires
questions.explanation: Grip returns suddenly. A hard steer or a hard brake at that moment can break the tires loose again. Ease the speed down while the wheel stays settled.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Hard braking on a water film is a poor hydroplane response because
options: Braking is useless only on dry pavement
A locked tire always finds the pavement faster than a rolling tire
The brake pedal should be pumped the whole time you are floating
Locked or overloaded tires cannot cut through the water and the car keeps sliding
questions.explanation: Brakes work through the contact patch. If water is holding the tire up, a hard application does not restore steering and can make the slide longer. Ease off and stay straight.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The back of the car swings toward the left on a slick curve. Where should you steer?
options: Ease off and steer where you want to go
Steer hard the opposite way and hold the brake to the floor
Add throttle so the rear tires can spin the car straight
Close your eyes briefly and let the wheel center itself
questions.explanation: In a skid, look and steer where you want the front of the car to go. That is the same idea as steering toward the direction of a rear skid. Lifting off the gas helps the tires regain grip.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The front tires wash wide in a corner and the car is not turning as much as the wheel. What should you change?
options: Shift to neutral and keep the wheel cranked
Ease off the gas and unwind some steering
Add more steering angle until the wheel is at the stop
Brake hard while you increase the steering input
questions.explanation: A front skid means the front tires are already past the grip they have. More lock and a hard brake demand still more grip. Soften the inputs and aim your eyes where you want to go. Ease off the gas, reduce the extra steering lock, and look along the path you still want.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Slamming the brake pedal in the middle of a skid on ice usually
options: Is the fastest way to end every skid on every surface
Is required before you are allowed to look where you want to go
Warms the ice so the tires stick immediately
Steals the remaining tire grip and can take away your ability to steer
questions.explanation: Tires can brake or they can steer, and on ice they cannot do a sudden hard version of both. Ease off the gas first and steer the front toward your intended path.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A patch of ice starts the car sliding while you are still holding a steady throttle. The skilled sequence is
options: Lift off smoothly and steer where you want to go
Downshift violently and brake to the floor at the same instant
Add throttle and steer away from the path you hope to use
Pull the parking brake up in one motion to spin the nose around
questions.explanation: The extra power is part of what is breaking the tires loose. Lift smoothly so the tires can roll again, and point the front of the car along the path you want. Lift off the accelerator smoothly, then steer toward where you want the front to go.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child runs toward the street and you must stop hard in a car equipped with anti-lock brakes. How do you use the pedal?
options: Tap the brake once and then release it for the rest of the stop
Use the parking brake only and leave the service pedal alone
Press the brake firmly and hold it down
Pump the pedal quickly so the anti-lock system can wake up
questions.explanation: ABS pumps the brakes for you, faster than your foot can. A firm, continuous press lets the system keep the tires at the edge of lock so you can still steer. Do not pump the pedal.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Why is pumping the pedal the wrong habit on a vehicle that has ABS?
options: ABS already pulses the brakes for you
Pumping is required or ABS will not arm on a wet road
ABS only works if you release the pedal between each push
Pumping is safer
questions.explanation: ABS exists so you do not have to cadence-brake. A steady firm push gives the controller the pressure it needs. Pumping fights that controller. Your pumps interrupt the system that is already releasing and applying the brakes for you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The brake pedal sinks toward the floor and the car barely slows. What sequence fits a service-brake failure?
options: Shift to neutral and coast until the car happens to stop
Yank the parking brake up in one pull and take your hands off the wheel
Switch the ignition off at once so the steering column locks
Pump the pedal, downshift, and apply the parking brake gradually
questions.explanation: Pumping can rebuild a little pressure. A lower gear uses the engine to slow the car. The parking brake must come on gradually so the rear wheels do not lock and spin you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Brakes fade on a long downgrade after you have been riding the pedal. What is the better control choice?
options: Ride the pedal harder in a higher gear until the smell stops
Turn the engine off and coast with the column locked
Shift to a lower gear so the engine holds the car and the brakes can cool
Shift to neutral so the brakes are the only thing working
questions.explanation: Fade means the brakes are overheated and losing friction. Engine braking in a lower gear takes the load off the drums or rotors. Neutral does the opposite.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You pump the service brakes during a failure and feel a little pressure return. What else still belongs in the response?
options: Downshift and ease on the parking brake
Release the pedal and accelerate
Shift into neutral and take your feet off every control
Hold the parking brake at full lock while you turn sharply
questions.explanation: Partial pressure is not a full repair. Keep pumping if it helps, use a lower gear, and add the parking brake smoothly while you aim for the shoulder or another open safe place.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A front tire blows and the car jerks toward that side. What is the first pair of actions?
options: Take your hands off the wheel and let it self-center at full speed
Grip the wheel firmly and ease off the accelerator while you steer straight
Brake hard immediately and twist the wheel toward the blowout
Accelerate so the car rides over the torn tire
questions.explanation: A blowout yanks the car. Two firm hands keep the wheel from being ripped into a swerve. Easing off the gas slows you without the extra upset of a hard brake.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Why is a hard brake the wrong instant response to a tire blowout?
options: A hard brake reseats the tire on the rim and is the preferred first move
You should brake hard and steer off the pavement at the same moment
Weight shifts and the damaged tire can lose the little grip it has, making the pull worse
Braking is wrong only when the blowout is on a rear tire in a parking lot
questions.explanation: The car is already unstable. A sudden brake can overload the blown tire and spin or dart the car. Hold the wheel, ease off the gas, and keep it straight until speed comes down.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: After a blowout the car has settled and speed is dropping with the wheel straight. When is braking appropriate?
options: Never touch the brake
Brake only after you have jerked onto the opposite shoulder
Use a full ABS stop while the wheel is cranked toward the median
Brake gently once the car is stable, then steer to a safe place off the road
questions.explanation: The danger is the first violent swerve and a hard brake at high speed. Once you are straight and slower, a gentle brake and a controlled move off the road finish the stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A rear tire blows and the back of the car starts to wag. Which response matches the front-tire lesson?
options: Hold firm, ease off, and steer straight
Steer sharply left and right to cancel each wag with a bigger one
Accelerate and brake in a quick alternation
Shift to neutral and take your hands off the wheel
questions.explanation: A rear blowout can feel like a skid. Firm hands, less power, and a straight path keep you from overcorrecting. Gentle braking comes after the car is stable. Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and steer straight rather than chasing the wag.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your right tires drop off the paved edge onto a lower shoulder. What is the safe order of moves?
options: Accelerate and climb the edge at a sharp angle
Ease off the gas, slow while you stay on the shoulder, then steer gently back when the lane is clear
Yank the wheel left immediately at the same speed you were traveling
Brake hard with the right tires still in the dirt and the left tires on pavement
questions.explanation: The pavement edge can catch a tire and sling the car across the lane if you climb it fast. Slow first, stay straight, and return with a shallow steer.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Why is a hard yank back onto the pavement after an edge drop so dangerous?
options: The shoulder is always higher than the pavement
Yanking is the method driving courses prefer at highway pace
The car can shoot across into other lanes
A yank is dangerous only if you signal first
questions.explanation: Different grip on each side plus a sharp steer makes the car pivot. Ease off, slow down on the shoulder, and re-enter gently when no one is beside you. The tire grabs the edge and the car can shoot across the lane into oncoming or adjacent traffic.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have slowed on the shoulder after drifting off and the lane beside you has a gap. How do you return?
options: Steer gently up at a shallow angle
Wait until a car is beside you and then yank across its bow
Turn the wheel to full lock and accelerate up the face of the edge
Back up on the shoulder at speed until you find a ramp
questions.explanation: A shallow angle and a modest speed let the tire climb without grabbing. Check the lane, commit smoothly, and unwind the wheel once you are fully back on the pavement. Steer gently up the edge at a shallow angle and straighten as soon as all tires are on the pavement.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Dense fog makes your high beams bounce back as a white wall. Which lamps should you use?
options: Use only the interior dome light to read the lane
Low beams, which light the road, not the fog
Leave high beams on
Turn every lamp off and drive by the glow of the instrument panel
questions.explanation: High beams aim up into the fog and glare back at you. Low beams aim lower, at the pavement, which is the part you need to see. Switch to low beams so the light reaches the road instead of reflecting off the droplets.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: In fog, how do you choose a speed that matches sight distance?
options: Speed up so you spend less time in the fog bank
Use the posted dry-road number even when you cannot see a car length ahead
Slow until you can stop within the stretch of road you can actually see
Hold your usual open-road pace and trust the car ahead to warn you
questions.explanation: If a stopped vehicle or a sharp curve sits just beyond the visible patch, only a speed that stops inside that patch will save you. Sight distance sets the pace, not habit.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Parking lamps alone in thick fog are a poor choice because
options: Parking lamps are brighter than low beams in fog
They replace headlights whenever moisture is in the air
Other drivers read parking lamps as a signal that you are stopped off the road
They do not light the road for you and they do not make the car as visible as headlights
questions.explanation: Parking lamps are for a parked car, not for seeing or being seen in fog. Low-beam headlights do both jobs better.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Fog becomes so thick that you cannot see far enough to continue safely. Where should you stop?
options: Keep rolling at a walking pace in the middle of the lane with the lamps off
Leave the travel lane at a safe pull-off
Stop in the lane and leave high beams on so people can aim at you
Stop on a curve if that is where the fog is thickest
questions.explanation: A car stopped in a live lane is an obstacle other fog-bound drivers cannot see in time. Get fully off the road, then make the car visible without inviting people to follow you into a ditch. Do not stop in the lane where others will find you too late.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are tempted to hang close behind another car's taillights to find your way through fog. Why is that a bad gap?
options: Fog makes the lead car's stop shorter than yours
Following time is not needed when you can see their lamps at all
You no longer have enough room to stop
Taillights are a recommended target to follow at less than one second
questions.explanation: Those lamps can disappear into a driveway or stop suddenly. Low beams plus a gap you can stop inside beat a tight chase through fog. You are using their lamps as a guide and you no longer have enough seconds to stop if they do.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An oncoming driver leaves high beams on and your eyes start to sting. Where should you look?
options: Stare at the oncoming lamps so your eyes adjust faster
Look at the oncoming driver's face as you pass
Close your eyes until you feel the car pass
Look toward the right edge of your lane
questions.explanation: Looking at the glare wipes out your night vision. The right edge line still shows you where your lane is. Ease off so you can stop inside the distance you can still see. Into the lamps, and slow if your sight has shrunk.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The oncoming high beams feel hostile. What should you do with your own beams?
options: Do not retaliate by switching on your high beams and blinding them in return
Turn your high beams on and hold them until the other driver dims
Flash a long punishment beam and then leave the highs on
Aim your lamps at their windshield by drifting toward the center
questions.explanation: Two blinded drivers are worse than one. Keep your low beams, look to the right edge, and let the other car pass without a glare contest.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: After the glaring car has passed, the road ahead is dark and empty of other traffic. When may you use high beams again?
options: Park on the shoulder and wait for dawn before using any forward lamp
Return to high beams only when no vehicle is ahead of you or coming toward you
Leave the low beams off for the rest of the night as a courtesy
Use high beams whenever you are angry, even with a car close ahead
questions.explanation: High beams are for seeing farther on an open dark road. As soon as a vehicle is close ahead or oncoming, they belong back on low so you do not blind anyone.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are following another car at night and your high beams are still on. When should you dim?
options: Never dim when following
Move closer so the beams pass over the roof and you can leave them on
Dim as soon as your beams shine into that driver's mirrors or light up their cabin
Dim only after they flash you several times and brake-check you
questions.explanation: High beams in a mirror blind the driver ahead the same way they blind an oncoming driver. Drop to low beams and keep a full following count.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A quick flash to remind an oncoming driver to dim turns into a long high-beam duel. How do you end it?
options: Hold the high beams and drift left so they feel the point
Match them beam for beam until one of you leaves the road
Stop in their lane and wait for an apology
Dim at once and look to the right edge
questions.explanation: A brief reminder is not a contest. If they do not dim, protect your own sight: low beams, eyes on the right edge, and less speed. Return to low beams at once, look to the right edge, and do not keep punishing them with glare.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: On a freezing morning the bridge deck looks darker and shinier than the road leading to it. What should you assume?
options: Bridges freeze first
A darker deck is always bare pavement and can be taken at full pace
Bridges thaw before the approach road
Ice on a bridge can be ignored if the radio temperature sounds mild
questions.explanation: A bridge is cooled from above and from the air underneath, so ice forms there while the ground-warmed road is still just wet. Shed speed before you are on the deck.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Sun has melted the frost on the open highway, but the overpass still glistens. How should you treat the overpass?
options: Brake hard at the midpoint to test whether ice is present
Treat it as icy until you are across it
If the highway is wet, every overpass is dry and grippy
Accelerate on the overpass to spend less time on the shine
questions.explanation: Pavement on the ground warms sooner than a deck with cold air on both sides. The shine on the overpass is a reason to be slow and smooth, not a reason to test the tires. Elevated decks stay frozen longer.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A bridge sits in shade while the rest of the road is in sun on a cold day. Where is ice most likely?
options: Shade has no relationship to bridge ice
Ice forms on bridges only during afternoon thunderstorms
On the shaded deck after sunny pavement melts
Only in the sunny stretches, where meltwater refreezes first
questions.explanation: Shade plus a deck that is exposed underneath is a classic ice spot. Slow before you enter it and avoid sudden brake or steer inputs while you cross. On the shaded deck, which can stay frozen after sunlit pavement has turned merely wet.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You must keep driving on a morning when shaded spots may be icy. Which control habit belongs with that risk?
options: Follow the car ahead at one second so you share their heat
Make every input gradual and leave extra room
Use cruise control so the speed cannot change on the ice
Brake in short locked bursts to polish a path
questions.explanation: Smooth inputs stay inside the small grip ice allows. Cruise can keep pushing when the tires let go, and a short gap leaves no room when someone slides. Make every steer, brake, and throttle change gradual, and leave extra following seconds.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Where, besides bridges, should you most expect black ice on a cold clear night?
options: Only on brand-new concrete that has never been rained on
Black ice is limited to parking garages and cannot form on highways
Shaded stretches, low spots, and places that looked wet when the temperature fell
Only in sunny uphill lanes where the pavement is light colored
questions.explanation: Anywhere the surface can cool below freezing while moisture is present can glaze over. Shade and low ground hold that cold. Slow and keep inputs small there.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The first drops fall after a long dry spell and the lane looks barely wet. Why is this moment especially slick?
options: The first drops wash the surface cleaner than a long storm does
A light rain always increases grip by cooling the tires
Oil on the road is only a problem after several hours of heavy rain
Oil and dust float up into a slippery film
questions.explanation: Dry weather leaves a film of oil and dust in the texture of the pavement. The first water lifts it. Slow down and add following seconds until a longer rain washes it away.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You enter a curve during the opening minutes of a rain. Why is the curve worse than a straight stretch in that film?
options: Turning asks the tires for sideways grip that the oily film cannot give
Curves dry first
You should add speed in the curve to push through the oil
Steering grip is unrelated to a wet surface
questions.explanation: On a straight road you mostly need braking and accelerating grip. In a curve you also need cornering grip. The oily first rain takes that away, so slow before the bend.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A steady rain has been falling long enough to wash the surface oil away, but puddles remain. What risk is left?
options: You should accelerate through each puddle to dry the brakes only
Hydroplaning on the standing water
Once the oil is gone the tires cannot lose grip in water
Puddles after a long rain are safer than dry pavement
questions.explanation: Washed pavement can still hold a water film deep enough to lift the tires. Treat puddles with less speed, a straight wheel, and no hard brake if the car starts to float. Hydroplaning on the standing water, so do not return to a dry-road pace through the puddles.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Until that first oily film is washed away, which following decision matches the surface?
options: Keep a dry three-second count and brake later than usual
Shift to neutral so the tires are free to slide in a controlled way
Add seconds to the gap and make brake and steer inputs gentler than on a dry day
Close the gap so you can see whether the lead car is sliding
questions.explanation: The opening rain is a low-grip surface. More time ahead and smoother controls are how you avoid using grip you do not have.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Water covers the road ahead and you cannot see the pavement under it. What is the correct decision?
options: Enter at speed so a wave does not enter the engine
Follow the vehicle ahead if their roof is still visible
Cross if the water looks calm, even when you cannot see the lane
Turn around and find another route
questions.explanation: Hidden depth, missing pavement, and current can stall or float a car. If you cannot see the road surface, the safe choice is to turn around. Do not drive into water of unknown depth.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Tire tracks lead into a flooded dip and disappear. Do those tracks make it safe to follow?
options: No; that car may have stalled or the depth changed
Yes, tracks prove the water is shallower than your bumper
Yes, if the tracks are centered in the lane
Tracks matter only at night
questions.explanation: Tracks are not a depth gauge. Water rises, roads wash out, and the last driver may already be stuck. Turn around instead of following them in. No; the vehicle that made them may have stalled, and the depth can change after they passed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A stream of moving water crosses a low point in the road. Why is moving water a reason to stay out?
options: You should aim downstream and add power
Current can float or push a car away
Moving water is safer than still water
Current cools the brakes and improves the crossing
questions.explanation: Moving floodwater has force. It can take the tires off the pavement and carry the car. Do not enter; turn around. Current can push or float a car off the road even when the water does not look deep.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Shallow splash from a puddle you could not avoid leaves the brakes feeling weak. What is a careful way to dry them?
options: When traffic allows, apply the brakes gently while moving so heat dries the linings
Immediately enter a deeper flood to rinse the brakes clean
Ignore a soft pedal and resume full speed
Set the parking brake at full lock while you are at highway pace
questions.explanation: Water on the brakes can reduce the first stops. A light application at modest speed dries them. This is not permission to drive into a flooded road in the first place.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The signal facing you is dark, no officer is directing traffic, and no temporary sign gives different instructions. How do you proceed?
options: Honk and roll through
Treat the intersection as an all-way stop, then go only in turn when it is clear
Treat the dark signal as a green light
Take the intersection without stopping if you arrived first in time
