questions.explanation: A dark signal does not assign you the right-of-way. With no officer and no temporary direction, every approach stops, and drivers take turns as they would at an all-way stop.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Other drivers are flowing through a dark signal as if it were green. Does their flow change your duty?
options: Yes; the majority of drivers can vote a dark signal into a green
You should stop only if a pedestrian waves you down
No; you still stop fully before entering
Yes; match their speed so you do not get hit from behind at the line
questions.explanation: A dark signal with no officer and no overriding temporary sign is an all-way stop. Other people's impatience does not change the conflict that happens if two of you enter together. No; you still stop fully and enter only when you have a safe turn, because their rolling does not create a green.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An officer is standing in a dark intersection and motioning your lane to stop while cross traffic moves. Whom do you obey?
options: Obey the officer
Ignore the officer and take a turn as if it were an all-way stop
Go because the signal is dark and darkness means go
Follow the car beside you if it disagrees with the officer
questions.explanation: A directing officer is the control at that intersection. The all-way-stop fallback is for a dark signal when no officer is present and no temporary sign says otherwise. A person directing traffic replaces both the dark signal and the all-way habit.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Rain, smoke, or dusk makes other people hard to see even though you can still pick out the lane. What lamps should be on?
options: Turn on the headlights so your car is visible
Leave all exterior lamps off so you do not glare on a gray day
Use parking lamps only and save the headlights for full night
Flash the high beams continuously as a substitute for headlights
questions.explanation: If you need help seeing or being seen, headlights belong on. This is a visibility decision. It does not depend on quoting a wiper statute. Only the daytime running lamps.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Daytime running lights are on, but the sky is dark with storm clouds and wipers are moving. What is still missing?
options: The hazard flashers as your only rear-facing light while you hold highway pace
Full headlights, so your rear lights are on too
Nothing; running lights meet every visibility need in rain and smoke
Only the dome light, which other drivers can see from behind
questions.explanation: Running lights help a little from the front and often do not light the tail lamps. In poor visibility, switch the headlights on so drivers ahead and behind can see you. That is not a claim about a specific wiper law. Full headlights, because running lights often leave the rear of the car dark and the front lamps dimmer than headlights.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You can see well enough to drive, but oncoming traffic may not pick your car out of a gray rain. Why add headlights?
options: Other drivers are required to see an unlit car in rain, so lamps are optional decoration in storms
A gray car is most visible with every lamp switched off
Headlights make your car visible to others when contrast is poor, even if your own view feels adequate
Headlights are only for the driver who cannot see the hood ornament
questions.explanation: Visibility works in both directions. If the background is gray or smoky, an unlit car disappears. Turn the headlights on as a seeing-and-being-seen skill, without relying on a statute citation.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At night your headlights show a limited patch of road and a curve is unlit beyond that patch. How fast is too fast?
options: Any speed you cannot stop within your lights
Any pace is acceptable at night if the posted daytime number is legal
You should drive beyond the beam so your eyes adjust to darkness
High beams remove the need to fit speed to sight distance
questions.explanation: Overdriving the headlights means you cannot stop for something that is still in the dark. Slow until the stopping distance fits inside the lighted road. Too fast is any pace at which you could not stop inside the patch your headlights already light.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your head nods and the car drifts inside the lane. What actually fixes drowsy driving?
options: Conversation with a passenger used as a substitute for sleep
Sleep; only real sleep restores the alertness driving requires
A louder radio and an open window for the rest of the trip
Coffee alone, then continuing without a stop
questions.explanation: Drowsiness is a sleep problem. Air, noise, and caffeine can mask it for a short time and then let it return. The cure is to stop and sleep.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You realize you do not remember the last few miles you just drove. What does that mean?
options: You may have had a microsleep
A memory gap is normal and means your driving has become automatic and safer
You should speed up to a more stimulating pace
The cure is to stare harder at the lane lines
questions.explanation: Missing miles are a warning that part of your attention was already gone. The only reliable repair is sleep, taken at a safe stop, not farther down the same road. Get off the road and sleep before you continue.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You glance down at a phone and the glance lasts longer than you meant. What is happening to the car during that glance?
options: The car pauses its motion until your eyes return to the lane
A glance is safe
Blind travel applies only to paper maps
It keeps moving
questions.explanation: The vehicle does not wait. In the seconds your eyes are down, you cover real distance with no view of traffic, people, or a stopped car. That is the hazard of the glance. You travel blind for the whole time your eyes are off the road.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You start reading a message while stopped at a red light, and the light changes while your eyes are still down. What is the risk as you roll?
options: A message begun at a red light is safe to finish after you are moving
Pedestrians wait until phones are put down
The car cannot enter the intersection until the message is done
The first part of the move is blind
questions.explanation: The stop does not freeze the scene. If your eyes stay on the phone as you pull away, you drive into a crosswalk and an intersection you have not scanned. You can miss people stepping off the curb or traffic that has not cleared.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A child is riding with you and both the front passenger seat and the back seat are available. Where is the child safest?
options: In the back seat
On the driver's lap so you can hold the child in a sudden stop
Standing in the front footwell if a belt is nearby
In the front seat leaning on the dashboard
questions.explanation: The back seat keeps a child farther from the most common impact and away from the front airbag. Use the back seat whenever the vehicle has one. The safest seating position for a child.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A rear-facing child restraint and an active front airbag are both in the picture. Where must that restraint not go?
options: Either seat is equal as long as the vehicle is moving slowly
It must not be placed in front of an active airbag
It belongs on the front seat with the airbag left on
The front seat is preferred for rear-facing restraints so the driver can see the child's face
questions.explanation: A front airbag inflates toward the seatback with great force. A rear-facing restraint puts the child's head in that path. The back seat is the place for that restraint. This is not an age rule; it is an airbag rule.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The lap belt is riding up across the soft stomach instead of the bony hips. Why move it?
options: Across the stomach is the designed position for every body
A high lap belt is safer
Lap-belt position does not matter if a shoulder belt is also worn
A lap belt belongs low on the hips so crash forces hit the pelvis
questions.explanation: The pelvis can take belt load. The abdomen cannot. Pull the lap belt down onto the hips and keep it snug before you move.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Tucking the shoulder belt under the arm feels more comfortable. What protection do you lose?
options: The belt cannot spread force across your chest
You lose nothing
You gain protection
The underarm position is required when an airbag is present
questions.explanation: The shoulder belt works when it crosses the strong parts of the chest and shoulder. Under the arm it can injure the ribs and it lets the upper body pitch forward.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Wearing the shoulder belt behind your back leaves only the lap belt in play. Why is that a bad trade?
options: A lap belt behind the back is stronger than a belt worn correctly
Your upper body is left unrestrained
Behind the back is the right position whenever the belt rubs your neck
The airbag replaces the shoulder belt completely
questions.explanation: Both parts of the belt are needed. If the shoulder strap is behind you, it does not hold your torso, and the lap belt can ride up. Move the strap across your chest or adjust the seat. Your upper body is unrestrained and can strike the wheel, the bag, or the dash, while the lap belt alone loads you poorly.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A pregnant driver asks how the belt should cross the body. What placement protects both the driver and the pregnancy?
options: Skip the belt so the belly is not touched by webbing
Place the lap belt across the middle of the belly
Wear only the shoulder belt and leave the lap belt behind the seat
Lap belt low under the belly, shoulder belt across chest
questions.explanation: The belt should not be skipped and it should not cross the belly. Low on the hips and across the chest, it holds the driver so the body and the pregnancy are not thrown into the wheel.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are hunched against the steering wheel so the airbag cover is inches from your chest. What seating change belongs with that bag?
options: Distance from the wheel is only a style choice and does not affect the bag
Sit back so the bag has room to inflate
Move closer so the bag contacts you sooner and softer
Rest your chest on the cover to hold it shut
questions.explanation: An airbag needs space to fill. Sitting on top of the cover means it hits you while it is still expanding. Move the seat back, and if you are short, use a position that still lets your feet reach the pedals without hugging the wheel.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Horn blasts, flashing lights, and a tight tail tell you the driver behind is angry. What space decision protects you?
options: Match their aggression and race to the next light
Block them from passing so they have to calm down
Give them room and let them pass
Brake sharply to teach them a following lesson
questions.explanation: An aggressive driver is a hazard you do not fix by escalating. Open space, let them go, and keep your own speed and lane position steady.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Your eyes stay on the pavement just beyond the hood at highway pace. What is wrong with that scan?
options: The hood area is the only useful view and mirrors are optional
Looking far ahead causes you to miss the lane you are in
A short stare at the bumper is the recommended highway scan
You see problems too late
questions.explanation: A useful scan reaches far down the road so brake lights, a curve, or debris arrive as information instead of as a surprise. Keep the near lane in your awareness, but do not park your eyes on the hood. Look well ahead to the place you will reach in many seconds.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You have a fresh green at a city intersection. Why look left and right anyway?
options: You should watch only the car ahead until you are through
Someone may run the red or step off the curb
A green means every other direction is physically unable to move
Scanning sideways is needed only at stop signs
questions.explanation: Signals reduce conflicts; they do not erase them. A scan to both sides before and as you enter is how you catch the driver or the person the signal did not stop. A green light is not a promise the conflict is gone.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Before you brake hard for a queue you just noticed, a mirror check belongs in the scan because
options: A mirror check replaces the need to slow down
The rear view matters only when you are parking
You need to know whether a driver behind is too close to survive a sudden stop
Mirrors are only for lane changes and must stay unused while braking
questions.explanation: Looking ahead finds the queue. A quick mirror check tells you how hard you can brake. If someone is tight behind, you brake as early and as smoothly as the space allows and you keep extra room in front next time.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: At an uncontrolled neighborhood junction with no signal and no sign on your approach, what scan happens before you enter?
options: Enter at pace if you do not see a car in the first glance
Watch only the direction you are turning and ignore the other
A junction without a sign is always yours to take
Look left, then right, then left again, and be ready to yield
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled does not mean unoccupied. A three-part look catches a vehicle that was hidden on the first glance. Slow until that scan says the crossing is open. Nobody has a signal to protect you.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: The garage door is closed and you want to warm the engine before a trip. What is the safe choice?
options: Do not run the engine in a closed garage
Idle inside with the door closed so the cabin heats faster
A closed garage is safe if you open one window of the car
Carbon monoxide is a problem only for older engines
questions.explanation: Exhaust in a closed space builds carbon monoxide, which you cannot see or smell reliably. Never warm the car inside a closed garage. Open the door fully and move the car out, or do not start it yet.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Carbon monoxide from an idling car is dangerous in a garage because
options: It sinks into the floor drain and cannot reach the cabin
It is poisonous and can build up unnoticed
It only fogs the windows and has no effect on breathing
It is harmless once the heater is set to recirculate
questions.explanation: People die in garages because the gas does not announce itself in time. The prevention is simple: do not run the engine in that closed space. It is poisonous, it can accumulate without a strong warning smell, and it replaces the oxygen your body needs.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A flagger in a work zone faces you and the paddle or the hand direction says stop. What is the correct response?
options: Proceed if you think the workers are far enough away
Squeeze past the flagger
Honk so the crew steps aside for you
Stop and wait for the flagger to direct you to move
questions.explanation: The flagger can see conflicts you cannot, including equipment and opposing traffic. Obey the flagger completely, not your own guess about the zone. The flagger controls your lane.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Inside a work zone a signal seems to favor you, but the flagger is holding you. Which control wins?
options: The flagger wins
The signal always outranks a person with a paddle
You may choose whichever instruction lets you go sooner
A flagger only advises commercial traffic and you may pass
questions.explanation: Work zones put a person in charge because the usual devices may not match the temporary path. When the flagger says stop, you stop. Follow the flagger even when another device seems to say something else.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Cones begin a taper and your lane is ending well ahead. When should you move over?
options: Use the shoulder to pass the line of cars that merged early
Move early and smoothly into the open lane
Accelerate to the end of the taper and force a gap
Stop in the closing lane and wait for someone to wave you over
questions.explanation: An early move is the predictable one. A last-second dive into a tight gap is how work-zone side-swipes happen. Follow the devices and the flagger.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Workers are close to the lane you are using, even though no one is standing directly in your path. How should you pass them?
options: Honk as you pass so they know to stay back
Move closer to them to avoid the cones on the other side
Slow down, give them room, and obey flaggers
Hold speed if your lane paint is still visible
questions.explanation: People on foot in a work zone have almost no protection. Lower speed and extra space are the courtesy that is also the safety rule, and the flagger's direction still governs if one is present. Slow down, give them lateral room, and obey any flagger rather than holding your usual pace.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A siren and flashing lights approach while you are still inside an intersection. What is the order of your moves?
options: Stop immediately in the intersection and wait there
Speed up and turn left across the approaching vehicle
Back up through the intersection to the stop line
Clear the intersection, then pull right
questions.explanation: Stopping in the box traps you where the emergency vehicle needs to go. Finish the crossing, then move right and yield. Clear the intersection first, then pull to the right and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You hear a siren behind you on a multi-lane street and you are not in an intersection. Where do you put the car?
options: Signal, pull right, and stop clear of its path
Stop in the left lane
Accelerate ahead of the siren so you are not in the way
Pull into the oncoming lane and stop facing them
questions.explanation: Moving right and stopping is how you open a path. Do not race the vehicle and do not stop where you block the intersection you have not yet cleared. Signal, pull to the right, and stop clear of the lane the emergency vehicle needs.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A fire truck is moving through traffic with lights and siren, and a gap opens behind it. Why not follow in that gap?
options: Staying on their bumper helps them by adding another set of lights
Other drivers cannot see you, and you may enter the scene
The gap behind an emergency vehicle is a legal express lane
You should draft them so you get the same right-of-way
questions.explanation: Other drivers yield to the emergency vehicle, not to you. A close follow can cause a crash at the next intersection. Let them go and leave a long gap. Following closely hides you from other drivers and can lead you into the scene they are still clearing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: An emergency vehicle is stopped on the shoulder ahead with its lights flashing and people working beside it. What should you do as you approach?
options: Stop beside the crew and offer directions from your window
Use the shoulder on their side to slip past the slowdown
Move over if you can, or slow and give room
Pass at your usual speed inches from the bumper
questions.explanation: People are standing next to fast traffic. Changing lanes away from them, or slowing if you cannot move over, is the protection they need. Do not crowd the scene. Move over a lane if you can, or slow and give the stopped vehicle a wide berth.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Low sun fills the windshield and the lane markings disappear in the glare. What two responses belong together?
options: Speed up to get the sun out of your eyes sooner
Stare at the sun so your eyes adapt, and hold your pace
Close one eye and continue at the same speed
Slow down and use the visor to block the sun
questions.explanation: Glare steals contrast. The visor blocks the disc of the sun, and a lower speed means you can stop for a car or a person you could not see at the old pace. Slow down and use the visor so you are not driving faster than the road you can see.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A dirty windshield turns ordinary sun into a blinding haze. What should you do before you drive into that glare?
options: Clean the glass inside and out
Leave the film
Smear the haze with a dry hand and continue
Add a darker film of road dust to cut the light
questions.explanation: Grime scatters sunlight across the whole windshield. Cleaning it, dropping the visor, and slowing are the three parts of dealing with glare. Do not outrun the view you have left. Clean the outside and the inside of the glass so the visor and a lower speed have a clear view to work with.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A deer stands at the edge of the road as you approach, and you still have room to slow. What should your right foot do?
options: Accelerate so you pass before it decides to move
Leave the foot on the accelerator and watch only the left mirror
Cover the brake and slow, and expect that another animal may follow the first
Hold speed and swerve toward the deer to scare it back
questions.explanation: Covering the brake shortens the time to a real stop. Animals do not behave predictably, and deer are often in groups. Slowing with your foot ready is the skill.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You pass an animal-crossing warning and the roadside brush is high. How should your feet and eyes be set?
options: Cover the brake and scan both shoulders
Ignore the warning unless an animal is already in the tire path
Speed up through the posted area to spend less time exposed
Look only at the center of the hood until the sign is behind you
questions.explanation: The sign is a prompt to be early, not a decoration. A covered brake and a scan of both edges give you the time a sudden animal takes away. An animal can enter from either side.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Where should both hands rest so you can turn quickly without inventing a legal clock position?
options: Both hands in the center hub is the required emergency grip
On the wheel in a balanced grip that lets you turn without crossing your arms
One hand at the bottom spoke is the only legal grip
A specific clock number is a criminal rule you must memorize or be cited
questions.explanation: You need two hands placed so a turn does not start with crossed arms or a reach across the wheel. Teaching a useful position is not the same as inventing a law that names one clock face. A skill and not a made-up statute.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: One hand is on the wheel and the other is holding a hot drink in moving traffic. What control do you lose?
options: One-handed driving is preferable
Turns only require one finger if the car has power steering
You cannot make a full, quick turn if a hazard appears
A drink hand is as fast as a hand on the wheel
questions.explanation: Hazards do not wait for you to find a cup holder. Both hands belong where they can turn the wheel. Secure the drink before you move. The second hand is busy.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: During a turn you let your arms cross and the wheel slip through a loose palm. What is the better hand skill?
options: Let the wheel spin back through an open palm from a full arm cross
Hook a wrist inside the rim and pull with one arm
Take both hands off and let the wheel unwind at speed
Feed the wheel hand to hand with both hands
questions.explanation: Crossed arms and a spinning rim are slow and easy to lose. A hand-over-hand or push-pull feed keeps you able to steer. That is technique, not a fabricated legal clock position. Feed the wheel with both hands so you stay in a position that can add or remove steering quickly.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Halfway down a steep hill you are riding the brakes and they are starting to smell hot. What shift is useful, and which shift is not?
options: A lower gear is useful
Neutral is useful
A higher gear is the way to increase engine braking
Turning the engine off in neutral is the standard cooling method
questions.explanation: Heat means the brakes need less work, not more. A lower gear supplies engine braking. Neutral does the reverse and is not a coasting strategy. A shift into neutral removes the engine help you still have.

questions.q: Hanae feels steady while leaving a restaurant valet lane and must respond to a dog trotting out between parked cars. What should Hanae assume about reaction time?
options: A familiar moment while leaving a restaurant valet lane keeps Hanae's reaction at a sober speed
Alcohol can already have slowed Hanae's reaction to a dog trotting out between parked cars even though Hanae does not feel drunk
A steady feeling means Hanae's reaction to a dog trotting out between parked cars is still as quick as when sober
Alcohol delays reaction only after Hanae feels drunk, so this response is unaffected
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time before a person feels drunk. Hanae should not treat a steady feeling while leaving a restaurant valet lane as proof that a response to a dog trotting out between parked cars will be as fast as when sober.

questions.q: You are turning left at an intersection. Where should you complete your turn?
options: In the right-most lane of the new street.
In the lane that is most convenient for you.
In the shoulder of the new street.
In the left-most lane going in your direction.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you should complete the turn in the left-most lane available for traffic moving in your direction.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You and Car A are both turning into the same road. Who has the right-of-way?
options: The vehicle turning left.
The vehicle turning right.
The vehicle that signals first.
The vehicle that is larger.
questions.explanation: Generally, a vehicle turning right has the right-of-way over a vehicle turning left into the same lane from the opposite direction.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: Why is it dangerous to pass another vehicle on a hill or curve?
options: Your engine might stall.
The other driver might speed up on the way downhill.
It is harder to stay in your lane.
You cannot see oncoming traffic far enough ahead.
questions.explanation: Passing is prohibited on hills and curves because your view of the road ahead is obstructed, making it impossible to see oncoming hazards.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: You are driving in thick fog. Which lights should you use?
options: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights only.
No lights at all.
questions.explanation: High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Low beams provide the best visibility in foggy conditions.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?
options: Traffic is moving in the same direction.
Passing is prohibited for all traffic.
Passing is allowed when it is safe.
The road is for emergency vehicles only.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line indicates that traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.

provenance.manual: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD)

questions.q: You see a stationary emergency vehicle (A) with flashing lights on the shoulder. What should you do?

Stop immediately in your lane.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.
Honk to let the emergency workers know you are passing.

provenance.manual: California Driver's Handbook (model handbook for general rules of the road)

questions.q: A traffic signal is malfunctioning and showing a flashing red light in all directions. What should you do?

options: At a fixed rate that you cannot speed up

As fast as you choose to drink it

questions.q: What happens if you have drinks faster than your body can get rid of them?
options: The extra alcohol passes straight through you unchanged
Your body speeds up its work to keep pace with you
Only the first drink of the evening can affect you
More alcohol stays in your body and affects your driving
questions.explanation: If you have drinks faster than your body can get rid of them, you will have more alcohol in your body, and your driving will be more affected.

questions.q: Where does alcohol go once you drink it?
options: It stays in the stomach until the next morning
Directly into the bloodstream and on to the brain
It goes only into the muscles of the legs
Nowhere at all until you have eaten some food
questions.explanation: Alcohol goes directly into the blood stream and is carried to the brain.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

options: Only the liquor, because it is the strongest drink
Only the beer, because there is more liquid in it
Only the wine, because it is sipped more slowly
All of them, because it is the alcohol that matters
questions.explanation: It is the alcohol in drinks that affects human performance.

A 1 1/2-ounce shot of 80 proof liquor

questions.q: What does blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measure?
options: The amount of alcohol in your body
How many hours ago you had a drink
The strength of the drink in the glass
How well you can walk a straight line
questions.explanation: The Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) commonly measures the amount of alcohol in your body.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Which of these raises your blood alcohol concentration?
options: Drinking the same amount more slowly
Drinking faster
Choosing beer instead of liquor
Sitting down while you drink
questions.explanation: How much you drink, how fast you drink and your weight decide your BAC. Faster drinking means a higher BAC.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Two people have the same number of drinks in the same time. One is much smaller. What is likely?
options: Both reach exactly the same BAC
The larger person reaches a higher BAC
The smaller person reaches a higher BAC
Body size has nothing to do with BAC
questions.explanation: A small person doesn't have to drink as much to reach the same BAC.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Which part of the brain does alcohol affect first?
options: The part that controls judgment and self-control
The part that controls your hearing and nothing else
The part that keeps your heartbeat regular
The part that stores your oldest memories
questions.explanation: The first part of the brain alcohol affects controls judgment and self-control.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Why do drinkers often not realize they are getting drunk?
options: Alcohol sharpens the senses at first
Alcohol affects judgment first
Alcohol only acts hours later
Alcohol affects only the legs
questions.explanation: Alcohol first affects the part of the brain that controls judgment, which can keep drinkers from knowing they are getting drunk.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: As blood alcohol keeps building up, what is affected more and more?
options: Nothing beyond a mellow and relaxed feeling
Only the sense of taste and the sense of smell
Only the ability to speak in clear sentences
Muscle control, vision, and coordination
questions.explanation: As BAC continues to build up, muscle control, vision, and coordination are affected more and more.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Which driving abilities does alcohol affect?
options: Only reaction time, and only when it is dark
Only vision, and only in very bright sunlight
Judgment, vision, coordination, and reaction time
None of them, as long as the driver feels fine
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects judgment, vision, coordination, and reaction time.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Which drivers are affected by drinking alcohol?
options: All drivers
Only new drivers
Only drivers who rarely drink
Only drivers over 65

questions.q: How does drinking change a driver's chance of a crash?
options: It stays about the same as for any other driver
It is much greater than for a driver who has not drunk
It drops, because drinkers tend to drive more slowly
It changes only when driving on the freeway
questions.explanation: The chance of a crash is much greater for drivers who have been drinking than for drivers who have not.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: How many drinks does it take before a person can show signs of impairment?

questions.q: Besides reaction time, what else does alcohol impair?

Only the memory of the route

Nothing a driver relies on

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

Safe ways to stay alert on a long drive

A rising blood alcohol concentration
